He says he wants to convince us that tongues are Bible and are for today, and that this is Paul’s teaching, not his: “I’m just his microphone.” When we speak in an unknown tongue we speak to God, he says, and there is nothing wrong with talking to God.
Are speaking in tongues and spiritual gifts for today?

That is the requirements. I want to take a closer look at tongues here. I want to convince you today that tongues are Bible, and they are for today, from Paul’s teaching, the chiefest apostle’s teaching. This is not my teaching; I’m just his microphone. It says in 1 Corinthians 14, when we speak in an unknown tongue, we speak to God, not to man. Now what’s wrong with us speaking to God? Is there anything wrong with me speaking to God? When I pray, am I supposed to be praying to men or to God? To God. So what’s wrong with talking to God? Nothing. It’s important.
Are speaking in tongues and spiritual gifts for today?
1 Corinthians 14:2: For he who speaks in a tongue does not speak to men but to God, for no one understands him; however, in the spirit he speaks mysteries.
Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?

He says one who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, and he sees nothing wrong with building yourself up in the faith; he should be encouraged to do it and not wait for someone else to do something for him. He adds that tongues are a sign to the unbeliever, and that if they get the unbeliever’s attention, that is a good thing.
Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?

Secondly, he edifies himself; he builds up himself. What’s wrong with me building up myself in the faith? Is there anything wrong with that? No, it’s not only not wrong, I should be encouraged to do it. I need to not wait for the J.B. [unclear], the mighty man of God, to do something for me. I should be, what? Building myself up. Are you with me? Now Paul’s good. I’m telling you, this apostle Paul’s good. Tongues are a sign to the unbeliever. What’s wrong with that? If tongues will get the unbeliever’s attention, is that a good thing? Yes. See, miracles also get the unbeliever’s attention. See, those are good things.
Is it wrong to build yourself up in the faith by speaking in tongues?

1 Corinthians 14:4: He who speaks in a tongue edifies himself, but he who prophesies edifies the church. 1 Corinthians 14:22: Therefore tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe but to unbelievers; but prophesying is not for unbelievers but for those who believe.
Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?

He says if there is no interpretation the one who speaks mysteries is no profit to others, so it should not be done publicly in the service, but it can be done quietly during worship. If it is not done decently and in order, he says, people will say you are mad, and he says the spirit of the prophet is in control.
Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?

But if there’s no interpretation, there should be an interpretation. If there’s no interpretation, the guy speaks mysteries, and it is no profit to others. Okay, so I shouldn’t be doing it publicly in the service, but I can be doing it quietly myself during worship, can’t I? [unclear], you know, I’m not bothering anybody. I’m building myself up, I’m talking to God. But when I leave decently and in order, I told [unclear] the people go, “Well, what’s going on?” Paul says they’re going to say you are what? Mad. You’re crazy. People, and that’s exactly what they said about us Pentecostals: they’re a bunch of nuts. Why? Because we didn’t do it mannerly and in proper order. “Well, the Spirit’s upon me.” Oh, shut up. Paul said that the spirit of the prophet is in control. You can control yourself and not say anything and just feel good. Amen.
Should tongues be spoken in church without an interpretation?

1 Corinthians 14:23: Therefore if the whole church comes together in one place, and all speak with tongues, and there come in those who are uninformed or unbelievers, will they not say that you are out of your mind? 1 Corinthians 14:32: And the spirits of the prophets are subject to the prophets.
Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?

He says Paul says “forbid not to speak in tongues,” yet in most churches it is taboo and has been said to be not for today. He says he wants these things: a sign for the unbeliever, edifying yourself, talking to God. The Holy Spirit must give the utterance, there will be an interpretation, and if there is none, keep silent.
Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?

Hallelujah. Then Paul says, “Forbid not to speak in tongues.” Boy, you go to most churches, it’s taboo. In fact, they have said it’s not for today. They’ve rewritten the whole Bible. “Well, it’s just not for today.” Well, isn’t that nice. What else is not for today? A sign for the unbeliever, and it’s not for today. I can edify myself, and it’s not for today. I can talk to God, and it’s not for today. No, thank you. I want these things. And the Holy Spirit, again, must give the utterance. It can’t be you showing off with your [unclear], it can’t be you, you know, doing your little thing. The Holy Spirit’s got to move. There will be an interpretation if the Holy Spirit is moving in an unknown language to edify the body of Christ, to comfort it. There will be an interpretation, and if there isn’t, what does Paul say? Keep silent. But he still says what? Don’t forbid to speak in tongues. And so I submit to you today, tongues are important when it’s done right. As a young believer it touched my life, that power of the presence just touched my life. I might have not have known what was said, but the Holy Ghost was backing it up.
Does the Bible say not to forbid speaking in tongues?

1 Corinthians 14:39: Therefore, brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues. 1 Corinthians 14:28: But if there is no interpreter, let him keep silent in church, and let him speak to himself and to God.
What are the goals when we come to church?
He says there are four goals: understanding how spiritual things work, taking spiritual things seriously (covet earnestly the best gifts), pursuing love, and prophecy, which he calls the best gift.
He says “gifts is a spiritual ability, okay, a supernatural spiritual ability,” and that “best gifts” means the higher gifts.
Is it ever right to covet?
He says the Ten Commandments say “Thou shalt not covet,” but here in 1 Corinthians you are allowed to covet spiritual gifts, and the best gifts, earnestly or seriously.
Does sin keep us from the power of the Spirit?

He says sin such as adultery or stealing hurts the people we should be loving, and that eliminates us from spiritual expressions. Paul says you cannot get into the power of the Spirit but through love.
What does he say is wrong with the church today?
He says everybody is worshiping now but not everybody is loving. “We’re into the music, we’re into all that, but we’re not into love.”
Is prophecy my own doctrine or opinion?
No, he says. Prophecy is speaking by the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, “not your little hobby-horse doctrine, not your Calvinist, Lutheran, or Catholic or whatever doctrine.”
Can everyone sing, pray and prophesy in church?

He says we can all sing, we can all pray, and we can all read a Psalm, which is spiritually anointed Scripture, and we can all prophesy one by one. But Paul also said not all prophesy, not all speak in tongues, and not all interpret.
Does Paul say healing and miracles are the best gifts?
He says Paul lists the utterance gifts as the best, and that there is “no mention of healing, no mention of miracles, no mention of discerning of spirits, no mention of faith.”
Why must what we say in church be understandable?
He says it has to be easily understandable, and gives the example of lifting up his voice with a mix of Scripture phrases that makes no sense. “You can’t just use scripture without it making sense.”
Why did Spirit-filled churches have the power of God’s presence?

He says that as a young believer he could walk into a Spirit-filled church and feel the power of his presence about 90% of the time, because they purposed and had a purpose. He adds that they did not do everything right and made a lot of mistakes.
Did he always understand all this?
No. He says he had to work through all of this as a young Christian and was baffled for a year or two with some of it until God began to give him understanding.
Why are people afraid of tongues?

He says people are scared to death of tongues because Pentecostal, charismatic, Spirit-filled churches have “made a mess of this thing,” so people want to throw it out of the Bible. Paul plainly says tongues should be spoken the same way, with an interpretation.
Can I speak in tongues quietly during worship?

He says that without an interpretation he should not be doing it publicly in the service, but he can do it quietly himself during worship. He is not bothering anybody, he is building himself up and talking to God.
Can you control yourself when the Spirit is upon you?
He says Paul said the spirit of the prophet is in control, so you can control yourself and not say anything and just feel good. “Well, the Spirit’s upon me. Oh, shut up.”
What if there is no interpretation of a tongue?

He says the Holy Spirit must give the utterance, and there will be an interpretation if the Holy Spirit is moving in an unknown language to edify the body of Christ. If there is none, he says, Paul says to keep silent.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer describes churches that pursued the presence of God, from a country Methodist church to Baptist churches in Mexico and Ghana, and says the name on the outside does not…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer describes churches that pursued the presence of God, from a country Methodist church to Baptist churches in Mexico and Ghana, and says the name on the outside does not matter. He then explains what he says 1 Corinthians 14:34-35 and 1 Timothy 2:12 mean for women in the church, and ends with what 1 Corinthians 14 says about unbelievers, the Holy Ghost, and orderly use of the gifts.
What does the testimony of Jesus have to do with the church coming together?

He asks what Revelation says about the testimony of Jesus and answers that “the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.” He says “when the church comes together, the Holy Ghost wants to do things, but to do that we got to have understanding and we got to be serious about it.”
What does the testimony of Jesus have to do with the church coming together?

These utterance gifts. What does it say in Revelation about the testimony of Jesus? The proof of Jesus, the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy. Wow. And see, this is what I’m telling you: when the church comes together, the Holy Ghost wants to do things, but to do that we got to have understanding and we got to be serious about it, because we’re the ones that He’s going to use.
What does the testimony of Jesus have to do with the church coming together?

Revelation 19:10: And I fell at his feet to worship him. But he said to me, “See that you do not do that! I am your fellow servant, and of your brethren who have the testimony of Jesus. Worship God! For the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
How does he describe churches that pursue the presence of God?

He says in spirit-filled churches “they pursued the Holy Ghost, they pursued the presence of Jesus, and God would come.” He tells of a country Methodist church where he felt “the power of His presence,” a congregation “in unity, worshiping, praising God,” and a message that was alive, and notes the Bible says God inhabits the praises of His people.
How does he describe churches that pursue the presence of God?

And that’s why I told you at 90% of the time, maybe less, when I walk into a spirit-filled church, they had a purpose to meet with God, the Holy Ghost to come, and you could feel the presence of God. Every once in a while in other churches they would get the presence of God, because God just comes sovereignly and in spite of themselves, but in the spirit-filled churches they pursued the Holy Ghost, they pursued the presence of Jesus, and God would come. See, they would pray, they would worship, and, and God would come. I remember visiting my parents in Alabama, and I usually went to a country church, and one summer when I was there I went to a country church. It was a Methodist church, and I walked in and you could feel the power of His presence just when I walked in. And they were worshiping, this whole congregation was just in unity, worshiping, praising God, and the Bible says He inhabits what? The praises of His people. They knew that when that guy preached the message, it was alive. I mean, that, that message was alive, and these are country bumpkins.
How does he describe churches that pursue the presence of God?
Psalm 22:3: But You are holy, Enthroned in the praises of Israel.
What does he say about having teaching without power? (Luke 5:17, 1 Corinthians 8:1)

He says the power of His presence “was there to heal,” and he told his group it was strange “that we have all this teaching and no performance” while a country church had “the performance without the teaching.” He says “Knowledge can make you proud,” and “you possess because you have it, and these people had it.”
What does he say about having teaching without power? (Luke 5:17, 1 Corinthians 8:1)

And the thing that I noticed, that the power of His presence was there, there to heal. How many of you know in Luke it says the power of His presence was there to heal? And I go, wow. I came back and I talked to the leaderships of our group, and I go, it’s, it’s strange to me that we have all this teaching and no performance, and I walk into this country bumpkin church and they have the performance without the teaching. Are you there? How many you know knowledge puffs up. Knowledge can make you proud, and you can think you possess because you have knowledge, and you don’t, because you have knowledge. You possess because you have it, and these people had it.
What does he say about having teaching without power? (Luke 5:17, 1 Corinthians 8:1)

Luke 5:17: Now it happened on a certain day, as He was teaching, that there were Pharisees and teachers of the law sitting by, who had come out of every town of Galilee, Judea, and Jerusalem. And the power of the Lord was present to heal them. 1 Corinthians 8:1: Now concerning things offered to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love edifies.
What did he see in the Baptist churches in Mexico and Ghana?

He tells of a Baptist church outside Mexico City that “didn’t waste any time,” sang “Majesty,” and “went down on their knees,” until “the presence of God just flooded that place.” In Ghana he says he told another Baptist church, “you got Baptist on the outside of your church and there’s nothing Baptist about you,” because “the presence of God was in the worship.”
What did he see in the Baptist churches in Mexico and Ghana?

I was in a Baptist church outside Mexico City. When I go to third world countries, I preach in all kinds of denominations, and also, uh, here. And I walk into this Baptist church on the outskirts of Mexico City, and they started that service and they didn’t waste any time. Bam, right in. They, they sang “Majesty.” That, that time Baptists didn’t sing choruses, they only sing hymns, but not this guy, this church sing “Majesty,” and they went down on their knees, and the presence of God just flooded that place. I was over in Ghana, and also there I speak in all kinds of denominations. I go into another Baptist church, and when I got done, I scratched my head, you know, I said, you know, you guys, you got Baptist on the outside of your church and there’s nothing Baptist about you. The presence of God was in the worship. When they gave announcements, the power of God was there. They were so sincere and so genuine that everything they did, the presence of God just flooded that place. Are you with me?
Does the name on the church matter, and what happened in Brazil?

He says “it’s not the name on the outside, it’s what you are on the inside.” He tells of a spirit-filled church in Brazil that was “really messed up in their doctrine,” where he preached three times a day for two weeks, speaking “by prophecy,” “by revelation,” and “by doctrine.” He says “when people seek Him, they find Him, and when they find Him, He expresses Himself.”
Does the name on the church matter, and what happened in Brazil?

Hallelujah. See, it’s not the name on the outside, it’s what you are on the inside. And I’m sharing these things with you. When I went to [unclear], to Brazil, the capital of Brazil, there was a church there that was a spirit-filled church, and they were really messed up in their doctrine. I mean, ridiculous doctrine. And I spent two weeks there preaching three times a day, straightening out their doctrine. And you know, when we got, they got it, they got it, they would look at me and say, “Man, you’re a young man, and yet you, you know this Bible.” Well, yeah. I, I spent time, I got serious with the Bible, and I could speak by prophecy, I could speak by revelation, and I could speak by doctrine. I had an advantage. I didn’t have to know everything when I got up there. Are you, are you there? I was getting truth while they were getting truth. That’s the utterance of revelation. God takes the cover off while you’re talking. Oh man, that’s good, huh? You see, and I could speak by prophecy, so I didn’t have to have a lot of notes and stuff, because I had all these sources that the Spirit could use me in. Are you there? Because I had understanding and because I pursued them. Are you there, church? That church grew, as I told you before, in the year 2000 they had 1,300 churches. They just took off once they got understanding. They just took, took off. Hallelujah. This are just a few examples I could give you. A lot of examples here in America and everywhere else, when people seek Him, they find Him, and when they find Him, He expresses Himself, and He knows, God knows no denominational, He doesn’t have any.
What does he say “let your women keep silent in the churches” means? (1 Corinthians 14:34-35)

He reads the verse and says “Now, the law does not say women to be silent. The law says women should be under the rulership of their husband.” He says “it’s not women in general, it’s the husband-wife relationship,” that “the husband is directly under Christ and the woman is under her husband,” and “if I’m not following Christ, she’s got no reason to follow me.” He says people use the verse to “tell women to sit down and shut up,” and he says that is not what Paul is saying.
What does he say “let your women keep silent in the churches” means? (1 Corinthians 14:34-35)

Now we’re going to hit the woman thing again. All right. “Let your women, your wives, keep silent in the churches, for it’s not permitted unto them to speak, but they are commanded to be under obedience, as also saith the law.” Now, the law does not say women to be silent. The law says women should be under the rulership of their husband. Nowhere in the Bible will you find the Bible saying women, when they come to the house of God, the temple of God, the church of God, that they got to be silent. But you will find that they are not to usurp authority over their husband. “If they will learn anything, let them ask their” what? Husband. See, it’s not women in general, it’s the husband-wife relationship that Paul stress back in 1 Corinthians chapter 11, just a few chapters back, that the husband is directly under Christ and the woman is under her husband, and the woman cannot follow her husband if her husband isn’t following Christ. The only thing that gives us authority to say, “Come on, woman, let’s do it this way,” is we’re doing it His way. We can’t, well, “Submit, woman, the Bible says submit.” Now, submit, no, will you, hon, follow me as I follow Christ? See, I have a responsibility to be under the authority of Christ, and if I’m not following Christ, she’s got no reason to follow me. That’s Bible. And people take this and tell women to sit down and shut up, and I’m going to show you that it’s not true, that this isn’t what Paul is saying at all.
What does he say “let your women keep silent in the churches” means? (1 Corinthians 14:34-35)

1 Corinthians 14:34-35: Let your women keep silent in the churches, for they are not permitted to speak; but they are to be submissive, as the law also says. And if they want to learn something, let them ask their own husbands at home; for it is shameful for women to speak in church.
What does he say 1 Timothy 2:12 means by “usurp authority”?

Reading “I permit not a woman to teach,” “nor to usurp authority,” he says that means to “dominate the man,” and that Paul is speaking against control and manipulation, saying “Paul is saying that is wrong.” He says men are wrong when they give in to manipulation “because they should be following Christ.” He says a wife who disagrees should “talk to him at home” and not use church or prayer meetings to “telegraph everything about their husband.” His remarks about how wives behave are his own generalizations.
What does he say 1 Timothy 2:12 means by “usurp authority”?

All right, in 1 Timothy 2:12 he says, “I permit not a woman to teach,” a wife again, “nor to usurp authority,” see, dominate the man. How many know women can be dominators? Yeah. “You don’t do it my way, you ain’t getting any tonight.” That’s control. “You don’t do it my way, then nuts on you.” And they’ll yak at you for two hours, yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak yak, till they just wear you out. And Paul is saying that is wrong. And boy, they’re good at crying. “You’re not going to get me that Thunderbird car.” I mean, they’re good at manipulation, and Paul says it’s wrong, and when men give into the manipulation, they are wrong, because they should be following Christ. Can I hear an amen? A lot of you women have a big grin out there like, “I’m guilty.” See, but to be in silence, and you know there’s a lot of, there’s a lot of expressions of this. Some people say, well, historically the church had the women sitting on one side and husbands sitting on the other, and so, you know, if the woman didn’t understand something, she would yell over at the husband, “What the world is he talking about, Ned?” I mean, no, that’s not keeping the service decently in order, but I can’t really find that in my research. I don’t care if she’s sitting by him. I mean, Becky can try to control my life just two inches away. She doesn’t need a 20 feet. And women like to show they’re more spiritually superior. No, it’s true, it’s true, especially if the man works all day, you know, he works 12 hours a day and he comes home and she’s in prayer meetings during the day and women’s meetings over here, and that man, and the boy, the husband comes in and, “Oh, man, you carnal guy.” And Paul is saying this should not be. That’s what he’s saying. And women should not be doing anything in the church to show that they’re a usurp authority over the man or acting like they know more than the husband and so forth. Paul is saying this is the kind of order you need in the church. And you know, if you got something against your husband or you disagree with him, then talk to him at home. Don’t use the church to speak out your hobby horse belief or whatever. I’ve heard women in prayer meetings telegraph everything about their husband. “Oh, my husband, well, you know, he’s lazy, and you know he a paying the bills.” And so the rest of us, in the next time we seen that man, we, “Oh, jeez.” It’s true. Am I right, Barnes? Yeah. And I would get up and I’d say, “Listen, prayer time isn’t a time to telegraph everybody’s problems.” Can I hear an amen? And all that does is turn the man off.
What does he say 1 Timothy 2:12 means by “usurp authority”?
1 Timothy 2:12: And I do not permit a woman to teach or to have authority over a man, but to be in silence.
What does he say about Anna the prophetess? (Luke 2:36)

He says Anna “departed not from the temple,” and asks, “How do you prophesy silently?” He says she served “with fastings and prayer night and day,” “spoke of Jesus to all of them,” and “no one was shutting her up.” He adds that “this is a Jewish woman,” so “don’t give me this stuff about Jews not letting women talk.”
What does he say about Anna the prophetess? (Luke 2:36)

Anyway, now more proof. Anna, a prophetess, was of great age in Luke 2:36, and departed not from the temple. Departed not from what? Where the people gathered to worship and pray and serve the Lord. She departed not from the temple, and she was a what? Prophet. She [unclear] prophesying. How do you prophesy silently? I haven’t figured that one out yet. [unclear]. You see, it’s not in the Scriptures I’m showing you. It’s not in the Scriptures, folks. She was a prophetess, she was in the temple, she served God with fastings and prayer night and day. That’s more than most of us men do. We can’t even get in one day a year of a little long night-and-day prayer, praying every day, good Lord. And she gave thanks to the Lord and spoke of Jesus to all of them. How you know there’s nothing wrong with that? When you prophesy about Jesus, Jesus Christ, it’s good. You prophesy about the cross, you prophesy about the gospel, the word of God, it’s good. No one was shutting her up, and this is a Jewish woman. Are you there? So don’t give me this stuff about Jews not letting women talk. She’s talking.
What does he say about Anna the prophetess? (Luke 2:36)

Luke 2:36-38: Now there was one, Anna, a prophetess, the daughter of Phanuel, of the tribe of Asher. She was of a great age, and had lived with a husband seven years from her virginity; and this woman was a widow of about eighty-four years, who did not depart from the temple, but served God with fastings and prayers night and day. And coming in that instant she gave thanks to the Lord, and spoke of Him to all those who looked for redemption in Jerusalem.
Which women does he list as prophesying? (Exodus, Judges 4:4, 2 Kings 22:14, Acts)

He lists Miriam and Deborah as prophets, another woman called a prophetess in 2 Kings 22:14 (her name is [unclear] in the captions), the passage “Your sons and your daughters shall” prophesy, and four virgin daughters who prophesied. The reference numbers are as he gave them; see the editor note.
Which women does he list as prophesying? (Exodus, Judges 4:4, 2 Kings 22:14, Acts)

Then you got Exodus 20 and Judges 44, Miriam and Deborah were prophets. [unclear] was a prophetess in 2 Kings 22:14. Acts 21:17, “Your sons and your daughters shall” what? Prophesy. Acts 219, Stephen had four virgin daughters which did what? Prophesy.
Which women does he list as prophesying? (Exodus, Judges 4:4, 2 Kings 22:14, Acts)

Exodus 15:20: Then Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took the timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her with timbrels and with dances. Judges 4:4: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, was judging Israel at that time. 2 Kings 22:14: So Hilkiah the priest, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum the son of Tikvah, the son of Harhas, keeper of the wardrobe. (She dwelt in Jerusalem in the Second Quarter.) And they spoke with her. Acts 2:17-18: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. Acts 21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
How does he explain Genesis 3:16 and 1 Corinthians 11:3?

He reads Genesis 3:16, “Your desire shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you,” and says “the woman works with that husband. She doesn’t drive him nuts, and she doesn’t try to be the kingpin of the home.” He says “a good woman knows how to make her man look good” because men “miss the mark.” Reading 1 Corinthians 11:3, he says women are free to “open your mouth and edify the body of Christ.”
How does he explain Genesis 3:16 and 1 Corinthians 11:3?

Genesis 3:16, “Your desire shall be to your husband, and he shall rule over you.” That’s what the law says, that the woman works with that husband. She doesn’t drive him nuts, and she doesn’t try to be the kingpin of the home and all that. In fact, a good woman knows how to make her man look good, ‘cause a lot of us men, we miss the mark, we need to be made look good. Yeah, we need help. We don’t follow Christ like we’re supposed to. Second, 1 Corinthians 11:3, “the head of the man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man.” He’s just keeping the continuity of the Scriptures, that’s all. Can I hear an amen? So now you women don’t have any excuse. Now you can pray and you can sing, you know, you can open your mouth and edify the body of Christ. Can I hear an amen? Hallelujah.
How does he explain Genesis 3:16 and 1 Corinthians 11:3?

Genesis 3:16: To the woman He said: “I will greatly multiply your sorrow and your conception; In pain you shall bring forth children; Your desire shall be for your husband, And he shall rule over you.” 1 Corinthians 11:3: But I want you to know that the head of every man is Christ, the head of woman is man, and the head of Christ is God.
What happens when unbelievers come in and the Holy Ghost is involved? (1 Corinthians 14:24-25)

He says unbelievers fall on their face and worship, and that this happens “not because we got eloquent speakers, not because we got great musicians,” but “because the Holy Ghost is involved.” He says the Holy Ghost “knows how to convict the person of sin,” and that it is a better testimony when the unbeliever can “touch God and hear His word.” He says “Not some church program, not divorce recovery, the Holy Ghost changes them.”
What happens when unbelievers come in and the Holy Ghost is involved? (1 Corinthians 14:24-25)

The results and accomplishments. Okay, “unbelievers and unlearned come in,” when you’re gathered together, “they are convinced and judged of all, their heart secrets are made plain,” revealed, “and so falling down on their face, they worship God and report that God is in you of a truth.” You see, this happens not because we got eloquent speakers, not because we got great musicians. This happens because the Holy Ghost is involved. And the Holy Ghost, Jesus said, knows how to convict the person of sin, knows how to convict the person of righteousness, knows how to convict a person of the judgment to come, and knows how to show them things to come and knows how to show them the word of God. And when a spirit does things and they get understanding, they change their heart and they worship and say, “God’s in your midst.” And how, you know, that’s a better testimony than we saying God’s in our midst, when the unbeliever and the unlearned can come in and touch God and hear His word, and the Holy Ghost can change them. Not some church program, not divorce recovery, the Holy Ghost changes them. Are you there?
What happens when unbelievers come in and the Holy Ghost is involved? (1 Corinthians 14:24-25)

1 Corinthians 14:24-25: But if all prophesy, and an unbeliever or an uninformed person comes in, he is convinced by all, he is convicted by all. And thus the secrets of his heart are revealed; and so, falling down on his face, he will worship God and report that God is truly among you.
Why does he say many church services in America lack power? (1 Corinthians 14:3, 26)

He says “church services in America don’t have a lot of power in them, in a large percentage of the churches,” because the manifestations were pushed out. Reading 1 Corinthians 14:26, he says “all attending are built up, encouraged, and comforted.” He says “we’re leaning on teachers and, and good speakers today,” when we should be what? “Pursuing the manifestations of the Spirit that comes from the whole body of Christ.”
Why does he say many church services in America lack power? (1 Corinthians 14:3, 26)

But see, we got the Holy Ghost and these manifestations just pushed right out of the church, and so church services in America don’t have a lot of power in them, in a large percentage of the churches. 1 Corinthians 14:3 and verse 26, all attending are built up, encouraged, and comforted. All learn and understand what the Spirit is saying to the text, not what the preacher is saying. How many you know the Holy Ghost knows how to enlighten you to some part of the message or some part of a prophecy, and another guy gets something enlightened from a different part of the same message? Yes. See, that’s the Holy Ghost moving. And we’re leaning on teachers and, and good speakers today, when we should be what? Pursuing the manifestations of the Spirit that comes from the whole body of Christ. Hallelujah.
Why does he say many church services in America lack power? (1 Corinthians 14:3, 26)

1 Corinthians 14:3: But he who prophesies speaks edification and exhortation and comfort to men. 1 Corinthians 14:26: How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification.
What does he say about miracles without theatrics? (1 Corinthians 14:22)

Reading “Tongues are for a sign to unbelievers,” he says so are miracles, and that God can do things “without theatrics, without emotional nonsense.” He tells of Africa, where people were healed “just during the service,” and says “when we don’t have the power, we fake it.” He says he doubted at first, and it happened because “they were pursuing God.” These are his accounts and have not been verified here.
What does he say about miracles without theatrics? (1 Corinthians 14:22)

1 Corinthians 14:22, “Tongues are for a sign to unbelievers,” and, as I said earlier, so are miracles. You get into this thing, you get into the power of His presence, and it’s amazing what God can do without theatrics, without emotional nonsense. He can just do things. When I was in Africa especially, people would get healed. I mean, tremendous things, just during the service, without any camera and the guy, [unclear], “Man, in the name of Jesus!” You know, when we don’t have the power, we fake it. And these people would get healed, just tremendous things would happen in the church service. I told you I doubted it at first. I challenged it. I was an unbeliever. I’m Americanized, it ain’t done that way. God just comes and touches people. I didn’t get to pray for them. My, the Holy Ghost just did it. People come up for salvation, people come up with it’s just amazing. And I’m not talking about one service, I’m talking about steadily, service after service in different churches, God just moved. Why? Because they were pursuing God. Hallelujah.
What does he say about miracles without theatrics? (1 Corinthians 14:22)
1 Corinthians 14:22: Therefore tongues are for a sign, not to those who believe but to unbelievers; but prophesying is not for unbelievers but for those who believe.
How should prophecy and songs be used, and can we have both heart and knowledge?

He says prophecy and tongues are “done one at the most three,” and for all of us who sing and pray, “it’s got to encourage, it’s got to comfort, it’s got to construct the person’s life, not destruct.” Of his early days he says “we had a heart but not according to knowledge,” and he answers “Yes, we can have both worlds.”
How should prophecy and songs be used, and can we have both heart and knowledge?

Wouldn’t we like to be a church like that? Yes. Okay, there’s the utterance gifts, prophecy in tongues, done one at the most three, all right, and, uh, all of us can sing, all of us can pray, all of us can sing and give a song, but it’s got to encourage, it’s got to comfort, it’s got to construct the person’s life, not destruct. You know, in my young believer days I heard the prophecy of [unclear] so many times. You know, he named his child [unclear] because the glory was departed from Israel. Well, that’s really edifying. I mean, that really makes you want to come to church, you know what I mean? I couldn’t wait to get to the next service. “Glory is not here, God’s not around.” Hallelujah. Boy, I go, you know, and I had to wait through all this stuff, I go, what’s going on? You see, because we didn’t have understanding, we had a heart but not according to knowledge, and we created a lot of problems while we also had a lot of results. But we can have both worlds, can’t we, church? Yes, we can have both worlds.
How should prophecy and songs be used, and can we have both heart and knowledge?

1 Corinthians 14:27: If anyone speaks in a tongue, let there be two or at the most three, each in turn, and let one interpret. Romans 10:2: For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
What does he say the testimony of Jesus is?
He says “the testimony of Jesus is the spirit of prophecy.”
How does he say spirit-filled churches are different?

He says “in the spirit-filled churches they pursued the Holy Ghost, they pursued the presence of Jesus, and God would come,” and that in other churches God sometimes comes “sovereignly and in spite of themselves.”
Why does he say knowledge can be a problem?
He says “knowledge puffs up. Knowledge can make you proud, and you can think you possess because you have knowledge, and you don’t.”
Does he say the church’s name matters?
No. He says “it’s not the name on the outside, it’s what you are on the inside,” and he preaches “in all kinds of denominations.”
What does he mean by “the utterance of revelation”?
He says it is when “God takes the cover off while you’re talking,” and he was “getting truth while they were getting truth.”
Does he say the law tells women to be silent?
No. He says “the law does not say women to be silent. The law says women should be under the rulership of their husband.”
What does he say about a wife following her husband?
He says “the woman cannot follow her husband if her husband isn’t following Christ,” and that the husband says “follow me as I follow Christ.”
What does he say it means to “usurp authority”?
He says it means to “dominate the man,” and that Paul says that kind of control and manipulation is wrong.
What does he say about prophesying about Jesus?
He says “When you prophesy about Jesus, Jesus Christ, it’s good. You prophesy about the cross, you prophesy about the gospel, the word of God, it’s good.”
What does he say convicts and changes unbelievers?
He says the Holy Ghost “knows how to convict the person of sin,” and “Not some church program, not divorce recovery, the Holy Ghost changes them.”
What does he say happens when all attend and the Spirit is moving?
He says “all attending are built up, encouraged, and comforted. All learn and understand what the Spirit is saying.”
Does he say God needs theatrics?
No. He says God can do things “without theatrics, without emotional nonsense.”
How many does he say may speak with prophecy and tongues in a meeting?
He says “done one at the most three.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer finishes 1 Corinthians by looking at “church servants,” teaching from Paul’s words about Timothy what a young leader’s essentials are, as distinct from the qualifications…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer finishes 1 Corinthians by looking at “church servants,” teaching from Paul’s words about Timothy what a young leader’s essentials are, as distinct from the qualifications of 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1. He then turns to 1 Timothy 4:12-13 and to Apollos in Acts 18, saying a skilled minister works hard in the Word and stays teachable.
What is a church servant, and how should a church treat a young leader? (1 Corinthians 16:10)

He says a minister is a servant, and “if you want to be great in God, be great in God’s kingdom, what do you become? A servant.” He says Paul closes 1 Corinthians by telling the church how to treat Timothy, a young leader, “without fear.”
What is a church servant, and how should a church treat a young leader? (1 Corinthians 16:10)

Okay, we are in 1 Corinthians 16, of course the last chapter, and Paul’s going to wrap up his seminar talking about leadership. And so we’re going to look at church servants. That’s what a minister is; a minister is a servant, okay, that’s what it means. And so it’s a leader. “He that is servant of the greatest among you is” what? Servant of all. He serves everyone. So if you want to be great in God, be great in God’s kingdom, what do you become? A servant. You know, just simple, that simple. And, uh, he starts out in verse 10: “If Timothy comes, see that he may be with you without fear.” Now he’s approaching it from the Corinthians’ membership standpoint, of how they’re supposed to treat a leader.
What is a church servant, and how should a church treat a young leader? (1 Corinthians 16:10)

1 Corinthians 16:10-12: And if Timothy comes, see that he may be with you without fear; for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do. Therefore let no one despise him. But send him on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I am waiting for him with the brethren. Now concerning our brother Apollos, I strongly urged him to come to you with the brethren, but he was quite unwilling to come at this time; however, he will come when he has a convenient time.
What is the difference between a leader’s qualifications and a leader’s essentials?

He says the qualifications in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus 1 (such as running your own home and being married to one spouse) are different from “the basic things that a leader must have.” He says having the qualifications “does not mean you have the basics of leadership.”
What is the difference between a leader’s qualifications and a leader’s essentials?

Timothy is a young leader. He’s a young guy coming up through the ranks, okay, and Paul is admonishing the congregation how you should treat a young leader. All right, and so I’m going to call this a young leader’s essentials. Now this is different from the qualifications of a leader found in 1 Timothy 3 and Titus chapter 1. You can’t even be a leader if you don’t qualify. Okay, you got to be able to run your own home, all, you got to be the, you can only be married to one spouse, you can’t take much wine and all that stuff. That’s the qualifications. But here are the basic things that a leader must have to be a leader. Just because you got the qualifications found in 1 Timothy and Titus does not mean you have the basics of leadership. Do you understand that? Yeah, see, all right.
What is the difference between a leader’s qualifications and a leader’s essentials?

1 Timothy 3:1-7: This is a faithful saying: If a man desires the position of a bishop, he desires a good work. A bishop then must be blameless, the husband of one wife, temperate, sober-minded, of good behavior, hospitable, able to teach; not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for money, but gentle, not quarrelsome, not covetous; one who rules his own house well, having his children in submission with all reverence (for if a man does not know how to rule his own house, how will he take care of the church of God?); not a novice, lest being puffed up with pride he fall into the same condemnation as the devil. Moreover he must have a good testimony among those who are outside, lest he fall into reproach and the snare of the devil. Titus 1:5-9: For this reason I left you in Crete, that you should set in order the things that are lacking, and appoint elders in every city as I commanded you— if a man is blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children not accused of dissipation or insubordination. For a bishop must be blameless, as a steward of God, not self-willed, not quick-tempered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for money, but hospitable, a lover of what is good, sober-minded, just, holy, self-controlled, holding fast the faithful word as he has been taught, that he may be able, by sound doctrine, both to exhort and convict those who contradict.
Why must a young minister lead without fear, and why will some people reject him?

He says a young leader will not be in fear “if they have their confidence in God and His Word,” and should expect to make “non-flagrant mistakes.” He says some people will reject a minister for reasons like an accent or a divorce, and if they find no reason, “they’re going to reject you because you’re preaching the Word.”
Why must a young minister lead without fear, and why will some people reject him?

So he says first of all, “without fear.” So not only are they not to put him in fear, you know, congregations vote pastors in, vote them out, you know, I know pastors that have died and the family just got kicked out of the church, didn’t even care for the family and all the rest. See, that puts ministries in fear. You know, they can’t support their home, they, you know, they got no security for tomorrow and all this. And he’s said the congregation shouldn’t do that, and neither should the ministry be in fear. And a young leader will not be in fear if they have their confidence in God and His Word, not in their [unclear]. Did you hear that? See, they don’t have to be fearful if their confidence is in the power of God and the power of His Word. Uh, a young leader should know that they’re going to make non-flagrant mistakes, they’re going to fail in a non-flagrant way, they’re going to mess up sometimes, and they know they can correct them, so they’re, you know, they’re not in fear. A young minister knows some people will reject him because of who he is. You know, I’m a country boy, and when I first started preaching I had an accent like you couldn’t believe, and I said words funny, like “resturant” instead of “restaurant,” and some people are going to reject you because of that. I’m a divorced man; some people reject me because my wife ran off with some man back in the old days. Uh, a young minister is going to know people are going to, they’re going to find a reason to reject you. And if they don’t find a reason to reject you, if you’re really preaching the Word, they’re going to reject you because you’re preaching the Word, and the Word holds them responsible, and they don’t want to be responsible. And so a young minister knows that, he doesn’t let that stuff bother him. See, he preaches without fear.
Why must a young minister lead without fear, and why will some people reject him?
1 Corinthians 16:10: And if Timothy comes, see that he may be with you without fear; for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.
Who should a young minister imitate?
He says a young minister “must imitate the apostles,” Jesus, Paul, John and Luke, not popular preachers. He says when we copy some minister, “we are missing the goal way short.”
Who should a young minister imitate?

Number two: “He does the work of the Lord, as I also do.” See, a young minister must imitate the apostles. Imitate Jesus, not Joel Osteen, not Robert Schuller, not [unclear], not the Pope. Amen. A young minister must imitate Paul and John and Luke and these guys in the Bible that were with Jesus Christ. Can I hear an amen? That’s the basics. See, when we copy after some minister, we are missing the, we are missing the goal way short. You got to go to the apostles and to Jesus Christ Himself.
Who should a young minister imitate?
1 Corinthians 16:10: And if Timothy comes, see that he may be with you without fear; for he does the work of the Lord, as I also do.
Should the church look down on young ministers? (1 Corinthians 16:11)

He says “we’re not to count young ministers as nothing,” and that Paul is telling the church to support them and not “look down on them.” He says a young minister also cannot count himself as nothing, because “you’re something in Christ.”
Should the church look down on young ministers? (1 Corinthians 16:11)

Number three: “For this reason let no one despise him.” See, we’re not to count young ministers as nothing, and this is the danger of young ministers, it’s the danger in this church, you know, young ones are coming up, hopefully one day to take my place and so forth, and some older ones, you know, just can’t stand young ministers. And Mike and Christina and Stephanie and some of these younger ones, you know, that, he, Paul is telling the church, support them, don’t look at them like they’re nothing. Sure, they’re starting out; “don’t despise,” the Bible says, “the day of small beginnings.” You know, they’ve been faithful, they’ve got the qualifications to be a leader, and yes, they got to grow in it, yes, they got to expand in it, but don’t look down on them and count them as nothing. Can I hear an amen?
Should the church look down on young ministers? (1 Corinthians 16:11)

1 Corinthians 16:11: Therefore let no one despise him. But send him on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I am waiting for him with the brethren. Philippians 4:13: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.
What does “send him on his journey in peace” mean for a church and its young ministers?

He says peace is “the absence of war,” so the church should not fight young ministers over details, and the young minister has to be at peace too. He says that means not retaliating, not getting angry, not getting depressed, and not quitting “when things get difficult.”
What does “send him on his journey in peace” mean for a church and its young ministers?

Amen. Hallelujah. And the young minister can’t count himself as nothing because people disagree with him and pick on him. And you got to know you’re something in Christ. “I can do all things through Christ who” what? See, young minister, that’s the basics, that is the essentials of a young minister. Number four: “Send him on his journey in peace.” Peace is the absence of war. Don’t fight with the young ministers growing in the church, and, I don’t contest them all the time. They’re not going to do it your way, but as long as it gets done, isn’t that the objective? We be at peace. He’s telling the congregation, be at peace, but the young minister has to be at peace. You see, when you’re at peace, you don’t have to retaliate because people don’t like you, you don’t have to give up. See, a young minister, when they got the peace, how many, you know, Jesus is the Prince of Peace? Have you know most people only know Jesus the Savior; that’s all they know. They don’t know the other 10 things Jesus is. But meeting the Prince of Peace is very important. Hallelujah. And we need to be at peace with young ministers, and young ministers need to be at peace with themselves and the congregation. So young ministers don’t, the basics of young ministry, the essentials is they don’t get angry and lose their temper when they’re talked about evilly and harmfully. They don’t sulk and get depressed. That’s the basics of young ministers. Now that’s good preaching, folks. This Paul knows what he’s doing. They don’t retaliate, and they don’t give up and quit when things get difficult. They hang in there. They don’t say, “The Lord’s leading me somewhere else.” See, that’s the difference between a leader and someone that qualifies for a leader. Say you get the qualifications of 1 Timothy and Titus, you still have to get the essentials for leadership. Can I hear an amen? Amen.
What does “send him on his journey in peace” mean for a church and its young ministers?
1 Corinthians 16:11: Therefore let no one despise him. But send him on his journey in peace, that he may come to me; for I am waiting for him with the brethren.
What does 1 Timothy 4:12 mean when it says “let no one despise your youth”?

He says old folks should remember “you were young ones” and that “there was a time in your life when you were a mess.” He says these essentials apply to everyone, because “you’re all leaders” who are supposed to lead your own life and your own home.
What does 1 Timothy 4:12 mean when it says “let no one despise your youth”?

Hallelujah. And so this is good stuff for us. And how many of you know you’re all leaders? You’re supposed to lead your own life, and how you going to lead your own life if you don’t even know the essentials of leadership? Hallelujah. You got to lead your own home, and see, these are the essential ingredients for leadership. It’s not just not drinking, and keeping your finances together, and ordering your home, and got your kids under control. These are things that are necessary to lead a church. Hallelujah. Now number five, 1 Timothy 4:12. He writes to Timothy, and Paul tells Timothy, “Let no one despise your youth,” or render you as nothing because of your youth. And old folks, remember, you were young ones, and I don’t care how together you are today, there was a time in your life when you were a mess. Oh, you might have thought you weren’t, but ask the older ones when you were younger. Are you there? We all think we’re the, we’re the greatest. Man, well yeah, I’m 20 years old, man, I had my act together. You didn’t have anything together.
What does 1 Timothy 4:12 mean when it says “let no one despise your youth”?
1 Timothy 4:12: Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
How can a leader be an example in word and conduct?

He says a church leader “shouldn’t be using profanity” or losing their temper “and shooting off words that are hurting and tearing down people.” He says “you got to control that tongue of yours,” and that conduct matters too, since Jesus “didn’t need caffeine or anything for a picker-upper.”
How can a leader be an example in word and conduct?

And that’s one thing God taught me, Dave: before you act, go back to your age that they were at. And boy, that made a whole difference in how I approached everything. Go back to when you were that age. So he tells young ministers, “be an example to the believers,” and he tells them what to be an example in. “Live” a way that people can follow you; “in word,” be an example in the Scriptures; “in speech,” the way you talk. Here the word is “speech.” Here, be an example in your, in your speech. You know how many, you know, a church leader shouldn’t be using profanity, and they shouldn’t be losing their temper and shooting off words that are hurting and tearing down people. Isn’t that right? And so young leaders, this is the basic: you got to control that tongue of yours. I don’t care if you don’t drink, I don’t care if you got your home in order and your finances and you’re raising your kids right. Do you talk right? Hallelujah. All right, are you an example in conduct? Young leaders have to be an example in conduct. You know, if they’re out there smoking marijuana with the rest of the kids and doing all these things that other teenagers in America are doing, is that an example?
How can a leader be an example in word and conduct?
1 Timothy 4:12: Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
What does it mean to be an example in love?

He says love “lays down his life,” “sacrifices,” and “you got to give Him time,” whether it is time for God, your spouse or the church. He says “you can’t love God without loving His people, and you can’t love His people without spending time with them.”
What does it mean to be an example in love?

No. See, Jesus wouldn’t do that stuff. Jesus didn’t need caffeine or anything for a picker-upper. You know, we’re leaning on medicine so much, I mean drugs just keep Americans going. Now, you know, they take a drug so they don’t get depressed, and then they take a drug so they can get out and get excited. Jeez, get a hold of the Holy Ghost, and you will be excited for the rest of your life. Hallelujah. “In love.” Love your wife, love your husband, good Lord, love lays down his life, love sacrifices. Love your kids, love your parents, love the church members, and love is spelled T-[unclear] in another way. Love God, you got to give Him time. Love your spouse, you got to give them time, time that relates to them. Not, you know, well, Becky, we’re going to go hang gliding. She’s about as excited about going hang gliding as the man in the moon. I might want to go; we’re going to bond together, Becky, we’re going to spend time together, we’re going hang gliding. That isn’t love. Love is going window shopping. Good Lord, that is a sacrifice, let me tell you. Love is watching some chick flick on TV that just drives you crazy, the boohoo and all the [unclear]. Yeah, “Is the movie good, Dave?” “Oh yeah, great.” Yeah. “Give me Rambo.” Ah, let me tell you something: if you loved the church of the living God, you would assemble with the church. Don’t tell me you love God, you can’t love God without loving His people, and you can’t love His people without spending time with them. These people that stay home, they don’t love, they only love themselves. Am I right? I mean, it’s Paul, right? “In spirit.” You know, you can’t just have the knowledge of God’s Word, folks, you got to have the Spirit of it. There’s two things that are essential in the church. What are they? I’ve drilled it into you for 40 years: the living Word and the living presence, that’s Spirit of God. Those two things are essential. And which one is the highest? The Word. I don’t care how you get, if you can’t love your husband on Monday morning and you can’t go to work on Monday morning and you can’t live in life on Monday, what good is the feel-good stuff? Can I hear an amen? So you [unclear], you speak in tongues, you prophesy, so what? Friday through Saturday you’re a mess.
What does it mean to be an example in love?
1 Timothy 4:12: Let no one despise your youth, but be an example to the believers in word, in conduct, in love, in spirit, in faith, in purity.
What do “in spirit, in faith, in purity,” reading and doctrine mean for a leader? (1 Timothy 4:12-13)

He says there are two essentials in the church, “the living Word and the living presence,” and the Word is the highest. He says our faith has to be in the Word and in Jesus Christ, and that to exhort and encourage people you have to read and study the Bible, so “doctrine has to come from the Bible.”
What do “in spirit, in faith, in purity,” reading and doctrine mean for a leader? (1 Timothy 4:12-13)

Are you with me? Got to have that Spirit. That Spirit drives us into the Word, the Spirit drives us to live right, the Spirit, we need that power, the Spirit in our life. “And in faith”: faith in the Word, faith in Jesus, not faith in Joel [unclear] or Robert Schuller or the Mormon church or the Pope. Your faith has got to be in the Word, amen, and in Jesus Christ. “And in purity.” That goes back to good conduct. “Till I come, give attention to reading, to exhortation, and to doctrine.” How you going to exhort, encourage people if you don’t read the Bible? Huh? If you don’t study it, if you don’t get in a Bible study and learn it, how you going to exhort, how you going to encourage anyone? And so the basic essentials is a young minister must be an example in these things. Can I hear an amen? “And to doctrine.” You got to have the right doctrine. You know, don’t tell me you believe in Calvinism, I don’t even want to hear it. You tell me you believe in Paulism, I’ll listen. You tell me you believe in Johnism and Markism and Matthewism, I’ll listen. But don’t come telling me the [unclear] has some special connection with God, and don’t come tell me Calvin did, or Luther, or anybody else. Doctrine has to come from the Bible. Amen. Hallelujah. That’s number five.
What do “in spirit, in faith, in purity,” reading and doctrine mean for a leader? (1 Timothy 4:12-13)
1 Timothy 4:13: Till I come, give attention to reading, to exhortation, to doctrine.
Why does he say Timothy was the one who cared about the church’s condition?

He says Paul could find only one who would “naturally care for your state,” and that a basic young minister must have “a compassion for the church to see them grow in God.” He asks leaders whether they care about the condition of God’s church “or do you just care about yourself.”
Why does he say Timothy was the one who cared about the church’s condition?

Number six. Here he is writing to Timothy again: “I have no man like-minded who will naturally care for your state,” or your condition. See, Timothy was the only one Paul could find at that time that cared how the church condition was, if they were growing or not. And see, a basic young minister must have the essential of a compassion for the church, to see them grow in God, not waiting for the rapture, but growing in maturity, growing in wisdom, growing in knowledge, growing in life. And Paul, who had a lot of people he was connected with, said the only one I could find was this young minister. Timothy, let me ask you: do you care about the condition of God’s church, or do you just care about yourself? Do you go out of your way to be there to encourage, to live an example before them so they could see it, or you just there because you’re going to get something out of the church? “For all seek their own.” Number seven: you can’t seek your own way of living. “All seek their own, not the things which are Christ’s.” See, what is Christ interested in?
Why does he say Timothy was the one who cared about the church’s condition?
Philippians 2:20-21: For I have no one like-minded, who will sincerely care for your state. For all seek their own, not the things which are of Christ Jesus.
What does “no one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of this life” mean? (2 Timothy 2:4)

He says that as a young minister he gave up the bowling league and the bridge club to get into the Bible and church, and tells of a judge who said, “this guy’s done nothing wrong.” He says it is scriptural to work, raise a family, handle finances and have leisure time, “but then when that’s all we do, we’re not ministers.”
What does “no one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of this life” mean? (2 Timothy 2:4)

See, let me, let me further illuminate that. “No one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who enlisted him to be a soldier.” You know, as a young minister I had to give up the bowling league and the bridge club and all this stuff to get into the Bible and get into church. I was taken to court because I was supposed to be some fanatical Christian that all I did was spend my time in court, I mean in, uh, church. And you know what the judge said? The judge said to my adversary, “What do you do on Monday night?” “Well, we go bowling.” “What do you do on Tuesday night?” “Well, you know, we have a cards, we play cards.” “What do you do on Wednesday night?” “We bowl again.” The judge stopped there and says, “What’s the difference? He’s going to church, you’re playing cards and going bowling. This guy’s done nothing wrong.” Can I hear an amen? Amen. But see, my heart was in the what? Church. I wanted to grow and I wanted to help people, and I can’t help them if I’m out bowling, surfing, got to have my Saturdays [unclear]. Are you there? You wish you weren’t. See, a young minister has got to get his priorities together. Listen, we are told to work in the Scriptures. It is scriptural to work, it is scriptural to raise a family, it is scriptural to have kids, it is scriptural to handle your finances right, it is scriptural to have leisure time. But then when that’s all we do, we’re not ministers. Now we can’t leave any of these necessary things undone, can we? We got to raise our children, we’ve got to work on a job, we got to do those, but we also got to add to it what? God’s time for His church and helping people.
What does “no one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of this life” mean? (2 Timothy 2:4)
2 Timothy 2:4: No one engaged in warfare entangles himself with the affairs of this life, that he may please him who enlisted him as a soldier.
Who was Apollos, and what made him a skilled minister? (1 Corinthians 16:12, Acts 18:24-25)

He says Apollos was “a skilled, focused minister” who was eloquent, powerful in the Scriptures, instructed in the way of the Lord, and fervent in the Spirit. He says “people with just head knowledge kill you with the Scriptures,” and that the Spirit “knows how to present the Word, when to present the Word.”
Who was Apollos, and what made him a skilled minister? (1 Corinthians 16:12, Acts 18:24-25)

Hallelujah. All right, let’s continue here, verse 12. He talks about Apollos. Now, Apollos isn’t a young minister. Apollos is a skilled, focused minister. He isn’t coming up through the ranks, he is in the ranks. Acts 18:24: “A certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, eloquent” and skilled in speech. By the way, Timothy was a half-breed Jew; he was half Jew and half Gentile. That would turn Jews off. He was uncircumcised at the beginning, that would turn off all Jews. See, he got circumcised so that he could be accepted. That’s how you know that’s a good heart, when you do something that you don’t scripturally have to do so you can win people. But this guy is eloquent, he is skilled in speech, man, and he is “mighty,” he is powerful in the Scriptures, because he spent time in the Scriptures, he spent time learning. He is “instructed in the way of the Lord,” “knowing only the baptism of John,” but he’s instructed in the way of the Lord. He’s limited in his knowledge. He’s “fervent,” he’s boiling hot in the Spirit. See, he has the Holy Spirit involved in his life, not just head knowledge. People with just head knowledge kill you with the Scriptures. You ever noticed that? They just beat you to death with Scriptures.
Who was Apollos, and what made him a skilled minister? (1 Corinthians 16:12, Acts 18:24-25)

Acts 18:24-25: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man and mighty in the Scriptures, came to Ephesus. This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things of the Lord, though he knew only the baptism of John.
Why does a skilled minister have to work hard in the Word?

He says diligent means you work hard, and “you’re not going to be a skilled minister if you don’t diligently put time into the Scriptures.” He tells how he got rid of his TV for several years to make time, and says one of the signs of the Holy Ghost is that He “will lead you into all truth,” so he doubts the baptism of anyone with no hunger for the Word.
Why does a skilled minister have to work hard in the Word?

But see, the Spirit knows how to present the Word, when to present the Word. People with the head, no, just, just shoot off everything they know. Timing doesn’t mean anything. “He spoke and taught diligently the things of the Lord,” not the popular speakers of the day. See, he taught diligent, he worked hard. Diligent means you work hard. You’re not going to be a skilled minister if you don’t diligently put time into the Scriptures and speaking the Word of God. When I was a young minister, I turned, I got rid of my TV for several years, because I told God I didn’t have any time, and the Holy Ghost goes, “Huh? You got time to watch 6:00 news, you got time to watch Bonanza, and you don’t have time to read the Word?” “You know, I’m unwinding.” “Well, unwind with Me.” Boy. And so I stopped reading the newspaper for a while, and I gave God that time. See, that’s what it takes. You’re never going to be powerful and you’re never going to be able to speak if you don’t work hard at learning the Word and sharing it with people. Can I hear an amen? That’s how you get skillful. You’re not going to get skillful in the Holy Ghost, [unclear], you know, back in old Pentecost and all that. We would shake, roll on the floor and all that, and feel the presence of God, and we got up thinking, “Man, we’ve arrived,” and they were just as dumb when they got up as when they went down. Why? Because they didn’t spend time in the Word. I had to work through that stuff. God wasn’t excited about me being excited about His presence; He was excited about me learning and obeying the Word. Hallelujah. And what is one of the signs of the Holy Ghost? He will lead you into all truth. And I challenge my Pentecostal brethren, you know, I doubt your Holy Ghost baptism if you don’t have a hunger for the Word, you don’t care about reading it, you don’t care about learning it. There’s, I’m missing here, is that a right challenge? Yeah. “He began to speak boldly in the synagogue.” The synagogues, where the Jews would come, and they had a time where everybody could get up and say their thing. It was a mess, you ever seen those things? Everybody just, man, somebody, man, stood up and he gave him what for.
Why does a skilled minister have to work hard in the Word?

John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.
Why does he say a skilled minister must be teachable? (Acts 18:26)

He says Apollos was limited in his knowledge but “this skilled man was teachable,” and Aquila and Priscilla “expounded unto him the Scriptures more perfectly.” He says the Word may come through a woman, a child or a wife, and asks, “are you teachable?”
Why does he say a skilled minister must be teachable? (Acts 18:26)

And see, the Jews didn’t believe in Christ. He was in a foreign church, a foreign assembly, speaking the words of Christ. And then “Aquila and Priscilla,” they are a husband and wife team, both of them equal in knowledge of the Word, equal in caring for people. They got him aside and they took and expounded unto him the Scriptures more perfectly. See, I told you he was limited in his knowledge, but listen to this: this skilled man was teachable. Are you teachable, or you got this blockheaded look? You were raised a Baptist or a Presbyterian, you’re going to die one. I was raised a Catholic, I’m going to die c-- Are you teachable? A skilled teacher that moves up in the ranks is teachable. Hallelujah. And it’s coming from a woman. Priscilla is a woman, and she’s te-- this Jew don’t like women, you know, a normal Jew, they, women got to shut up, and here comes Priscilla explaining the Word of God, and he’s got enough common sense in him to listen to the Word no matter who it come through. Ah, church, that was good. And it may, it may come through your child. You know, God picks some strange people to bring you the word, let me tell you. Ah. Some husbands can’t even listen to their wife. That’s a good indication He’ll use your wife.
Why does he say a skilled minister must be teachable? (Acts 18:26)
Acts 18:26: So he began to speak boldly in the synagogue. When Aquila and Priscilla heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
What does he say a minister is?
He says “a minister is a servant, okay, that’s what it means,” and that the one who wants to be great in God’s kingdom becomes a servant.
Does meeting the qualifications make someone a leader?
He says no. Qualifications such as those in 1 Timothy and Titus do not mean “you have the basics of leadership”; you “still have to get the essentials for leadership.”
What does he say about congregations putting ministers in fear?
He says it should not happen, mentioning congregations that vote pastors in and out and families left with no security, and says neither the congregation nor the ministry should be in fear.
Why does he say people may reject a young minister?
He says they will find a reason, and “if you’re really preaching the Word, they’re going to reject you because you’re preaching the Word, and the Word holds them responsible.”
Does he say to copy popular ministers?
No. He says to imitate Jesus and “Paul and John and Luke and these guys in the Bible that were with Jesus Christ,” because copying some minister misses the goal.
What does he say peace is?
He says “peace is the absence of war,” and that when you are at peace “you don’t have to retaliate because people don’t like you, you don’t have to give up.” He calls Jesus the Prince of Peace.
What does he say about profanity and temper in church leaders?
He says a church leader “shouldn’t be using profanity” or “losing their temper,” and asks, “do you talk right?” even if your home and finances are in order.
He says love “lays down his life,” “sacrifices,” and takes time: “love God, you got to give Him time. Love your spouse, you got to give them time, time that relates to them.”
Does he say you can love God without loving His people?
No. He says “if you loved the church of the living God, you would assemble with the church,” and “you can’t love God without loving His people.”
What two things does he say are essential in the church?

He says “the living Word and the living presence, that’s Spirit of God,” and that the Word is the highest. He says if you can’t love your husband on Monday morning, “what good is the feel-good stuff?”
What does he say about doctrine?
He says “you got to have the right doctrine” and “doctrine has to come from the Bible,” not from a name or a denomination.
What does he say about priorities among work, family and leisure?

He says it is scriptural to work, raise a family, handle finances and have leisure time, and we cannot leave those undone, “but we also got to add to it what? God’s time for His church and helping people.”
Why did he get rid of his TV?
He says that as a young minister he told God he had no time, and the Holy Ghost asked, “you got time to watch 6:00 news … and you don’t have time to read the Word?” so he “gave God that time.”
What does he say about learning the Word from a woman like Priscilla?

He says Priscilla explained the Word to Apollos, and “he’s got enough common sense in him to listen to the Word no matter who it come through.” He adds that “God picks some strange people to bring you the word.”

p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues through 1 Corinthians 16 with the devoted leaders, the ones who serve behind the scenes and refresh others. He teaches that it matters who you follow, that unity and music in worship are tied to God’s presence, and that “Anathema” in verse 22 is about not loving the Lord Jesus Christ. He closes by saying that loving Jesus means keeping his commandments and learning how to treat other people, and that making Jesus Lord of your life keeps false leaders from leading you astray.
What does it mean to be alert and stand fast in the faith?

He tells the congregation “you are to … be alert,” not just to come and wait for the minister, and to “stand fast in the faith.” He says the faith is “The Scriptures, in Jesus Christ,” and urges “Have the courage of your convictions. Have the guts to stand up for what the Scriptures say.”
What does it mean to be alert and stand fast in the faith?

Now he goes into the attendees, the members, and devoted leaders. A different area of leadership. We had the young leader, we had the skilled leader, and now we got devoted leaders. And he talks to the congregation and says, “Be alert.” Congregation, you are to what? Be alert. You’re not supposed to come just to wait for the minister to get you into the third heaven and all that. You’re to come in alert. Hallelujah.
