What do “serpents and scorpions” mean in Luke 10, and why should babies rejoice? (Luke 10:19-22)

Luke 10:19: Behold, I give you the authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall by any means hurt you. Luke 10:20: Nevertheless do not rejoice in this, that the spirits are subject to you, but rather rejoice because your names are written in heaven.” Luke 10:22: All things have been delivered to Me by My Father, and no one knows who the Son is except the Father, and who the Father is except the Son, and the one to whom the Son wills to reveal Him.”
What are the weaknesses of baby Christians? (1 Corinthians 3:1-3)

He says babies in Christ may still have “some fleshly things working in their life,” and drink milk where the next stage is to eat meat. He says Paul calls them babies because they envy, are jealous, quarrel and argue, and are always in contention.
What are the weaknesses of baby Christians? (1 Corinthians 3:1-3)

Now that’s evidence that you’re in a baby stage, and that’s powerful things, don’t you think? Amen, young people. Yeah, this baby stage is pretty good. All right, 1 Corinthians 3:1, here’s babies’ weaknesses. This is the weakness of babies, that’s why we got to go on to the next three stages. 1 Corinthians 3, verse 1: “I couldn’t speak to you as unto spiritual but as to carnal,” fleshly, “even as babies in Christ.” So babies in Christ may still have some fleshly things working in their life, some carnal things. “I fed you with milk and not with meat.” So babies drink milk, but the next stage is eat what? Meat. Yeah. Hallelujah. And then he tells them why they are babies and carnal: “you envy.” You are jealous, you quarrel, you argue about everything, you’re always in contention. You’re jealous if God uses somebody or God blesses somebody, you’re jealous. See, that’s what the world is. “And you are sectarian.” Now, the word “sectarian” isn’t in your Bible. The word “division” is, and it’s in italics because they added it, and they added it because of the following scripture. All right, they added it because of the following scripture says, “I’m of Paul, and I’m of [unclear],” “I’m a Baptist,” “I’m a Catholic,” “I’m a Methodist,” “I am Independent.”
What are the weaknesses of baby Christians? (1 Corinthians 3:1-3)

1 Corinthians 3:1-3: And I, brethren, could not speak to you as to spiritual people but as to carnal, as to babes in Christ. I fed you with milk and not with solid food; for until now you were not able to receive it, and even now you are still not able; for you are still carnal. For where there are envy, strife, and divisions among you, are you not carnal and behaving like mere men?
What is sectarianism, and why is it a problem?

He says sectarian means “you’re bigoted” and intolerant of other people, and that we “put names on things, and that’s where we make our error.” He says when you possess God and His Word, “you don’t have to be afraid of anybody’s doctrine,” and the new commandment Jesus gave was to love one another.
What is sectarianism, and why is it a problem?

None of that is in the Bible. The word “Catholic” is not in the Bible. The Baptist name of a church is not in the Bible. See, we put names on things, and that’s where we make our error and we become sectarian. And what it is, sectarian means you’re bigoted. Okay, you’re intolerant of other people. Baptists won’t have anything to do with Catholics, Catholics won’t have anything to do with Protestants. That’s sectarianism. You’re bigoted, you’re intolerant, and you don’t know how to love. The new commandment that Jesus gave us was what? Love one another. We quote it, but we don’t do it, right? We’re scared to death of one another. When you possess God and you possess His Word, you don’t have to be afraid of anybody’s doctrine. I’m not afraid to be around anybody, and I haven’t been since I was a year or two old in God. Man, I knew who I was, I knew where I was going, I knew this book, and what I didn’t know of the book, I knew He would reveal it to me and keep me on the middle of the road. Are you there? So I could mingle. I wasn’t looking for people to direct me. Jesus was directing me. I’m yoked up with Him. Are you there? And that’s what the baby stage is. “And because you envy, you quarrel, and you’re sectarian, you walk as mankind.” You walk as humans. That’s what the secular world does. You’re doing exactly what the secular world is, you’re doing exactly what you did before you came to Christ. That’s babies’ problems. Now we’re going to amplify that. You’re ready for the amplification? You need the amplification of this fleshly thing, because you really need to know what you need to work on.
What is sectarianism, and why is it a problem?

1 Corinthians 3:4: For when one says, “I am of Paul,” and another, “I am of Apollos,” are you not carnal? John 13:34: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another; as I have loved you, that you also love one another.
What are the works of the flesh, and what does he call rebellion? (Galatians 5:19-21)

He reads the works of the flesh in Galatians 5:19 and says babies are still working on these weaknesses. He lists sexual immorality, profanity, outbursts of anger, selfishness and rebellion, and says “you’re rebellious when you want to do nothing but criticize the church instead of” contributing to its health.
What are the works of the flesh, and what does he call rebellion? (Galatians 5:19-21)

Ready? Galatians 5:19, the works of the flesh. Now what do babies do? They work things of the flesh still. They’re working on these weaknesses. Okay, “the works of the flesh are evident,” they’re plain, “which are adultery, fornication,” sexual immorality. Churches that are buying into this, homosexuals and acceptable lifestyle, they are not even in the baby stage, right? They’re still trying to get formed in the embryo stage. See, we should be telling people to come out of sexual immorality, pedophilia, sex with children, and all this stuff. “Impurity,” profanity, “idolatry, sorcery, hatred, contentions.” How many you know Christians that use profanity like a secular truck driver? They just curse and, yeah, there’s something wrong. You say what? They need to grow on up. “Outbursts of anger”: they hate one another, they lose their temper. You don’t know anybody loses their temper, I bet. How do you? Yeah. “Selfish.” They only think of themselves. I’m not going to do this because I’m selfish? Oh, they don’t say “I’m selfish,” but that’s why they’re only concerned about their feelings and no one else. They’re only wanting things that benefit them. They’re not interested in anybody else. Very selfish. See, they’re babies in Christ, they need to change this and go on to the next stage. Could that be an amen? Amen. Yeah, see, we need to recognize where we’re at. And I was watching Killing Kennedy, and [unclear] Oswald said, “I’m the man of the house. I’m the man of the house.” He needed to get Christ in his life and be the man that Jesus told him to be. Amen. Jesus Christ should be the man of the house. That’s scripture. That’s right. Hallelujah. Okay, “selfish ambitions”: they’re only looking for things that benefit them. They’re rebellious. You see, when the Bible says “lift up your hands and your name” and they won’t do it, what’s that called? Rebellion. When the Bible says “watch with Me one hour” and we won’t give one hour to God, what is that? Rebellion. When the Bible says pay your tithe and we won’t do it, what is it? Rebellion. Aren’t you glad you came to church today? You see, a rebel draws attention to himself by being out of sync. Hallelujah. The Bible says assemble yourselves together, “even the more so as you see the day approaching.” “I’m not going to church, all those hypocrites, and oh, those churches, they’re so phony, and they’re a mess.” Well, come in and change it. You got to obey the Scripture. You’re rebellious when you want to do nothing but criticize the church instead of saying, “Hey, I’m going to come and I’m going to contribute to the healthiness of the church.” Could that be an amen? See, that’s rebellion, and that’s what babies do. They rebel because they’re selfish, they only think of themselves.
What are the works of the flesh, and what does he call rebellion? (Galatians 5:19-21)

Galatians 5:19-21: Now the works of the flesh are evident, which are: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, contentions, jealousies, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and the like; of which I tell you beforehand, just as I also told you in time past, that those who practice such things will not inherit the kingdom of God.
What does he say about heresy, and what is the difference between ignorance and doing it on purpose?

He says heresies are “doctrines that contradict Scripture,” and that heresy can come from ignorance. He says group theology can make you “a clone of that group,” and “the heresy out of ignorance won’t do much to damage you, but the one on purpose will.”
What does he say about heresy, and what is the difference between ignorance and doing it on purpose?

“Heresies.” Heresies is doctrines that contradict Scripture. All right, and I got that a big one in there, because heresy can be out of ignorance. You know, there’s people that have the ladies wear something on their head to come into the house of God, which the Bible doesn’t say at all. They got that all messed up, but it’s, I’ve been around them, it’s ignorance that they’re doing it. They’re not trying to purposely oppose God’s Word, they’re just really ignorant. They’ve been taught in that group, and this is the problem with group theology: when you’re only fed on one group’s theology, you become a clone of that group, and it may not all be truth. Yes. Wow, that was good. I don’t even know if I can repeat that, but that was good. See, we’re not following a group, we’re not following some new event, we’re following Christ and His Word. And some people, they twist the Scriptures to their own destruction. They do it on purpose because they want to sin. Okay, they want to sin, and it’s on purpose. That is the horrible heresy, and you got to be careful of that. The heresy out of ignorance won’t do much to damage you, but the one on purpose will. “Envy, murders, drunkenness, partying.” So that’s babies. So when Christians do that, they’re babies. Now the party group, they laugh at the heresy group, and the heresy group laughs at the rebellious group, but we’re all in the same stage, and what stage is it? We’re babies. We got to grow up, we got to go on to maturity, we got to get this meat of the Word in us.
What does he say about heresy, and what is the difference between ignorance and doing it on purpose?

2 Peter 3:16: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.
What does it mean that believers are God’s house, built on the apostles? (Hebrews 3:6, Ephesians 2:19-22)

He says “the people are the house of God,” not a building, and that we hold on “until you die or Jesus comes.” He says believers are built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, growing into a holy temple, and that the goal of assembly is God’s presence: “that’s where Dave Kincer learns, that’s where Dave Kincer gets changed.”
What does it mean that believers are God’s house, built on the apostles? (Hebrews 3:6, Ephesians 2:19-22)

What is the spiritual house and the priesthood being built up? Hebrews 3:6: “Jesus Christ, His Son over His own house, whose house are we?” We are the house of God. Crystal Cathedral isn’t the house of God, this barn isn’t the house of God, the people are the house of God. “If we hold the confidence and rejoicing of hope firm to the end.” You know, once saved always saved, don’t believe it. You got to hold on until you die or Jesus comes. “Upon this rock,” Matthew 16:18, “I will build My church, and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” Very powerful, young people. He wants to build you up to where you are the aggressor and tearing down the strongholds of the enemy, and the gates of hell cannot keep you from, uh, setting captives free and all the rest. That’s the baby stage. Ephesians 2:19-20: “You are built upon the foundation of the apostles and the prophets.” I trust that that is your goal, to only listen to the teachings of the apostles and the prophets. Be careful of people’s opinions. “Jesus Christ Himself being the chief cornerstone, in whom all the building, fitly framed together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord.” See, we’re growing into a temple, and we’re growing into righteousness. All through my Christian walk, I’ve heard these people say, “Well, you know, I used to couldn’t do that, but I’m mature now.” It is a holy temple we’re growing into. You see, a righteous temple we’re growing into, and when you say, “Now I’m at a place where it’s okay for me to violate God’s Word,” that’s not maturity, that’s stupidity. “You also are built together for a habitation of God through the Spirit.” Now this is the power of the corporate body. When we come together, we’re supposed to come with something. It says in 1 Corinthians 11, we don’t come to get, we come with something to give. And the corporate place is where God has designed the real growth. When we come together, we grow into a habitation, a dwelling place. God comes and dwells, and He ministers to us, He teaches us, He changes us, if we allow His presence to come. And so the goal of assembly is what? His habitation. Not to get a lady, not to get a man, not to get someone to buy my product of my business, but the main goal is we assemble together for His presence to come. That’s where Dave Kincer learns, that’s where Dave Kincer gets changed. 1 Peter 2:9: “You are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood.” Now, young people, this is powerful. Jesus said, “You haven’t chosen Me, I’ve chosen you.” He came along and touched your life and you responded. You are a royal, kingly priesthood, a holy nation, a special people. “Peculiar” doesn’t mean you’re weird and you do weird things; it means you’re special, you’re valuable.
What does it mean that believers are God’s house, built on the apostles? (Hebrews 3:6, Ephesians 2:19-22)

Hebrews 3:6: but Christ as a Son over His own house, whose house we are if we hold fast the confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm to the end. Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it. Ephesians 2:19-22: Now, therefore, you are no longer strangers and foreigners, but fellow citizens with the saints and members of the household of God, having been built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, Jesus Christ Himself being the chief cornerstone, in whom the whole building, being fitted together, grows into a holy temple in the Lord, in whom you also are being built together for a dwelling place of God in the Spirit. 1 Peter 2:9: But you are a chosen generation, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, His own special people, that you may proclaim the praises of Him who called you out of darkness into His marvelous light; John 15:16: You did not choose Me, but I chose you and appointed you that you should go and bear fruit, and that your fruit should remain, that whatever you ask the Father in My name He may give you.
What does it mean that Christians are “kings and priests”? (Revelation 1:6)

He says priests ministered both to God and to the people, so he comes to minister to God through prayer, worship and learning His Word, and also to serve the people. He says “when the people aren’t in my agenda, I’m off balance, and when God isn’t on my agenda, I’m off balance.”
What does it mean that Christians are “kings and priests”? (Revelation 1:6)

“That you should show forth” the what? “Praises of Him who has called you out of darkness and into His marvelous light.” Revelations 1:6: Jesus has made us kings and priests unto God. Now, if you know your Bible, priests both ministered to God and ministered to the people. So see, I come to minister to God through prayer and worship and learning His Word and so forth, but I also come to serve the people. And when the people aren’t in my agenda, I’m off balance, and when God isn’t on my agenda, I’m off balance. I’m a priest who ministers to God, and then because I minister to God and He touches me, then I can, then I can with some power minister to others. All right, you guys got that? Now we are the spiritual house being built up. Very powerful stuff.
What does it mean that Christians are “kings and priests”? (Revelation 1:6)
Revelation 1:6: and has made us kings and priests to His God and Father, to Him be glory and dominion forever and ever. Amen.
What are the spiritual sacrifices of babies: praise and partnership? (Hebrews 13:15-16)

He says the first sacrifice is praise, “the fruit of our lips,” meaning to boast about and brag about Jesus Christ and His Word, and the second is to do good. He says “fellowship” here is partnership, a commitment to work together toward the goal of the church, not just talking together.
What are the spiritual sacrifices of babies: praise and partnership? (Hebrews 13:15-16)

All right, now we’ll go to the fourth one: what are the four spiritual sacrifices of babies? You know, the fourth stage was they offer up spiritual sacrifices. What are these four spiritual sacrifices of babies? Okay, number one, Hebrews 13:15: “By Him, therefore, let us offer the sacrifice of” what? Praise. You learned Friday what the word “praise” means. What does the word “praise” mean? I heard you guys say it: to boast about, to brag about. Okay, Jesus Christ and His Word. Okay, that is “the fruit of your lips.” It tells you where the praise comes from. If I zip my lip, there’s no praise. “The fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.” Now, how many know we should be thankful that our name is written in the Lamb’s Book of Life? Yes. We should be thankful that Jesus forgave us. If nothing else, “Lord, thank You for saving me. Thank You, Lord, for putting my name in heaven.” You got powerful things to praise Him and thank Him for. All right, that is number one, the sacrifice of praise. Say the word “praise.” Praise, praise. Praise should be a very high priority in the church. Praise is mentioned in joy way more times than mourning and sorrow and all that stuff. Number two, Hebrews 13:15 and 16: “Do not forget to do good.” And number three, fellowship, “for with such sacrifices,” plural, “God is well pleased.” So these sacrifices are three. Fellowship is not what you think it is here. It isn’t just us coming together and talking. Fellowship here is partnership, koinonia, partnership, commitment to work together, to partner together to the end result that’s profitable for the whole. See, I can fellowship with you without partnering with you. I can come in, fellowship and say, “Hi, Jacob, how you doing? It’s good to see you,” and, but when I partner with him, I work with him for the end goal of the church. It’s not me doing my thing, it’s not him doing his thing, it’s us doing what we need to do to reach the goal of the church. Are you with me? So when you’re a partner in a business, you make sure you are productive and the product is the best quality, because the end result is a profitable business. And that’s the word in here, “partner.” I must show up for work, I must be involved in this.
What are the spiritual sacrifices of babies: praise and partnership? (Hebrews 13:15-16)

Hebrews 13:15-16: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
Why does he say babies’ praise defeats the enemy and the avenger? (Psalm 8:2)

He says Jesus quoted Psalm 8:2, “out of the mouth of babies and sucklings,” and that God has given baby Christians “a very powerful tool”: if you praise and thank Him, He will use it to defeat your enemies and the avenger, who is Satan. He says “you never hear them say, ‘Let’s praise about it.’”
Why does he say babies’ praise defeats the enemy and the avenger? (Psalm 8:2)

Jesus said unto them, “Have you never read?” I want to show you why your praise is so important. “Have you never read?” And that’s the problem, we don’t read. “Out of the mouth of babies,” out of the mouth of what stage? Babies “and sucklings You have perfected,” or prepared, “praise.” See, this is Jesus talking. All right, then we go to Psalm 8:2 that He quoted, and it says in Psalm 8:2, “Out of the mouth of babies and sucklings You have ordained,” or appointed, “strength, because of Your enemies, that You might still the enemy and the avenger.” Now, young people, God has given babies, young Christians, a very powerful tool. If you will praise Him, if you will thank Him, He will use it as a tool to defeat your enemies and defeat the avenger, who is Satan. You see? Are you there? Now everybody wants to call on a prayer hotline or 24-hour hotline or something else. I guarantee you, if you will operate this principle and get up in the morning and praise and thank God and come to church and praise and thank God, that God will go before you and defeat your enemies and defeat the avenger. You see, the avenger has a right to come and hold you accountable for your sin, that’s Satan. But praise, God says, “Back off.” Amen. Yeah. Yes. You see, we need God in here. When you praise Him and you speak well of Him and you boast to Him, when the Satan comes to say, “Hey, this guy deserves to be punished, be sick and lose his job and all this because he’s disobeyed in this area,” God says, “Back off. He’s a baby growing, and he’s praising Me. Stay in your place.” Very powerful tool. Hallelujah. You always hear baby Christians say, “I pray about it.” Well, let’s pray about it. You never hear them say, “Let’s praise about it.” You know, “I got this problem in my life.” “Well, let’s pray about it.” Why don’t you switch it around and say, “Let’s praise about it”? God said if I, as a baby, would praise Him, I would thank Him, I would lift up my voice unto Him with my lips, that He would still the enemy and the avenger. Wow, that was good. You got that, young ones? Sometimes you can’t follow these older ones. They get into retirement and the old folks’ mentality, and they just kind of putting in their time, you know, punching the clock, waiting to die and go to heaven. You got to follow people that are following Christ, like Paul says, “Follow me as I follow Christ.” Hallelujah. That’s true. A lot of Christians, older ones, just waiting to go to heaven, watching the clouds go by, or watching the TV screen go by, or bowling, or whatever else, just waiting for the rapture, and they’re not operating the principles that bring power to the church. They’re selfish. They don’t come to church with praise because they’re not interested in where God delivers other people or not.
Why does he say babies’ praise defeats the enemy and the avenger? (Psalm 8:2)

Matthew 21:16: and said to Him, “Do You hear what these are saying?” And Jesus said to them, “Yes. Have you never read, ‘Out of the mouth of babes and nursing infants You have perfected praise’?” Psalm 8:2: Out of the mouth of babes and nursing infants You have ordained strength, Because of Your enemies, That You may silence the enemy and the avenger.
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice? (Romans 12:1-2)

He says “the body’s got to be involved”: lifting hands, lifting voices, kneeling, bowing, dancing and praying. He says “transformed” means changed into something beautiful through a process, and the “renewing of your mind” is “the complete changing of your thinking.”
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice? (Romans 12:1-2)

The fourth one: “Present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy and acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service.” Bible, the people always tell me, “Well, I don’t want to be in the flesh, I want the Spirit, I want to be in the Spirit.” The Bible says, “Let all flesh praise the Lord.” How you going to lift your hands without your flesh responding? How you going to bow until you tell your body to respond? Your body has got to be involved. So present your body as a what? Living sacrifice. Not only living, holy, but doing the things God tells us to do: lifting our hands, lifting our voices, kneeling, bowing, dancing, playing instruments, worshiping God, praying. You see, the body’s got to be involved. You’ve got to engage your body to get this stuff done. “And do not be conformed to this world.” Don’t imitate the world, young people, “but be transformed.” That word “transformed” is “metamorphous,” changed into a beautiful creature. You see, changed into something beautiful, change totally, and it is a process. That’s why we’re in the baby stage, we’re in a process. And when you’re in the baby stage and you know it’s okay, don’t throw babies out of the church. Don’t throw yourself out of the church. Just recognize, I’m a baby, I’ve got to change. And we do that by giving our bodies a living sacrifice. And the word “renewing of your mind” really means the complete changing of your thinking. How many need some changing in your thinking? Yeah. And it comes from the sacrifice of your body: reading the Word, studying the Word, going to church, praying, discipline this body to do what God said to do, and then God takes it and makes it a spiritual power. Thank God for the baby stage. Now see, somehow I learned this as a young Christian, and when people would attack me and accuse me, I didn’t worry about it, because I knew I was in the process of being changed. I couldn’t teach it like I’m telling you, but I knew I was in that process, and I knew somewhere tomorrow this problem I had, this sin I had, the selfishness I had, would be gone, because that’s what He promised. But as years went by, then I can teach it clearly because I understand, and it’s in the book. Look, the sad thing is people are staying babies when they need to go on.
What does it mean to present your body as a living sacrifice? (Romans 12:1-2)

Romans 12:1-2: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service. And do not be conformed to this world, but be transformed by the renewing of your mind, that you may prove what is that good and acceptable and perfect will of God.
Does praise work? (2 Chronicles 5:13 and following God’s pattern)

He checks whether praise worked in the Bible, pointing to the trumpeters and singers who praised as one so that “the presence of God came when they praised Him.” He says music is a tool and “don’t worship music, use music to worship God,” and that God’s presence came when the pattern was followed, not when we decide what we want to do.
Does praise work? (2 Chronicles 5:13 and following God’s pattern)

All right. Now in closing, does praise work? Okay, and you’ll see I do this with a lot of God’s principles. I go back to the Bible and I check out if it worked, because God is the same what? Yesterday, today, and forever. Okay, so we go to [unclear] Chronicles 5:13: “As the trumpeters and singers were as one to make one sound in praising,” what’s the word? Praising and thanking the Lord, saying, “For He is good, for His mercy endures forever,” that then the house was filled with a cloud, even the house of the Lord. The presence of God came when they praised Him. Music is very important in the church, but let me tell you, it is not to be worshiped. Jesus, we got no record of Him using music, we got no record of Him having concerts, but we do have a record that it is a tool that the church is to use to praise and worship Him. Are you with me? Don’t worship music, use music to worship God. All right, next one. Hebrews 8:5 in Exodus 25:40: “Make all things according to the pattern shown to you on the mount.” Mr. Barnes covered this clearly. There was a pattern that had to be followed, and when it was followed in Exodus 40:34, the glory of the Lord filled the tabernacle. But they had to first follow the pattern, they had to first follow God’s order, then the presence come. We want God to bless what we decide we want to do. We don’t want to lift our hands, we don’t want to bow, we don’t want to shout to the Lord with a voice of triumph. So, you know, we go, “This is us, bless me.” God says, “No, you change, and I’ll bless you.”
Does praise work? (2 Chronicles 5:13 and following God’s pattern)

2 Chronicles 5:13: indeed it came to pass, when the trumpeters and singers were as one, to make one sound to be heard in praising and thanking the LORD, and when they lifted up their voice with the trumpets and cymbals and instruments of music, and praised the LORD, saying: “For He is good, For His mercy endures forever,” that the house, the house of the LORD, was filled with a cloud, Hebrews 8:5: who serve the copy and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was divinely instructed when he was about to make the tabernacle. For He said, “See that you make all things according to the pattern shown you on the mountain.” Exodus 25:40: And see to it that you make them according to the pattern which was shown you on the mountain. Exodus 40:34: Then the cloud covered the tabernacle of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.
How did praise free Jonah and Paul and Silas?

He says Jonah, in the belly of the fish, praised and thanked God instead of calling “the 24-hour hotline,” and was released. He says Paul and Silas, beaten and shackled at midnight, prayed and sang praises, and an earthquake opened the doors and set every prisoner free.
How did praise free Jonah and Paul and Silas?

Amen. Hallelujah. We got to follow the pattern. All right, now Jonah 2:9 and 10. You guys all know the story of Jonah, right? Yeah, he rebelled against God, didn’t want to go preach to the sinners, so they threw him overboard and a fish swallowed him. Now he’s down in the belly of this big fish that God created, special fish. Okay, special fish God created, and if you don’t think God can get you, He’s got a lot of fish waiting for you. You may not be a fish in the water, but He’s got a fish waiting for you. That fish swallow you. So here’s Jonah in the dark belly of the, well, all right, and this fish is swimming all around the ocean and all this, and Jonah comes to his senses, and this is what he did before he was released from the fish: “I will sacrifice unto You with a voice of thanksgiving. I will pay that which I have vowed.” And the Lord spake unto the fish, and it vomited out Jonah upon the dry land. See, Jonah said, like we do, “Lord, I’m going to serve You,” and then he decided he didn’t want to in this area. All right, so in the belly of the fish he came to his senses. Instead of praying, instead of calling the 24-hour hotline, he began to praise God and thank God for this fish, thank God for being thrown overboard, thank God that God would come and tell him to go to Nineveh with a message. And then God spoke to the fish and, whoop, Jonah was released from his situation. See, it does work. It worked back then at midnight. Midnight, Paul and Silas are in prison. They’re shackled, rats running all over, human dung everywhere, human, ear, on everywhere. They had to go to the bathroom in the shackles, they, you, ah, it was the pits, it stunk, it was horrible. Now they are there, they had just been beaten for the testimony of Christ, for preaching the gospel, so their back is raw, they’re in these shackles. Instead of calling the 24-hour hotline, instead of saying, “Church, pray for us, oh God, that’s such a bad thing,” they prayed and sang what? Praises unto God, and the prisoners heard them. What? None of this silent stuff. The prisoners heard them, and suddenly there was a great earthquake, so the foundations of the prisons were shaken, immediately all the doors were open, and all the prisoners’ bands were loosed. Every prisoner was set free. You want to be set free from the bondage of sin, from bondages of habits and addictions and so forth? I guarantee you, if you will use this principle of praise that babies have a right to use, you may not be perfect yet, you may have some sin in your life, but if you will use this principle of praise, God will liberate you, and God will spew you out of your predicament.
How did praise free Jonah and Paul and Silas?

Jonah 2:9-10: But I will sacrifice to You With the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.” So the LORD spoke to the fish, and it vomited Jonah onto dry land. Acts 16:25-26: But at midnight Paul and Silas were praying and singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening to them. Suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken; and immediately all the doors were opened and everyone’s chains were loosed.
Can praise move a city or a nation?

He says the American church wants “the latest band” and music without praising or focusing on Jesus, and there is “no growth.” Pointing to the crowd that praised Jesus entering Jerusalem so that the city “was moved,” he says that if the church praises, God “has the power to perform” what He promised, and “we got to change things from the top down, and that’s Jesus.”
Can praise move a city or a nation?

Amen. But not the American church. We want to come with the latest band, we want to come with the best singers, and we want to enjoy music like we do Monday through Friday going to work. We want to hear the same kind of music, you know, just put a little God, you know, word “Jesus” in it or something, and, uh, music does nothing for you. You’re not meeting with God, nothing is happening in your life. Why? Because you’re not operating the principle of praise, and you’re not focusing on Jesus, who is the liberator, the healer, the deliverer, the forgiver, the builder of the church. You’re not focusing on Him, and so you’re going and you’re coming, day after day, Sunday after Sunday, week after week, and no growth. And God forbid that you get up in the morning and thank God and praise God first thing. But I submit to you, praise works. How many want to see [unclear] reach for the gospel? America. Okay, look here. Jesus had been to Jerusalem every feast day since He was born, and nowhere is this recorded that the city was moved when Jesus came in, but a great multitude would spread their clothes and the tree branches on the road, crying out, “Hosanna to the Son of David! Blessed is He that comes in the name of the Lord! Hosanna in the highest!” And when He had come into Jerusalem, the city was what? Moved. It was shaken, and they responded and said what? “Who is this man?” He had been there every feast day since he was born, and they never, ever were moved to ask who Jesus was. And I submit to the church in America, if we will come in and sacrifice the praise, the fruit of our lips, lifting our hands, lifting our voices unto Him, that God who is the same yesterday, today, and forever, the God who promised these things also has the power to perform them, and we can see our families moved, we can see [unclear] move, we see California move, and America moved, because God will move them. Amen. Doesn’t matter who’s elected and all this stuff; it’s going to matter what God does with the ones who are elected. Now I’m not saying don’t vote, don’t take that wrong. I’m saying don’t lean on the fact if we get the right person in office, things are going to change. We got to change things from the top down, and that’s Jesus.
Can praise move a city or a nation?

Matthew 21:8-10: And a very great multitude spread their clothes on the road; others cut down branches from the trees and spread them on the road. Then the multitudes who went before and those who followed cried out, saying: “Hosanna to the Son of David! ‘Blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD!’ Hosanna in the highest!” And when He had come into Jerusalem, all the city was moved, saying, “Who is this?”
What does he say the embryo stage is?

He says if you are not in the Word and growing, not coming to Jesus, and not letting God build you by the Word and the Spirit, “you’re still in the embryo stage.” In other words, “you haven’t been born again.”
Who does he say we come to?
He says we come “to Jesus only,” and not to a church, a minister or a group.
How much time does he say a believer should spend with God and His Word?
He says you “should be spending an hour a day with God and His Word, growing,” and should be in the house of God learning the Word and “getting built.”
What three baptisms does he list?

He lists baptism in the body of Christ, “where God places in as He sees fit,” baptism in the Holy Ghost, “where the power of God comes upon you to be a witness unto Him,” and baptism in water, “where your old man of sin is put to death and you rise a new creature.”
What does he say about the resurrection of the dead?

He says there is going to be a resurrection of the dead, that God knows where everyone is whether “buried at sea” or cremated, and that you will live in an undecaying body forever, “either in hell or in heaven.”
Does he say everyone will give account to God?
Yes. He says “everyone shall give account of himself to God,” and one day people “got to stand before Jesus and give an account of everything they said and everything they did, and that is no joke.”
What does he say repentance looks like for a baby Christian?

He says a baby Christian “is one that’s turned from sin,” stopping being a thief, stopping sexual immorality and stopping getting drunk and high, and turning to right. He says you may still struggle but “you’re turning from them, that’s the baby stage.”
What does he mean by being yoked with Jesus?
He says when two oxen are yoked, the weak one follows the lead of the strong one, so he had to “yoke up with Jesus” and let Him be his example and teacher rather than “brother so-and-so.”
Does he say Luke 10:19 is about handling snakes?
No. He says some people “handle snakes and so forth,” but that the “serpents and scorpions” are spirits of the kingdom of darkness, and “you’re destroying them, and you’re tearing them down.”
Does he say it’s okay to be a baby Christian?
Yes. He says “there’s nothing wrong with the baby stage if that’s where I’m at,” but “I got to grow in this power.” The thing to thank God for is that your name is in the Book of Life.
What does he say the new commandment is?
He says it is to love one another: “we quote it, but we don’t do it.”
What does he call refusing to assemble, give an hour, or tithe?
He calls it rebellion. He says when the Bible says to watch one hour, pay your tithe, or assemble together and “we won’t do it, what is it? Rebellion.”
What does he say the goal of assembling together is?
He says it is “his habitation,” God’s presence coming. It is “not to get a lady, not to get a man, not to get someone to buy my product,” but to assemble for His presence to come.
What does he say about praying about a problem versus praising about it?

He says baby Christians always say “I pray about it,” but “you never hear them say, ‘Let’s praise about it.’” He says God said that if a baby would praise Him, He would “still the enemy and the avenger.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer uses Acts 18 to show how the church in Corinth was built, going from no Christians to thousands in under three years without a building, seminars or recorded miracles. He…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer uses Acts 18 to show how the church in Corinth was built, going from no Christians to thousands in under three years without a building, seminars or recorded miracles. He lists what Paul did: worked to support himself, reasoned from the Scriptures, used a team, preached a compelling message, faced rejection, and relied on God’s word and presence.
How does the Bible show a church being built? (Acts 18:1)

He says people buy books and seminars on church growth, but “there is an illustration in the Bible of a church being built, how it was built,” in Acts 18. He begins with Paul leaving Athens and coming to Corinth, and shows maps and a drawing of the city.
How does the Bible show a church being built? (Acts 18:1)

You’ve heard a lot about church growth. Seminars and, uh, people go to these things and they tell people how to build a mega church and so forth. They write books about it, but there is an illustration in the Bible of a church being built, how it was built. We find this in Acts 18:1, and it always amazes me how people will buy books and not go to the Book. So let’s take a look in the Bible how a church gets started and what happens after that. Okay, it says in Acts 18, verse 1: “Paul left Athens and came to Corinth.” You can see Corinth up here, uh, that little narrow space between Athens and the lower part of the, uh, peninsula. There, here’s another view of it, uh, showing also the same area, but the Roman provinces or Roman states, and the seven churches of Asia, of course, are over here. There is a satellite view of that little narrow area where Corinth is, and here is a drawing of the archaeologist that uncovered Corinth, of, uh, the layout downtown. Up at the top there are markets, then you got all these temples right here. You got the temple of, uh, Apollo, Hermes, [unclear], and, uh, all these Greek and Roman gods. You got the bath houses and so forth, shops all over the place, just a typical city.
How does the Bible show a church being built? (Acts 18:1)
Acts 18:1: After these things Paul departed from Athens and went to Corinth.
What was the city of Corinth like when Paul arrived?

He says history describes Corinth as filled with gamblers, legalized temple prostitution, slaves, amusements and idol temples, with “a lack of standards” but “a freedom of thought.” He asks whether it sounds like America today and says it did, with about 500,000 people.
What was the city of Corinth like when Paul arrived?

Uh, when you look up the civilization at that time of Corinth, history tells us it was filled with gamblers, legalized temple prostitutions including males, uh, business ventures, agriculture, manufacturing, trade, especially bronze. They had paved roads where they charged for cargo going between the narrow place from sea to sea, because they didn’t want to sail around it. They had athletes there, they had, uh, the games were there. They had homeless slaves, they had regular slaves, they had slave masters, uh, a lot of amusements. They had prostitutes, both male and female, that weren’t in the temple; they were abundant. They had a lack of standards, but they had a freedom of thought in that city. Everybody had their own opinion, their own thought, and everything was okay. Does it sound like America today? Yeah, sounds like a normal city in America today. Uh, there was about 500,000 people according to history in this city at this time when Paul comes to Corinth. And, uh, they had in their marketplaces, the Greeks would always, uh, sacrifice their meats to their idols and then they would sell the meat in the markets, and this created a problem for Christians, if you remember.
How could Paul build a church of 15,000 in under three years?

He asks how Paul went “from no Christianity to 15,000 people in the church in no more than three years,” without a building. He says the usual advice is miracles, seeker-friendly programs and entertainment, and he sets out to see what Paul actually did.
How could Paul build a church of 15,000 in under three years?

Um, now let’s say, according to today’s marketing principles, you try to reach 500,000 people, 1% respond, and so that would be what? 5,000 believers. Right. So how did Paul do this? How did he build a church here with these kind of people? Multicultural, people, different races, uh, different religions. The Jewish religion was there and other religions. How did he do this in no more than three years, going from no Christianity to 15,000 people in the church in no more than three years? Isn’t that a good question? Question, because I used to hear all the time when I was a young preacher and a young believer, that, “Boy, if you get the miracles, people will believe.” And so, uh, according to that theory, you know, he must have been doing a lot of miracles. These church seminars and all that, they say you got to have a seeker-friendly, you got to do things to entertain them and get their attention and so forth. Okay, let’s see what Paul did to create a mega church in less than three years, and didn’t even have a building. Sounds good.
Why did Paul work to support himself? (Acts 18:2-3)

He says the first thing, “against all of these church building seminars,” is that Paul worked to support himself and his co-workers, making tents with Aquila and Priscilla. He says persecution and lack of money, with no missionary support from Antioch or Jerusalem, did not stop him.
Why did Paul work to support himself? (Acts 18:2-3)

So this next slide says the starting of a church. All right, starting of a church, number one, which is against all of these church building seminars: Paul worked to support himself and his co-workers. Now that’s a switch. Are you there? Paul made tents with two Christian Jews forced from Rome, Aquila and Priscilla. So in the midst of tribulation, in the midst of persecution, all Jews were removed from Rome, including Christians. Okay, Jews are Jews by nationality, and Jews are also Jews by their religion. Today’s present Israel, most of the Jews there are secular, they’re just Jews by bloodline, and then you got the Jews that observe their religion. Did you know that? Yeah, there’s a difference. See, you can be an American or you can be a Christian American. We are a Christian nation, but that doesn’t mean you’re a Christian, but you’re still an American. All right, so here we got persecution, and you know, persecution didn’t stop Paul from building a church, and the lack of money didn’t stop Paul. He didn’t have any missionary support coming from Antioch, he didn’t have any missionary support coming from the church in Jerusalem. He was out there working on his own, providing for himself and his staff members.
Why did Paul work to support himself? (Acts 18:2-3)

Acts 18:2-3: And he found a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus, who had recently come from Italy with his wife Priscilla (because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome); and he came to them. So, because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and worked; for by occupation they were tentmakers.
How did Paul reach people in the synagogue? (Acts 18:4)

He says Paul reasoned in the synagogue every Saturday, persuading Jews and Greeks, speaking the Word of God. He says there was “no dance company, no drama, no orchestra, no music, no nursery, no children’s church, no youth group,” just “convincing people from the Scriptures.”
How did Paul reach people in the synagogue? (Acts 18:4)

The second thing we see here is in verse 4 of Acts 18: “He reasoned in the synagogue every Saturday, persuading Jews and Greeks.” Greeks are non-Jews. You got to remember that in the temple in Jerusalem the Gentiles were not allowed in the inner circle. They were only allowed on the porch of the Gentiles, the area of the Gentiles. But in the synagogues, everybody was welcomed to come in and observe and see what was going on. And so Paul went to the synagogue, and sure enough there were non-Jews there checking out what the Jewish religion was, and he was persuading, convincing, pleading his case. In other words, he was speaking the Word of God. No dance company, no drama, no orchestra, no music, no nursery, no children’s church, no youth group, he was just simply convincing people from the Scriptures something that they needed to hear. Do you have that? Do you understand that so far? He’s using nothing that the churches in America use trying to build a congregation.
How did Paul reach people in the synagogue? (Acts 18:4)
Acts 18:4: And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and persuaded both Jews and Greeks.
What moved Paul to persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

He reads 2 Corinthians 5:10 and says Paul understood “everybody’s going to be judged by the things they do,” and did not want people to experience “the terror, the fear of the Lord, the eternal lake of fire.” He says “people aren’t going to avoid hell if you don’t tell them and convince them about Jesus Christ and the Word.”
What moved Paul to persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

In 2 Corinthians 5:10 he says, “We must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that everyone may receive the things done in his body according to what he has done, whether it be good or bad. Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we” what? “Persuade men.” See, what moved him to do this, to persuade men? He understood everybody’s going to be judged by the things they do, whether they’re good or whether they’re bad, and so he didn’t want people to be experiencing the terror, the fear of the Lord, the eternal lake of fire, so he tried to persuade them how to escape it. So in other words, church, we got to open our mouth. People aren’t going to avoid hell if you don’t tell them and convince them about Jesus Christ and the Word. Could that be an amen?
What moved Paul to persuade people? (2 Corinthians 5:10-11)

2 Corinthians 5:10-11: For we must all appear before the judgment seat of Christ, that each one may receive the things done in the body, according to what he has done, whether good or bad. Knowing, therefore, the terror of the Lord, we persuade men; but we are well known to God, and I also trust are well known in your consciences.
Why did Paul use a team? (Acts 18:5, Ecclesiastes 4:9-12)

He says Jesus sent the disciples out two by two, and cites Ecclesiastes 4:9, “two are better than one,” and that “a threefold cord is not” easily broken. He counts five on Paul’s team, including Priscilla, and says that a woman involved in leadership answers those who say you can’t have a woman pastor.
Why did Paul use a team? (Acts 18:5, Ecclesiastes 4:9-12)

Thirdly, he used a team. In verse 5: “Silas and Timothy arrived from Macedonia.” They were up there in Philippi and Thessalonica and so forth, and they had been with Paul, and now they come down to join him again at Corinth. And team is important. Jesus sent out the disciples two by two, didn’t He? As a team. Why? Because in Ecclesiastes 4:9, “Two are better than one. If they fall, one will lift up his companion. Two can keep warm, but one alone can’t keep warm. Two can overcome opponents,” robbers, those that are opposing, those that are attacking, “but one is at their mercy, and a threefold cord is not” what? “Easily broken.” So three are better than two, four are better than three. Duh. He had five on the team here now: him, Paul, Silas, Priscilla, and Aquila. A woman. Wow. And if you read your church building today, they’ll tell you you can’t have a woman pastor. Well, here’s a woman involved in leadership. Are you there?
Why did Paul use a team? (Acts 18:5, Ecclesiastes 4:9-12)

Acts 18:5: When Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ. Ecclesiastes 4:9-12: Two are better than one, Because they have a good reward for their labor. For if they fall, one will lift up his companion. But woe to him who is alone when he falls, For he has no one to help him up. Again, if two lie down together, they will keep warm; But how can one be warm alone? Though one may be overpowered by another, two can withstand him. And a threefold cord is not quickly broken.
What message did Paul preach in Corinth? (Acts 18:5)

He says Paul’s message was not “positive thinking, possibility thinking, purpose-driven thinking, … prosperity thinking.” He says Paul was “compelled” to show the Jews that Jesus is the Christ, the Messiah, the Prophet and the King they were looking for, all in one Person.
What message did Paul preach in Corinth? (Acts 18:5)

Now, the fourth thing is the message. What he was preaching to persuade, to convince, to plead his case, the message. The message he had was not positive thinking, possibility thinking, purpose-driven thinking, uh, prosperity thinking. His message was that he was compelled. There was a force in him, a drive within him. Have you ever felt that drive in you, that push of God in you? See, that’s what he had. And what was it about? He was pressed, he was compelled, he was moved, forced in the Spirit to testify, confirm, and show to the Jews that Jesus was Christ, He was the Messiah. Now, all of you know this, old-timers here, that the Jews were looking for three things in the New Testament. What was the first one? The Messiah, the Christ. They were looking for Him to come. What was the second one? The Prophet. They were looking for the Prophet that was promised in Deuteronomy. What was the third one? The King. See, God promised a king out of David’s seed. And so they were looking for these three, and they thought there were going to be three different people, and it was all in one Person, Jesus Christ. And so he’s convincing these Jews, he’s telling them, “This is the Messiah, the Prophet, the King that you guys are looking for. Jesus is Him.” Hallelujah.
What message did Paul preach in Corinth? (Acts 18:5)
Acts 18:5: When Silas and Timothy had come from Macedonia, Paul was compelled by the Spirit, and testified to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
Why does the love of Christ compel us to persuade others? (2 Corinthians 5:14-15)

He says “the love of Christ compels us,” and that love shows in a move to persuade people. He explains that if One died for all, then all died, “that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.”
Why does the love of Christ compel us to persuade others? (2 Corinthians 5:14-15)

And see, he was pressed in his spirit, moved by his spirit to preach this Word. In 2 Corinthians 5:14, “the love of Christ compels us.” “For God so loved the world, He gave His only begotten Son” is more than just a little football scripture, John 3:16, at the stadium. It explains for us, out of love God did this stuff. So does God love the world? Yes. If we know God, are we going to love the world? Yes. And that love is going to show forth in what? A compelling, a move to what? Persuade them. “Because we judge this: that if One died for all, then all” what? “Died.” Did you get that? See, He died for us. Therefore, as a simile, we all died with Him, “that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.” See, this is what he’s compelling to say to these people, that not only do we accept the salvation, we accept Christ, but it should move us to live for Him. This love, that we say we love God, there should be a force compelling to live for Him. Now. Amen.
Why does the love of Christ compel us to persuade others? (2 Corinthians 5:14-15)

2 Corinthians 5:14-15: For the love of Christ compels us, because we judge thus: that if One died for all, then all died; and He died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again. John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life.
What should you do when people reject the message? (Acts 18:6)

He says if Paul had 15,000 believers, “485,000 people rejected him,” and that those who reject are actually “opposing themselves” because the gospel pricks their hearts, so you do not have to take it personally. He says Paul shook his raiment and went to the Gentiles, as Jesus told His disciples to do, and that family members who compromise lose their power to win someone to Christ.
What should you do when people reject the message? (Acts 18:6)

Now, number five: rejection of the message. Oh, we hate rejection. That’s why we like to keep our mouth shut, because we get rejected more. If Paul had 15,000 believers, that means that 485,000 people rejected him. Think about it. And this is what turns a lot of Christians off: they get rejected, so they just start shutting up. “When they opposed themselves.” I like the way they said it: these people that reject are rejecting God and what they can have, so they’re actually opposing themselves. You see, because the gospel is so powerful, it pricks the hearts. They have to fight that in themselves to say, “No, I don’t want it.” So they’re not rejecting you, they’re rejecting what? That pricking in their heart of the Scriptures, and said, “No, I don’t want it.” So they’re actually opposing themselves. Do you understand that? See, that can help you not to take it personally. “And they blaspheme.” Blaspheme means what? Speak evil of, harmful of. And so Paul shook his raiment, saying, “Your blood be upon your own heads. I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles,” the non-Jews. Now, this is what Jesus told them to do in Luke 9:5 and Matthew 10:14: “Whosoever will not receive you nor your words, when you go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet for a testimony against them.” And that’s what Paul did. He said, you know, don’t get down in the dumps over it. You know, your family can reject the message, your sons, your daughters can reject the message, believers can reject the message. These Jews were believers in God, but they were rejecting the message. Can that be happening in America, that there’s a lot of people that, you know, say they love Christ, but they reject living for Him? And so he did what Jesus told him to do. I know a lot of families, and when their family member doesn’t want to serve God, they just kind of negotiate and compromise and, uh, trying to keep a connection or something, and then they have no power to help win him to Christ, because they’re giving in to what that person wants to do. Are you there?
What should you do when people reject the message? (Acts 18:6)

Acts 18:6: But when they opposed him and blasphemed, he shook his garments and said to them, “Your blood be upon your own heads; I am clean. From now on I will go to the Gentiles.” Luke 9:5: And whoever will not receive you, when you go out of that city, shake off the very dust from your feet as a testimony against them.” Matthew 10:14: And whoever will not receive you nor hear your words, when you depart from that house or city, shake off the dust from your feet.
Were there miracles in Corinth, and what is the real miracle? (Acts 18:8)

He says “there’s no recorded miracles being done here in Corinth at all,” only “the preaching of the Word.” He says the real miracle is salvation, changed lives, and that healing the sick is part of God’s package but “no more important than the Word.”
Were there miracles in Corinth, and what is the real miracle? (Acts 18:8)

A rejection is going to come. Well, that’s not positive thinking. That’s, you can’t say that. Well, it’s true, it’s truth. They’re going to reject you. They may reject you 10 times, they may reject you for the rest of their life, they may never decide to believe and live for Christ. But “many believed and were baptized,” and none of this shows any recording of any miracles. All was done by what? Preaching Jesus Christ. There’s no recorded miracles being done here in Corinth at all. No demons cast out, no sick being healed, people weren’t coming and burning their magic books like it happened in other places, no aprons, prayer cloths used, nothing. Just the preaching of the Word, and that’s how powerful the Word is. See, God decides when He does things. God decided to do miracles in certain places and to use aprons and prayer cloths. He didn’t decide to do anything like that here, just the Word. Got it, church? The Word is that powerful. And what is the real miracle here, by the way? Salvation, changed lives. That’s the real miracle, being healed from your sin, being changed from a prostitute, a homosexual, a thief, a gambler, to one that doesn’t do it anymore is a miracle. Hallelujah. See, we got to think right. And if God does heal the sick, that’s fine, that’s part of His package, but we shouldn’t make it any higher than it’s supposed to be. You know, when you’re sick, yeah, you want to be healed, I mean, come on, geez. If you got a demon and, no, your child’s got a demon, yeah, you want it to be cast out, but it’s no more important than the Word. And the Word is the most important, because you can’t even cast out a demon but by the Word. “Now many believed”: Justus, one that worshiped God and lived right by the synagogue; Crispus was the chief ruler of the synagogue, and all of his family accepted the message. And “many,” say that word “many.” Now, “many” is used when Christ, uh, multiplied the loaves and the fishes. He said there were many, and then it says how many? 5,000 men plus women and children. That gets us back up to 15,000, and there’s always more women than men. I don’t know what it is with us knuckleheaded men, we’re a little slow. And so it was over 15,000 people. He’s got a mega church here and no building to meet in. Are you there? I mean, this is something.
Were there miracles in Corinth, and what is the real miracle? (Acts 18:8)
Acts 18:8: Then Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed on the Lord with all his household. And many of the Corinthians, hearing, believed and were baptized.
How did God get involved in the message? (Acts 18:9-11)

He says the Lord told Paul in a night vision, “be not afraid, speak, hold not your peace,” and that visions and dreams are always about the message, not about seeing things. He says Paul stayed a year and six months teaching “the Word of God,” not psychology or positive thinking.
How did God get involved in the message? (Acts 18:9-11)

Now the next one is God got involved in the message. Verse 9: “The Lord said to Paul by night vision, ‘Be not afraid, speak, hold not your peace.’” And I always told you, when angels come, when visions come, and dreams come, it’s always a message. Not for you to go and say, “I saw Jesus, I saw Jesus, oh, I had a vision.” No, the message is what’s going to change your life. It’s not seeing things, it’s the message. And He says, “You keep speaking.” So He was giving Paul a responsibility to open his mouth. And He told Paul, don’t be afraid. He said, “I am with you. No man shall hurt you. I have much people.” How many? Much people in this city. “Paul continued there a year and six months, teaching” what? The Word of God. Not psychology, not possibility thinking, not positive thinking, not purpose-driven thinking, not prosperity thinking, but he preached the Word of God.
How did God get involved in the message? (Acts 18:9-11)

Acts 18:9-11: Now the Lord spoke to Paul in the night by a vision, “Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not keep silent; for I am with you, and no one will attack you to hurt you; for I have many people in this city.” And he continued there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
Why should older believers stay driven, and what does Mark 16:20 say about “working with them”?

He says Paul was an old man and “he ain’t retiring,” and that younger believers need to see older ones “still compelled, still driven.” On Mark 16:20 he says the words “with them” are in italics and not in the original, and that “the Word worked” even through Judas, because the power is in speaking the Word.
Why should older believers stay driven, and what does Mark 16:20 say about “working with them”?

Now, most of us here are senior saints. Do you get this? Paul is an old man. He ain’t retiring. Yeah, teaching the Word. He’s moved, he’s compelled. And do our younger believers need to see us old ones stable, still compelled, still driven? Yes. It’s infectious. It will catch on with them. Mark 16:20: “They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them.” “With them” is in italics. Why is it in italics? Because it’s not in the original Scripture. It’s put there by the writers to help you understand. When you see it’s in italics, it means it’s not in the original Scripture, they put it there to help you understand. Here they messed up the understanding. All right, have I got your attention? Watch this: “working with” the Word. I put that in. When you see parentheses in my things, it’s usually me putting in a description. Okay, I’m telling you this is what it should be, but let’s just read it: “They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs,” or “signs following.” Now I’m going to take out the italics. Now let’s read it: “They went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with and confirming the word.” Is what it should say. But He needs a vessel. Yeah, Judas was a vessel. He was a thief, he was a betrayer, but the Word worked through Judas. The Word worked. The power is in speaking what? The Word. That’s why you don’t have to wait to be perfect, to grow up to maturity, because the Word is mature, the Word is perfect, and the Word will work regardless of your level in God.
Why should older believers stay driven, and what does Mark 16:20 say about “working with them”?
Mark 16:20: And they went out and preached everywhere, the Lord working with them and confirming the word through the accompanying signs. Amen.
What were the signs in Corinth?

He says the signs were souls saved and lives transformed: “homosexuals aren’t homosexuals anymore, adulterers aren’t adulterers anymore,” and the same for prostitutes, gamblers and drunkards. He says “that’s the power of the Word” and calls this “a great illustration in the Bible how a church is to be built.”
What were the signs in Corinth?

Hallelujah. Now, what are the signs here in Corinth? Souls are saved, lives are transformed from all of these walks of life: homosexuals aren’t homosexuals anymore, adulterers aren’t adulterers anymore, prostitutes aren’t prostitutes anymore, gamblers aren’t gamblers anymore, drunkards aren’t drunkards anymore. See, that’s the power of the Word. And we have a great illustration in the Bible how a church is to be built. There is no Christian in this city when Paul came. He started on virgin territory. We don’t have that here. We got so many religions out there to deal with, it’s not even funny. But Paul had to deal with Jews that didn’t want to accept the message, also didn’t. Now these Jews take Paul to court to silence the message. He go before the judgment seat. These guys are preaching contrary to the law. They go to the Roman judge. The Roman judge threw it out of court: “I’m not going to hear you guys, this is your own problems.” So the Jews beat Sosthenes, a ruler of the synagogue, in the courtroom, and the court did nothing.
What should Christians do when opposition and rejection come? (Acts 18:12-17)

He says the Jews took Paul to court to silence the message, and the Roman judge threw it out. He says life is normal in America like in Corinth, God has many people to reach, and “when people reject it, move on and find somebody that’s worth putting time into.”
What should Christians do when opposition and rejection come? (Acts 18:12-17)

Are Christians getting pushed around in America today? Yeah, and America is doing what? Nothing. You say anything about the Muslims, you’re in trouble. You say anything about blacks or Mexicans or some minority, right, you’re in trouble. But you say anything about Christianity, no problem. What I’m trying to tell you is life is normal in America, just like it was at Athens, and yet God had many people, or I’m sorry, Corinth, God had many people in Corinth that He wanted to reach and change their lives. And we got to get over, “Oh, this is a rough harvest field. Oh, things are so bad. Oh, the homosexuals are taking over, and the atheists are taking over.” We got to let God arise, and He will draw people to Himself, and those that reject, we got to learn that when people reject it, move on and find somebody that’s worth putting time into. I had to learn that as a young Christian, to quit fooling around with these sap suckers and move on to people that really wanted to touch God and move on in God. And that’s what Paul did.
What should Christians do when opposition and rejection come? (Acts 18:12-17)

Acts 18:12-17: When Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose up against Paul and brought him to the judgment seat, saying, “This fellow persuades men to worship God contrary to the law.” And when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, “If it were a matter of wrongdoing or wicked crimes, O Jews, there would be reason why I should bear with you. But if it is a question of words and names and your own law, look to it yourselves; for I do not want to be a judge of such matters.” And he drove them from the judgment seat. Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the judgment seat. But Gallio took no notice of these things.
How big does he say the church in Corinth became?

He says it went “from no Christianity to 15,000 people in the church in no more than three years.” He bases this on 500,000 people in the city and the “many” who believed, comparing it to the 5,000 men plus women and children Jesus fed.
What does he say church-building seminars teach?
He says they say you have to be “seeker-friendly” and “do things to entertain them and get their attention,” and that earlier he heard that if you get the miracles, people will believe.
Did Paul have missionary support in Corinth?
No. He says Paul “didn’t have any missionary support coming from Antioch” or from the church in Jerusalem, and was “out there working on his own, providing for himself and his staff members.”
What did Paul not use to build the church?

He says there was no dance company, drama, orchestra, music, nursery, children’s church or youth group. He says Paul was “just simply convincing people from the Scriptures something that they needed to hear.”
What does he say “the terror of the Lord” moved Paul to do?
He says it moved Paul to persuade people, because everyone will be judged and Paul did not want anyone experiencing “the eternal lake of fire.”
What three things does he say the Jews were looking for?
He says they looked for the Messiah, the Prophet promised in Deuteronomy, and the King out of David’s seed, and “it was all in one person, Jesus Christ.”
Why does he say people reject the message?
He says the gospel “pricks the hearts,” and people have to fight that in themselves to say “no, I don’t want it,” so “they’re not rejecting you, they’re rejecting” that pricking of the Scriptures.
What does he say about families that compromise?

He says when a family member doesn’t want to serve God, families “negotiate and compromise,” and then “they have no power to help win him to Christ, because they’re giving in to what that person wants to do.”
Does he say people may reject the message for life?
Yes. He says “they may reject you 10 times, they may reject you for the rest of their life, they may never decide to believe and live for Christ,” but many believed and were baptized.
Does he say healing and casting out demons are unimportant?
No. He says “if God does heal the sick, that’s fine, that’s part of His package,” and you want a demon cast out, “but it’s no more important than the Word.”
What does he say about visions and dreams?
He says “when angels come, when visions come, and dreams come, it’s always a message,” and “the message is what’s going to change your life. It’s not seeing things.”
Does he say the Word works only through perfect people?
No. He says “you don’t have to wait to be perfect, to grow up to maturity, because the Word is mature, the Word is perfect, and the Word will work regardless of your level in God.”
