p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the opening of 1 Corinthians to show what a young church possessed: holiness, calling on and summoning Jesus, grace as divine enablement, understanding of Scripture, stability, the gifts of the Spirit, looking for His coming, and fellowship with Christ. He contrasts this with the American church and urges believers to start the year seeing the Word of God as bigger than the opposition.
Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?

He says Jesus warned, “Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to the councils,” and that they will “beat you in their synagogues” and bring you before governors and kings “for My sake.” He adds that brother will betray brother, and father the son.
Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?

Paul stayed a good while before leaving. So he was there a year and a half, and then a good while. We don’t know what the good while is, but the way I said it, it couldn’t be no more than three years. It could have been a lot less; could have been two and a half years. “Beware of men, for they will deliver you up to the councils,” Jesus said in Matthew 10:17. “They’ll beat you in their synagogues. They’ll bring you before governors and kings for My sake,” because you’re living for Me, because you’re proclaiming Me, “for a testimony against them,” and a testimony against nonbelievers. Unbelievers. He says in Matthew 13:12, “Brother shall betray brother to death, father the son, and children—their parents.”
Will following Jesus bring persecution, even from people close to you?

Matthew 10:17: But beware of men, for they will deliver you up to councils and scourge you in their synagogues. Matthew 10:21: “Now brother will deliver up brother to death, and a father his child; and children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death. Acts 18:18: So Paul still remained a good while. Then he took leave of the brethren and sailed for Syria, and Priscilla and Aquila were with him. He had his hair cut off at Cenchrea, for he had taken a vow.
Can you live for Christ on behalf of your children or spouse?

He says parents cannot live for Christ for their children: “God doesn’t have any stepchildren,” and each adult child has to decide to live for Him. He says a spouse may go another way too, and believers must “stick with the Bible” and not water everything down.
Can you live for Christ on behalf of your children or spouse?

Parents, you know, you can’t get down in the dumps because your kid decides to go sin after you raised him in a Christian school and in a Christian home and all the rest. They become an adult, they got to choose for themselves what road they’re going to take. Your job is to get them there; their job is to take the baton and live for Him. God doesn’t have any stepchildren. You can’t live for Christ for your children; they got to decide to live for Him themselves. Your spouse may decide to go another way, and it’s happening in America, isn’t it? They want to twist who God is and who Jesus is, and they want to water everything down, and they want you to accept them with their own beliefs, and you can’t do it, because you can’t change the Bible. You got to stick with the Bible. Can I hear an amen?
How do you stay consistent when family pressure and Satan’s attacks come?

He says a believer cannot “go along” with a spouse just to keep harmony at home, because “we’re supposed to be a light to the world, not a shadow.” He says Satan hits in several areas, naming health, position and money, and that you have to “rise above these things” and stay consistent.
How do you stay consistent when family pressure and Satan’s attacks come?

Seniors, spouses get a hair in their nose and want to do things, you know, you can’t go, “Well, I got to keep harmony in my home, so I got to go along.” [unclear] on that. We’re supposed to be a light to the world, not a shadow. I’ve been taken to court four times, so I know it’s true. I know about persecution. I know Satan has four areas he’ll hit you in. He happened to hit me and my family. Sometimes it’s health, sometimes it’s, uh, position, sometimes it’s, uh, money. You know, it just seems like you can’t keep a steady job.
What should a young church or a young Christian possess?

He says Paul was training a new church in Corinth and asks, “will He do it for all churches? Absolutely.” He says Corinth was not a church of “worshiping a hero,” and he lists ten things from 1 Corinthians 1 that a young Christian should be possessing.
What should a young church or a young Christian possess?

You know, you got to rise above these things that Satan tries to distract you with and stay consistent. Now here is Paul training a new church. We jump over to 1 Corinthians. He writes a letter to them later. You see, a little bit later he writes back to this church and gives them instruction. Wow. And I want you to see right quick here the powerful statements he makes about this new church. And, folks, God is not a what? Respecter of persons. If He will do this for the Corinthian church, will He do it for all churches? Absolutely. Watch how he writes to these people. I mean, something happened in Corinth. It wasn’t like your mega churches today, where people are worshiping a hero or something. These people had something. Watch this, this is powerful. You ready? Ten things. Ten things that you should be possessing even as a young Christian.
What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?

He says Paul did not say the Corinthians were going to be holy, but that “they are,” set apart for holiness and right living after turning from their sins. “Called to be saints” means morally blameless, which they were not yet, but they were “shooting for that mark.”
What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?

Ready? “Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother.” Remember who got beat in front of the court? Sosthenes. Here he’s helping write this, uh, letter, this book. Hallelujah. See, his beating, his persecution, didn’t change him at all. He’s still with Paul, he’s still in the church, he’s still communicating, serving God. And number one: “to the church of God at Corinth, to them that are” what? Sanctified. They’re holy. He said, didn’t say they’re going to be holy; they are. What? Holy. Set apart for holiness, right living. They turn from their sins, their prostitution, their, their homosexuality, their lying, and their stealing, and all these things they had experienced. Holiness. Isn’t that good? Look at the next one: “called to be saints.” You see, saints are blameless people. People that are blameless morally. Blameless. Now they’re called to be morally blameless, so obviously they’re not quite morally blameless yet. Ain’t that right? But they are what? Shooting for that mark. Isn’t that powerful? This church is not even three years old, and they’re experiencing things in God. “And in every place,” with all that, “in every place call upon the name of Jesus Christ.” Okay, so they’re calling on the name of Jesus Christ. Now that word “calling” means this: it’s not just inviting, or invoking, or hollering. It is summoning.
What does it mean to be sanctified, holy and “called to be saints”?

1 Corinthians 1:1: Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ through the will of God, and Sosthenes our brother, 1 Corinthians 1:2: To the church of God which is at Corinth, to those who are sanctified in Christ Jesus, called to be saints, with all who in every place call on the name of Jesus Christ our Lord, both theirs and ours:
What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?

He says “calling on the name of Jesus Christ” means summoning, like a court summons: “Can you send a substitute? No.” These believers summoned His presence, expecting and demanding that Jesus be there, while many people “go to church and never touch Jesus.”
What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?

See, it’s acquiring. When you get a court summons, do you go? Yes. Can you send a substitute? No. Can you say, “I’m too busy, excuse me”? No, you ought to appear. Then see, what is he saying? These people summon Jesus Christ. They summon His presence. He appears in their midst, not by the physical eye, but His presence touching our presence, our spirit. Amen. Do you see that? Now see, these are things this young church were possessing. When they come together, they were expecting, they were demanding, that Jesus Christ be there, like He said, “If two or three are gathered together, I will be” where? “In the midst.” They summoned Him. And so many people go to church and never touch Jesus, but yet this Corinthian church were touching Him. They were summoning Him. Isn’t that beautiful? I think that’s tremendous. Folks, I mean, our mega churches today don’t have anything like this. We’ve gotten off of these basic things. Now remember, these are ex-prostitutes, homosexuals, idolaters, gamblers, Jews, non-Jews, slaves, slave masters, sailors, merchants, soldiers, drunkards, contractors, athletes and entertainers. They were all coming to Christ: different races, different nationalities, different cultures.
What does it mean to “call on the name of Jesus Christ” in church?
Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?

He says grace is more than “just favor”: it shows in “the divine influence upon your life, divine enablement to live a lifestyle different than you lived before.” He says the American church has done members “a disservice” by teaching that God favors you no matter what you do.
What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?

Verse three of 1 Corinthians 1: “Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and from the Lord Jesus Christ. I thank my God always on your behalf for the grace of God given you by Jesus Christ.” And this is where the American church has done the church members a disservice. They keep telling them grace is just favor, God just favors you no matter what you do, He favors you. But it’s much more than that. He favors you, and it shows in a result of the divine influence upon your life, divine enablement to live a lifestyle different than you lived before. That’s the full measure of grace. That’s the whole purpose of grace: that He favors you, He loves you, He’s going to work with you so that people will see that there’s a divine influence, a divine enablement, that changed your life from this way to His way.
What is grace? Is it just God’s favor?
1 Corinthians 1:3-4: Grace to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. I thank my God always concerning you for the grace of God which was given to you by Christ Jesus,
Why should Christians learn the Scriptures well enough to speak them?

He says being enriched “in all utterance and all knowledge” means we have to “get into the Book” and into Bible studies that teach it, because “when you understand something, you can speak it.” He calls knowing the Scriptures the true wealth of the church.
Why should Christians learn the Scriptures well enough to speak them?

Amen. And these guys experienced this. And it says in the next verse, verse 5, that “in everything you are enriched by Him, in all utterance and all knowledge.” So in everything: the holiness, the summoning Christ, the grace, and now speaking and understanding. Did Jesus open the disciples’ understanding to understand the Scriptures? Can we understand the Scriptures? Yes. But to understand them, we got to get into the Book, and we got to get into Bible studies that are teaching that Book, and then we can speak it. See, when you understand something, you can speak it. See, the people that run the horse program, I don’t know a lot of things about horses, but they do, and they can speak it.
Why should Christians learn the Scriptures well enough to speak them?
1 Corinthians 1:5: that you were enriched in everything by Him in all utterance and all knowledge,
What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?

He says “confirm” means “stable, unchanging,” and that the young Corinthian Christians might make a mistake but “got back up and kept moving forward.” He says the American church has a lot of “instability,” with people who can’t overcome alcohol, drugs or anger because they are not experiencing these things.
What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?

Amen. That’s what God says He wants us to know: the Scriptures, that way we can what? Speak it. And that makes us wealthy. That’s the true wealth of the church. “Even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you.” That word “confirm” is to be stable, unchanging. These young Christians were stable. They weren’t going in and out, up and down. They were unchanging. They might make a mistake here and there, but they got back up and kept moving forward. How many would like to be stable in God? Now, in the American church, we got a lot of instability. We got big buildings, and we got great authors, and book authors, and preachers, and everything else, and God’s people can’t handle the slightest tribulation or problems in their life. They can’t overcome alcohol, they can’t overcome drugs, they can’t overcome anger, they ain’t going to overcome nothing. Why? Because they’re not experiencing these things.
What does it mean to be “confirmed” and stable in Christ?
1 Corinthians 1:6: even as the testimony of Christ was confirmed in you,
Should a church have all the spiritual gifts at work?

He says the Corinthians “come behind in no gift”: no spiritual ability was lacking when the church came together, and “the nine gifts were expressed.” He says an American church today usually has “one gift expressed,” depending on the circle, and sometimes “nothing.”
Should a church have all the spiritual gifts at work?

They’re given dramas and dance companies and preachers that preach with, you know, [unclear] excellence, and we’re not getting the Word in us. Hallelujah. Now, this is a good message for us to start this year with. Amen. Senior saints, amen. A young church, and they possess these things. It’s just extraordinary. It’s just amazing. Verse seven, “you become—you come behind in no gift.” Spiritual abilities, they didn’t lack any of them. Now, one person didn’t have them all, but when the church came together, they were there. See, the nine gifts were expressed. Do we have them at an American church today? No. We usually got one gift expressed. If you’re in certain circles, it’s prophecy; if you’re in other circles, it’s tongues; if you’re in other circles, it’s, uh, uh, healing; if you’re in other circles, it’s nothing. Ah, they just throw out the gifts.
Should a church have all the spiritual gifts at work?
1 Corinthians 1:7: so that you come short in no gift, eagerly waiting for the revelation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?

He says looking for the coming of the Lord means being faithful and wise, thinking, living and talking with superiority, because you may meet Him when you die and don’t have to “wait for the rapture.” He cites Matthew 24:46 and says Jesus told them to “watch, be ready.”
What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?

“And the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ.” You say, “Oh, big deal, the coming of the Lord.” Well, you got to understand what he means by the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ. Well, I know what it means: He’s coming again. That’s right, but you got to understand your part in it. See, how are you supposed to think about the coming of the Lord? These guys were looking for the coming, and Jesus wasn’t coming for 2,000 years down the road or more, but they’re what? Looking. They’re what? Looking. And don’t you believe these people to tell you. See, they didn’t even understand. They thought He was coming in, you know, right then and during their lifetime. That does not mean that at all. Let me show you what it means. Are you ready for this? Matthew 24:46: “Blessed is he that is faithful and a wise servant, whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.” Doing what? Being wise and faithful, ain’t that right? So they’re looking for the coming of Christ. What does that mean? They’re being faithful, and they’re talking with superiority, thinking with superiority, and living a superior life. Remember what wisdom was in Proverbs: superior thinking, superior living, and superior talking. Why? Because He can come and take you. You can die, you know. You don’t have to wait for the rapture. You’re going to meet Him when your heart starts beating. So you should be what? Faithful, and you should be a wise servant. Now look, but if that servant begins to beat his fellow servants, mistreat them, and to eat and drink with the drunkards, the master of that servant will come on a day when he’s not looking for him, and it goes on to say bad things. So see, when we’re saying we’re looking for Christ’s return, we’re saying what? I am faithful, I am living a wise life, I am speaking wisely, I am thinking wisely, because Christ may show up, or I may die and I will appear before Him. So it’s a lifestyle. And this is what Jesus told them to do: watch, be ready.
What does it mean to look for the coming of the Lord Jesus Christ?
Matthew 24:46: Blessed is that servant whom his master, when he comes, will find so doing.
What does it mean to be “blameless” in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ?

He says, “It doesn’t matter if He comes in your lifetime or not.” God will make them stable and unchanging to the end and keep them blameless, which he defines as “unaccusable” in the day of the Lord Jesus Christ, because Christ will finish the good work He began.
What does it mean to be “blameless” in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ?

It doesn’t matter if He comes in your lifetime or not. It is the attitude, it is the motive of your heart. Are you with Me? “Who shall also confirm you.” What’s “confirm” mean? Stable, unchanging. See, He’s going to confirm you, make you stable, unchanging, and to the end. What’s the end? That day when He comes the second time and judges the world, “that you may be blameless.” And what’s blameless? Unaccusable. “In the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.” How many of you want to be unaccusable in the day of the Lord Jesus Christ? How many? You know, this Corinthian church is on its way. It’s sanctified, it’s calling on the Lord, summoning Him, it’s looking for the return of Christ, they have the gifts of the Spirit working in the church. I mean, isn’t this beautiful? They are stable, they’re unchanging, they might make some mistakes, they are saints that are looking forward to being blameless, knowing that Christ will finish the good work that He began in us, and on that day they will be blameless.
What does it mean to be “blameless” in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ?
1 Corinthians 1:8: who will also confirm you to the end, that you may be blameless in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?

He says the last thing the Corinthians had was “the fellowship of His Son”: not a ministry or church group but “an intimate relationship with Christ.” He cites John 17:3 and defines eternal life as “knowing God and Jesus Christ,” not “head knowledge.”
What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?

Hallelujah. Ain’t that powerful? Now, senior saints, he did this with five people in his team. We got more than five here this morning. We got a head start. Verse 9: “God is faithful, by whom we were called unto the” what? “Fellowship.” Here’s the last one. See, “the fellowship of His Son.” Not some ministry, not some church group. These guys are in partnership with Jesus Christ. Not Paul, not Aquila, not Priscilla, not Silas, not Timothy. They are in partnership with Christ. They are in an intimate relationship with Christ. This is the biggest thing these guys had: they actually know Him. How, you know, that makes a difference. Not head knowledge. This is a real possession of Christ, a fellowship, a partnership with Him. It says in John 17:3, “This is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.” Definition of eternal life is what? Knowing God and Jesus Christ, an intimate relationship. The Bible says that Joseph knew not Mary until after Jesus was born; in other words, he didn’t have an intimate relationship with Mary. And see, we have this intimacy with God. We know God, we fellowship with Him, we partner with Him. We’re not partnered with just Silas and Timothy and Paul. We’re partnered with Jesus Himself, and that makes the difference.
What is the “fellowship” of God’s Son, and what is eternal life?

1 Corinthians 1:9: God is faithful, by whom you were called into the fellowship of His Son, Jesus Christ our Lord. John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent. Matthew 1:25: and did not know her till she had brought forth her firstborn Son. And he called His name JESUS.
How do we know that we know Jesus?

He cites 1 John 2:3, “We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments,” and says it is imperative that people meet and know Jesus in their salvation. “It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know.”
How do we know that we know Jesus?

1 John 2:3: “We know that we know Him if we keep His commandments.” See, “He that says, ‘I know Him,’ and keeps them not is a liar, and the truth is not in him.” So is it imperative, very important, that people in their salvation meet and know Jesus Christ? Yes. It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know. And this is what changed the Corinthians in this wild, wild city that any normal modern ministry would look at and go, “This city is impossible.” And yet the Word of God changed these people’s lives, and they knew Him. They encountered Christ.
How do we know that we know Jesus?
1 John 2:3-4: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?

He says to “stop looking at all the opposition and the problems” and see that the Word of God is bigger than this world. He closes with the overcomers’ song in Revelation 15, where “all nations shall come,” and says “shall” means it is impossible for it not to happen.
How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?

Hallelujah. Now, we got a year ahead of us, and we got to start looking and seeing like Paul looked and saw. Amen. We got to stop looking at all the opposition and the problems and see that the Word of God is bigger than this world. It’s bigger than anybody’s lack of faith, or whatever. Now, I chose Revelation 15:3 because the verse before this says, “These that overcame the beast,” they that overcame his mark, the number of his name, and his image. And in Revelation 12, the same people overcame Satan by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, and loved not their life to death. These people who what? Overcame. Then these people sang the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying, “great and marvelous”—why, there’s, they’re overcomers, they’re seeing the good stuff, “great and marvelous are Thy works, Lord God Almighty, just and true are Your ways, You King of saints. Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and honor Your name? For You only are holy, and all nations shall come.” That word “shall” means it is impossible for it not to happen. “They will come and worship before You,” whether they believe in You or not, they’re going to come. But we want to be like Paul, to get the nations to come and worship Him because they accept Him, amen, and not reject Him.
How should Christians face a new year, and will the nations worship?

Revelation 15:2-4: And I saw something like a sea of glass mingled with fire, and those who have the victory over the beast, over his image and over his mark and over the number of his name, standing on the sea of glass, having harps of God. They sing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb, saying: “Great and marvelous are Your works, Lord God Almighty! Just and true are Your ways, O King of the saints! Who shall not fear You, O Lord, and glorify Your name? For You alone are holy. For all nations shall come and worship before You, For Your judgments have been manifested.” Revelation 12:11: And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives to the death.
How long did Paul stay at Corinth?

He says Paul stayed “a year and a half, and then a good while.” He says nobody knows what the good while is, but the way he said it, it couldn’t be no more than three years and could have been two and a half.
What should parents do when a grown child chooses sin after a Christian upbringing?

He says parents can’t “get down in the dumps”: “Your job is to get them there; their job is to take the baton and live for Him.” He says you can’t live for Christ for your children; they have to decide to live for Him themselves.
Will God do for churches today what He did for the church at Corinth?
He asks, “If He will do this for the Corinthian church, will He do it for all churches? Absolutely.” He says something happened in Corinth that is not like the mega churches of today.
What does he say about the man who was beaten in front of the court and is named in 1 Corinthians 1:1?
He says his beating and persecution “didn’t change him at all”: he is still with Paul, in the church, communicating and serving God, and is helping write the letter.
Were the Corinthians already holy, or just going to be?

He says the verse does not say they are going to be holy; “they are.” He explains holy as set apart for holiness and right living, since they had turned from their sins and the things they had experienced.
Why does he compare calling on Jesus to a court summons?

He says when you get a court summons you go, you can’t send a substitute and you can’t say you’re too busy. In the same way, the Corinthians summoned His presence and He appeared in their midst, “not by the physical eye,” but touching “our spirit.”
What kinds of people made up the Corinthian church?

He lists ex-prostitutes, homosexuals, idolaters, gamblers, Jews, non-Jews, slaves, slave masters, sailors, merchants, soldiers, drunkards, contractors, athletes and entertainers. He says they were “all coming to Christ: different races, different nationalities, different cultures.”
What does he say is the full measure of grace?
He says it is not only that God favors and loves you but that He is going to work with you so that people will see “a divine influence, a divine enablement, that changed your life.”
Why does he say the American church has a lot of instability?

He says there are big buildings, authors and preachers, but God’s people “can’t handle the slightest tribulation or problems in their life.” They can’t overcome alcohol, drugs or anger, he says, “because they’re not experiencing these things.”
Which spiritual gifts does he say American churches usually express?

He says an American church usually has “one gift expressed”: in certain circles prophecy, in others tongues, in others healing, and in other circles “nothing.” He says the Corinthians lacked none of the gifts when the church came together.
Do you have to wait for the rapture to meet Jesus?
He says “you don’t have to wait for the rapture,” because you can die and appear before Him. So he says you should be faithful and a wise servant now.
What does he say “watch, be ready” means?

He says it is a lifestyle: “I am faithful, I am living a wise life, I am speaking wisely, I am thinking wisely,” because Christ may show up or you may die and appear before Him. He says it is “the attitude” and “the motive of your heart.”
Does a baptismal certificate or church membership make you right with God?
He says, “It’s not the baptismal certificate, it’s not what church you belong to, it’s who you know.” He says it is imperative that people in their salvation meet and know Jesus Christ.
What does he say about the overcomers’ song in Revelation 15?

He says the people who overcame sang the song of Moses and the song of the Lamb: “great and marvelous are Thy works.” He says “all nations shall come” means it is impossible for it not to happen, and that they will come and worship whether they believe or not.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 5:14-16 that Christians are the light of the world and are responsible both to do good works that bring honor to the Father and to speak the word of…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Matthew 5:14-16 that Christians are the light of the world and are responsible both to do good works that bring honor to the Father and to speak the word of salvation. He explains that grace and works do not conflict, which “works of the law” we are not saved by, and why quiet Christianity is not enough, ending with Paul’s converting gospel before Felix in Acts 24:25.
What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)
He reads Matthew 5:14-16 and asks, “why are Christians hiding out?” He says our responsibility is to let our light shine before men, which means that they “may see your good works.”
What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)

Uh, we’re going to be talking about Christians’ responsibility. Matthew 5:14-16: “You are the light of the world,” talking to us, and as they say down south, “A city that is set on the hill cannot be hid.” Why are Christians hiding out? They hide out in their homes, they hide out in the church. They’re worthless. “Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a bushel. A city set on a hill cannot be hid. They put the lamp on a lampstand so it gives light to all that are in the house.” He’s just using a natural illustration; that doesn’t make the book an allegorical book. He’s just given us natural illustrations to understand spiritual things. “Let your light shine before men.” So what is our responsibility? To let our light shine. That is our responsibility. You accept Christ, you accept salvation, you accept eternal life, He puts a responsibility on you to let your light shine before who?
What does it mean that Christians are the light of the world? (Matthew 5:14-16)

Matthew 5:14-16: “You are the light of the world. A city that is set on a hill cannot be hidden. Nor do they light a lamp and put it under a basket, but on a lampstand, and it gives light to all who are in the house. Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.
Should Christians keep their faith private, or let others see it?

He says people “should see our religion,” and that when men see our good works they “will give honor to your Father in heaven.” He asks, “do you want the world giving honor to God, or are you looking for honor?”
Should Christians keep their faith private, or let others see it?

Men, you see. And He tells us what that shining of the light is: “that they may see your good works.” That’s the shining light. These politicians that say, “I don’t wear my religion on my arm, on my sleeve”: that’s ridiculous. People should see our religion. Right here it says it. Hallelujah. And if you do that, He said those men that you do good works before will give honor to your Father in heaven. Now, do you want the world giving honor to God, or are you looking for honor? So.
Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)

He says “grace and faith and works do not conflict with each other.” We are saved by grace through faith with nothing we can do to earn it, yet we are “created to do” good works, and he says people who “eliminate works” are reading only part of the passage.
Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)

Who’s the light of the world? Those of us who are following Jesus. What does the light of the world do? Good works. And who is to see our good works? Men. Now, grace and faith and works do not conflict with each other. We need to get this clear. There is so much emphasis on grace and faith and no works. I want you to get this in your head, your cranial vacuum; I want to fill it up with some truth right now. All right. “It is by grace that you have been saved through faith, and this is not of yourselves.” Nothing you could do about it. “It is the gift of God.” God freely did it. “Not by works, so that no man can boast.” I can’t win enough souls to get into heaven. I can’t pray enough hours to get into heaven. I can’t take communion enough to get into heaven, to be saved from my sin. There’s absolutely nothing, for my point, that I can do besides believe the gospel, accept His favor, His death on the cross for my sins. Is that an amen? It’s free. Now, “not of works.” Now, if they would just continue reading, the subject hasn’t stopped yet. He’s still talking about salvation. “We are God’s workmanship.” He’s fashioning us. See, He’s fashioning us into what? A people that are created, they that in Christ Jesus are what? A new creation. Okay, this grace and faith that brought salvation also is the thing that got us born again, made a new creature. Do you see that? We are a new creature, old things passed away, all things made new. We are His workmanship, created in Christ Jesus to do what? But we just read, “not by works,” but we were created to do what? Good works. We have a responsibility to do good works. “Let your light so shine before men that they may see your” what? Good works. And it’s right here in the Scripture, that they eliminate works.
Do grace, faith and good works conflict? (Ephesians 2:8-10)

He says Jesus is God, life, the Word and light, so “the Word is light, and the spoken word is what brings light to people.” He quotes the Word becoming flesh, full of grace and truth.
Should Christians stop preaching because people don’t want to hear it?
No. He asks, “does that mean we stop preaching that word because people don’t want to hear it?” and says “that’s what the American church has done.”
Should I feel bad if my light is only a little light?
No. He says “don’t ever feel bad about your dawning light,” that it is okay and “it’s going to grow,” but “you got to be in the Word for it to grow.”
What does he say were Jesus’ first words?
He says Jesus’ first words were “repent, believe the gospel, get baptized for the remission of sin,” and that this was His message.
What does he say is missing in the church?
He says Felix “shook in fear” and that something missing in the church is people “getting saved from the fear of the Lord,” knowing that if they don’t change their life they’re going to hell.
Does he say telling people the truth is hating them?
No. He says “we’re not hating people by telling them the truth. We care for them, we have a compassion for them,” and it gives them a chance to convert and change their life.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer says many of Jesus’ disciples in John 6 left because they wanted what they could get rather than what they could give, and he applies that to prosperity preaching and other teaching he calls fractured. He plays recorded clips of public figures and ministers speaking about heaven, other religions and sin, and responds to them. He ends with the phrase “my faith,” saying the Bible uses it with works and with the faith of Jesus, and that our faith must be in Jesus Christ and his word, not in a group.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

Pastor Kincer says these were disciples who did not believe: they were disciplined to follow Christ to a certain degree, but they left when it came down to God being involved, and to accountability and responsibility. He says Jesus told them you cannot decide to serve God on your own, since the Father and the Spirit must be involved in your salvation, and it is not about joining a church or being a Jew, Protestant or Catholic.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

But this morning we’re going to talk about some deflective, defective disciples. Not everybody in the Bible turned out to be heroes. Deflective, defective disciples. They deflected because they had a defect. A disciple is one that’s disciplined, a pupil of Christ, a follower of Christ. And in John 6 we find him talking to what he called disciples, and he said, “There are some of you that believe not.” These are disciples that believe not. “For Jesus knew from the beginning who believe not and who should betray him.” Wow, powerful statement. “No man,” Jesus said, “can come unto me except it were given unto him by my Father.” Jesus said, listen, you can’t decide to serve God on your own. Me and my Father have to be involved in your conversion, in your salvation. It’s not joining a church, or being a Jew, or being a Protestant, or being a Catholic. Jesus said my Father has to be involved. The Spirit of God has to be involved. That’s why the Bible says you must be born again of the Spirit and of the word. Well, the disciples didn’t like this statement. Okay, now these are disciples. They’re disciples that didn’t believe. See, they were disciplined to follow Christ to a certain degree, but “from that time many of his disciples went back and walked no more with him.” They left him. And they were called disciples, but when it come down to God being involved, and accountability and responsibility, they left Jesus. And we’re going to show you what was really in their heart here.
Why did many of Jesus’ disciples leave him?

John 6:64-66: But there are some of you who do not believe.” For Jesus knew from the beginning who they were who did not believe, and who would betray Him. And He said, “Therefore I have said to you that no one can come to Me unless it has been granted to him by My Father.” From that time many of His disciples went back and walked with Him no more.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

He says Jesus asked the twelve whether they would also go away, and he says that is what God is saying to the churches in America today: will you stop walking with me and join your little clique? He says Peter and the others answered that there is nowhere to go, because Jesus has the words of eternal life, and he says eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

Here Jesus is. Then Jesus said to the twelve apostles, “Will you also go away?” Right now they’re the twelve disciples, apostles. Later they said, “You going to leave also?” And that’s what God is saying to the churches in America: Are you people going to leave me? Are you going to stop walking with me? You’re going to join your little clique and take your little clique and go out and think you got something? Are you going to stop walking with me? And they said, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life.” Now, as a young Christian this scripture just jumped right out at me, really did. There’s nowhere to go. Jesus has the words of eternal life. And remember, a couple weeks ago we learned that eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever. And then the disciples, his twelve disciples, replied and said, “We believe and we know that you are that Christ, the Son of the living God.” You see, they had experienced that dimension of God being involved in their salvation. It wasn’t a little hand-me-down Christianity: my parents were Christians, so I’m a Christian. Hallelujah.
What does “Lord, to whom shall we go?” mean?

John 6:67-69: Then Jesus said to the twelve, “Do you also want to go away?” But Simon Peter answered Him, “Lord, to whom shall we go? You have the words of eternal life. Also we have come to believe and know that You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.” John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
Are we following Jesus for what we can get or for what we can give?

He says the fractured followers were after what they could get from following Jesus, not what they could give to him, and a lot of Christians are the same. He says what God wants us to give him is a Bible morality lifestyle, living right and stopping sinning, and that praise and prayer are wonderful but what he wants from you is to live right.
Are we following Jesus for what we can get or for what we can give?

Now, so that you understand why these disciples left, we’re going to go back to the early part of the scripture. And I’m going to make this statement: these fractured followers were after what they could get from following Jesus, not what they could give to Jesus. And a lot of Christians are only out for what they can get from God and not what they can give from God. And what God wants you to give him is a Bible morality lifestyle: living right, stop sinning. Hallelujah, that’s what he wants out of you. Oh, praise is wonderful and prayer is wonderful, but what he wants out of you is you to live right. That’s what he wants you to give him back. Doesn’t matter if you’re a Catholic or a Jew or a Protestant or whatever. And we only want what we can get.
Is prosperity preaching what Jesus taught?

He says the crowd followed Jesus in John 6 for signs and then for free food, and Jesus said so plainly, and he says that is where prosperity, positive-thinking and similar preaching comes in today. He says Jesus wants us to give him Bible morality and self-control, not these approaches, and he recalls an emphasis on miracles in earlier decades that made a sick person feel faithless.
Is prosperity preaching what Jesus taught?

And so, you know, the prosperity people come in. Like today, in John 6:2, this is the multitude, this is the disciples that were following him. They followed him in John 6:2 because they saw his signs which he performed on those who were diseased. They wanted to show— you know, Oral Roberts back in the old days: “Expect a miracle every day.” The emphasis was on a miracle. You couldn’t go through a day without a miracle. God help you if you were sick and God never healed you, because during the ‘50s, during the ‘60s, in the Spirit-filled world there was such an emphasis on divine healing that, man, if you’d got sick you were just a faithless, weak, worthless person. See, are we— we want what we can get out of God. And Jesus said it plainly. Okay, then later, in verse 26, he says, “You don’t seek me now because you see the signs and wonders and miracles. Now you seek me, you follow me, because I fed you with the loaves and the fishes and you were filled.” You want free food. Now you don’t want a show anymore, you want free food: what we can get out of God. And this is where your prosperity preaching today comes in: today’s faith and grace camps, prosperity, psychotherapy, Purpose— Purpose Driven, possibility thinking, positive thinking, and prophecy— one-on-one independent individual prophecy. We got all the— all these P’s. And they’re fractured followers. They are deflecting from Christ because they have a de— defect in them. They’re wanting something instead of giving him something. Can I hear an amen? And that’s where we’re at in America, and America needs to hear this message, and you need to get it out to them. Now, Jesus wants us to give to him Bible morality, not grace and faith, or prosperity, positive, purpose, possibility, psychotherapy, reparative therapy. There’s no reparative therapy in the Bible. In the Bible it’s self-control: just stop what you’re doing. Hallelujah. Now, I’m going to give you some examples of some deflective, defective ministers. All right, these are their statements.
Is prosperity preaching what Jesus taught?

John 6:2: Then a great multitude followed Him, because they saw His signs which He performed on those who were diseased. John 6:26: Jesus answered them and said, “Most assuredly, I say to you, you seek Me, not because you saw the signs, but because you ate of the loaves and were filled.
Is a Mormon a true Christian?

He plays a recorded clip in which a speaker says he is not the one to judge the little details and believes Mormons are Christians. He then says he phoned the headquarters of the Mormon church and was told Jesus Christ is not God and did not exist until Mary, which he says is not what the Bible teaches. He asks whether Christ cares what you believe or that you believe what he believes.
Is a Mormon a true Christian?

[Recorded clip begins.] And what about Mitt Romney? And I got to ask you the question, because it is a question, whether it should be or not, in this campaign: Is a Mormon a true Christian? Well, in my mind they are. Mitt Romney has said that he believes in Christ as his Savior, and that’s what I believe. So, you know, I’m not the one to judge the little details of it. So I believe they are. And, you know, Mr. Romney seemed like a man of character and integrity to me, and I don’t think he would— anything would stop me from voting for him, if that’s what I felt like. So, for instance, when people start talking about Joseph Smith, the founder of the church, and the golden tablets in upstate New York, and God assumes the shape of a man, do you not get hung up in those theological issues? I probably don’t get hung up in them, because I haven’t really studied them or thought about them. And, you know, I just try to let God be the judge of that. I mean, I don’t know. I certainly can’t say that I agree with everything that I’ve heard about it, but from what I’ve heard from Mitt, when he says that Christ is his Savior, to me that’s a common bond. [Recorded clip ends.] So I personally talked with headquarters of the Mormon church this week. I didn’t act like I was somebody else; I just personally called them, and I said, I want some questions answered, and they answered them. I said, is Jesus Christ God? And they said no. I said, is Jesus Christ eternal, without a beginning and without an end? And they said no, Jesus Christ is only the Son of God, and he didn’t exist until Mary. Now, how many you know the Bible teaches he existed before Mary? [Clip replayed:] He believes in Christ as his Savior, and that’s what I believe. So, you know, I’m not the one to judge the little details of it, so I believe they are. I’m not the one to judge them. I believe— say that statement: I believe, I believe. Who cares what he believes? See, when he says that Christ is his Savior, to me— is— does Christ care what you believe, or does he care that you believe what he believes? Yeah.
Does 1 Corinthians 15 teach three kingdoms after death?

He says the Mormon church told him there are three places to go when you die, tied to the sun, moon and stars, and he says there is nothing in 1 Corinthians 15 that says the sun, moon and stars are kingdoms. He says he was told that their modern prophets taught it.
Does 1 Corinthians 15 teach three kingdoms after death?

Now, they also told me that there were three places to go when you die. I said, really? Is a certain type of people going to hell? And they said no. And 1 Corinthians 15: there’s the sun, moon and stars, the terrestrial, the celestial, and the— they got a new word, terrestrial, telestial. They created a new word. And they said the sun, moon and the stars: the first kingdom after you die is where people that believe God and follow God and do good go. The second one is where people that can change later, and then the third one is for people that just resent God, and, you know, and all this. I said, man, that sounds like Catholicism. I said, you know, I happen to know 1 Corinthians 15. I happen to know it by heart, and there is nothing in 1 Corinthians 15 that says that the moon and sun and the stars are kingdoms. They said, oh no, no, he says our modern prophets told us that. I go, really? I go, who are your modern prophets telling you this? He said, Joseph Smith. I go, okay, all right. Now, folks, that’s from the horse’s mouth. That’s from Utah.
Does 1 Corinthians 15 teach three kingdoms after death?

1 Corinthians 15:40-41: There are also celestial bodies and terrestrial bodies; but the glory of the celestial is one, and the glory of the terrestrial is another. There is one glory of the sun, another glory of the moon, and another glory of the stars; for one star differs from another star in glory.

He calls what he has just described fractured philosophy, taking the Bible and making it be what they want it to be, and says Mormons are not going to heaven. He also says a well-known Christian preacher who does not know this has not studied it, and he calls that sad.

Okay, now, is that fractured philosophy? Yes. Biblical? Yeah, it is. You see, they are— they are taking the Bible and making it be what they want it to be. And so, no, Mormons aren’t going to heaven. Joel Osteen’s out of his mind. He is a Christian preacher, and he doesn’t know that, and he hadn’t studied it, and yet he’s got— he’s the biggest church in America. It’s sad. Are you with me? It’s very sad.
Do works matter if you believe in Christ, and what about people of other religions?

He plays a recorded clip in which a speaker says a believer will have some good works, calls it a cop-out to say you are a Christian but never do anything to help, and says he is very careful about saying who would and wouldn’t go to heaven. The speaker speaks of the sincerity of people of another religion he saw in India.
Do works matter if you believe in Christ, and what about people of other religions?

Now, let’s go on. [Recorded clip begins.] Who said your record don’t count? You either believe in Christ or you don’t. If you believe in Christ you are going to heaven; if you don’t, no matter what you’ve done in your life, you ain’t. Yeah, it— I don’t know. There’s probably a balance between— I believe you have to know Christ, but I think that if you know Christ, if you’re a believer in God, you’re going to have some good works. I think it’s a cop-out to say, well, I’m a Christian but I don’t ever do anything to help. What if you’re Jewish or Muslim and you don’t accept Christ at all? No, I— I just— I’m very careful about saying who would and wouldn’t go to heaven. I don’t know. I think only God— you believe you have to believe in— I believe they’re wrong. Well, I don’t know if I believe they’re wrong. I don’t know if I believe they’re wrong. I spent a lot of time in India with my father, and, you know, I don’t know all about the religion, but I know they love God, and I don’t know, I’d have to— you know, I’ve seen their sincerity, so I don’t know. I don’t know. [Editor’s note: about 20 seconds of this stretch have no captions.]
Is there only one way to God, or are there many paths?

He plays a recorded exchange in which a questioner says being gay is a gift from God, one speaker says there are millions of ways to be a human being and many paths to God, and another replies there is one way and only one way, Jesus. A panelist answers that there are many paths to Jesus and that everybody is going to heaven. He presents these as examples of deflective, defective ministers.
Is there only one way to God, or are there many paths?

Hey, glad to have you. Hello, Oprah! Awesome to have you. We love you, we pray for you. Joel Osteen’s church. Oprah brought a friend with her today. He’s an entrepreneur, an actor, just— Tyler Perry is with us as well. Mr. Tyler Perry. All right, what’s your question for our spiritual panel? I’m a thirty-three-year-old guy. I grew up in a rural part of Alabama, and I happen to be gay, and the troubling part of our culture, which is largely anti-gay— being gay is a gift from God. Being gay is a gift from God. Now, where’s that in the Bible? But our culture doesn’t understand that, and consequently the culture sends messages that you ought to isolate it, that you ought to isolate, that you ought to isolate. Well, you’re the first minister I ever heard say being gay is a gift from God. I can say now here human beings make is believing that there is only one way to live, and that we don’t accept that there are diverse ways of being in the world, that there are millions of ways to be a human being, and many ways— no, but many paths to what you God, and her path might be something else, and when she gets there she might call it the light, but her loving and her kindness and her generosity brings her— if it brings her to the same point that it brings you, it doesn’t matter whether she called it God along the way or not. And I guess the danger that could be on that, I mean, it sounds great on the onset, but if you really look at both sides, there could possibly be just one way. What— what about Jesus? What about Jesus? There isn’t only one way— there is— there’s one way and only one way, and that is Jesus. So here’s the big question: are there many paths to get to the one God? Well, I believe, Oprah, that there— I believe that Jesus is the way to the one God, but I believe there are many paths to Jesus. So are gay people also included? Absolutely. [unclear] many ways to Jesus, and gays are in. I think— I don’t think any of us would make it to heaven. I think that it’s going to be open for all of us, or everybody’s going to heaven.
Should churches stop talking about sin to reach people?

He plays clips in which speakers say people are beaten down by doctrine, dogma, guilt and rules, that God is portrayed as mad and out to get them, and that churches should not look at their sins or try to judge. After a clip in which a speaker says an issue is hard and he does not fully understand it, he asks whether a preacher doesn’t need to understand.
Should churches stop talking about sin to reach people?

And we’re living in a country now where so many people have been raised or were raised under doctrine and dogma, and they feel so beaten down by the guilt and the punishing, wrathful telling people they’re wrong. It’s beating them. They want something more, but they don’t want to be punished. Yeah, I think just what you said, that’s the— that’s the era that we’re living in, that so much of God has been portrayed as, you know, mad and out to get them and just the— the rules and the— and the regulations, the rules and the regulations. I know our message is, yeah, like the— the goodness of God that leads people to repent. I don’t know. I think the— the— the reason some churches don’t grow, some of them have been stagnant, is because, you know, people are already beaten down enough by life. We need people telling us that God is on our side. It’s not the— it’s the people that we’re after. We’re not— we’re not looking at their sins. We’re not trying to judge. Forget sin, just give us the people. Try to encourage them, and their money of course, and let them know that we love them, and that, you know what, you’re only going to— you’re only going to reach people by reaching out to them. And, you know, like if Elton John was sitting here today, and, you know, like if Elton John was sitting here today— if Elton John was there, he would— [unclear] Elton John has told a US magazine that he believes Jesus was gay. The singer described Christ as a compassionate, super-intelligent gay man who understood human problems. So here we got a guy saying Jesus was a homosexual, and the [unclear] are going to accept them and get him into heaven. I say, I love you, John, you are a talented— I love you, John. People that come to our church and sit there, we, I mean, that’s not going to get Elton John saved. It’s an issue that, you know, it’s a hard issue, and I don’t know that I fully understand it. I don’t think I fully understand it. [Recorded clip ends.] Well, as a preacher, don’t you think he needs to understand? Now, I wanted you to hear it from the horse’s mouth, okay.
Should churches stop talking about sin to reach people?
Romans 2:4: Or do you despise the riches of His goodness, forbearance, and longsuffering, not knowing that the goodness of God leads you to repentance?
Will love, kindness and generosity get you into heaven?

He says a speaker claimed that love, kindness and generosity will get you into heaven whatever God you serve, and that there are many ways to God and to Jesus. He says they do not bring up adultery, fornication, incest and pedophilia, that we are so callous now that even sex outside of marriage is not mentioned, and he calls these deflective, defective ministers.
Will love, kindness and generosity get you into heaven?

Oprah said love, kindness and generosity will get you into heaven, whatever God you serve. Did you hear that? Wherever, whatever you want to call God. And they said there are many ways to God and many ways to Jesus, and homosexuals are included. Now, folks, you will notice that they’re not talking about adultery, fornication, incest and pedophilia. Oprah lives in daily sexual immorality. She’s unmarried, and she shacks up with some rich businessmen there in LA. But see, we’re so callous now that adultery, sex outside of marriage, even— they don’t even bring up the issue. Don’t even bring it up. These are deflective, defective ministers.
Is heaven open to people of other religions, according to this clip?

He plays a recorded exchange in which a Muslim caller asks a Pentecostal bishop whether only Christians can hope to enter heaven. The bishop says he believes Christianity is right but leaves who goes to God, says he is not so dogmatic as to condemn anybody, and cites Jesus’s words about other sheep and about casting the first stone. Kincer then calls that a Pentecostal preacher talking.
Is heaven open to people of other religions, according to this clip?

Now, here is T. D. Jakes. He’s a Pentecostal preacher, great big church, speaks in tongues and all that stuff, and look what he got to say about Muslims and homosexuals. [Recorded clip begins.] This is Annette. Annette with us from Portland, Oregon. Yes, hi, thanks for taking my call. Sure. I’m a Muslim here in Portland. I’m part of the Shiite community, and we had a wonderful interface dialogue last weekend with the local Unitarian church, and I’d like to ask you, please, to speak about concrete experiences you’ve had as far as interface dialogues, and also I’d like to ask you, do you feel that only Christians can hope to enter heaven? Very great question. When it comes to interfaith experiences, I’m currently serving, by the appointment of President— former President Bush and President Clinton, as co-chair of an interfaith advisory committee to help people get back up on their feet, and we do have on the board Muslims, Catholics, Jewish rabbi, Baptist, Methodist, Pentecostals, across the board, and we’re working together very effectively because we all care about common goals. We have our distinct theology and our own ideology, but there are common grounds that we can work together very effectively in many, many cases. When it comes to heaven, I try to leave that up to God. I certainly believe that Christianity is right, but when it comes down to the final test, who goes and who doesn’t go, Jesus said, “other sheep I have who are not of this fold; them also I must bring.” I’ll let him identify who those sheep are, and I stay out of the conversation. Thanks for that, Bishop. You don’t stay out of that conversation necessarily when homosexuals are the issue. What makes you say that? Well, I’ve read that you consider homosexuality a sin, so if you’re a practicing homosexual, you’re not going to have it, you know. Some— I don’t know anybody of any faith who can say that they have no sin in their lives. I mean, whether it’s homosexuality or lying on your income tax or speaking rudely to somebody at a window, what we call sin may differ from person to person, but who amongst us can say that they have no sin? Jesus said that, and he said, “He that’s without fault among you, let him cast the first stone.” I’m certainly not casting any particular stones at any particular group of people. All of us have sin and come short of the glory of God. But when it— the question was about hell, and when it comes down to hell, that’s an issue that I believe in a way of salvation. I believe that Jesus is the way, the truth and the life, that no man comes to the Father but by him, but I’m not so dogmatic in my views that I’m willing to condemn anybody and send them to hell. I leave that up to— [Recorded clip ends.]
Is heaven open to people of other religions, according to this clip?

John 10:16: And other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd. John 8:7: So when they continued asking Him, He raised Himself up and said to them, “He who is without sin among you, let him throw a stone at her first.” Romans 3:23: for all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God, John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
Is “believe on Jesus, you’re in” enough, with no change of life?

He plays a clip in which a Southern Baptist says gay people do not go to hell because they are gay and that anyone who accepts Christ is going to heaven, no change, no nothing. He calls this the grace and faith doctrine that is so prominent in America, without any change of life, and calls the ministers defective and deflective.
Is “believe on Jesus, you’re in” enough, with no change of life?

Now, that is a Pentecostal preacher talking. Now, here’s the Southern Baptist. [Recorded clip begins.] Are gay people going to hell? No, not because they’re gay. Everybody— we go to hell because we choose to reject the grace of God. The only way you can go to hell is— you, a person accepts, accepts Christ Jesus Christ, he’s going to heaven, okay, without a doubt. Okay. Fair, fair, fair, fair enough. Believe on Jesus, you’re in. No change, no nothing. [Recorded clip ends.] This is this grace and faith doctrine that is so prominent in America, without any change of life. Okay, defective, deflective ministers of the gospel.
Who are the “other sheep” Jesus spoke about in John 10?

He says that any person reading the Bible with open-mindedness knows the other sheep are the Gentiles, not sinners, the non-Jews. He says the Bible is very clear on that, and that the Spirit guides you into all truth.
Who are the “other sheep” Jesus spoke about in John 10?

Now, let’s look at Bible statements of “my faith.” You’ll see how they said “my faith,” “I believe,” and “don’t judge.” And this guy, this Pentecostal, said the other sheep not of this fold can include homosexuals. The Mormons believe they are the other sheep not of that fold. And any idiot that’s read his Bible with any kind of open-mindedness knows that the other sheep are the Gentiles. It’s not sinners, it’s the non-Jews, with the other sheep. The Bible’s very clear on that. And this Pentecostal preacher don’t know that. There’s something wrong with that Pentecost, because the Spirit guides you into all truth. Can I hear an amen?
Who are the “other sheep” Jesus spoke about in John 10?

John 10:16: And other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd. John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.
What does “my faith” mean in the Bible?

He says the statement “my faith” is found only twice in the Bible and is used in conjunction with a lifestyle, the fruits. He cites the passage where someone says show me your faith without your works and I will show you my faith by my works, and says that the demons believe and tremble, so what people say they believe is insignificant: what God told us to believe is what counts. The second time is Jesus’s own words in Revelation, which he says speaks of the faith of Jesus.
What does “my faith” mean in the Bible?

Now, the Bible and the statement of “my faith,” it’s only found twice in the Bible, the statement “my faith.” How many times? Twice. James 2:1 [Editor’s note: the verse he reads is James 2:18.]: “You have faith and I have works; show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works.” So “my faith” is only used in conjunction with my lifestyle. The fruits. You know, “you know them by their fruits,” not their words, their fruits. “You believe that there is one God; you do well.” See, they say, I believe, I believe, I believe. Well, I believe you do well, but the demons believe, and they’re not going to heaven. They tremble. And these guys are wrong when they say, well, I believe— what they believe is insignificant. It’s what God told us to believe that is significant. Amen. Now, second time it’s used: Revelation 2:13. Jesus Christ himself is talking: “I know your works, and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. You hold fast to my name and did not deny my faith.” Whose faith? The faith of Jesus. Now, should my faith be the faith of Jesus? Absolutely. I can’t just come up with my own little ideas and say, well, I believe, and my faith. And to illustrate that, I gave a little chart there on your sheet. 1 Corinthians 2:5 says your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. See, and that’s what Jesus did. He told them that God had to be involved in their salvation. Even to come to Christ, God had to be involved, and they left him. And here Paul said your faith can’t be in the intellect of men. This can’t be intellectually done; it’s got to be in the supernatural power of God involved in your life.
What does “my faith” mean in the Bible?

James 2:18: But someone will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without your works, and I will show you my faith by my works. James 2:19: You believe that there is one God. You do well. Even the demons believe—and tremble! Matthew 7:20: Therefore by their fruits you will know them. Revelation 2:13: “I know your works, and where you dwell, where Satan’s throne is. And you hold fast to My name, and did not deny My faith even in the days in which Antipas was My faithful martyr, who was killed among you, where Satan dwells. 1 Corinthians 2:5: that your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God.
Whose faith should we have: our own, our group’s, or Jesus’s?

He says Jesus’s faith was in the scriptures and in the Father, while “my faith” is whatever I choose or am convinced of, such as saying people of various religions go to heaven. He says the Catholics, Protestants and Jews all have faith in their group, but your faith has to be in Jesus Christ and his word, not in your faith or your denomination.
Whose faith should we have: our own, our group’s, or Jesus’s?

Now, we have over here: faith, my faith, my faith, anything I choose, is I’m convinced of, I’m right. All right. Over on the left you got Jesus’s faith. Jesus’s faith is in the scriptures. See, when the rich man came to Jesus and said, “Well, what must I do to have eternal life?” he says, “What does the scripture say?” [Editor’s note: in Luke the question “What is written in the law?” is put to a lawyer (Luke 10:25-26); the rich ruler of Luke 18:18 is answered with the commandments.] See, Jesus’s faith was in the word of God and in the Father. He said, “I do nothing except what the Father tells me to do.” See, Jesus’s faith was in the Father, and it was in the scriptures. Over here, my faith, what I believe, I can come up with any concocted ideal I want to. For instance, like [unclear] Hindus go to heaven. That’s what he said in his interview. He was in India, and, oh, those are nice people, and they’re going to heaven also. There’s Buddhists in India, they’re going to heaven. All right, the Muslims and the Mormons are going to heaven. See, that’s what they said: my faith, I believe they’re going to heaven. Well, that’s wonderful, but what does this side say? Are you getting the picture now? The Catholics, the Protestants and the Jews all come up with the— they all have some weird doctrines, and the problem with these groups is their faith is in their group. Catholics really believe, because they’re Catholics, most of them, they’re going to go to heaven. Their faith is in the Catholic church. But so are Protestants. Baptists, their faith is in the Baptist; Pentecostal, their faith is in the Pentecostal. Your faith has to be in Jesus Christ and his word. Are you hearing me? Your faith cannot be in your faith. Your faith has to be in his faith.
Whose faith should we have: our own, our group’s, or Jesus’s?

Luke 10:25-26: And behold, a certain lawyer stood up and tested Him, saying, “Teacher, what shall I do to inherit eternal life?” He said to him, “What is written in the law? What is your reading of it?” John 5:19: Then Jesus answered and said to them, “Most assuredly, I say to you, the Son can do nothing of Himself, but what He sees the Father do; for whatever He does, the Son also does in like manner.
He says they deflected because they had a defect. He says a disciple is one that’s disciplined, a pupil and follower of Christ, and he says not everybody in the Bible turned out to be heroes.
Can you decide to serve God on your own?

He says no: Jesus said the Father and he have to be involved in your conversion and salvation. He says it is not joining a church or being a Jew, Protestant or Catholic, and that the Spirit of God has to be involved.
What does he say eternal life means?

He says a couple of weeks earlier they learned that eternal life is to know God and Jesus Christ, not just live forever. He says the disciples who stayed had experienced God being involved in their salvation, and that it is not a hand-me-down Christianity.
What does God want us to give him?

He says God wants a Bible morality lifestyle: living right and stopping sinning. He says praise is wonderful and prayer is wonderful, but what God wants back from you is for you to live right, no matter if you are a Catholic, a Jew or a Protestant.
Why does he say the crowd followed Jesus in John 6?

He says they followed him because they saw the signs he performed on those who were diseased, and later because he fed them with the loaves and fishes. He says Jesus told them plainly that they now wanted free food, which he describes as wanting what we can get out of God.
What are the “P’s” he warns against?

He lists prosperity, psychotherapy, Purpose Driven, possibility thinking, positive thinking and individual prophecy. He says these followers are fractured and are deflecting from Christ, wanting something instead of giving him something.
What does he say the Bible calls for instead of therapy and positive thinking?
He says Jesus wants us to give him Bible morality, not grace and faith, prosperity, positive thinking or psychotherapy, and that in the Bible it is self-control: just stop what you’re doing.
What does he say the Mormon church told him about Jesus Christ?

He says he called their headquarters, did not act like somebody else, and asked questions. He says they told him Jesus Christ is not God, is not eternal without a beginning and an end, and did not exist until Mary, and he says the Bible teaches he existed before Mary.
Where does the Bible use the phrase “my faith”?

He says it is found only twice: once where someone says I will show you my faith by my works, and once in Jesus’s words to a church in Revelation, where he says you did not deny my faith. He says the phrase is used in conjunction with lifestyle, not just words.
Do the demons believe in God?

He says the demons believe and they are not going to heaven, they tremble, so saying you believe is not enough. He says what people say they believe is insignificant; it is what God told us to believe that is significant.
What does 1 Corinthians 2:5 say about where our faith should be?

He says it says your faith should not be in the wisdom of men but in the power of God. He says Paul meant that faith cannot be done intellectually: it has to be in the supernatural power of God involved in your life.
What does he say Jesus’s faith was in?
He says Jesus’s faith was in the scriptures and in the Father. He points to Jesus saying he does nothing except what the Father tells him to do.
Can your faith be in your church or denomination?

He says no: the problem with Catholics, Protestants and Jews alike is that their faith is in their group. He says your faith has to be in Jesus Christ and his word, and your faith cannot be in your faith but has to be in his faith.

items.d: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the previous message by saying the Bible’s “I believe” statements are about believing Jesus is the Son of God and that God will do…
p: In “Deflective Defective Disciples Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues the previous message by saying the Bible’s “I believe” statements are about believing Jesus is the Son of God and that God will do what he said. He argues from Acts and 1 Corinthians that Christians and ministers are meant to judge, reads Revelation 21:8 on who goes to the lake of fire, and criticizes ministers he says flatter people. He points to Jeremiah 3:15 as God’s solution and calls believers to virtue and to speak up.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?

Pastor Kincer lists prosperity, positive thinking, possibility, Purpose Driven and psychotherapy thinking, and adds personal prophecy thinking, which he says is a dime a dozen in many Spirit-filled circles. He says he does not need personal prophecy; he needs the Bible, the sure word of prophecy. He says the claim that atheists, humanists and anyone who is good can go to heaven is lying, and that the end result of Jesus’s faith is a disciple pursuing the divine nature and doing good works.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?

Adultery, homosexuality, incest, intoxication. Okay, see, “my faith,” “I believe,” nothing’s wrong with it. Prosperity, positive thinking, possibility— you ever met these people that won’t say a negative thing? There: possibility thinking, prosperity thinking, Purpose Driven thinking, psychotherapy thinking, and one I didn’t have up there is this personal prophecy thinking. My gosh. And in a lot of Spirit-filled circles, you know, personal prophecy is just a dime a dozen. Just everybody’s giving out personal prophecies. Where is that in the Bible? They’re just flat out wrong. I don’t need no personal prophecy; I need the book. I need the Bible. Amen. It’s the sure word of prophecy, that’s what the Bible says. Atheist and humanist and everybody’s got their own ideas. And in one of these they talked about atheists, and they said, yeah, everybody can go to heaven. And as Oprah put it, if you’re good— generosity, kindness and love— you can go to heaven no matter what. They’re just lying. Now, over here the end result is a Christian, a disciple of the divine nature. They’re pursuing the divine nature. Hallelujah, because that’s what this faith, Jesus’s faith, whole focus is on: you being a light to the world, living for him by doing good works.
Do Christians need personal prophecy, and will good people go to heaven without Christ?
2 Peter 1:19: And so we have the prophetic word confirmed, which you do well to heed as a light that shines in a dark place, until the day dawns and the morning star rises in your hearts;
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

He reads Revelation 21:8 and says it plainly tells who is going to the lake of fire, including the unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters and all liars. He says homosexuals miss out on two counts, sexual immorality and abomination, and that you cannot change the Bible because you want to be nice to people. He says preachers are not challenging Christians living in sexual immorality, and that America and the homosexual need to hear it so he can get saved and change his ways.
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

Now, Revelation 21:8: “The cowardly, the unbelieving, the abominable”— abomination means God hates it, all right— “murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers,” which is witchcraft, “idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.” And Joel Osteen doesn’t know, and T. D. Jakes doesn’t know, that these people are going to hell, and Rick Warren doesn’t know, and Oprah doesn’t know. It’s very plain in Revelation. This is just one scripture. He tells us plainly who’s going to the lake of fire, and homosexuals miss out on two counts: sexual immorality and abomination. It’s listed under both. Adultery, incest— these sins, will you burn for them? You can’t change the Bible because you want to be nice to people. Can I hear an amen? And Christians are living in sexual immorality and doing all kinds of stupid things, and the preachers aren’t challenging them on Sunday to stop it, and everybody thinks they’re okay. Folks, you can’t change this. Idolatry is an abomination. Idolatry is listed twice up there, under abominations and under idolatry. Are you with me? And all liars: these guys are lying. How many liars go to hell? All of them. Now, folks, this is flagrant lying just so they can get crowds and money. They like the money, man. They live in million-dollar mansions and they drive big cars, and they got all these people coming wanting to hear their flattering messages. And America needs to hear that that’s wrong, and the Christians need to hear, the homosexual needs to hear that he’s wrong, so that he can get saved and change his ways. Can I hear an amen?
Who goes to the lake of fire according to Revelation 21:8, and should preachers challenge sin?

Revelation 21:8: But the cowardly, unbelieving, abominable, murderers, sexually immoral, sorcerers, idolaters, and all liars shall have their part in the lake which burns with fire and brimstone, which is the second death.”
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

He says “I believe” is used four times in the passages he reads and every time it means believing that Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the only begotten Son of God, or believing that God will do what he said he would do. He reads the statements in John 11, John 9, Acts 8 and Acts 27, and says that is what “I believe” should say, not that any sin is fine and you can still go to heaven.
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

But so, the adulterers. John 11:27, the statement of “I believe”: “I believe you are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” Okay. “I believe” is used four times, and every time it’s used this way. All right: I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God, the only begotten Son of God. Lucifer is not a begotten Son of God. Lucifer was a created being. Jesus was birthed in the flesh by God. Amen. John 9:35: “Do you believe on the Son of God?” Jesus asked the man.
