He said, “Who is he, Lord, that I might believe on him?” Jesus said, “You have seen him, and it is he that talks with you.” I’m him, Jesus said. The man quickly says, “I believe.” I believe what? That you are the Son of God, that Jesus is the Son of God. How many believe that Jesus is the only begotten Son of God? Yeah. See, that’s what “I believe” should say: not “I believe homos can go to heaven,” and, “Oh, you know, I can get intoxicated and still go to heaven,” and all the rest. No. Acts 8:37: Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may get baptized,” and the eunuch said, “I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” He said it again. Paul, in Acts 27:25, on the island— or before he got to the island, on the boat: “Be of good cheer, I believe God.” What’s the statement? “I believe God that it shall be as it was told me.” Now, that sums it up: I believe that God will do what he said he would do. Amen. I can’t come up with my own little gizmo doctrines, my feel-good doctrines.
What does “I believe” mean in the Bible?

John 11:27: She said to Him, “Yes, Lord, I believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, who is to come into the world.” John 9:35-37: Jesus heard that they had cast him out; and when He had found him, He said to him, “Do you believe in the Son of God?” He answered and said, “Who is He, Lord, that I may believe in Him?” And Jesus said to him, “You have both seen Him and it is He who is talking with you.” Acts 8:37: Then Philip said, “If you believe with all your heart, you may.” And he answered and said, “I believe that Jesus Christ is the Son of God.” Acts 27:25: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it will be just as it was told me.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

He says ministers are supposed to preach the Bible, and the Bible already judges, so telling people they are going to hell is telling them what the Bible said, not judging them himself. He compares it to a doctor who will not tell a patient with cancer he is going to die, and says Paul boldly told the Jews who rejected the word that they had judged themselves unworthy of eternal life.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

The Bible, in judging: you hear them all say they wouldn’t judge. You hear that? I’m not going to judge anybody. Well, no, all sinned. T. D. Jakes, all not going to judge: I’m not going to judge. Well, the Bible already judges it. And ministers are supposed to be preaching the Bible. See, I’m not judging people when I, you know, when I tell people you’re going to hell. I’m telling them what the Bible said. God’s judgment is you’re going to hell. And I told you people last year said nobody talks like that. I said, the Bible talks like that. And can you imagine going in for cancer, and the doctors don’t want to make a judgment? They don’t want to tell you that you’re going to die, and they just say, oh, you’re just fine, you’re just fine, you’re not going to die, you don’t need treatment, you’re just— you don’t need any kind of treatment, you don’t need any kind of medicine or anything else, you know. And in the end you what? Die, when you could have got some treatment and lived. And these preachers don’t want to tell people they’re going to die. See, the lake of fire we read is the second death. You’re going to die for eternity. The Jews opposed things spoken by Paul, in Acts 13:45. So Paul boldly said— Paul what? Boldly said. He didn’t sit there silently and, well, I’m not going to judge. Well, you know, I haven’t read into that, I don’t have knowledge. No, he boldly said, “It was necessary the word of God be spoken to you first, you Jews, but since you reject it and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we’re going to the Gentiles.” See, they judged themselves. They made a decision themselves to miss out on eternal life.
Does the Bible say we should not judge anyone?

Acts 13:45-46: But when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with envy; and contradicting and blaspheming, they opposed the things spoken by Paul. Then Paul and Barnabas grew bold and said, “It was necessary that the word of God should be spoken to you first; but since you reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

He says 1 Corinthians 6 asks whether the saints will judge the world and angels, so they are not unworthy to judge the smallest matters of this life. He reads Acts 15:19, where the decision is to write to the Gentiles to abstain from idols, sexual immorality, things strangled and blood, and he says ministers should make that judgment today.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

1 Corinthians 6:2: “Do you not know that the saints would judge the world?” Whoo! Are you out there, church? “If the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters?” You can’t make decisions on the least little thing! You got these homosexuals and these Oprah telling you that— “Judge not, lest you be not judged. For what judgment you judge you shall be judged.” Come on! “Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more things that pertain to this life?” Are we supposed to make judgments concerning this life? Yeah. Are we to make judgment on the very smallest matters, whether we buy a car we can’t afford, or will we buy a car we can’t afford? Are we supposed to make judgments? Yeah. Good grief. Raise your child up in the way they should go, or raise them up the way Dr. Spock said they should go? We got to make— we’re to make judgment. They’re lying to you, people out there. Acts 15:19: “I judge.” What did he say? “I judge.” [Editor’s note: in Acts 15:19 the speaker is James, not Paul.] Oh my gosh, [unclear] is going to fall off his chair. Oprah and T. D. Jakes and Warren, what’s this? What are they going to do with this scripture? Paul’s judging. He’s making a decision. What’s his decision? “That we should not trouble the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols, sexual immorality, things strangled, and from blood.” Sexual immorality: no homosexuality, no adultery, no incest, no sex with kids, all sex in the marriage. That’s it. And he made that judgment. Don’t you think ministers should be making that judgment today? Absolutely.
Are Christians supposed to make judgments, according to 1 Corinthians 6 and Acts 15?

1 Corinthians 6:2-3: Do you not know that the saints will judge the world? And if the world will be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge the smallest matters? Do you not know that we shall judge angels? How much more, things that pertain to this life? Matthew 7:1-2: “Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you. Acts 15:19-20: Therefore I judge that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who are turning to God, but that we write to them to abstain from things polluted by idols, from sexual immorality, from things strangled, and from blood.
Why are so many Christians weak, and what should they do?

He says God’s people are weak because they listen to weak preachers and do not have enough discipline to read the Bible themselves every day. He says Christians in trouble are non-readers who go to Bible studies mostly to associate with a group, and that they should get a connection with Jesus and his word, since we go to church to spiritualize, not socialize.
Why are so many Christians weak, and what should they do?

God’s people are wimps because they’re listening to wimpy ministers. That’s right. They’re weak because they listen to weak preachers, and they ain’t got enough discipline to get on their knees and open that Bible up themselves and read a proverb a day and read [unclear] a day and read the Bible every day. I guarantee you, Christians that are in trouble are non-readers, and they don’t go to Bible studies where they actually hear somebody expound and open up the scriptures to them. They go to Bible studies mostly to associate, you know, they’re associating with this group, they got a connection with the group. You better get a connection with Jesus and his word. Yeah, that’s worth a clap. We don’t go to church to socialize. These churches, America’s churches, have got it wrong. We go to church to spiritualize. We need to become better spiritual people. Hallelujah.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

He reads 1 Corinthians 5 and says Paul told the church not to keep company with the sexually immoral and others in the list, and that those inside the church are to be judged while God judges those outside. He says the man there was committing incest, and Paul passed a judgment to kick him out of the church.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

1 Corinthians 5:9: “I wrote to you not to keep company with sexually immoral brethren, or greedy people, extortioners”— and revilers, they that blast people with their mouth— “drunkard, or idolaters. Not to eat with such a person. What have I to do with judging outsiders? Do you not judge those who are inside?” Did you hear that? “But those outside God judges. For this reason, put away yourselves from that evil person.” This guy was committing incest. He was having sex with his father’s wife, and Paul passed a judgment to kick this guy out of the church, and he told the Corinthian church, you got to make decisions.
Should a church put out a member who is living in sexual sin?

1 Corinthians 5:9-13: I wrote to you in my epistle not to keep company with sexually immoral people. Yet I certainly did not mean with the sexually immoral people of this world, or with the covetous, or extortioners, or idolaters, since then you would need to go out of the world. But now I have written to you not to keep company with anyone named a brother, who is sexually immoral, or covetous, or an idolater, or a reviler, or a drunkard, or an extortioner—not even to eat with such a person. For what have I to do with judging those also who are outside? Do you not judge those who are inside? But those who are outside God judges. Therefore “put away from yourselves the evil person.”
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

He reads 2 Corinthians 5:14 and calls it basic kindergarten Christianity: if Christ died for you, you should live not for yourself but for him. He says selfishness is why churches have problems, and that following Jesus’s example means laying down our life, working, getting married, staying married and raising children right.
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

2 Corinthians 5:14: “The love of Christ compels, because we judge this: if one died for all, then all died, and he died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves.” Good Lord, that’s so simple. That’s basic kindergarten Christianity: that if Christ died for you, you should be living not for yourself but for him who died for you and rose again. Can I hear an amen? I don’t have to live to please Rick Warren or T. D. Jakes or Joel Osteen. I’ve got to please Jesus Christ. Amen. And let me tell you something, church: selfishness is why you got your problems. You’re only thinking about yourself and your feelings and what you want, and it creates problems. You just want your own way because you feel it’s right. Jesus, our example, laid down his life for us. If we’re going to follow his example, we’re going to what? Lay down our life. We’re not going to do what we want to do; we’re going to do what he wants us to do. Amen. We’re going to work, we’re going to get married, we’re going to stay married, we’re going to raise children, we’re going to raise them right. We judge this way. Are we to judge? Yes.
What does it mean to live for Christ instead of for yourself?

2 Corinthians 5:14-15: For the love of Christ compels us, because we judge thus: that if One died for all, then all died; and He died for all, that those who live should live no longer for themselves, but for Him who died for them and rose again.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

He reads 1 Corinthians 14:29, let two or three prophets speak and let the others judge, and says he has a right to decide whether what ministers say is scripturally correct. He says personal prophecy has no one to verify it and that prophets should not be wrong, and that people must depend on the scriptures. He also says we are to judge ourselves, and that the Sermon on the Mount means start with yourself before helping a brother with a splinter.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

1 Corinthians 14:29: “Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others”— what? Judge. See, I have a right to take what Joel Osteen, Rick Warren, T. D. Jakes and Oprah and all these guys say. I have a right to make a decision if they’re scripturally correct. And I’m not out to lambaste the brethren or to divide the church. I am out to speak the truth so people can know the truth and the truth can set them free. Is that an amen? I mean, it plainly says when somebody’s talking, there’s got to be somebody checking out whether they’re saying it right or not. Hallelujah. And that’s where personal prophecy goes right out the tube. There’s no one there to verify you’re speaking right. And let me tell you, I’ve heard a lot of lousy personal prophecies, and I just flat out— to him, you’re wrong, you missed it, bud. I mean, no, I can prophesy too. I mean, they act like they’re the only ones that’s got the gift, but let me tell you, I can prophesy. And when these prophets come in and they said this, that and the other, I said, you’re wrong. And they go, no way. I said, I got the proof, you’re wrong. I know that person, and this is why you’re wrong. They got mad at me. But prophets should not be wrong. Can I hear an amen? And getting people dependent on your personal prophecies, that’s not scriptural. People have got to get dependent on the scriptures. Amen. And prophecies are good when they confirm and all that, but when they don’t, and they’re out of line, it’s destructive. 1 Corinthians 11:30: “Many are weak and sick among you, many are dead already, for if you would judge yourselves you would not be judged.” So we are to what? Judge ourselves. And that’s what the Sermon on the Mount is talking about when he says, “Judge not, lest you be judged. For with what judgment you judge you shall be judged,” and what you give out you’ll get given back to you. You better first get the 2x4 out of your eye, he said, so that you can see clearly to help the brother get a splinter out of his eye. All it’s saying is you start with yourself.
Should preaching and prophecy be tested against the Bible?

1 Corinthians 14:29: Let two or three prophets speak, and let the others judge. John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Corinthians 11:30-31: For this reason many are weak and sick among you, and many sleep. For if we would judge ourselves, we would not be judged. Matthew 7:1-5: “Judge not, that you be not judged. For with what judgment you judge, you will be judged; and with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you. And why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but do not consider the plank in your own eye? Or how can you say to your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye’; and look, a plank is in your own eye? Hypocrite! First remove the plank from your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

He reads Jeremiah 3:15, where God promises shepherds after his heart who feed with knowledge and understanding, and says people are destroyed for lack of knowledge because preachers in America are making them feel good instead of helping them grow and change. He says Christian divorce, children out of marriage and single-parent homes are as high as in the secular world, and that something is wrong.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

God’s solution for defective, deflective disciples and ministers: here’s his solution. Are you ready? Jeremiah 3:15: “I will give you shepherds according to my heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.” The Bible says, “For lack of knowledge my people are destroyed,” and gone into captivity. They lack knowledge. And why? Because preachers in America aren’t giving them the knowledge to make decisions during the week. They’re making them feel good where they’re at. They’re not growing, they’re not changing, and they wind up destroying themselves. Christian divorce is just as high as secular divorce. Christians having kids out of marriage is just as high as the secular. Christians in a single-parent home is just as high as the secular. Something’s wrong, church. Yes. The results aren’t there. At that time— I love this— he says he’s going to do it, and he tells us what’s going to happen at that time. Jerusalem— Hebrews 12 tells us Jerusalem is the church. Okay. At that time the church shall be called the Throne of the Lord. He is Lord; he’s ruling. We are following him. I love that. Do you see that? He’s not in a lot of churches. The throne is not in a lot of churches. The pastor is on the throne, because these people are worshiping pastors and ministers.
What is God’s solution for deflective, defective ministers?

Jeremiah 3:15: And I will give you shepherds according to My heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding. Hosea 4:6: My people are destroyed for lack of knowledge. Because you have rejected knowledge, I also will reject you from being priest for Me; Because you have forgotten the law of your God, I also will forget your children. Hebrews 12:22: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

He says Jerusalem is the church and that at that time it shall be called the Throne of the Lord, with all nations gathered to the name of the Lord, which is Jesus. He says in a lot of churches the pastor is on the throne instead, and that we gather to the King, not a minister or a group. He says we know the time we are in when we are doing what he wants, not what we want.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

“And all nations shall be gathered to the throne” that’s in the church now. Is that Bible? We don’t gather to a minister or a group. We gather to the King on the throne in the church. Wow. “To the name of the Lord.” What’s his name? Jesus. Don’t give me no Buddha stuff. Don’t give me no Joseph Smith stuff. Don’t give me no [unclear]— I mean, Moroni, some angel that’s supposed to give— don’t give me that garbage. Give me Jesus. It’s his name I gather unto, it’s his throne together unto, and it’s his word that I must follow. Now, that was good. No more— listen to this. See, you can tell what the time is. Am I making sense to you? I’m trying to give you Revelation here that can change your life. See, we can know what time frame we’re in. Are we in the time where the church has the throne of the Lord, and nations are gathering to the throne, and the King on the throne, and his name? “No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.” See, we know what time and what season we’re in when we aren’t doing what we want to do; we’re doing what he wants us to do. Oh gosh, that was good.
What does it mean for the church to be called the Throne of the Lord?

Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
Should you leave a church where Jesus is not on the throne?

He says to stop listening to shepherds who flatter you, because it is the word that sets you free, heals you and makes you grow. He says that if you are going to a church where he is not on the throne and people are doing what they want to do, you are in the wrong group, so get to where you can get fed and grow.
Should you leave a church where Jesus is not on the throne?

Oh, church, and you got to make decisions, and you got to stop listening to these idiot shepherds, because they flatter you and make you feel good. It’s the word that sets you free. It’s the word that heals you. It’s the word that causes you to grow. When we get distracted and deflect from the word, and deflect from the living word, Jesus, we’re going to fall into problems. Christians don’t have any power and strength today. They can’t overcome sin, and the preacher just feeds them: they’re okay where they’re at. “No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil heart.” When you come to that place, you know you’re in this time, and you’re in the right group. And see, if you’re going to a church where he isn’t on the throne and not gathering to his name, and that people are doing what they want to do, you’re in the wrong group, man. Get out. Get to where you can get fed, get to where you can grow, get to where we can do something for Christ in this world together. Can I hear an amen?
Should you leave a church where Jesus is not on the throne?

Jeremiah 3:17: “At that time Jerusalem shall be called The Throne of the LORD, and all the nations shall be gathered to it, to the name of the LORD, to Jerusalem. No more shall they follow the dictates of their evil hearts.
What is virtue, and why is cowardice listed as a sin?

He says the first thing added to baby doctrine is virtue, which is the courage to live and stand up for Bible morals, and you have to add it to your faith. He says that if you will not tell your spouse, children, parents, neighbors and enemies Bible truths and Bible morality you are a coward, and that it is still the foolishness of preaching that saves people.
What is virtue, and why is cowardice listed as a sin?

Cowardly. Are you a coward today? You know, the first thing added to baby doctrine is virtue. Virtue is the courage to live and stand up for Bible morals, and you got to add that to your faith. Am I right? I’m just giving you Bible scriptures. And when you are a coward and you won’t stand up— I’m talking about your spouse, your children, your parents, your brothers and sisters, your neighbors, your enemies— and you don’t tell them Bible truths and Bible morality, you are a coward. What’s going to save them? They got to know. It’s still the foolishness of preaching that saves people.
What is virtue, and why is cowardice listed as a sin?

2 Peter 1:5: But also for this very reason, giving all diligence, add to your faith virtue, to virtue knowledge, 1 Corinthians 1:21: For since, in the wisdom of God, the world through wisdom did not know God, it pleased God through the foolishness of the message preached to save those who believe.
What do abominations, hatred, witchcraft and lying mean in Revelation 21:8?

He says there are about thirty-three abominations in the Bible and that Christians who hate others over skin color or social status are included under the New Testament teaching that hatred is the same as murder. He says Christians should not be afraid of witches because there is no witchcraft against God’s people, and that liars will have their part in the lake of fire, so do not be afraid to say it.
What do abominations, hatred, witchcraft and lying mean in Revelation 21:8?

Unbelieving: and we saw these disciples were what? Unbelievers, in John 6. Abominable things that God hates, which is idolatry, homosexuality, rape, things like that. There’s a whole list. There’s about thirty-three abominations in the Bible. There’s a whole— God hates them. Murderers: Jesus said if you hate— or the New Testament says if you hate, that is the same as murder. And we got Christians that hate skin color, social status, whatever. We have hatred, despise, we look down on people. Sexually immoral, sorcerers, witchcraft. And I meet Christians in the witchcraft, and I meet Christians that are afraid of witches. Back at the Vine, these women got together and they read this book about how the witches were keeping Christian churches from growing and affecting the church, and I go, that’s not true. The Bible says there is no witchcraft against God’s people. Those witches can do all they want to do; it has no effect on the church. And they just look, well, you don’t know everything. I don’t, but the book knows everything. Ain’t no witch doctor can get outside the church and do the [unclear] thing and have any effect on us. Are you there? But silly women— Paul said led astray. But you know, silly women, you got to watch, women, don’t— don’t be silly. Amen. Don’t be foolish. And “all liars shall have their part in a lake of burns with fire.” Were these guys lying? Were they lying? Absolutely. Don’t be afraid to say it, and don’t be afraid to email them and say, that’s not scripture. You know, I learned from people telling me like it was, because I wanted to be told like it was. I didn’t learn from people that were wimps. I didn’t learn from people that didn’t take an interest in people. I learned from people that took an interest in people, the right interest.
What do abominations, hatred, witchcraft and lying mean in Revelation 21:8?

1 John 3:15: Whoever hates his brother is a murderer, and you know that no murderer has eternal life abiding in him. Numbers 23:23: “For there is no sorcery against Jacob, Nor any divination against Israel. It now must be said of Jacob And of Israel, ‘Oh, what God has done!’ 2 Timothy 3:6: For of this sort are those who creep into households and make captives of gullible women loaded down with sins, led away by various lusts,
Why should Christians speak up instead of staying silent?

He says people who come to church, never share Christ with anybody and go home are silent saints who have no effect in the kingdom. He says that when you really know something it is natural to talk about it, without pumping up courage, and that you should speak the truth and not argue, since if one person is silent the argument ends.
Why should Christians speak up instead of staying silent?

You know, there’s people that come to church and they never share Christ with anybody. They have no effect and [unclear] in the kingdom at all. They just come, hear a sermon, go, oh wow, what a great sermon. Hallelujah. Do their little thing that they do in their church and then go home, and they’re silent saints. They are worthless. And I’m looking at some today. We got the internet; you can talk to anybody. I told you I went right to Utah, talked right to headquarters. How you know it’s time to speak up, hallelujah: it’s natural. When you really experience something and you know something, it’s just natural to talk about it. It isn’t like you got to get the courage up and pump it up. It’s just natural. You know, when somebody’s into baseball, it’s natural that they talk about baseball, right? People that are into God and truth, it’s just natural to speak truth, and you don’t have to argue about it. Just speak it and shut up. The Bible says it takes two people to argue; if one is silent, the argument ends. If you read your Proverbs you would know, but most of you do not read your Proverbs every day, principles of life. Someone was telling me this week they got into a heated argument. I said, well, if you’d have just shut up after you said your statement, that wouldn’t have been a heated argument. Amen. I mean, what’s the sense, and just keep harping on it, harping on it, harping on it? Just say it and go on. Let God do the work. Can I hear an amen?
What responsibility do believers have to get this message out?

He says to whom much is given much is required, so the church has a responsibility to get organized and tell everyone, believer and unbeliever alike, that Bible morality is part of getting into heaven. He says Bible morality, not psychotherapy and positive thinking, is what blesses a family and helps people in the church, and that it challenges immoral people to change.
What responsibility do believers have to get this message out?

They’re all going to the lake of fire, folks. Now, because we know that to whom much is given, much is required, we have a responsibility to get this word out. We have a responsibility, church, to get organized and get out this message to everyone, believer and unbeliever alike, that Bible morality is part of getting into heaven. Amen. And Bible morality is what blesses my family. That’s what’s going to encourage my children, being an example and teaching them and directing them that way. That’s what’s going to help my family. It isn’t psychotherapy and positive thinking. Bible morality is what’s going to help people in the church, and it’s going to challenge the unmoral people to change their way. And that’s what the basic gospel is all about.
What responsibility do believers have to get this message out?

Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more.
What does he say prosperity, positive thinking and similar movements have in common?

He lists prosperity, positive, possibility, Purpose Driven, psychotherapy and personal prophecy thinking together, tied to the idea of saying “my faith” and “I believe” with nothing wrong with it. He says that in the Bible there is no place for personal prophecy and that he needs the book.
Does he say Lucifer is a son of God?
He says Lucifer is not a begotten Son of God, and was a created being. He says Jesus was birthed in the flesh by God and is the only begotten Son of God.
Why does he compare telling people the truth to a doctor and cancer?

He says a doctor who tells a patient he is fine and does not need treatment lets the patient die when he could have got treatment and lived. He says preachers who will not tell people they are going to die for eternity, the second death of the lake of fire, are doing the same.
Why does he say we go to church?

He says we do not go to church to socialize but to spiritualize, to become better spiritual people. He says many go to Bible studies mostly to associate with a group, and that they should get a connection with Jesus and his word.
What does he say the Corinthian church was told to do about a man who had his father’s wife?

He says Paul passed a judgment to kick the man out of the church and told the Corinthian church they had to make decisions. He points to the passage that says to judge those inside the church while God judges those outside.
What does he call basic kindergarten Christianity?

He says it is that if Christ died for you, you should be living not for yourself but for him who died for you and rose again. He says he does not have to live to please any minister but has to please Jesus Christ.
Why does he say selfishness is the cause of problems in the church?

He says people are only thinking about themselves, their feelings and what they want, and they just want their own way because they feel it is right. He says Jesus laid down his life for us, so if we follow his example we lay down our life and do what he wants, not what we want.
What does he say about prophets who are wrong?

He says that he has heard a lot of lousy personal prophecies and told the prophets they were wrong, and some got mad at him. He says prophets should not be wrong, and that prophecies are good when they confirm but destructive when they are out of line.
What does he say about Christian divorce and single-parent homes?

He says Christian divorce, Christians having kids out of marriage and Christians in single-parent homes are each just as high as in the secular world. He says something is wrong in the church and that the results are not there.
What does he say about witchcraft and the church?

He says he meets Christians who are afraid of witches, and that some women in the church read a book about how witches were keeping churches from growing. He says that is not true: the Bible says there is no witchcraft against God’s people, and no witch doctor can have an effect on the church.
How does he say you know it is time to speak up?

He says it is natural when you really experience something to talk about it, like someone into baseball talking about baseball. He says people into God and truth naturally speak truth, and you do not have to argue about it.
What does he say about avoiding heated arguments?

He says you can say your statement and shut up, since it takes two people to argue and if one is silent the argument ends. He says there is no sense in harping on it again and again; just say it and go on and let God do the work.

items.t: Except You Become as Little Children
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his series on stages of Christian growth and explains the child stage: those who are born again and now obey the Word. He reads Matthew 18:3, the disciples…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his series on stages of Christian growth and explains the child stage: those who are born again and now obey the Word. He reads Matthew 18:3, the disciples called “children” who still needed the meat of the Word, and 1 John 2 on the last time and the many antichrists. He then describes what a spiritual person looks like and what he believes the “little child shall lead them” of Isaiah 11 points to: a coming move of God led by grown, obedient believers.
What are the embryo and newborn stages of growth in the Christian life?

He says in the embryo stage people respond to hearing the Word: some reject or mock it and say it is “an inconvenient time,” while others believe, repent and follow Christ, “not a church, not an author, not an apostle.” In the newborn stage “their sins are forgiven” and they “desire the sincere milk of the Word.”
What are the embryo and newborn stages of growth in the Christian life?

So today we’re going to look at the child stage of growth from the Bible. Okay, remember the embryo stage is when they hear the Word. It’s how they responded when they heard the Word. And they rejected the Word, they mocked when they heard the Word and rejected the Word. They not only mocked, but some of them abused the Bible, Jesus, and His followers, mistreated, lambasted, put down, persecuted others. Said, “It’s not a convenient time, it’s an inconvenient time. Wait, I’m out to high school. Wait, I’m out of college. Wait till I’m done raising my family,” whatever. It’s an inconvenient time for me to follow God. “Okay, we’ll hear you again. I’ll hear you again, but you know, I’m not ready to make that decision.” And then others believed, repented, and followed Christ. The important word there is “follow.” They followed who? Christ. Not a church, not an author, not an apostle, but they followed Christ. The newborn stage, you remember, their sins are forgiven. They come to Jesus to learn from Him. So this is their growing effort: they desire the sincere milk of the Word, the Scriptures, to grow, which is repentance from dead works, faith toward God, not toward a denomination, not toward a minister, faith toward who? God. Repentance from works that brings the second death, destruction, the lake of fire. Baptisms: how many baptisms are there? Three: baptism of the Holy Ghost, baptism in water, and baptism into the body, and He chooses where you fit into the body, not you. He chooses.
What are the embryo and newborn stages of growth in the Christian life?

Hebrews 6:1-2: Therefore, leaving the discussion of the elementary principles of Christ, let us go on to perfection, not laying again the foundation of repentance from dead works and of faith toward God, of the doctrine of baptisms, of laying on of hands, of resurrection of the dead, and of eternal judgment. 1 Peter 2:2: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby,
What do baby Christians do: praise, doing good, and partnership?

He says babies are being built into “a spiritual house” looking for the presence of Jesus, and their main weapon is “the sacrifice of praise.” They also offer “the sacrifice of doing good” and “the sacrifice of partnership,” going to church “not to be entertained” but to reach the unbeliever and grow the unlearned, and they offer their bodies as a living sacrifice.
What do baby Christians do: praise, doing good, and partnership?

Okay, and then we have the resurrection of the dead and eternal judgment, after laying on of hands, and that is the second coming, resurrection and the eternal judgment is the second coming. And it’s baby doctrine. It’s kindergarten doctrine. It’s not mature doctrine and sound doctrine at all. They are also being built a spiritual house, inhabited by who? Jesus. Not a rock concert, not a dance company, not mimes. Those are all tools we can use, but these people are looking for the presence of Jesus. And presence of who? Jesus. Not Allah, not Joseph Smith, Jesus Christ. It’s very important that people understand this stuff. We read it, we don’t get it, but we got to get it. Okay, that’s their effort of growth. Their main weapon is the sacrifice of praise to still the enemy and avenger. They boast about Jesus, they sing about Him, they shout unto Him, they speak of His greatness, and that is the weapon that destroys the devouring enemy and the avenger. Hallelujah. So the babies are very strong in praising God, boasting of God, because that destroys their enemy. They have a tremendous tool. They also offer the sacrifice of doing good. They don’t want to do good. They may not want to get up on Monday morning and go to work, but it’s good. See, they might not want to clean the toilet in the house, but it’s good. It’s good. They may not want to love the lousiest member of the body of Christ, but it’s a good thing to do, so they do it. It’s a sacrifice. A sacrifice is something you don’t want to do. So see, babies go to church by a sacrifice, not a compelling. They’d rather sleep in on Sunday, they’d rather, you know, relax on Friday night or whenever their church services are, but it’s a good thing, so they do what is good. It’s a sacrifice. Partnership. The sacrifice of partnership, fellowship, koinonia. They go to church, not to be entertained, not to get a man and a woman to marry them, but that’s a good place to find one. They go to church for a partnership. Partnership to what? To reach the unbeliever and to grow the unlearned. Are you there? They don’t come to church just to get something. They come to church to get and to give, and they’re there to help the unlearned grow up. They’re there to help the unbeliever become a believer. That’s the partnership. And sadly, in America we don’t have a lot of partners. Why? We haven’t passed the newborn stage yet. You see, going to church is just something convenient for them, going to a Bible study is something convenient for them, or whatever. They do everything out of convenience. But a real born again person will hear the Word and respond to the Word in that area of growth. Could that be an amen? You see, we have a responsibility to the unlearned and the unbeliever. We have that responsibility. And then they offer their physical body a living sacrifice unto God. So they do get up in the morning, they tell that body what to do, they do lift their hands and praise God, they do get involved. See, they offer their bodies, their physical body, a living sacrifice for Christ.
What do baby Christians do: praise, doing good, and partnership?

1 Peter 2:5: you also, as living stones, are being built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood, to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ. Hebrews 13:15-16: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name. But do not forget to do good and to share, for with such sacrifices God is well pleased. Romans 12:1: I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service.
What weaknesses do baby Christians have, and how should the church treat them?

He says babies are “jealous, they argue and quarrel, they’re sectarian, they divide” because “they haven’t learned the Word yet,” and still struggle with the works of the flesh. He says “we don’t throw babies out of the house because they haven’t grown up yet,” that “our job is to help them grow up,” and that they are “tossed about by every wind of deceptive doctrine.”
What weaknesses do baby Christians have, and how should the church treat them?

Now, they have a weakness. Their weaknesses are they’re jealous, they argue and quarrel, they’re sectarian, they divide. “I’m a Baptist, I’m a Pentecostal, I’m a Catholic, I’m a this, I’m a that.” You see, they’re very sectarian. They’re weak in that. Why? Because they haven’t learned the Word yet. They haven’t developed spiritually yet. And we don’t throw babies out of the house because they haven’t grown up yet, have we? Yeah. Our job is to help them grow up. And so when a baby needs you, you give them attention that they need. They have problems in the flesh, the carnal, with sexual immorality, anger, hatred, intoxication, partying, profanity, heresies, selfishness, and rebellion. Those are all works of the flesh, those are what the people of the world do, and so a baby hasn’t conquered a lot of these things yet. And that’s our responsibility to help them what? Grow up. Not put them down. You recognize the problem and you help them grow through that problem. Now that’s a good place for a good amen. You see, we got to get the mindset that we come to church for a purpose, not just for ourself and our convenience. It is not convenient to fight a war, it is very inconvenient, and we are in a war. The Bible says, hallelujah, they are tossed about by every wind of deceptive doctrine. Any new book that comes out, babies, they’re tossed about. “Oh, this is the new thing.” And it’s our job to what? Bring them back to the soundness of the Scripture. Yes. Not separate and divide.
What weaknesses do baby Christians have, and how should the church treat them?
Ephesians 4:14: that we should no longer be children, tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in the cunning craftiness of deceitful plotting,
What is the child stage, and how do you know the Father? (1 John 2:13; 2:3)

He says the child stage is when people are not only born again but “now they’re obeying the Word of God.” He says knowing God is a relationship that births “a desire, a compelling that is birthed in us to obey,” so the proof that I know God is the desire to obey “because I met the Man.” He says every Christian came through these stages: “none of you went from zero to maturity on the night you accepted Christ.”
What is the child stage, and how do you know the Father? (1 John 2:13; 2:3)

Now, the child stage. In 1 John 2:13: “I write to you, little children, because you have known the Father.” Now this word is used in the New Testament from infant, John the Baptist and Jesus, to 12 years old. The girl that got delivered by Jesus was 12 years old and called a little child. And so it’s basically used from age two and up. The little children that got killed by Herod were to age two and down. Okay, so it’s basically used from age two and up. All right. Now, how do I know the Father? 1 John 2:3: “We do know that we know Him if we keep His commandments.” Now we know that knowing God is a relationship with Him, but in that relationship there is a desire, a compelling that is birthed in us to obey the one we’re in relationship with. It’s not just having an experience with Jesus. It’s because of that experience, from that experience, I am compelled to obey Him. And so the fruit and the proof that I know God is not my experience with Him by itself, it’s the desire and the compelling to obey Him because I met the Man. Amen. So this is the child stage. They have got past the baby stage. They not only now have an experience with God, they not only been born again, but now they’re obeying the Word of God. That’s the child stage. Ain’t that good? Hallelujah. And this is the problem in America: American Christians do not know what stage they’re at, and most of them are at baby stage, and they haven’t even conquered the baby doctrines yet, and it’s sad. And that’s why we as a church need to get the Word out to everybody. Could that be amen? We need to partner to get this word up. This definition, by the way, this definition clears up other Scriptures. When you understand when the Bible’s talking about this age group, that it’s talking in metaphors and parables, spiritual truths, of Christians that obey the Word of God. And we know in the embryo stage, that we’re in the embryo stage because we are responding different ways to the Word we hear. And that’s right, but when we obey in the embryo stage that Word and respond to it and repent, we get born again and we become new babies. Now, in the new baby stage we learn these baby doctrines and we start walking in them. We know the Father because there’s a desire to learn and a desire to walk in them. Amen. And so we know the child stage is when we obey and learn each stage’s word that we’re at. And folks, there’s nothing wrong with being in the embryo stage if that’s where you’re at. We just got to help them what? Get born again. There’s nothing wrong with being a newborn Christian if that’s where they’re at. Every one of us came through these stages. Am I right? None of you, I know the Bible, none of you went from zero to maturity on the night you accepted Christ. I know that’s not true. All of us went through these stages. We just didn’t know there were stages. In fact, the enemy tried to come in and destroy my faith in God because I hadn’t overcome things in my life. I’d been saved a week and I still had some sin in my life, and he comes in and tries to accuse me of being a phony and everything else. Any of you ever experienced that? And people will accuse me. But somewhere the Holy Ghost would say, “No.” I didn’t know the Word, but the Spirit of God would say, “No, give me time. You’ll get through these things.”
What is the child stage, and how do you know the Father? (1 John 2:13; 2:3)

1 John 2:13: I write to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, Because you have overcome the wicked one. I write to you, little children, Because you have known the Father. 1 John 2:3: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments.
What does “Except you become as little children” mean? (Matthew 18:3)

He says that as a “greenhorn minister” he illustrated childlikeness, but “it’s not a little kid He’s talking about.” He says it means getting to the stage where “you not only know God, but you obey His Word,” going through the embryo and newborn stages into the child stage, because the kingdom of God is “righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost.”
What does “Except you become as little children” mean? (Matthew 18:3)

So let me give a Scripture that’s cleared up by understanding what a little child is, that knows God through a relationship, through an experience, through being born again and obeying the Word. Matthew 18:3: “Except you be converted and become as little children, you will not enter the kingdom of God.” Now, when I was a greenhorn minister, I illustrated childlikeness. But when revelation come, it’s not a little kid He’s talking about. He’s talking about getting to the stage where you not only know God, but you obey His Word. “Unless you be converted,” changed, “and become as that child,” you get through the embryo, you get through the newborn stage and into the child stage, “you will not enter the kingdom of God.” You see how clear that makes it? And it’s backed up when the rich man came to Christ, the noble man. He said, “What must I do to inherit the kingdom of God,” in, eternal life I should say. He said, “What says the Scriptures?” And he said, well, he went through the Scriptures. “Okay, you do this and you will live.” See, it backs that up, the child stage. And see, the kingdom of God is righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost, and if you want the righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Ghost, you got to what? Get to the child stage.
What does “Except you become as little children” mean? (Matthew 18:3)

Matthew 18:3: and said, “Assuredly, I say to you, unless you are converted and become as little children, you will by no means enter the kingdom of heaven. Romans 14:17: for the kingdom of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in the Holy Spirit.
Why did Jesus call grown disciples “children” and ask if they had “meat”? (John 21:5; Luke 24:41)

He is coming to punish the wicked. There is a lake of fire. There is an eternal punishment, and we need to tremble at that word. But there’s also the message that something powerful is going to happen before that day arise. And look at this: “when He shall come to be glorified in His saints, and be admired in them that believe, in that day.” Now, we’re always talking about the God is coming for His saints, but folks, this verse says He’s coming in His saints. Did He come in His saints the first time He came? Yes. The day of Pentecost, out of their innermost being these rivers of life-giving water flowed. You see, He came, He died on the cross, and He came in. He said the Holy Spirit is with you but shall be what? In you. So He’s coming in them. And when He came in the apostles, they were transformed from people that were weak and quarreling and denying Christ and all the rest to a group of people that nothing could move them. He came in them, and so He is coming in His people in that end time period. There is a move of God coming in His church that will cause the Jews and the Muslims and other people to recognize the truth and come in, and there will be a great harvest. Hallelujah. Now that’s exciting.
What does 2 Thessalonians 1:7-10 say about Christ coming “in His saints”?

2 Thessalonians 1:7-10: and to give you who are troubled rest with us when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels, in flaming fire taking vengeance on those who do not know God, and on those who do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ. These shall be punished with everlasting destruction from the presence of the Lord and from the glory of His power, when He comes, in that Day, to be glorified in His saints and to be admired among all those who believe, because our testimony among you was believed. John 7:38: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.”
What does Jeremiah 33:7-9 promise, and what must believers do now?

He reads “I will build them as at the first,” says “the church is the Israel of God,” and that God’s people are believing lies, so “it’s somebody’s job to speak up and restore and recover God’s people.” He says “if He did it at the first, He is going to do it a second time,” and “we need God, and we need to grow,” with the Holy Ghost active in the church.
What does Jeremiah 33:7-9 promise, and what must believers do now?

Jeremiah 33:7: “I will cause the captivity of Judah and Israel to return.” We know that Judah, in the Scriptures, the real Jew is not one outwardly, and circumcision is not in the flesh, but a real Jew, Paul said, was one inwardly, and circumcision of the spirit, and that’s the church. Amen. And Israel, Paul said, we are the Israel of God. The church is the Israel of God. “I will cause the captivity of Judah.” Is God’s people in captivity right now? Yeah. They’re believing lies, and it’s somebody’s job to speak up and restore and recover God’s people. “I will build them as at the first.” You see, He came and He started building, and the apostles did a great job, and then, as the Bible says, there was a falling away. But in these last days we started seeing the restoration when Luther came on the scene, and it’s been going on, this restoration, for quite a few, long time. Are you there? Now listen to this. The church, Judah and Israel, this thing’s going to be built, this house that’s being built. “It will be a name of joy, praise, and honor before all nations, which shall hear all the good that I do unto them, and the nations shall fear and tremble.” Now I submit to you, has that ever happened since Jesus ascended, where the nations shook and was in fear because of what God was doing in His church? No. There’s no history of it. Did Jesus say every Scripture will be fulfilled? Yeah. So does there have to be something going to take place at this end of the age? Yes. If He did it at the first, He is going to do it a second time. And that’s what we got to be believing for, folks. We need God, and we need to grow. “The enemy comes in like a flood, the Spirit of the Lord will lift up a standard against him.” We need the Holy Ghost active in the church and in our lives. We can’t do this on human thinking, we can’t do this in human power. And God promised that the Holy Ghost would come and empower us and give us things to edify and build the church. That’s why tongues and interpretation are important, prophecy is important, healing and miracles are important, faith, discerning of spirits, wisdom and knowledge is important, coming from the Holy Ghost. It builds, it edifies, it never draws attention to itself, it always points toward Jesus.
What does Jeremiah 33:7-9 promise, and what must believers do now?

Jeremiah 33:7-9: And I will cause the captives of Judah and the captives of Israel to return, and will rebuild those places as at the first. I will cleanse them from all their iniquity by which they have sinned against Me, and I will pardon all their iniquities by which they have sinned and by which they have transgressed against Me. Then it shall be to Me a name of joy, a praise, and an honor before all nations of the earth, who shall hear all the good that I do to them; they shall fear and tremble for all the goodness and all the prosperity that I provide for it.’ Romans 2:28-29: For he is not a Jew who is one outwardly, nor is circumcision that which is outward in the flesh; but he is a Jew who is one inwardly; and circumcision is that of the heart, in the Spirit, not in the letter; whose praise is not from men but from God. Galatians 6:16: And as many as walk according to this rule, peace and mercy be upon them, and upon the Israel of God. Isaiah 59:19: So shall they fear The name of the LORD from the west, And His glory from the rising of the sun; When the enemy comes in like a flood, The Spirit of the LORD will lift up a standard against him.
What three baptisms does he list?
He lists “baptism of the Holy Ghost, baptism in water, and baptism into the body,” and says “He chooses where you fit into the body, not you.”
Why does he say babies in Christ go to church?

He says they go “not to be entertained,” but for partnership: “to reach the unbeliever and to grow the unlearned.” He says “they come to church to get and to give,” and that “sadly in America we don’t have a lot of partners.”
Why does he say baby Christians divide into groups?

He says they say “I’m a Baptist, I’m a Pentecostal, I’m a Catholic, I’m a this, I’m a that,” and are weak in that “because they haven’t learned the Word yet.” He says the church’s job is to help them grow up, not put them down.
What age does he say “little children” refers to in the New Testament?
He says the word is used from infants to 12 years old, so “it’s basically used from age two and up.”
Does he say Christians know what stage of growth they are at?
No. He says “American Christians do not know what stage they’re at, and most of them are at baby stage, and they haven’t even conquered the baby doctrines yet, and it’s sad.”
Is there anything wrong with being in the embryo or newborn stage?
No. He says “there’s nothing wrong with being in the embryo stage if that’s where you’re at,” or a newborn Christian, but “we just got to help them” get born again and grow.
What is the difference between the milk and the meat of the Word?

He says “there is the milk of the Word and there is the meat of the Word,” and that the disciples were called children because they could not yet handle the meat. He says meat starts in the child stage and goes on to the next stages.
Why does he call the baptism of the Holy Ghost “baby doctrine”?
He says, “We’ve been baptized in the Holy Ghost, hallelujah. Okay, grow up. Say baptism of Holy Ghost is baby doctrine. Grow up. It’s there to help you grow up.”
Does he say one Antichrist is coming?
No. He says “there are many antichrists, many opponents,” that “the last time” began long ago, and that there is “no big superhuman like that movie.”
How does he say you can tell who is an antichrist?
He reads, “Who is a liar but he that denies that Jesus is the Christ?” and says “the person that denies that Jesus is the Christ is antichrist,” a “very plain definition.”
Does he say he hates people who deny Jesus is God?
No. He says “I’m not preaching hatred, I’m preaching truth” and “I don’t hate anybody. My job is to tell the truth.”
Can anyone know how long this age will last?
No. He says “nobody knows how long this age is going to go on,” and that people who say they know are lying because “the Bible says nobody knows.”
What does he say grace is?
He says “we’ve taken this grace thing and just distorted it horribly. Grace is the divine enablement of God,” which was upon Jesus, empowering Him as He grew in grace, wisdom and spirit.
What does he say it means that Christ is coming “in His saints”?

He says we are always told that He is coming for His saints, but the verse says He is coming in them. He says He came into the apostles at Pentecost and transformed them, and “so He is coming in His people in that end time period.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Ezekiel 18, the “laws of life and death,” and answers the charge that “the way of the Lord is not fair.” He teaches that each person is judged by his own…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Ezekiel 18, the “laws of life and death,” and answers the charge that “the way of the Lord is not fair.” He teaches that each person is judged by his own ways, that God takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and that God offers a new heart, mind and spirit. He then turns to Ezekiel 33 and the watchman, and calls the church to speak what God said to speak.
What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?

He says he is going to Ezekiel 18 and 33 to look at “the laws of life and the laws of death.” He reads Ezekiel 18:20, “the soul that sins it shall die,” and says “A law is a statement that has a punishment,” adding that “the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father.”
What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?

And today we’re going to be going to Ezekiel chapters 18 and chapters 33 and we’re going to be looking at the laws of life and the laws of death. Now Ezekiel was a prophet after the first captivity. He was carried away captive about 25 years of age and uh in the in the sixth year of captivity, 31 years of age, he started prophesying. Now he’s several hundred miles away from Jeremiah who is speaking the same things. And that’s very important for you to know. These two are not connected with each other at all. Ezekiel was not even called to prophesy. Until the sixth year of the captivity. Jeremiah had already been prophesying for quite a while. All right? And though Ezekiel is hundreds of miles away in Babylon, he is saying the same thing that Jeremiah is talking about. And it’s very important for you to know that. You see, God is a supernatural God and he does supernatural things. All right? Uh in Ezekiel 18:20 he starts out saying the soul that sins it shall die. Now that’s a law. The soul that sins it shall die. A law is a statement that has a punishment. All right? If you violate that law, there is a payment to pay. And so the person that sins, soul is just a person that sins, it shall die. All right? Now, that’s the first thing. Number two, the son shall not bear the iniquity of the father. He says you can’t blame the son or punish the son for the father’s bad doing. Okay. Number three, nor shall the father bear the iniquity of the son. You see, my sons go out in sin and they’re of age. You know, you can’t blame me. I did my job. They just didn’t listen.
What are the laws of life and death in Ezekiel 18?

Ezekiel 18:20: The soul who sins shall die. The son shall not bear the guilt of the father, nor the father bear the guilt of the son. The righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon himself.
Is a sinful thought the same as a sin?

He says the wicked who turn from “committed sin” will live, and stresses “It’s not sins in your mind.” He says “Nowhere in the Bible was anyone stoned for thinking sexual immorality,” and that “You have to commit it.”
Is a sinful thought the same as a sin?

Number four, the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon him, and the wickedness of the wicked shall be upon him. Now, that sounds logical. If a guy does right, that he’s going to get the rewards of right. If the guy does wrong, he’s going to get the rewards of wrong. Amen. But if the wicked will turn, repent, turn from all his committed sins. Now, it’s important you understand that it’s committed sin. It’s not sins in your mind. It’s not, you know, everybody uses this thing. In fact, I just heard it this morning. Whosoever looketh a woman to lust after her has committed adultery already within his heart. So the Piers Morgan says, “You got to stone that person.” These people on TV and these radio and TV host and and anchor people, they they they get into areas they know nothing about. Nowhere in the Bible was anyone stoned for thinking sexual immorality. Never. No one was ever stoned for thinking about stealing something. You have to commit it. You have to do it. All right. But if the wicked see the evil person will turn from those committed sins, keep my statutes. Do that which is lawful and right, he shall live.
Is a sinful thought the same as a sin?

Ezekiel 18:21: “But if a wicked man turns from all his sins which he has committed, keeps all My statutes, and does what is lawful and right, he shall surely live; he shall not die. Matthew 5:28: But I say to you that whoever looks at a woman to lust for her has already committed adultery with her in his heart.
What two lives does the Bible promise?

He says the law of life is “doing what’s right,” and “Even if I’ve messed up, I can turn.” He says the Bible promises “two lives,” eternal life and “the life that now is,” and that he doesn’t “want to wait to go to heaven to enjoy life.”
What two lives does the Bible promise?

Truly live. He shall not die. That’s the laws of sin and death. Even if I’ve messed up, I can turn and I will not be remembered for my past sins anymore. It’s just doing what’s right is the law of life. The law of life is doing what’s right. And when you go to the New Testament, the New Testament backs it up. Jesus backs it up. So that’s the laws of life and death. There are two lives in the Bible. Eternal life and the life that now is 2 Timothy 4:8. Godliness is profitable unto all things, having promise of the life that now is and that which is to come. I don’t know about you, but I don’t want to wait to go to heaven to enjoy life. And the Bible promises two lives. You will be blessed here on this earth. Say the laws of life and when you die, you will inherit eternal life. How many want God to bless you in this life? Yes. And how many are thankful there’s nowhere to go but eternity when you die? Hallelujah. With him. Now we’re going to move on here in Ezekiel 18 14-18 number six. If he a wicked father, he’s talking about a wicked father a son.
What two lives does the Bible promise?
1 Timothy 4:8: For bodily exercise profits a little, but godliness is profitable for all things, having promise of the life that now is and of that which is to come.
Do children pay for their parents’ sins?

He says “the children pay a big price for sinning parents,” but the son who sees his father’s sins and repents “shall not die for the iniquity of his father. He shall live.” He adds that God is not “up there” eager to condemn anyone, and asks whether the wicked should die and not “return from his wicked ways and live.”
Do children pay for their parents’ sins?

Oh, that’s cut off. Wow. That sees all his father’s sins. Okay. This son sees dad being bad, mom being bad, and the son is paying a big price. How many know the children pay a big price for sinning parents? Absolutely. They do. We put kids through hell on earth because us adults act like kids and we do bad things. Okay. He sees all that the parents have done. He considers it. He [unclear] it. He rationalizes it and does not [unclear] such like, but executes God’s judgments, walks in God’s statutes. He shall not die for the iniquity of his father. He shall live. See it. Instead of blaming or following the bad parents, these guys are repenting from their bad behavior. And it works. The one that repents and turns and does right shall live. God will bless you in this life and in the life to come. Now verse 23, number seven. Have I any pleasure delight in the wicked that they should die and not return from his wicked ways and live? God is just reminding us. He’s not up there saying, “Oh boy, I get to get that one. That one’s a Oh, hallelujah. Boy, get to put that one in hell. Okay, who’s next here?” No.
Do children pay for their parents’ sins?

Ezekiel 18:14-18: “If, however, he begets a son Who sees all the sins which his father has done, And considers but does not do likewise; Who has not eaten on the mountains, Nor lifted his eyes to the idols of the house of Israel, Nor defiled his neighbor’s wife; Has not oppressed anyone, Nor withheld a pledge, Nor robbed by violence, But has given his bread to the hungry And covered the naked with clothing; Who has withdrawn his hand from the poor And not received usury or increase, But has executed My judgments And walked in My statutes— He shall not die for the iniquity of his father; He shall surely live! “As for his father, Because he cruelly oppressed, Robbed his brother by violence, And did what is not good among his people, Behold, he shall die for his iniquity. Ezekiel 18:23: Do I have any pleasure at all that the wicked should die?” says the Lord GOD, “and not that he should turn from his ways and live?
Does God want the wicked to die, and will he still judge them?

He says God “gets no delight in you dying. It’s totally your choice,” but that does not mean he will not judge sin: “He is a just God and he is a judge.” He says that if you do wrong, “You know what you’re doing,” whether by conscience or God’s word.
Does God want the wicked to die, and will he still judge them?

God has no pleasure. He gets no delight in you dying. It’s totally your choice. But because just because he doesn’t delight in the death of the wicked does not mean he will not judge you and put you in an eternal lake of fire for your sins. He will do that. He is a just God and he is a judge. Number eight verse 24. When the righteous man turns from his righteousness and commits iniquities of the wicked man, shall he live? Whoa. All his righteousness he has done shall not be mentioned. Won’t even be brought up in court.
If a righteous person turns back to sin, do his past good works count?

He reads Ezekiel 18:24 and says “All his righteousness he has done shall not be mentioned.” He uses Judas as his example: he preached, laid hands on the sick and cast out demons, but when he turned and betrayed Christ “all those goodies were forgotten.”
If a righteous person turns back to sin, do his past good works count?

The heaven’s court won’t even be brought up. And I told you, I’ve seen a vision of that judgment and nobody’s saying anything because they knew they were wrong when they did it. They have no answer. You know what you’re doing when you do wrong, whether it’s by the conscience or God’s word. In his trespass, violation of the law, and sin, shall he die. Now, a good example of that is Judas. You see, Judas followed Christ. Judas preached the gospel. People got saved. Judas laid hands on people and they got healed. Judas cast out demons. All those are right good works, aren’t they? But when Judas turned and let Satan enter into him and betrayed Christ, all those goodies were forgotten. And he’s burning in hell today. Are you there? What’s fair? What’s not fair? I’m always hearing people, well, this isn’t fair, fair, fair, fair, fair. Ezekiel 18:29. Yet the house of Israel says, the way of the Lord is not fair. It’s not fair. I was good for 60 years my life, and I turned bad for the last three, and I’m going to hell.
If a righteous person turns back to sin, do his past good works count?

Ezekiel 18:24: “But when a righteous man turns away from his righteousness and commits iniquity, and does according to all the abominations that the wicked man does, shall he live? All the righteousness which he has done shall not be remembered; because of the unfaithfulness of which he is guilty and the sin which he has committed, because of them he shall die. Ezekiel 18:29: Yet the house of Israel says, ‘The way of the Lord is not fair.’ O house of Israel, is it not My ways which are fair, and your ways which are not fair?
Does God weigh good deeds against bad deeds, and is his way fair?

He says some think “my good things should have outweighed my bad things,” but God says “I will judge you … Everyone according to his ways.” He says “Not grace, not faith, not the church I attend, not helping the poor, not tithing, none of those things even come into the equation.”
Does God weigh good deeds against bad deeds, and is his way fair?

That’s not fair. I should be weighed in a balance and my good things should have outweighed my bad things like some people believe. How many of you know that? Therefore, what does therefore mean? For this reason. So, when we see the word therefore, we got to consider what it’s there for. Okay. Why is the word therefore therefore? For this reason, I will judge you, oh house of Israel. What reason? Everyone according to his ways, says the Lord God. Not grace, not faith, not the church I attend, not helping the poor, not tithing, none of those things even come into the equation.
Does God weigh good deeds against bad deeds, and is his way fair?

Ezekiel 18:30: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways,” says the Lord GOD. “Repent, and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin.
What does it mean to repent and cast away transgressions?

He says what’s fair is to “repent,” and “Turn from your evil ways so that iniquity would not be your ruin.” He says to cast away “all committed transgressions,” and if you pick one up again, “Cast it away again.”
What does it mean to repent and cast away transgressions?

What’s fair? Number three, repent. That’s what’s fair. Turn from your evil ways so that iniquity would not be your ruin. Verse 31, cast from you. Number four, all committed transgressions. There’s that word again. Say that word. So I cast away my iniquities, you know, and then I mess up and pick up one here and there, and then I got to what? Cast it away again. Get yourselves a new heart. Here is a tremendous part of this new covenant. We’re going to show you it’s in the new covenant next week. And then we’re going to show you how to get a part of the new covenant that you deserve in this life. All right? Get yourselves a new heart.
What does it mean to repent and cast away transgressions?

Ezekiel 18:30-31: “Therefore I will judge you, O house of Israel, every one according to his ways,” says the Lord GOD. “Repent, and turn from all your transgressions, so that iniquity will not be your ruin. Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel?
What does it mean to get a new heart, a new mind and a new spirit?

He says the heart is “Mind, will, and the emotions,” so a new heart is “a new way of thinking” and responding to emotions. He says that if you only accept salvation, grace and faith “you’re missing out on one of the most important parts of the new covenant,” and that you also need “a spirit that connects with God’s spirit.”
What does it mean to get a new heart, a new mind and a new spirit?

Now, what’s the heart? Mind, will, and the emotions. That’s the center part of man, the mind, the intellect. Get yourself a new way of thinking. Get yourself a new way of responding to emotions. How many can say, “Boy, I I need some help in my emotions.” A new heart. And so he’s telling us to what? Get it. So if you only accept salvation and grace and faith, you’re missing out on one of the most important parts of the new covenant. He promised you, as we will see next week, a new mind. Doesn’t the New Testament say, “If any man be in Christ, he’s a new creature.” Well, what do you think that means? Old things are what? Passed away. Behold, all things are new. What do you think that starts? A new mind. And if preachers don’t preach the word, how you going to get a new mind? If you don’t write, read, and study the word, how you going to get a new mind? And a new spirit. How many of you know you’re a three-part being? Yeah. Body, soul, and spirit. You have a physical body, you have a soul. Again, the word soul there is, the emotions, the intellect, and the will. And then you have a spirit. There is a spirit living in you. That when this body dies, the spirit continues. And so, you need a new spirit. You need a spirit that connects with God’s spirit.
What does it mean to get a new heart, a new mind and a new spirit?

Ezekiel 18:31: Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel? 2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.
Can God’s people die? Is “once saved always saved” true?

He says “house of Israel” is not Babylon or sinners but “God’s people,” and asks “Can God’s people die? Yeah.” He says of “once saved always saved,” “Come on. Common sense tells you,” and that God “takes no pleasure in punishing people. It’s just he has to do it because it’s the law.”
Can God’s people die? Is “once saved always saved” true?

Isn’t this good? See, these are tremendous promises. And and we fool around with nonsense when we got tremendous, exceedingly great and precious promises. For why should you die, oh house of Israel? Now, house of Israel is not talking about Babylon. It’s not talking about sinners and wicked people. It’s talking about what? God’s people. Can God’s people die? Yeah. This once saved always saved. Come on. Common sense tells you. For I have not no pleasure again in the death of the one who dies, says the Lord. Therefore, turn and live. He reminds us again. He takes no pleasure in punishing people. It’s just he has to do it because it’s the law. Now, we’re going to go to Ezekiel 33 and Ezekiel 3 and we’re going to look at the law of the watchman.
Can God’s people die? Is “once saved always saved” true?

Ezekiel 18:31-32: Cast away from you all the transgressions which you have committed, and get yourselves a new heart and a new spirit. For why should you die, O house of Israel? For I have no pleasure in the death of one who dies,” says the Lord GOD. “Therefore turn and live!”
What is the law of the watchman in Ezekiel 33?

He says the watchman stood on the wall and “would blow the horn” if enemies were coming. He says God made Ezekiel a watchman “to alert people, warn people,” that the message was “Repent,” and that “This church has a responsibility.”
What is the law of the watchman in Ezekiel 33?

The law of the watchman. The watchman was the guy that they put up on the wall and he was to look out and make sure that no enemies were coming, no armies were coming. And if they did, then he would blow the horn. I was going to bring my ram’s horn and do that and I forgot. We’re going to look at the law of the watchman. Now, you better listen closely. All right? Because you have a responsibility. This church has a responsibility. Christianity isn’t just Disneyland. I’ve made you a watchman to the house of Israel. Now he’s talking to Ezekiel. I’ve made you a watchman. Okay. You’re to alert people. I’ve chosen you to alert people, warn people, you know, of the coming destruction. You shall hear a word from what? My mouth. And warn them for me. Tell them what I’m saying. And what was the message to Ezekiel? Repent. He’s telling the people to repent. That is the message. What was Jesus’s first message? Repent and believe the gospel. Repent. What was John the Baptist’s message? Repent. What was the apostles message on the day of Pentecost? Repent. Duh. Turn from your sins. When I say to the wicked, “You shall surely die.” All right.
What is the law of the watchman in Ezekiel 33?

Ezekiel 33:7-9: “So you, son of man: I have made you a watchman for the house of Israel; therefore you shall hear a word from My mouth and warn them for Me. When I say to the wicked, ‘O wicked man, you shall surely die!’ and you do not speak to warn the wicked from his way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity; but his blood I will require at your hand. Nevertheless if you warn the wicked to turn from his way, and he does not turn from his way, he shall die in his iniquity; but you have delivered your soul.
What happens if we stay silent and do not warn people?

He says if you don’t speak to warn the wicked, “that wicked man shall die in his iniquity,” and says “Most American Christians just don’t care if the guy next door is going to hell or not.” On “his blood will I require at your hand,” he says the Hebrew is “seek” and “inquire,” and God will ask, “Why didn’t you speak up?”
What happens if we stay silent and do not warn people?

And that’s what exactly we heard in Ezekiel, wasn’t it? Isn’t that what John the Baptist said? Isn’t that what Jesus said? Yeah. You’re going to die. You’re going to pay a price for your sins, for being wicked if you do not speak. See the these these people say, “Well, I don’t wear my Christianity on my sleeve.” Well, you better be wearing it somewhere where people can see it. If you don’t speak silent, silent saints to warn the wicked from his wicked way, that wicked man shall die in his iniquity. That guy’s going to die. You don’t care. Most American Christians just don’t care if the guy next door is going to hell or not. They’re just concerned about themselves. I’m not going to speak up and rock the boat.
