Numbers 11:4: Now the mixed multitude who were among them yielded to intense craving; so the children of Israel also wept again and said: “Who will give us meat to eat?
How do emotions lead people to idolatry, as with the golden calf?

He says that after deliverance from the flesh, another hindrance is emotions: in Exodus 32:1 the people asked Aaron to “make us gods” while “all these emotions were flooding them.” He says Aaron tried to mix the Lord with idol worship, and “a lot of people are doing that today. They’re mixing in their own message with the message of Christ.”
How do emotions lead people to idolatry, as with the golden calf?

great, and the flesh is going to want to say, “I want to do this, I want to do that, I want to go back to what we did before.” And it has nothing to do with Satan, it’s our flesh. So we need deliverance from our flesh, and Christ has the power to do that too. You see, he has the power to deliver us from Satan, from, from enemies, from all these things, and our flesh, and he’s got the power. He doesn’t just save you from hell, he has the power. Let’s continue. Another hindrance: emotions. Exodus 32:1, “The people gathered themselves together unto Aaron and said unto them, ‘Up, get up, make us gods.’” And the reasoning behind this was because they said, “We don’t know where this man Moses is. This man, who, you know,” of course they, they distance themselves from him. This man, this man, you know, he was their family, he was part of the Levites. “Oh, this man, that church, I don’t want to go to that church, that church is just, I don’t know what’s going on with them. That pastor.” You know, we distance ourselves, so then we just, boom, hit him. And they, they got concerned and worried and they were unsure and uncertain and all these emotions were flooding them, so they decide to change things. “Go up and make us gods.” So Aaron just says, “Okay, give me your gold and I’ll make you a god.” He made a calf. I, hello, what is he thinking? And they were living it up again, dancing, stripping naked, yeah, you read it, drinking, partying, worship, worshiping the idol. Here God had just parted the Red Sea. I know, understand that they walked through the ocean. The army is destroyed. None of them were killed. I mean, come on, talk about the timing. There, come on. And you’re just going to follow the mixed multitude to worship gods, because they had gods in Egypt, so they want to, you know, seek your friend, whatever the people want. No. See, Moses, I’m sorry, Aaron, he made the god, and he said, “Tomorrow we’re, we’re going to have a feast to the Lord.” You see, he was trying to mix, he was trying to mix in the Lord and sin. He was trying to mix in wrong teaching, stuff that was just totally wrong. You don’t worship idols, and he was trying to mix in God and the Lord. And you see, a lot of people are doing that today. They’re mixing in their own message with the message of Christ, and it’s very conflicting, it’s very confusing. It’s just like Saul, if you remember the story, when he really, when, when God confronted him, he confronted him because he decided to sacrifice before Samuel got there. He took things into his own hands. He said, “Uh, there’s, you know, Samuel’s not here, there’s a delay, so I’m going to go outside of the pattern and do it my own way. I’m going to make up my own standard, I’m going to make up my own way of doing it, and I’m going to follow that.” You see, you can’t do that. You can’t just start serving [unclear], you can’t just start going outside of the pattern. We got to keep following the pattern. We can’t mix in our own patterns with God’s
How do emotions lead people to idolatry, as with the golden calf?

Exodus 32:1: Now when the people saw that Moses delayed coming down from the mountain, the people gathered together to Aaron, and said to him, “Come, make us gods that shall go before us; for as for this Moses, the man who brought us up out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.”
What does fear do, and where does deliverance come from?

He says that when ten of the twelve gave an evil report in Numbers 13:32, the people wept and wanted to go back to Egypt. He says “we have to confront the kingdom of darkness,” and that people do not say they will serve Satan: “They just say” they are going to go back. He ends with Jonah 2:9, “Salvation is of the Lord,” and “we need deliverance from our fears, our flesh, our emotions.”
What does fear do, and where does deliverance come from?

pattern. And of course, God had taken them all this way to the Promised Land. And we know that an evil report came in Numbers 13:32 regarding the Promised Land. Ten of the twelve that came back brought an evil report. Of course, Joshua and Caleb said, “No, you guys are totally wrong.” And the people begin to fear, they wept all night. Oh my gosh. And they started to say, “Let us make a captain and go back to Egypt,” cuz they were afraid. And we’ve been challenged to reach people with the gospel, and I’ll tell you, I’m afraid, but we can’t, you can’t turn back. There’s people that need to be reached, there’s an enemy that needs to be destroyed. They were afraid of the, the giants, they were afraid of the people, they didn’t want to confront them, and we have to confront the kingdom of darkness. We have to confront that influential kingdom of darkness. And you see, these people totally turn and said, “I’m going to go back to sin, I’m going to go back to the slavery. I don’t want to build the kingdom of God, I want to build the kingdom of darkness.” And you don’t say it like that, of course. People don’t say, “I’m going to serve Satan.” People don’t say, “I’m going to serve the kingdom of darkness.” They just say, “I’m going to go back.” And all the congregation said to stone Joshua and Caleb. You see here, you know, maybe at this point, when they wept all night, you know, maybe they could call on God right there and say, “God, explain this to us. God, help us.” You know, maybe right there they could have still went into the Promised Land. Maybe the threat, even when they said, “Let us make a captain and return,” you know, just the threat. But you see, right here, all the congregation said to stone Joshua and Caleb, God showed up and he said, “Get out of here.” He, he judged them, he, he was going to wipe them out. He, he just, he couldn’t stand that. In Jonah 2:9 it says, “Salvation is of the Lord.” And you see, we need to be saved. We need deliverance from Satan, we need deliverance from sin and its hold in our lives, and we need deliverance from our fears, our flesh, our emotions. You know, those emotions, you know, it’s not bad to have emotions, but when your emotions cause you to do things that are wrong against God’s word, against your family, you got a problem. And you see, salvation, deliverance is from Jesus Christ.
What does fear do, and where does deliverance come from?

Numbers 13:32: And they gave the children of Israel a bad report of the land which they had spied out, saying, “The land through which we have gone as spies is a land that devours its inhabitants, and all the people whom we saw in it are men of great stature. Jonah 2:9: But I will sacrifice to You With the voice of thanksgiving; I will pay what I have vowed. Salvation is of the LORD.”
Why does he begin with a story about a baby being born?
He describes the worry of the nine months and says “I was just glad they came out okay after all that.” He uses it to say a baby either is born and lives or dies, and the same is true spiritually.
How does he say a person is “conceived” spiritually?
He says some people, when they hear God’s word, “it triggers a conception, and they begin to grow,” and the church continues that growth until they decide to accept Christ.
Does he say God wants anyone to go to hell?
No. He says “God doesn’t want any babies dying,” and that it happens “when we don’t accept him and let him birth us.”
Why does he say Jesus is the only one who can pay for sin?
He says “the payment for your sin is death. Jesus Christ is the only one that has the power to pay for your sin,” and that he is “the only one that went down into hell, and hell couldn’t stand him.”
What does he mean by “the milk of the word”?
He says it is “the basic understanding”: you “read the Gospels and find out about the death, burial, and resurrection of Christ,” which is “getting saved, faith, believing in God.”
What does he say about going to church every week?
He says “It was a habit to be in the house of God on Sundays,” and asks, “what about Jesus’s custom?” He says “we need to be here at church.”
What does he say about babies and praise in the Psalms?
He quotes “out of the mouths of babies” God has ordained praise to still the enemy, and says “This word means more than that.” He concludes that when we come to church “there’s no sitting down.”
How did praising God help him as a new believer?
He says “As a new believer, I was always praising God,” that he sang with all his heart whoever was next to him, and “that helped me in my life.”
What does he say about being embarrassed when we praise God?
He says “it may be embarrassing,” but “That’s the great thing about kids,” who don’t care. For a teenager or adult with cares, “you just got to get rid of it.”
What does he say the “yoke of bondage” is?
He says Galatians 5:1 is “the New Testament talking about, don’t be entangled with the yoke of bondage again, the yoke of sin,” and that “Sin is going to put you through the ringer.”
What does he say children learn from their parents?
He says “they’re going to copy the things that I do, no matter if they want to or not,” and later have to decide whether to reject what they saw.
What does he say about losing friends when you follow Christ?
He says “it’s very difficult when friends don’t decide to follow Christ,” and that they may ask you “to leave, or they’re not going to associate with you anymore.”
What does he say happened at the Red Sea?
He says “God destroyed the armies of Pharaoh,” who followed the Israelites after “He parted the Red Sea, the Israelites walked through it.”
What does he say Luke 10:19 shows about power?
He quotes “Behold, I give you power to tread upon scorpions and serpents,” and says “He has the power to deliver us from sin.”
What does he say about Saul sacrificing before Samuel arrived?
He says Saul “took things into his own hands” and went “outside of the pattern,” and that “We got to keep following the pattern.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his series on the stages of Christian growth with the father stage of 1 John 2:13-14: fathers know Him who was from the beginning. He lays out John 1 and…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer continues his series on the stages of Christian growth with the father stage of 1 John 2:13-14: fathers know Him who was from the beginning. He lays out John 1 and Genesis 1 as proof that Jesus is God, then compares the characteristics of a natural father and a spiritual father: not provoking children, training and cherishing them, birthing others through the Word, being an example, and disciplining as God does in Hebrews 12. He closes with the meat of the Word, righteousness, and what it means to practice it.
Who are the “fathers” in 1 John 2:13-14, and what does it mean that they know Him from the beginning?

He says the Bible repeats itself in 1 John 2:13-14 because “when the Bible repeats itself, it means it’s important.” He says fathers “not only understand with the mind, but they have a personal relationship and they keep His commandments,” and that they understand Jesus “existed at the beginning” and “was God from the very beginning of the world.”
Who are the “fathers” in 1 John 2:13-14, and what does it mean that they know Him from the beginning?

In 1 John 2:13 and 14 he says the same thing. He repeats himself, and when the Bible repeats itself, it means it’s important. “I write unto you, fathers, because you have known Him from the beginning.” Now we know from past sessions that the word “know” means to understand, okay, to be aware of, to recognize something. We recognize God, we get knowledge of God, but we also know from the Bible that knowing God is an intimate relationship. It’s used as an intimate, personal relationship. And we also know that by this do you know Him: if you keep His commandments. So the fathers know Him. They not only understand with the mind, but they have a personal relationship and they keep His commandments. That is from the beginning. Now here Paul, John is saying that Jesus was at the beginning. Okay, He wasn’t just, when He came, was born of a virgin, but He existed at the beginning, and fathers understand that. They have a personal encounter with that, and they obey that Jesus that was at the beginning. So fathers know Jesus was God. See, the father stage clearly understands that Jesus was God from the very beginning of the world. All right, John chapter 1, verse 1 through 14. We find in John 1:1 through 14 that “in the beginning was the Word.” Now John is going to lay this out very clearly: “In the beginning was the Word, the Word was with God.”
Who are the “fathers” in 1 John 2:13-14, and what does it mean that they know Him from the beginning?

1 John 2:13-14: I write to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, Because you have overcome the wicked one. I write to you, little children, Because you have known the Father. I have written to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, Because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, And you have overcome the wicked one.
What does John 1:1-14 teach about Jesus as the Word, Creator and Light?

He says John 1 shows “the Word was with God” and “the Word was God,” that “Jesus created the world,” and “if the Word is Jesus Christ, then Jesus is the Word, Jesus is God.” He offers a “spiritual brain teaser” about light on the first day before the sun, pointing to verses where God and Jesus are light: “Jesus was at the beginning with God, and Jesus was what? Light.”
What does John 1:1-14 teach about Jesus as the Word, Creator and Light?

You see, at the beginning of time in Genesis, the Word was with God, but also “the Word was God.” Now this is very important. Now this chapter threw me for quite a few years till I grew in the Word, but it’s very clear. “The same was in the beginning with God.” So God was with God. You got it? The same, the Word was with God, the Word was God, the same, the Word, the God was in the beginning with God. So God was with who? God. He said, well, you have to be a father to understand that. See, you got to get past the little baby doctrines and get into the richness of the Bible. All right, now let’s keep going. “All things were made by Him,” the Word, God, “and without Him was not anything made.” He goes on to say the world was made by Him. So John here emphasizes that Jesus created the world, created everything, and without Him nothing was made that was made, and the Word was God. Number five: “In Him was life, and the life was the light of men.” In Him was life, and that life was the light of men. Now I’m going to throw a few teasers at you, for those of you who are Bible students. The atheists, the humanists, the liberals, our opponents, all say that the Bible contradicts itself, and one of the places they say that it contradicts itself is God said, “Let there be light” on the first day, and there was light, but the sun and the moon was not created till the fourth day. So let me just throw out a little spiritual brain teaser to you. In Jesus was life, and that life was the light of men. Matthew 17:2: Jesus was transfigured before them, and “His face did shine as the sun, and His raiment white as the light.” 1 Timothy 6:16: the Lord Jesus Christ “dwelling in the light which no man can approach unto.” 1 John 1:5: “God is light, and in Him is no darkness at all.” Psalm 104:2: God “covers Himself with light as with a garment, and stretches out the heavens like a curtain.” Revelation 21:23: the city, the heavenly Jerusalem, the bride, “has no need of the sun, neither of the moon, to shine in it, for the glory of God lights it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” Paul, on the road to Damascus, when he encountered Jesus, he encountered a great light. So when God said, “Let there be light,” and the sun was not created till the day before, we have a scriptural reference for light, because Jesus was at the beginning with God, and Jesus was what? Light. Just something for you to think on. See, human intellect cannot understand these things. All right, now we’ll get back to the kindergarten stage and continue. “The Word was made flesh and dwelt amongst us, and we beheld His glory, as of the only begotten Son of God, full of grace and truth.” And John the Baptist bore witness of Him. So clearly it is talking about the Word, who is Jesus Christ. So if the Word is Jesus Christ, then Jesus is the Word, Jesus is God, and fathers understand that. They’re not confused at all. Hallelujah. Now, Jesus from the beginning: is it true that back in Genesis I can find Jesus? All right, in Genesis chapter 1 you’re going to find the God four involved in creation. How many? Four. What are you used to? Three. But see, John very clearly brings out that the Word is also God. Have I got your minds thinking?
What does John 1:1-14 teach about Jesus as the Word, Creator and Light?

John 1:1-14: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. He was in the beginning with God. All things were made through Him, and without Him nothing was made that was made. In Him was life, and the life was the light of men. And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not comprehend it. There was a man sent from God, whose name was John. This man came for a witness, to bear witness of the Light, that all through him might believe. He was not that Light, but was sent to bear witness of that Light. That was the true Light which gives light to every man coming into the world. He was in the world, and the world was made through Him, and the world did not know Him. He came to His own, and His own did not receive Him. But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name: who were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God. And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth. Matthew 17:2: and He was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun, and His clothes became as white as the light. 1 Timothy 6:16: who alone has immortality, dwelling in unapproachable light, whom no man has seen or can see, to whom be honor and everlasting power. Amen. 1 John 1:5: This is the message which we have heard from Him and declare to you, that God is light and in Him is no darkness at all. Psalm 104:2: Who cover Yourself with light as with a garment, Who stretch out the heavens like a curtain. Revelation 21:23: The city had no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illuminated it. The Lamb is its light.
Do we find God, the Spirit and the Word in Genesis 1, and was Jesus always God’s plan?

He says Genesis 1 shows God, “the Spirit of God,” and the Word (“God said”) involved in creation, and that God spoke “let us” in the plural. He says God “never had a plan B”: “He had one plan the whole time, and that was Jesus Christ, reconciling people back to God,” and describes “one God doing things with four different explanations.”
Do we find God, the Spirit and the Word in Genesis 1, and was Jesus always God’s plan?

Now, is it true? And you know me, I always go back to see if what God says is true back there. So let’s go to Genesis chapter 1, and we find the first thing involved is God. “In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth.” We got it colored in blue so that you know everything is related to Him. Verse 2, we have the Spirit, the second part, the second one involved in the creation: “The Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.” Okay, and see, God continues His truth all throughout the Bible, and so it’s important that we understand it was set at the beginning. All right, so we have God and the Spirit, and then we have the Word. Verse 3: “God said.” God spoke, and this is the power of God. It’s in His spoken Word. God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. See, when God said, Jesus said, who is God, “For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whosoever believes on Him shall not perish but have everlasting life.” Just like when He said, “Let there be light,” and there was light. When God speaks something, He backs it up, and if you believe, you will not perish. See, just like He said, “I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh.” We know what His spoken word is. He accomplishes it, and you can have the infilling, the baptism of the Holy Spirit, because God backs up His spoken Word. Hallelujah. Now we know it is the printed Word, but it was only printed because He what? Spoke it. Yes, it’s that spoken Word, and you can have confidence that that Word is God. See, that Bible is Jesus. You can’t separate Jesus in the Bible. And then we have Jesus down there in verse 26: “Let us,” plural, “make man in our image,” plural, “and our likeness,” plural. He didn’t say, “Let me make man in My image.” He said, “Let us.” Why? Because that four-part, of identities and creating the world, is all God. And Jesus. The Bible says in Revelation He was the beginning of the creation of God. The Bible says that He died before the foundation of the world, His blood was shed before the foundation of the world. Well, it wasn’t shed before the foundation of the world, it was shed when it was shed, 4,000 years later, but God spoke it’s going to be, and when He spoke it’s going to be, it’s as good as done. Amen. So Jesus is the beginning. His plan. Somebody, people say, “Well, you know, Adam and Eve sinned so God had to have a plan B.” Uh-uh. He never had a plan B. He had one plan the whole time, and that was Jesus Christ, reconciling people back to God, back to what is right, and filling heaven with people that would repent and turn. That was His plan. All right, so that is Jesus. Remember, without Him not anything was made. Remember, the world was made by Him. All things were made by Him, John said. And so we have Jesus back there, part of the four-person God here, one God doing things with four different explanations: God, the Holy Ghost, the Word, and Jesus. Hallelujah.
Do we find God, the Spirit and the Word in Genesis 1, and was Jesus always God’s plan?

Genesis 1:1-3: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth. The earth was without form, and void; and darkness was on the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God was hovering over the face of the waters. Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light. John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. Joel 2:28: “And it shall come to pass afterward That I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your old men shall dream dreams, Your young men shall see visions. Genesis 1:26: Then God said, “Let Us make man in Our image, according to Our likeness; let them have dominion over the fish of the sea, over the birds of the air, and over the cattle, over all the earth and over every creeping thing that creeps on the earth.” Revelation 3:14: “And to the angel of the church of the Laodiceans write, ‘These things says the Amen, the Faithful and True Witness, the Beginning of the creation of God: Revelation 13:8: All who dwell on the earth will worship him, whose names have not been written in the Book of Life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.
What do spiritual fathers do that “baby food” churchgoers don’t?

He says fathers “grow up” and aren’t in a church “where they’re just getting baby food all the time”; they are “in the Word, they’re digging,” and “study to show themselves approved.” He asks how many could say, “I study the Book, I’m learning the Book, I’m becoming a father,” and says “most of us don’t even read it.”
What do spiritual fathers do that “baby food” churchgoers don’t?

Now see, fathers understand that they grow up, and they understand they’re not in some church where they’re just getting baby food all the time. They’re in the Word, they’re digging, they have their concordance, they have their Bible out, they have their reason. They “study to show themselves approved, rightly dividing the word” to God. They what? Study. They just don’t read the Bible through in a year, they study that Bible. And I would say, raise your hand, how many fathers we got here this morning, but we don’t want to do that. But think, if Jesus came and said, “How many fathers we got here?” how many could really raise their hand and say, “I study the Book, I’m learning the Book, I’m becoming a father”? See, we don’t study. Most of us don’t even read it. We’re waiting for some megachurch pastor to write another book to inspire us.
What do spiritual fathers do that “baby food” churchgoers don’t?
2 Timothy 2:15: Be diligent to present yourself approved to God, a worker who does not need to be ashamed, rightly dividing the word of truth.
What does it mean for a father not to provoke his children to anger? (Ephesians 6:4)

He says a real father “doesn’t irritate and drive his children crazy” to the point of resentment and hatred, which can happen “by being a bad example, by not knowing how to raise kids, by not putting kids first.” He says children lose motivation “because there’s a lack of fatherhood in the home,” and that “fathers are there to motivate you.”
What does it mean for a father not to provoke his children to anger? (Ephesians 6:4)

Now, characteristics of a father. The Bible says first the natural, then the spiritual. You say, Jesus said, “If I spoke to you of heavenly things, you wouldn’t understand them, so I speak to you in natural things about heavenly things so you understand them.” Isn’t that smart of Him? Yeah. I can connect with things that I can relate to. So here’s the characteristics of a real father, an earthly father, a genuine father, and so you men wake up. All right, Ephesians, first characteristic. Ephesians 6:4: “Fathers, do not provoke your children to anger.” A real father doesn’t irritate and drive his children crazy, all right, to where they get resentment in their heart and hatred in their heart. They hate life, they hate their parents, they hate their dad, they hate, and they resent. All right, and fathers can do that by being a bad example, by not knowing how to raise kids, by not putting kids first. See, but a good father will not drive his kid crazy, neither will a good mother. “Lest they be discouraged,” or so that they be discouraged, or they lack motivation. They lack motivation in spiritual things, they lack motivation in natural things. They’re only motivated to play Nintendo games, or the Xbox, the latest Xbox stuff. That’s the only motivation they got in this generation, or to put earphones on and listen to their music. And now that’s our young people’s motivation today because there’s a lack of fatherhood in the home. Yeah, they become discouraged, they lack motivation. And you kids better listen to this, because fathers are there to motivate you. Fathers are there to make you into an adult later that can sustain themselves.
What does it mean for a father not to provoke his children to anger? (Ephesians 6:4)
Ephesians 6:4: And you, fathers, do not provoke your children to wrath, but bring them up in the training and admonition of the Lord.
What does it mean to “train up” and “cherish” your children?

He says the quality of a real father is “how he handles his kids,” that “trains” means “cherish,” putting a value on children as a husband values his wife, and that “training” is “instruction with discipline.” He says the goal is to “raise them up to maturity” so they can provide for themselves, and he tells young women to get a job skill.
What does it mean to “train up” and “cherish” your children?

He goes on to say, number two, the characteristic of a father. Characteristic is defining features, the qualities, the defining feature of a real father, the quality of a real father is how he handles his kids. Now that child can reject it. Don’t blame the father when the child rejects what a father is trying to train him up to be. So the second characteristic, a real father “trains up.” That word “trains” has a meaning, it’s “cherish.” You put a value on your children. He says John “emphasizes that Jesus created the world, created everything, and without Him nothing was made that was made.”
What does he mean by “four” involved in creation?

He says in Genesis 1 “you’re going to find the God four involved in creation. How many? Four. What are you used to? Three,” and later describes “one God doing things with four different explanations: God, the Holy Ghost, the Word, and Jesus.” This is his teaching, shown here as he said it.
Did God have a “plan B” after Adam and Eve sinned?

No. He says “He never had a plan B. He had one plan the whole time, and that was Jesus Christ, reconciling people back to God, back to what is right, and filling heaven with people that would repent and turn.”
Why does he say many young people lack motivation?
He says it is “because there’s a lack of fatherhood in the home,” and that “fathers are there to motivate you” and to make you into an adult “that can sustain themselves.”
What does he say most ministers are teaching?

He says “most ministers are just teaching baby doctrines all the time” and “a lot of ministers are teaching embryo stuff,” and that listeners are also at fault for “listening to the radio where all you hear is embryo preaching.”
Does he say evil spirits came from God?

He asks who the Father of spirits is (God) and whether the evil spirits came from God, answering “yeah, they did” since “without Him was not anything made,” and says “they rebelled and became evil spirits.”
What does he say about fathers who correct children for their own convenience?

He says a real father “doesn’t correct for their own convenience,” but “to train them up in the way they should go,” and calls it “the difference between disciplining for convenience and disciplining for future development.”
What does he say are the “first principles” of Hebrews 6:1?

He lists faith toward God, repentance from dead works, baptism of the Holy Ghost, baptism in water, baptism in the body, laying on of hands, resurrection, and eternal judgment, and calls them baby doctrine.
What does he say people who are still babies want to hear?

He says, “You want to hear that once saved always saved. You want to hear that no matter what you do God loves you and you’re going to go to heaven. That’s what you want to hear, because what? You’re a baby.”
Does he say Christians should judge?
He says “everybody’s saying don’t judge, and here the apostle is telling us to what? Judge,” meaning to discern “what’s good and what’s evil,” and says “Jesus said it, the apostles are saying it.”
What does he mean by “faith in your faith”?

He says you can’t just believe you’re saved or going to heaven “and don’t have the evidence of it, the proof of it. That’s faith in your faith,” and that “the Bible doesn’t tell us to have faith in our faith.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Jeremiah to show what God told His prophet to preach: root out evil, plant the right seed, and do not be afraid. He explains the broken cisterns of Jeremiah…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer walks through Jeremiah to show what God told His prophet to preach: root out evil, plant the right seed, and do not be afraid. He explains the broken cisterns of Jeremiah 2:13, the three sources of opposition (civil government, temple leaders and church members), and how the captivities came while false prophets promised victory. He applies it to America today, urging Christians to amend their ways, humble themselves and pray, and to have compassion on those who oppose them.
What did Jeremiah say was wrong with the prophets of Jerusalem? (Jeremiah 23:14)

He reads Jeremiah 23:14, where the prophets commit adultery, walk in lies, and “strengthen the hands of evildoers” so that none returns from wickedness. He says this is what Sodom and Gomorrah did, “they held no one accountable,” and that when the gospel of repentance isn’t preached “we are strengthening their hand to live in sin.”
What did Jeremiah say was wrong with the prophets of Jerusalem? (Jeremiah 23:14)

And Jeremiah, of course, Ezekiel was a prophet in the captivity. Jeremiah was the prophet before and during the three captivities, and in Jeremiah 23:14, Jeremiah, through God, lifts up his voice and says, “I have seen also a thing in the prophets of Jerusalem that is horrible. They commit adultery,” number one, sexual immorality. “They walk in lies.” They don’t only lie, they walk in lies and say, “It’s my truth.” How many know people who walk in lies yet they say their truth? Yeah, you probably look at one in the mirror in the morning. Yeah. “They strengthen the hands of evildoers.” Now here’s the kicker: they strengthen the hands of evildoers “so none returns from his wickedness.” And this is the big problem. This is what Sodom and Gomorrah did. They held no one accountable for crime. They held no one accountable for sexual immorality, no one accountable for idolatry, no one accountable for all the abominations they were doing. And Jeremiah says God’s people, Jerusalem, the Jews, were just like them. They’re not holding God’s people accountable. See, but they strengthen their hands, so no one repents, no one is really turning from their evil ways, from their wickedness. Then he says they’re all “as Sodom, and the inhabitants like Gomorrah.” So it’s not just the prophets. The inhabitants, the people listening to these preachers, are as Gomorrah. Do we get it now? See, here’s the problem: when we don’t preach the gospel to repent, turn from your sin, admit you’re wrong and turn from it, we are strengthening their hand to live in sin, and God says that’s just exactly what Sodom did and Gomorrah did. They held no one accountable for doing wrong.
What did Jeremiah say was wrong with the prophets of Jerusalem? (Jeremiah 23:14)

Jeremiah 23:14: Also I have seen a horrible thing in the prophets of Jerusalem: They commit adultery and walk in lies; They also strengthen the hands of evildoers, So that no one turns back from his wickedness. All of them are like Sodom to Me, And her inhabitants like Gomorrah.
What message did God give Jeremiah to preach? (Jeremiah 1:10)

He says we are only allowed to preach the message God gives us, not our own opinions or other people’s. He explains God’s charge to “root out,” “pull down,” “destroy,” “throw down,” and “build,” saying “you don’t root up without planting the proper seed back in there,” and that God told Jeremiah not to be dismayed, because “too many of us Christians, when we are confronted by the enemy, we fold.”
What message did God give Jeremiah to preach? (Jeremiah 1:10)

We’re going to continue in Jeremiah, and look at God’s message to Jeremiah. God comes to Jeremiah in Jeremiah chapter 1, verse 1, and He gives Jeremiah a message. How many know we’re only allowed to preach the message God gives us to preach? We’re not allowed to preach our opinions and our ideas. We’re not allowed to preach other people’s opinions and their ideas. And so He comes to Jeremiah and He says, “Hey, this is what I want you to tell the people.” “This day I have set you over the nations,” over the unbeliever. The nations is the Gentiles, the pagans, the unbeliever. This message has got to go to the unbeliever. “And over the kingdoms.” A kingdom is where a king rules over you. You’ve got to take it to civil authorities. “This message that I’m giving you is going to root out.” You see, you’ve got to get to the root of the problem. Ain’t that right? Didn’t Jesus say the tree is evil because the root is evil? Yeah. So, Jeremiah, you’ve got to root out the roots of evil, these bad things. “You got to pull down.” The Bible says the weapons of our warfare are not carnal, but they’re mighty through God to the what? Tearing down, the pulling down of strongholds. We’ve got to pull down the stronghold of the enemy on people’s lives. “We got to destroy.” And the Bible says that Jesus destroyed the works of Satan. We’ve got to destroy the works of Satan. Amen. “And throw down, and to build.” Now, you don’t root up without planting the proper seed back in there. Amen. You can’t just go around tearing everything up. You’ve got to build, and you’ve got to plant the right seed and get the right root in people’s lives. Now, that’s a good place for an amen. And that’s a good message, isn’t it? Yeah. He also says, Jeremiah, and listen, church, he says, “Jeremiah, I don’t want you to be dismayed or discouraged, afraid and confused before their faces, before their presence, before their person.” And too many of us Christians, when we are confronted by the enemy, we fold. We don’t want to hurt their feelings, or we don’t have an answer to give them, or they threaten us. And He says, “Jeremiah, don’t you be discouraged. Don’t you be afraid of their person, of their faces.” How many could use a little of that in your life? Yeah, courage instead of fear. Yeah, we’re afraid to stand up for who we are in America right now. And then God gives a message to the people. He says, “You’ve committed two evils.”
What message did God give Jeremiah to preach? (Jeremiah 1:10)

Jeremiah 1:10: See, I have this day set you over the nations and over the kingdoms, To root out and to pull down, To destroy and to throw down, To build and to plant.” 2 Corinthians 10:4: For the weapons of our warfare are not carnal but mighty in God for pulling down strongholds, 1 John 3:8: He who sins is of the devil, for the devil has sinned from the beginning. For this purpose the Son of God was manifested, that He might destroy the works of the devil. Jeremiah 1:17: “Therefore prepare yourself and arise, And speak to them all that I command you. Do not be dismayed before their faces, Lest I dismay you before them.
What are the “two evils” in Jeremiah 2:13, and what is a broken cistern?

He reads that the people forsook God, “the fountain of living water,” and dug cisterns that can hold no water. He says “a lot of people believe in God and they have no life” because they don’t have Jesus and the Word, and asks whether it is true in America that “we believe in God, but we have no power, we have no life.”
What are the “two evils” in Jeremiah 2:13, and what is a broken cistern?

Jeremiah 2:13: “You’ve done two things wrong. You’ve forsaken Me, the fountain of living water, and you’ve cut out cisterns that can hold no water,” broken cisterns that can hold no water. Now, I’ve given you an example up here. Here’s a man-made system, okay? It would rain, the water would run down in here, and, you know, if there was an underground source, the system would have water down below, and when the water level was high, you’d have higher water. Now there’s also a vessel. It can be a vessel, container, a bucket with holes in it. He said you’re putting water in buckets with holes in it. Have you ever been at the beach and you dug a hole and the wave come in and it filled up that hole, and then you just watched as that water just disappears? See, that’s systems, that’s a container that won’t hold water. And a lot of people believe in God and they have no life. They don’t have Jesus and the Word, which are life. Amen. Because they got holes, it just runs out. God comes and it just goes out. Here is a spring coming right out of the ground, and it’s coming out of the ground at over 3,000 gallons per minute. Now this is an example of the fountain of living water. The guy who has the property that owns this spring runs this water through a generator, and he has free electricity. That’s how powerful the water is. How many know God wants us to have power? How many know we need the water flowing to have the power? Yeah, we can’t have systems that won’t hold no water. This water’s got to be flowing. It’s got to come from Him, pour out of us, continual strength. And He says that’s the problem with the people. Could that be true in America today? Yeah, we believe in God, but we have no power, we have no life, we have no source within us.
What are the “two evils” in Jeremiah 2:13, and what is a broken cistern?
Jeremiah 2:13: “For My people have committed two evils: They have forsaken Me, the fountain of living waters, And hewn themselves cisterns—broken cisterns that can hold no water.
What did God say would happen to the people, and why? (Jeremiah 1:14; 2:19)

He says God told Jeremiah war and captivity were coming from the north, and that “God’s people don’t like to hear bad messages. They like to hear positive thinking when they really need a spanking.” He reads Jeremiah 2:19 and says wrongdoing carries a payment: “your own sins, your own backslidings will correct you.”
What did God say would happen to the people, and why? (Jeremiah 1:14; 2:19)

Then He gives Jeremiah the message of his punishment, of his judgment for what the people are doing, okay? And He says in Jeremiah 1:14, “Out of the north calamity shall break forth on all the inhabitants of the land.” In other words, war is coming and you’re going to go into captivity. War is going to happen. That’s what He tells them in Jeremiah 1:14, right at the beginning when Jeremiah started prophesying in the days of Josiah. That was the message: war’s coming, captivity is coming. Hallelujah. God’s people don’t like to hear bad messages. They like to hear positive thinking when they really need a spanking. Chapter 2:19: “Your own wickedness will correct you, and your backslidings will rebuke you.” You see, when you do wrong, there is a payment to be paid. You’re going to commit sexual immorality, you’re going to get sexually transmitted diseases, you’re going to break up homes, you’re going to get depressed, it’s going to cause emotional problems. That’s the way sin is. You steal somebody’s car, you’re going to go to jail, you’re going to pay. That person ain’t going to let you just come and steal his car. He’s going to see that you pay for it. Society’s going to see that you pay for it. You see, your own sins, your own backslidings will correct you.
What did God say would happen to the people, and why? (Jeremiah 1:14; 2:19)

Jeremiah 1:14: Then the LORD said to me: “Out of the north calamity shall break forth On all the inhabitants of the land. Jeremiah 2:19: Your own wickedness will correct you, And your backslidings will rebuke you. Know therefore and see that it is an evil and bitter thing That you have forsaken the LORD your God, And the fear of Me is not in you,” Says the Lord GOD of hosts.
What are the three sources of opposition to God’s message?

He says every prophet had opposition and likens it to a storm that grows day by day. He names three sources: “civil government,” “temple leaders, religious leaders, church leaders,” and “false prophets and temple members, church members,” and says “if you don’t say nothing, they got no problem with you.”
What are the three sources of opposition to God’s message?

In Jeremiah there is three sources of opposition going to come to his message. How many know every prophet had opposition? Ain’t that right? Yeah, we act like nothing is supposed to happen to us, because there’s preachers preaching that and people believe those lies because they don’t read their Bible. There’s going to be three sources of opposition to Jeremiah’s message. I’m going to liken it to the Hurricane Katrina, which wound up being one of the five worst storms in America, in United States history, with winds of 175 miles per hour, did $5 billion worth of damage. Okay, it started as a tropical storm over here in the Atlantic. Then a few days later it diminished. “Ah, it’s not going to turn into a hurricane.” Everybody was relieved. A few days later it grew big. “Now, oh, what’s going to happen next?” The news is following. A few days later it’s twice as big as it was before. A few days later it’s twice as big as it was before, over twice as big. And then a few more days later it is a full-grown hurricane with the eye in the middle and headed toward Louisiana, Mississippi, and Alabama to do its destruction. Okay, I picked this because it’s an illustration that Christians need to understand. Now, let’s look at the three areas of opposition. Number one, civil government. They’re always punishing our prophets, punishing God’s people. Are you there? Genesis to Revelation, civil government just treats people who want to just live right horribly. Ain’t that right? The second source is temple leaders, religious leaders, church leaders. Church leaders oppose the message that a judgment’s coming. Church leaders oppose the message that God corrects and punishes His people and judges His people. And false prophets, and temple members, church members. You know, church members in Ezekiel are some of the worst. It’s sheep that stomped out the waters and made it muddy for the other sheep. It wasn’t leaders at all, it was just sheep. You sheep are a real problem sometimes. Are you there? Yeah. You distort the Word of God yourself, and then you distort it to other people. You twist it, mangle it like you know what you’re talking about, and you don’t know beans. Hallelujah. And there’s false prophets, folks. There’s just a lot of people preaching a false gospel. That’s the bottom line. Are you there? And they all oppose the right message, the true message. If you don’t say nothing, they got no problem with you. So you silent saints, yeah, you don’t know what’s going on because you’re never talking. You get out there and talk to these people and they hate your guts. They don’t like you telling them they’re wrong. So these are the three sources of opposition, and we’re going to look at these in more detail.
Is government and religious leadership today opposing the message of the Bible?

He says civil government today is “opposing the message of the Bible that there’s a punishment for violating what is right,” and that religious leaders are doing it too, “even collaborating with government officials.” He says “you can only preach what Jesus said to preach. You can only imitate Jesus.”
Is government and religious leadership today opposing the message of the Bible?

But is our civil government today opposing the message of the Bible? Absolutely, absolutely. From governors to state senators to House of Representatives, in Congress, to the President of the United States, they are opposing the message of the Bible that there’s a punishment for violating what is right. Is religious leaders doing it in America today? Absolutely. They’re even collaborating with government officials to promote things to America and demean the Bible in the name of Jesus. How can you do that? You can only preach what Jesus said to preach. You can only imitate Jesus. You can’t imitate somebody else. Here’s the opposition’s effects. Jeremiah starts preaching in Josiah’s day. Josiah is the king of Judah who was a good king. He cleansed the temple, he restored it, he kept the feast. When he read in the Law that God’s people were going to be judged, he sent to the prophet, “What can we do?”
Why did Judah still go into captivity after a good king like Josiah?

He says Josiah cleansed the temple and kept the feast, and the prophet told him judgment would not come in his day “because your heart is right with God,” though it would still come. After Josiah died his son “burned the Scriptures” and did evil, the first captivity came in 597 BC, and the false prophets had been saying “there’s no war coming.”
Why did Judah still go into captivity after a good king like Josiah?

And so, as we seen the storm Katrina, there was a storm brewing. His father was evil, and Isaiah was prophesying before that judgment’s coming. Isaiah was preaching it to the other kings, and so the storm was arising. And then Josiah comes along and we have a what? A decreasing and abatement, at least in Josiah. But the prophet said, didn’t say it wasn’t coming. The prophet came to Josiah and said, “It won’t happen in your day because your heart is right with God. You’re doing what’s right. So this isn’t going to happen in your day, but it’s still going to happen.” So the people thought, “Ah, we got a reprieve. The storm has shrunk. There’s a decrease. No war, no captivity, no plagues, no problems.” And then Josiah died. And his son [unclear] sat on the throne, ruled for 11 years, and the Bible said he burned the Scriptures. He took the Scriptures and had his scribe read them, and after he had stopped, he cut that scroll and he threw it into the fire. Then the scribe would read more and he’d cut that off and throw it into the fire. He decimated the Scripture. He had no respect for the Scripture. The Bible says he did evil. He killed innocent blood, he killed innocent people, and he committed abominations. That means sexual immorality, homosexuality, incest, idolatry. All these things that God says He detests are abominations. And then they went into captivity in 597 BC. They went into captivity, first captivity. Now the false prophets are preaching, “We ain’t going to go into captivity. There’s no war coming. Don’t you believe it. We’re going to win this war. We’re going to defeat it. Babylon’s going to turn around.” That’s what the false prophets were saying. And then, poof, they go into captivity. Now the storm has gotten big, and the first captivity and the first destruction and the first correction has come.
How did the false prophets respond as Babylon returned and destroyed Jerusalem?

He says the false prophets kept promising victory while Jeremiah said to surrender to Babylon, where “nobody will get hurt.” When the people refused, Babylon “burnt the city to the ground and destroyed the temple,” which the false prophets said would never happen, and he asks why God would not “be a good father and correct you.”
How did the false prophets respond as Babylon returned and destroyed Jerusalem?

[unclear] is replaced by Jehoiachin, who only lasted three months, and the Bible just sums him up by saying he did everything Jehoiakim had done. So he detested the Scriptures, he did evil, he created abomination, he killed innocent blood, he did everything Jehoiakim did, so he didn’t last long. Egypt come up and took care of him. Zedekiah gets on the throne. Zedekiah ruled for 11 years, okay, and the Bible says he did evil as Jehoiakim did. That means he detested the Scriptures, he shed innocent blood, he did evil, and he did these abominations all the time, believing in God. They were still going to the temple and keeping the feast and doing, you know, singing. Zedekiah imprisoned the messenger. The temple leaders and Zedekiah imprisoned him, beating him. Church leaders opposing the true message, they put Jeremiah in prison. So Babylon came back. The prophets are prophesying, “They ain’t coming back.” And when they did come back, they said, “We’re going to win the war again.” They didn’t win it the first time. Jeremiah was right the first time. But here they are prophesying, [unclear], you know, speaking in tongues, interpretation, all that goes with it, whatever. But their message is wrong. The city comes. Babylon comes in, in spite of them going to the temple and praying, calling on God, and having the false prophets prophesy a positive message. When God’s saying, “Hey, Babylon’s going to win. If you just surrender to Babylon, no one will die.” “We’re not surrendering to Babylon.” “Oh, hallelujah, that’s a negative confession.” And Jeremiah would say, “All you got to do is just open the gates, surrender to Babylon, nobody will get hurt.” They wouldn’t do it. They lost the war, and this time Babylon destroyed the city, just burnt the city to the ground and destroyed the temple. He didn’t just carry off the temple stuff, this time he destroyed the temple, which these false prophets said would never happen. Are you there? Hallelujah. “Nobody’s going to touch the house of God.” Somebody will when God says, “Touch My house.” Are you there? Yeah, you can think you’re strong because “I’m the temple of God, man, Jesus lives in me, ain’t nothing going to happen.” Well, if God says, “Get him.” Are you there? “But God wouldn’t do that.” Why wouldn’t He? You need a spanking. You need correction. Why would He allow you to continue in your destructive ways and not be a good father and correct you?
What happens when you stand up for the truth, even with family and friends?

He says Jeremiah’s own hometown and relatives conspired to kill him, and asks, “You think that your own family won’t get mad at you if you preach the gospel?” He says people are happy for you to be silent and “don’t rock the boat,” “but you speak up and you live up and see what happens.”
What happens when you stand up for the truth, even with family and friends?

Now we come to these false prophets and temple leaders and the citizens. Okay. Again, they are teaching no captivity, we’re going to win the war. They’ve already lost twice and they’re still preaching no more captivity, we’re going to beat Babylon, now we’re going to win this thing. The third captivity came. His hometown tried to kill him, his own people. You think that your own family won’t get mad at you if you preach the gospel, you stand up for right? You think it’s going to go well with you? Remember your family? You are living in a fantasy world. You think it’s going to go well with your group of friends when you really stand up for truth and preach truth? No, they’re going to try and destroy you. They’re going to come after you. You silent? Yeah, they don’t care. You just be silent, wear your religion, you know, in a hidden closet, don’t do anything or say anything, don’t rock the boat. Yeah, they like you being shut up. But you speak up and you live up and see what happens.
What happened when the people asked Jeremiah for a word from God about Egypt?

He says the people promised to obey whatever God told them, but Jeremiah said they had come “wanting to hear what you wanted to hear.” God’s word was “don’t go into Egypt,” to “give in to the Babylonians and you will live,” yet they called him a false prophet and forced him to Egypt, where, he says, they still faced war, plagues and captivity.
What happened when the people asked Jeremiah for a word from God about Egypt?

And his own hometown, his own relatives, conspired to kill him. Then they were carried captive in 582 BC, another captivity. I mean, these guys, I mean, one captivity, two captivity, and they still have the same message. Hello, church. And Jeremiah’s message is coming to pass and they still say he’s a false prophet. Imprisoned him, rejected him, beat him, you know, claimed that he wasn’t hearing from God. And then the people of faith, the people of the Jewish people, came during this time and they said, “Jeremiah, we need a word from God.” Okay, they recognized he could preach a word from God. They said, “We need a word from God, and whatever God gives you to tell us, you know, we’ll obey it.” So Jeremiah, he goes and he gets a word from God and he comes back and he says, “Listen, I know you’re lying to me.” This is what Jeremiah said: “You came in deceit. You’re not going to listen to what I said. You came here wanting to hear what you wanted to hear, and I’m not going to give you what you want to hear, and you’re not going to obey what God gives you to say. But here’s what God said: don’t go into Egypt. Stay right here. Give in to the Babylonians and you will live, and I will bless you.” And after Jeremiah got done preaching, they said, “You prophesy falsely. We’re not going to do what you say to do. We’re going to do what we just like.” Jeremiah prophesied, they forced Jeremiah, they wouldn’t listen to his message, and they forced him to go to Egypt with them. And if you know your history, Babylon went down and conquered Egypt, and guess who went into captivity anyway. The people that tried to run away from God’s message, human thinking. So God got them down there, they still had war, they still had plagues, and they still went into captivity. Are you there?
Are church people some of the biggest false prophets, and what is the solution? (Jeremiah 7:2)

He says “the people in the church are some of the biggest false prophets in the church” when they say “I believe it’s this way” instead of asking what the Scripture says. He says the solution is Jeremiah standing in the gate of the Lord’s house to tell worshipers their rituals mean nothing without changed ways: “What good is worship when you’re living in sin?”
Are church people some of the biggest false prophets, and what is the solution? (Jeremiah 7:2)

So we have these oppositions: the people of faith, the people in the church are some of the biggest false prophets in the church. They believe lies and they just simply say, “Well, I believe it’s this way.” Well, who cares what you believe? What does the Scripture say? “I don’t see nothing wrong with doing this.” Well, it doesn’t matter what you see nothing wrong with. What does the Scripture say? Can I hear an amen? Now, what’s the solution here? Here is the solution, and here is why we’re losing the war in America. Jeremiah, “Stand in the gate of the Lord’s house.” Where did he go? The Lord’s house. “Go to My people, go to where they come to worship Me and learn of Me, and proclaim this word to them.” So here’s these people going in and out of the temple in their real religious ways and bringing their sheep in and doing their little rituals and their sacrifices, and here’s Jeremiah saying, just like Isaiah said, “These sacrifices are nothing. Feast days are nothing. Amend your ways,” and your what? Doings, your actions. Yes, change your ways. Don’t give me these, you know, what good is prayer? What good is worship when you’re living in sin?
Are church people some of the biggest false prophets, and what is the solution? (Jeremiah 7:2)
Jeremiah 7:2: “Stand in the gate of the LORD’s house, and proclaim there this word, and say, ‘Hear the word of the LORD, all you of Judah who enter in at these gates to worship the LORD!’ ”
What does it mean to “amend your ways and your doings”? (Jeremiah 7:7, 7:9)

He says that if you want God’s blessings, you’ve got to “amend your ways and your doings. You’ve got to turn from your own wrongs and do right,” saying “it’s not grace and faith that’s going to do this.” He says God is patient while we grow, “but we should be growing,” and reads Jeremiah 7:9 as the list of what they were doing: stealing, murder, sexual immorality, false swearing and worshiping other gods.
What does it mean to “amend your ways and your doings”? (Jeremiah 7:7, 7:9)

Then he says, “I will cause you to dwell in this place.” See, it’s not grace and faith that’s going to do this. If you want God’s blessings, you’ve got to what? Amend your ways and your doings. You’ve got to turn from your own wrongs and do right. Now, that’s a good place for a good strong amen. Now, that’s Bible. “Will He be patient with me while I’m learning?” Right, of course. We’re children, we’re family, we grow into maturity. We’re soldiers, we go to boot camp. We don’t learn how to fight the enemy overnight, we grow into that ability. Ain’t that right? But we should be growing. Now, what was their ways and their doings? What exactly were they doing? Jeremiah 7:9: “You steal, you murder,” and hate is murder in the New Testament, “you commit sexual immorality, you swear falsely.” You’re a bunch of liars, and you tell lies about other people. “You burn incense to Baal, you worship Baal, and walk after other gods whom you don’t even know.” You can’t know them because they’re not real. “And then you come and stand before Me in this house.” You come into the church, “this house that’s called by My name.” You come in to worship, you come in to do your religious thing.
What does it mean to “amend your ways and your doings”? (Jeremiah 7:7, 7:9)

Jeremiah 7:7: then I will cause you to dwell in this place, in the land that I gave to your fathers forever and ever. Jeremiah 7:9: Will you steal, murder, commit adultery, swear falsely, burn incense to Baal, and walk after other gods whom you do not know,
Why does he say we are not winning “this religious liberty battle”? (2 Chronicles 7:14)

He says the people came into the Lord’s house saying “I am delivered to do all these abominations,” and asks, “isn’t that prominent in America right now?” He says “we wonder why we’re not winning this religious liberty battle” because “we’re not changing our ways,” that judgment must begin at the house of God, and that seeking God and praying “should bring us to a change in our life.”
Why does he say we are not winning “this religious liberty battle”? (2 Chronicles 7:14)

And you say, “I am delivered to do all these abominations.” I can commit adultery, I can commit incest, I can have more than one wife, I can have all gods lead to the same God, all religions lead to the same God. Hallelujah. “I can do all these. God delivered me because I believe in Him. I can do all these things, I’ll go to heaven, and God will bless me.” Isn’t that prominent in America right now? Oh, it is prominent, and we wonder why we’re not winning this religious liberty battle. We get in our little churches and we do our little thing and we’re not changing our ways, and so God cannot judge the sinner without judging His people. Judgment must begin where? At the house of God. So, “if My people will humble themselves,” and what? Pray. We stop there. “And seek My face and turn from their wicked ways, oh, then I will hear from heaven, forgive their sin, and heal their land.” So what’s the key? We need to seek God, we need to pray, but that prayer and that seeking should bring us to a change in our life. Then when that happens, God can say, “See, nation of America, here is My people, a light to you. Now I can deal with you who are sinning.”
Why does he say we are not winning “this religious liberty battle”? (2 Chronicles 7:14)

2 Chronicles 7:14: if My people who are called by My name will humble themselves, and pray and seek My face, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin and heal their land. 1 Peter 4:17: For the time has come for judgment to begin at the house of God; and if it begins with us first, what will be the end of those who do not obey the gospel of God?
How are Christians robbed of their thinking? (Colossians 2:8)

He reads Colossians 2:8 and says deceivers work through philosophy, intellectualism and “men’s ideas” rather than scriptural truth. He says “we don’t think right anymore, and we promote wrong,” and that “they are stealing our mind and getting us to believe things that are wrong.”
How are Christians robbed of their thinking? (Colossians 2:8)

Colossians 2:8: “Beware lest any man spoil you.” Steal, take your possessions by force or any other means. “Beware lest any man.” How’s he going to do it? Through his so-called philosophy, his principles to live by, his ideal, what’s right, and intellectualism, what he thinks is right. They use big words and “vain, worthless deceit.” See, their whole thing is to deceive people, following human tradition or men’s ideas. That’s what’s happening in America, men’s ideals rather than what scriptural truth, following undeveloped primary teachings of the world and disregarding the teachings of Christ. They come and taking the Christian mind and robbing their mind, their thinking. And so we don’t think right anymore, and we promote wrong, just like Jeremiah said. We’re strengthening the sinner that they don’t turn from their wicked way, because our thinking is wrong. Could that be an amen? But the Bible is a book of law, it’s a book of truth. Where in society are we to believe that promoting lies is going to be healthy for our nation? In our public schools, do we send our kids to public schools to be taught lies? Should the public school have a right to teach lies or just truth? Yeah, but they’re teaching lies. See, they are stealing our mind and getting us to believe things that are wrong. They’re getting us to believe they’re right and promote them as right. I made this statement: American Christians make the same mistake the Jews did. The Jews lost the battle, even the good ones. Ezekiel was a good man, Daniel was a good man, Shadrach, Abednego were good people, but they had to be a partaker of the judgment just like everybody else.
How are Christians robbed of their thinking? (Colossians 2:8)
Colossians 2:8: Beware lest anyone cheat you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men, according to the basic principles of the world, and not according to Christ.
Can America be turned around, and how should Christians treat those who oppose them?

He says “American Christians make the same mistake the Jews did,” and that even good men “had to be a partaker of the judgment,” but asks “Can we turn America around? Absolutely,” pointing to Josiah who turned from his father’s ways. He says we should have compassion for those who oppose and for unlearned believers, asking, “How are they going to hear it if we’re silent?”
Can America be turned around, and how should Christians treat those who oppose them?

Can we turn America around? Absolutely. Josiah did. Remember, Isaiah had already been preaching the message that captivity was coming, but Josiah turned from the ways of his father and the bad kings before and did what was right and brought blessing back to Judah. Can we do that to America? Should we do that to America? Should we be compassionate for their enemies that oppose God and don’t believe in the Bible and attacking us? Should we have the compassion to want them to hear the gospel and come to their senses and be saved? Yes. How are they going to hear it if we’re silent? If we let them silence us, how are they going to hear it? And should we have a compassion for the churches in America, the people sitting there, a lot of them with really innocent hearts, really wanting God, and preachers and books are telling them things that are not right? Should we have a compassion for God’s people who are unlearned, that God would come and teach them, and they can have an effect in their home and in their community and the nation? Yeah.
What does he say Sodom and Gomorrah did wrong?

He says they “held no one accountable for crime,” sexual immorality, idolatry or the abominations they were doing, and that Jeremiah says God’s people in Jerusalem were just like them because the preachers strengthened the hands of evildoers.
What are the “two evils” God charged the people with?
He says they forsook God, “the fountain of living water,” and dug broken cisterns that hold no water. He compares a cistern to “a bucket with holes in it.”
What does the spring that runs a generator illustrate?

He says it is an example of the fountain of living water: a spring coming out at over 3,000 gallons a minute that runs a generator for free electricity. He says God wants us to have power, and that the water “got to be flowing” and “come from Him.”
Why does he say God’s people dislike hard messages?

He says “God’s people don’t like to hear bad messages. They like to hear positive thinking when they really need a spanking.” He says Jeremiah’s message from the beginning was that war and captivity were coming.
What does “your own wickedness will correct you” mean?

He reads Jeremiah 2:19 and says that when you do wrong there is a payment to be paid, using stealing a car and going to jail as an example. He says “your own sins, your own backslidings will correct you.”
What three sources of opposition does he list?

He lists civil government, which “treats people who want to just live right horribly,” temple leaders and church leaders who oppose the message that God corrects and judges His people, and false prophets and church members who twist the Word.
What does he say about church members who twist the Word of God?

He says church members in Ezekiel were “sheep that stomped out the waters and made it muddy for the other sheep,” and that they “distort the Word of God yourself, and then you distort it to other people.” He says there are many people preaching a false gospel.
Why does he say God would let Jerusalem be destroyed?
He says people thought “nobody’s going to touch the house of God,” but asks, “Why would He allow you to continue in your destructive ways and not be a good father and correct you?”
What did Jeremiah tell the people to do about Babylon?
He says Jeremiah told them, “All you got to do is just open the gates, surrender to Babylon, nobody will get hurt,” and they wouldn’t do it.
Does he say family and friends will welcome you standing up for truth?

No. He says “you are living in a fantasy world” if you think it will go well with your family or friends, and that “they’re going to come after you,” while they like you being “shut up” in a hidden closet.
Does he say God is patient while we are learning?

Yes. He asks, “Will He be patient with me while I’m learning?” and answers, “Right, of course. We’re children, we’re family, we grow into maturity,” and compares it to soldiers in boot camp, “but we should be growing.”
What ways and doings does he list from Jeremiah 7:9?

He lists stealing, murder (and hate, which he says is murder in the New Testament), sexual immorality, swearing falsely, lying about other people, and burning incense to Baal and walking after other gods, then coming into God’s house to worship.
What does he say is the key in the verse about humbling ourselves?
He says “we need to seek God, we need to pray, but that prayer and that seeking should bring us to a change in our life,” and then God can say, “here is My people, a light to you.”
Should Christians have compassion for people who oppose them?

Yes. He asks, “Should we have the compassion to want them to hear the gospel and come to their senses and be saved? Yes,” and says we should also have compassion for churchgoers with “really innocent hearts” who are being told things that are not right.

items.t: Four Difficult Issues to Understand Part 1
