Hallelujah. No question about it. Matthew 24:29, “Immediately after the tribulation,” and the other one of the other gospels says “the great tribulation,” after the tribulation. Now, we’re always told that Jesus is going to come before the tribulation, and you really has to twist and rubber band scriptures to get that out of the Bible, you really do, but it’s a very popularized teaching, and, and, and Christians just accept it if it’s on the radio, TV, and they got nice clothes on and they can speak well, it must be true. But Jesus plainly said, after the tribulation of those days, “the sun shall be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven.” No scroll here, just the stars are falling from heaven. So there’s going to be a demonstration in the heavenlies, and then that’s the stars going dark. How, you know, when the sun goes dark, the moon goes dark, yeah, and the earth goes dark. Yeah. In Luke 21, same account, “signs in the sun, moon, and stars, and on earth.” Okay, on earth, earth, this is the who? There’s going to be distress, suffering, misery of who? The Gentiles. See, the church is going to be protected. Remember, we learned that God will what? Cover us. He will cover us. These death angels, these plagues, these things can’t touch it, he covers us like he did in Egypt, he’ll pass over us. “The distress of the Gentiles, with perplexity,” that means they can’t solve what’s going on, they’re puzzled, they can’t figure this out. You see, he’s going to show mankind that they are just human beings and he’s God. Now, they can’t figure this thing out, and believe me, they got their calculators, and they’re really, they’re really trying to figure this thing out, and they can’t. All right, “the sea and the waves roaring, and men’s hearts failing them for fear, for looking after those things coming on the earth.” God’s going to deal with the human [unclear] mentality before Christ comes. Okay, just continue with me: “for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” How many know we don’t fight against man, flesh and blood, but against principalities and powers and wickedness in high places? Okay, he’s going to expose the source of their thinking. See, there’s only two kinds of children in the world, the children of God and the children of Satan. Okay, when we follow God and do what’s right and preach his word, we are enemies of those who follow Satan and preach his philosophy, we’re clashing. And remember, Isaiah said there was going to be a time of peace on earth, and the lamb shall lay down with the lion, and so forth, a reverse evolution. Animals are not going to eat meat anymore. I mean, God’s going to do everything he can to get mankind’s attention and expose all their ideas, because he’s God and he can do this stuff. Amen. And does he need to? Yeah, he does need to, because mankind aren’t listening to the gospel being preached. So, “the powers of heaven,” then “they shall see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and glory.” So what happens before he comes? God demonstrating his power in the heavens, God dealing with the Gentiles to bring them to him, to get them out of that false science, in that humanistic religion where they are gone, and to bring them to himself, and we find in Revelation a multitude that cannot be numbered of Gentiles in heaven. Now, that’s power, folks, that’s a God. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Hallelujah. All he can do is snatch me out? Uh-uh. He’s going to do a lot more than snatch me out of this earth, he’s going to demonstrate to the world his power, his truth, for the whole purpose of bringing in a harvest of those that will listen, number one. God has ordained to deal with the Gentiles, and those who won’t repent, he will, they will die, that’s second death, in the lake of fire. But we found that many will when we preach the gospel and they hear and God demonstrates his power in the earth before he comes. And I want, boy, I’d love to be there. Wouldn’t you like to be there at that time where God’s doing his thing, and you’re like, “Moses, get him, God! Allelujah! Joshua, yeah, take that, Pharaoh! Yeah, I told you, [unclear], you should have listened.” See, we act like God never did these things before. He did do them before, in Egypt, and he, you know, he did them before, he rained rocks out of heaven to destroy armies, he demonstrated his power, he’s a supernatural God. About 10 or 15 years ago there was a woman in India. She was pregnant, her and her husband worked in India in the labor fields, they carried heavy loads, and if you didn’t show up for work, someone was there waiting in line to replace you. This woman’s pregnant, she’s working and carrying these heavy loads, building this construction project, she’s in her ninth month, and she’s carrying these heavy loads because she can’t dare, and her and her husband can’t dare quit, because they want this child to be born and they want this child to have the best chance of life they can, and so they know they need money to do that, cuz work is tough, big unemployment rate in India. So one day she’s working and the birth pains come. She works right through them, if she stops she’ll lose the job. Finally her water breaks, and then she knows that baby’s coming out of the canal, she goes off like she’s going to the bathroom, her husband goes with her, and that baby’s born, they cut the umbilical cord, wipe, wrap that baby up, put her around the mother like they do in the back there, you know, and she goes right back to working on that job. Why? Because she wants that baby to live. She puts her comfort, she puts her life on the line, cuz she wants, and her husband both want that baby to live. And I’m going to be emphasizing man and wife today instead of moms, I’m going to be emphasizing moms and dads. Folks, the humanists are winning the battle of the family. 40%, over 40% of kids are born to one-parent homes, 30% of Americans don’t even bother getting married. They’re changing the family structure, the Bible family structure. These two did whatever they could as a team, and, folks, mothers alone are not going to have the impact as a mother and a father will. Amen. Two are better than one, we need each other, and Father’s Day, I’m going to say the same thing, we need the family back to what God says it was, a man and a woman raising kids. Period. Hallelujah. And they did, they raised that baby, they were Christian people, that’s how I know the story, I got it from the missionary over there, couple in the church. Now, let’s go to the Middle East, where it’s a crime to be a Christian. Also a family pulls up, a family of five, they have a teenage daughter 17 years old, they have a 14-year-old boy and a young girl, they pull up to a roadblock trying to get to a refugee camp because they’re being persecuted where they’re at. The soldiers see the young girl, she’s mature, her breasts have grown, and she’s a young lady, and she’s a Christian, an infidel, and they tell that mother and father, “Leave your daughter here.” They plead with these three soldiers at the checkpoint, the mother even offers herself. But there’s a place where they knew if they didn’t stop they would just be shot and they’d have their daughter anyway. Now, they couldn’t do anything, but they could do this: go down the road, pull over to the side, shut the lights off, go back in the darkness around through the terrain to this shack where these soldiers lived, where they took their breaks, and sure enough they go there, they’ve got the daughter stripped naked, they’re molesting her, one of them’s in there molesting her, they go into that shed and they kill that soldier, they took his own gun and shot him cuz he was so involved in what he was doing he didn’t even notice him coming in, and then the two soldiers heard the shot and they come running in and they killed them too. Mom just laid them out. Why? Cuz she wanted her daughter to live. They put their life on the line so that their children could live, and specifically this young teenage girl went back to the car and drove away, got to the refugee camp, and, folks, that’s what God wants. The humanist, he wants them to live, and he’ll do anything, and he’s trying to move you to speak to them, to share the gospel with them, share truth with them. He wants them to live, he wants them to have eternal life, he wants them to know him.
How does he say God will win the Gentiles, and what does he say about the rapture and the tribulation?

1 Thessalonians 1:10: and to wait for His Son from heaven, whom He raised from the dead, even Jesus who delivers us from the wrath to come. Revelation 7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands, Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken. Luke 21:25-26: “And there will be signs in the sun, in the moon, and in the stars; and on the earth distress of nations, with perplexity, the sea and the waves roaring; men’s hearts failing them from fear and the expectation of those things which are coming on the earth, for the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
What are the two things God asks the Gentiles to do?
He says “hear number one and heed number two.”
Does he believe there is life on other planets?
No. He says “there is no life out there in space.”
What does he mean by “the army of the word”?
He says an army we forget about “is the word,” used “to convince people” and that “it’s not always swords and spears.”
What does he say Psalm 9:19 wants the Gentiles to know?
He says the prayer is to “put them in fear,” so that mankind knows “they’re just humans” and that God is “the supernatural God.”
What does he say the birthright is today?
He says “birthright to us today is being born again, born of the word, born of the Spirit.”
What does he say the oil and light in the ten virgins mean?
He says “the word is light, our right behavior is light,” and that the foolish virgins “had no word and they had no action to back up” it.
Who does he say Zion is?
He says “Zion is the church, Zion is the people of God.”
Does he say meteor showers fulfill the falling stars?
No. He says “don’t mistake these meteor showers we have for the fulfillment of this verse.”
Does he say he has to prove the Bible is true to skeptics?
No. He says “I don’t have to argue that the word of God is true,” and “I’m going to keep bringing you to the cross.”
How many times does he say the sun is darkened in the Bible?
He says “it says three times in Revelation that the sun’s going to be darkened,” and that Old Testament prophets spoke of it “five times.”
What does he say are the two ways to get eternal life?
He says the first is to “believe on Jesus, trust in him,” and the second is “keep the commandments,” and that preachers rarely teach it.
Where does he say Jesus is sitting now?
He says “he sits on the throne now… ever since he ascended.”
Does he say Christians should hate their enemies?
No. He says “we want to hate our enemies… no, no, God’s going to do things to get their attention so they can be delivered through Christ Jesus.”
What does he say God wants for those who reject him?
He says “he wants them to live, he wants them to have eternal life, he wants them to know him.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer begins in 1 Corinthians 15 with the gospel and the evidence for the resurrection, then teaches that grace is not only a favor but a power, “the divine influence upon the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer begins in 1 Corinthians 15 with the gospel and the evidence for the resurrection, then teaches that grace is not only a favor but a power, “the divine influence upon the heart,” that moved Paul to work. He follows grace through John 1, Luke 2, Luke 6, Acts 11 and Colossians 3, and asks whether our grace is increasing.
What responses to the gospel does Paul describe? (1 Corinthians 15:1-2)

Reading 1 Corinthians 15:1-2, he says there are two choices: “you can reject it or you can accept it.” He says “Receive means you accept it, you take it,” to stand means “you take your stand, you continue in it, you don’t waver,” and being saved means “you’re rescued, you’re set free from sin, from hell, from the lake of fire, and from the day of wrath.”
What responses to the gospel does Paul describe? (1 Corinthians 15:1-2)

We are in chapter 15, and in chapter 15, verse 1, Paul says, “I declare to you the gospel which I preached.” Now, there are four responses here to when he preached the gospel, and this is what the gospel should do. “Which you have received.” You accept it. See, you got two choices: you can reject it or you can accept it. Receive means you accept it, you take it. All right. Number two, “in which you stand.” You see, you take your stand, you continue in it, you don’t waver. Number three, “by which also you are saved.” You’re rescued, you’re set free from sin, from hell, from the lake of fire, and from the day of wrath. For instance, if God judged America in His anger to correct them, you would be rescued from that wrath of God, and then there’s a day of wrath coming at the end.
What responses to the gospel does Paul describe? (1 Corinthians 15:1-2)

1 Corinthians 15:1-2: Moreover, brethren, I declare to you the gospel which I preached to you, which also you received and in which you stand, by which also you are saved, if you hold fast that word which I preached to you—unless you believed in vain.
What is the gospel, and what does it mean to hold fast? (1 Corinthians 15:2-3)

He says to hold fast means “we hang on, we don’t give up, we don’t quit,” because “if you let it go, it doesn’t do you any good.” He says the gospel is that “Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,” which means the Old and New Testaments are both Scripture, and he says “the Old Testament is still for today.”
What is the gospel, and what does it mean to hold fast? (1 Corinthians 15:2-3)

Then He says, “if you hold fast.” See, we also hold fast, we hang on, we don’t give up, we don’t quit, to what was preached, this gospel that was preached, “unless you believed in vain,” or your belief was worthless. If you let it go, it doesn’t do you any good. And then he is going to tell us what the gospel is. He said, “For I delivered unto you first of all that which also I received: how that, number one, Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures.” Now, that means the Old Testament is considered Scriptures, and the New Testament is considered Scriptures, because the Gospels and the epistles talk about the death and burial and resurrection of Christ. So here is evidence that the canon, New Testament, is recognized as Scripture. Got it? You need to know that, because some churches say the new, the Old Testament is not for today. Uh, it is, the Old Testament is still for today.
What is the gospel, and what does it mean to hold fast? (1 Corinthians 15:2-3)
1 Corinthians 15:3: For I delivered to you first of all that which I also received: that Christ died for our sins according to the Scriptures,
What does he say about the burial and the third day? (1 Corinthians 15:4, Luke 24)

He says the gospel includes that Jesus “was buried” and “rose again the third day.” From the two disciples in Luke 24 who said it was “the third day since all these things happened,” he counts Friday, Saturday and Sunday and says, “These people are trying to keep Jesus in the grave for three 24-hour periods. It is ridiculous.” He says “Never diminish the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. It’s still the foundation of everything the Bible’s built on.”
What does he say about the burial and the third day? (1 Corinthians 15:4, Luke 24)

Now, number two, “he was buried.” He was put in the grave. “And that he rose again the third day according to the” what? Scriptures. Old Testament tells, Scriptures tell us that, and New Testament Scriptures tell us that. Now, he rose what day? Third day. Luke 24, on the road to Damascus, there they were, two, two disciples that were talking with Jesus, didn’t know it was Jesus, and they were telling Jesus that this is the third day since all these things happened, that he was died, he was killed, he was in the grave, and then he rose the third day before sunup. Okay, if Sunday was the third day, then what would Saturday be? Second day. And what would Friday be? Third day, the first day, I’m sorry, first, second, third. These people are trying to keep Jesus in the grave for three 24-hour periods. It is ridiculous. This Scripture plainly tells us that he died on what day? Friday. He was in the grave on what day? Saturday. He arose on what day? Yeah. When he went into the grave, he went down into, uh, where the dead souls were and preached to them before the flood and, uh, gave them the gospel. And so that is the gospel. It’s all about Jesus’ death, burial, and resurrection, and that’s the power of the gospel. That’s the, that’s the power that sets us free. Never diminish the death, burial, and resurrection of Jesus Christ. It’s still the foundation of everything the Bible’s built on. Okay.
What does he say about the burial and the third day? (1 Corinthians 15:4, Luke 24)

1 Corinthians 15:4: and that He was buried, and that He rose again the third day according to the Scriptures, Luke 24:13-21: Now behold, two of them were traveling that same day to a village called Emmaus, which was seven miles from Jerusalem. And they talked together of all these things which had happened. So it was, while they conversed and reasoned, that Jesus Himself drew near and went with them. But their eyes were restrained, so that they did not know Him. And He said to them, “What kind of conversation is this that you have with one another as you walk and are sad?” Then the one whose name was Cleopas answered and said to Him, “Are You the only stranger in Jerusalem, and have You not known the things which happened there in these days?” And He said to them, “What things?” So they said to Him, “The things concerning Jesus of Nazareth, who was a Prophet mighty in deed and word before God and all the people, and how the chief priests and our rulers delivered Him to be condemned to death, and crucified Him. But we were hoping that it was He who was going to redeem Israel. Indeed, besides all this, today is the third day since these things happened.
What evidence does Paul give that Jesus rose? (1 Corinthians 15:5-8)

He says Paul lists those who saw Jesus after the resurrection, including “500 brethren at one time,” and last Paul himself. He says “there’s over 500 people that witnessed Jesus alive and well on planet Earth after he died,” and “these people that want to challenge the Bible and all this, they have to ignore these facts.”
What evidence does Paul give that Jesus rose? (1 Corinthians 15:5-8)

Now he gives us some proof that Jesus rose, some evidence, some proof. In verse 5, “he was seen by [unclear], or Peter, then by the 12.” Now, you know there’s not 12 now, don’t you? How many are there? 11. So how did Judas see Jesus when Jesus went down to preach to those that were in the holding pen of the earth? That, yeah, yeah, he saw him a little too late, huh? Anyway. “And then by 500 brethren at one time, and then by James, and then by all the apostles. Then the last of all he was seen by me as one born out of due time.” And so he’s saying these people saw Jesus after the resurrection. There’s over 500 people that witnessed Jesus alive and well on planet Earth after he died. Now, how many you know that’s a good evidence? Hallelujah. These people that want to challenge the Bible and all this, they have to ignore these facts. You see?
What evidence does Paul give that Jesus rose? (1 Corinthians 15:5-8)

1 Corinthians 15:5-8: and that He was seen by Cephas, then by the twelve. After that He was seen by over five hundred brethren at once, of whom the greater part remain to the present, but some have fallen asleep. After that He was seen by James, then by all the apostles. Then last of all He was seen by me also, as by one born out of due time.
What does Paul say about the grace that made him who he was? (1 Corinthians 15:9-11)

Reading Paul, he says “I’m the least of all the apostles” and “not worthy to be called an apostle because I persecuted the church of God,” yet “by the grace of God I am what I am.” He points out that “labored” means work, and reads “I labored more abundantly than all the rest, yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.”
What does Paul say about the grace that made him who he was? (1 Corinthians 15:9-11)

Now he’s going to say something that’s going to be very powerful here. “I’m the least of all the apostles, who I’m not worthy to be called an apostle because I persecuted the church of God.” Now I’m going to jump down to verse 11. “Whether it were I or they,” these 500 and some people, “so we preached, and so you” what? Believed. You trusted in that gospel, you accepted it, you received it. Now he says, “I’m not worthy to be called an apostle, but by the grace,” say the word, grace, “by the grace of God I am what I am.” So he was an apostle by what? The grace of God. “And his grace toward me was not profitless,” in vain, “but I labored.” Say the word, labored. What’s another word for labor? Work. Yeah, you got intelligent people out there. I tell you, “I labored.” Watch this, watch this closely, because Paul knows what he’s talking about. “I labored more abundantly than all the rest, yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.” So this grace is what moving him to work.
What does Paul say about the grace that made him who he was? (1 Corinthians 15:9-11)

1 Corinthians 15:9-11: For I am the least of the apostles, who am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the church of God. But by the grace of God I am what I am, and His grace toward me was not in vain; but I labored more abundantly than they all, yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me. Therefore, whether it was I or they, so we preach and so you believed.
Does he say grace moves us to work? (Ephesians 2:8-9)

He says that although we are saved by grace through faith and not by works, “grace here moves us to what? Work.” He says “grace isn’t just something, you know, bestowed upon us, it also is a power that moves us,” and that “this grace was a power that worked in their life to be an example and a light for Jesus Christ.”
Does he say grace moves us to work? (Ephesians 2:8-9)

And you, you need to hear that, because this Scripture that everybody quotes, “We’re saved by grace through faith, and that not of itself, it is the gift of God, not by works, lest any man should boast.” But grace here moves us to what? Work. Are you there? Was, did Paul have to work to preach the gospel to the Corinthians? Yeah, he had to put forth some effort. And see, grace gave him a desire, I, I, to, to help people, to change people, to get the message out to people. See, grace isn’t just something, you know, bestowed upon us, it also is a power that moves us. Do you see that? See, so Paul had the grace of God that moved him to work for Christ, to preach the gospel, and to live for Christ. You never hear of the apostles running off with a church secretary, taking the church’s money, having a nervous breakdown, you never hear that stuff, getting drunk. Why? Because this grace was a power that worked in their life to be an example and a light for Jesus Christ. Hallelujah. Ain’t that powerful?
Does he say grace moves us to work? (Ephesians 2:8-9)
Ephesians 2:8-9: For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast.

He gives the lexicon definition as “graciousness of manner, behavior, or act” and “especially the divine influence or power upon the heart,” and says the heart is “The mind, the emotions, and the will.” He says “grace shows itself by how you live,” like a reflection in a mirror. He says the King James translates the same word as acceptable, benefit, favor, gift, joy, liberality, pleasure and thank.

Now let’s take a look at grace. The definition of grace in the lexicons is “graciousness of manner, behavior, or act, whether literal, figuratively, or spiritual.” Okay, then the definition says “especially the divine influence or power upon the heart,” the divine enablement upon the heart. Now, what is the heart? The mind, the emotions, and the will. Yeah, so grace has a what? An influence, an impact on our mind, on our emotions, and our will, our desire to do things, and its reflection in life. Now, we all want know, know what a reflection is. You’re looking in the mirror, you’re seeing a what? Reflection of yourself. And what does grace do? Grace shows by how you live. See, grace shows itself by how you live. Ain’t that powerful? Now it’s used in King James as “acceptable,” a benefit, “the benefit of God was upon him,” “the acceptable of God was on him,” “the favor of God was on him,” “the gift of God was on him,” “the graciousness of God was on him,” the joy of God, the liberality, the pleasure, and the thank. It’s all translated in these different words, but it’s the same word for what? Grace. That divine influence in our life, and it shows by how we behave, how we live. Now, folks, that’s a powerful God. Hallelujah. Grace is a powerful thing. If grace is that powerful, then it would behoove us to get it. All right.
What does “full of grace and truth” mean, and what did grace do for Peter? (John 1:14, 1:17)

He reads that “the Word became flesh and dwelt among us” and was full of grace and truth, so receiving Christ means “receiving what? Grace and truth.” He says the disciples went back to fishing, and “Grace came after them.” Although the Bible says “If you deny me, I will deny you before my Father,” he says “grace moved God to reach out to Peter and bring him back.”
What does “full of grace and truth” mean, and what did grace do for Peter? (John 1:14, 1:17)

Now, you know more about the Bible definition when you see its use in the Scripture. All right, now watch this. “The Word became flesh and dwelt among us,” which is Jesus. We all know that, right? Jesus was the Word, Jesus was God, He became flesh, dwelt among us, and He was full of what? Grace and truth. So when I receive Christ in my life, I’m receiving what? Grace and truth. Hallelujah. And we can, we can back that up. When Jesus told them, “I got to go away, I will come again,” so he died and he what? Rose and came back to them. See, that’s truth. He told him the truth. Right? But you know, Peter denied Him, Peter cursed first. Uh, Peter challenged Him, and then Peter got all the disciples to go back to work. They went back to fishing after He rose from the grave. And what did grace do? Grace came after them. See, Jesus came after them. See, Jesus is filled with grace. See, He’s going to do everything He can to get you to reach the maturity and the completeness of His goals and His promises. Ain’t that beautiful? See, He kept His word, He spoke the truth, and then what He didn’t, He put aside the fact that Peter denied Him, and the Bible says, “If you deny me, I will deny you before my Father,” yet grace moved God to reach out to Peter and bring him back. And, folks, if, if Peter can do something that cannot be forgiven, how much more will God reach out to us in our failures and in our, uh, amen. So grace is important. Truth’s also important. Hallelujah. Now, “the law was given through Moses,” in John 1:17, “but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.” All right, that divine influence came through Jesus Christ.
What does “full of grace and truth” mean, and what did grace do for Peter? (John 1:14, 1:17)

John 1:14: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we beheld His glory, the glory as of the only begotten of the Father, full of grace and truth. Matthew 10:33: But whoever denies Me before men, him I will also deny before My Father who is in heaven. John 1:17: For the law was given through Moses, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
How did Jesus increase in grace? (Luke 2:40, 52)

He says Luke 2:40 shows “the grace of God was” upon Jesus, and in verse 52 “Jesus increased in wisdom,” and “He increased in grace” with God and men. He says “grace moved Him to please the Father,” and also to “touch people.” He says “it’s grace that should drive us to church so we can grow and so we can what? Help others grow.”
How did Jesus increase in grace? (Luke 2:40, 52)

Now Luke 2:40, speaking of Jesus when he’s like 12 years old, the grace of God was what? Upon Him. Now, He was what? Filled with grace, but in His human form He was. See, the grace of God was upon Him, and look at verse 52. “Jesus increased in wisdom,” He increased in favor. What’s that word, favor? Grace. He increased in grace, look at this, “with God and men.” You see, grace moved Him to please the Father. Jesus said, “I do nothing except what I see and hear of the Father,” but grace also moved Him to what? Touch people. See, it’s grace that should drive us to church so we can grow and so we can what? Help others grow. Grace will give you a concern for other people. Amen. See, we don’t come to church just for ourself, we come for others too.
How did Jesus increase in grace? (Luke 2:40, 52)
Luke 2:40: And the Child grew and became strong in spirit, filled with wisdom; and the grace of God was upon Him. Luke 2:52: And Jesus increased in wisdom and stature, and in favor with God and men.
How does he say grace is different from a favor? (Luke 6:32)

He says doing a neighbor favors or giving him money “doesn’t change him,” but “if I influence him to change to a better man, that is what grace is about.” He says “God’s just not out to do us favors, folks. He’s out to make us in His likeness and His image.” From Luke 6:32 he says “the word thank is the what word? Grace,” and that grace is a “power by God to treat people better than they’re treating you.”
How does he say grace is different from a favor? (Luke 6:32)

And so grace is that power that moves us. Now, we’re not talking about the baptism of the Holy Ghost, we’re talking about grace. Grace isn’t some, you know, “the favor of God was upon him.” You know, I can do Mr. [unclear] here a favor. He lives close to me. I lend him a lawn mower. Not a lawnmower, he’s got a better one than I do. I lend him my weed eater, and I lend him this, and I lend him that. That doesn’t change him, that doesn’t make his character any better than it was before I’m doing. I could give him $1,000 dollars, and it’s not going to change his character. I did him a favor. Are you there? But if I influence him to change to a better man, that is what grace is about. Hallelujah. See, God’s just not out to do us favors, folks. He’s out to make us in His likeness and His image, make, make us a light to the world where people can see God in us. How many could use a little increase in grace? Yeah. You know, if Jesus increased in grace, who was full of grace, how many know we should strive to increase in grace, this grace that moves us to please God and to help people? Now let’s continue the use of the word. Luke 6:32, “If you love those that love you, what thank have you?” And the word thank is the what word? Grace. “What grace have you if you just love people that love you?” See, “if you lend to people that lend to you, what grace have you?” See, “if you do good to people that do good to you, what grace have you?” See, grace is a, a power by God to treat people better than they’re treating you, to give someone that needs something, not even expecting it back. See, that’s grace in action, the reflection in life. “You’re opposing me, I’m going to love you.” And He says, “but love your enemies and do good.”
How does he say grace is different from a favor? (Luke 6:32)
Luke 6:32: “But if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
What did Barnabas see at Antioch? (Acts 11:23)

He says grace is not something to “just take it as this favor word”: “He more than favors you, He is empowering you to please Him and to help others in this life.” In Acts 11:23 he says Barnabas “had seen the grace of God” because the Greeks were “now serving God and repenting from their sins and turning to what’s right.” He says grace “is a free gift, but you got to accept it and use it,” and that “He’s going to keep after you.”
What did Barnabas see at Antioch? (Acts 11:23)

I submit to you this morning, grace is a very powerful thing, and we shouldn’t just take it lightly, and we shouldn’t just take it as this favor word. “No matter what, or do God favors me.” No, He more than favors you, He is empowering you to please Him and to help others in this life. Now, Acts 11:23, Barnabas went down to Antioch. They had preached Christ to the [unclear], the Greeks, the Greek cultured people, and many of these Greeks believed it. It said before that they had only been preaching to Jews only, but here it says at Antioch they preached to the Greeks, see, the non-Jews, the Greek-speaking people, culture. And so when Barnabas came and had seen, see that word, he had seen the grace of God. Remember, the definition was reflection in life. See, he saw the grace of God. Why? Because he saw these Greeks now serving God and repenting from their sins and turning to what’s right. He saw the grace of God in evidence in the Greeks. Isn’t that powerful? The grace is a very powerful thing, and too many people just got this favor thing, and they don’t understand the power that’s in the grace of God, and it’s a free gift that He gives us. Grace, the Bible says, is a free gift, but you got to accept it and use it. See, Mr. Barnes could lend me his lawnmower, but if I never used it to mow my lawn, it what? Doesn’t do any good. Hallelujah. Now, “and he was glad, and encouraged them all with purpose of heart to continue with the Lord.” See, they had turned to the Lord. Isn’t that powerful? Should grace be seen in our life? Yes, church. Not only will Jesus go to the extreme to influence you to live for Him, I don’t care if you’re committing adultery, drunkenness, He’s going to keep after you. Why? ‘Cause He’s full of grace, and He wants to win you back, He wants to improve your life. But grace also is a power that works in me, that works in you, to help people and live a life that’s pleasing to God. Now, that changes everything.
What did Barnabas see at Antioch? (Acts 11:23)
Acts 11:23: When he came and had seen the grace of God, he was glad, and encouraged them all that with purpose of heart they should continue with the Lord.
How does grace relate to worship and the word? (Colossians 3:16, Acts 20:32)

Reading Colossians 3:16, he says singing “with grace in your hearts” means singing with “the divine influence of God.” He says “Grace wants you to worship God. Why? Because it’s a principle of God that brings His presence. When His presence comes, you start taking on His nature.” Reading Acts 20:32, he says the Scriptures are “grace, that divine influence upon your mind, your emotions, and your will.”
How does grace relate to worship and the word? (Colossians 3:16, Acts 20:32)

Colossians 3:16, “Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.” Singing with favor, singing with benefits, or singing with the divine influence of God upon you. Amen. See, and it agrees with the Holy Spirit. See, the Holy Spirit came upon them, the Holy Spirit was with them, and they did things by the Spirit. Here, grace comes upon, grace is with us, grace is working in us, and it’s the same result. We want to worship God. People that don’t want to worship God, they need an increase of grace. Yeah. Grace wants you to worship God. Why? Because it’s a principle of God that brings His presence. When His presence comes, you start taking on His nature. Hallelujah. Powerful, very powerful. Now, Acts 20:32, “I commend you to God, and I commend you to the word of grace.” Oh, see, the Scriptures are what? Grace, that divine influence upon your mind, your emotions, and your will to make you into someone who can act different than the people of the world. Isn’t that beautiful? And again, we’re not talking about the baptism of the Holy Ghost, we’re talking about grace. So even if you reject the infilling of the Holy Ghost, there’s still power in what? Grace. Power. Now, what does this grace do? Grace is able to what? Build you up. Build you up to what? His likeness and His image. He’s out to make you a light to the world, that people can see your good works and bring glory and honor to Jesus Christ. Isn’t that beautiful? Hallelujah. See, grace not only worked in Paul, drove him to work, but grace built Paul up to be the apostle that God had intended him to be.
How does grace relate to worship and the word? (Colossians 3:16, Acts 20:32)

Colossians 3:16: Let the word of Christ dwell in you richly in all wisdom, teaching and admonishing one another in psalms and hymns and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord. Acts 20:32: “So now, brethren, I commend you to God and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up and give you an inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
Can everyone be a light to the world, and what inheritance does grace give?

He says “you may not be an apostle, but you can still be a light to the world. You can be a disciple of Christ.” He says someone who stays a drunkard after being saved would show no “reflection” of grace, but at Antioch “he saw the change in their life.” He says grace “will give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified,” and that Jesus “has activated the will” through His death and resurrection.
Can everyone be a light to the world, and what inheritance does grace give?

Now, you may not be an apostle, but you can still be a light to the world. You can be a disciple of Christ. Can’t we all be disciples? Can we all come to maturity? Yes. We may not be a prophet, we may not be an apostle, we may not be a pastor, but we can be a light to the world. We can be a disciple of Christ that people can see the results of grace in. See, if I’m a drunkard and I get saved and I stay a drunkard, when Barnabas come, he would not have what? Seen the grace of God. Why? ‘Cause there’s no reflection. See, but there was a reflection when he went down there to Antioch. He saw the change in their life. And, folks, that’s what grace will do to all of us. And this grace will give you an inheritance among all them which are sanctified. Now, we have an inheritance: Jesus Christ, the gifts of the Spirit, the fruit of the Spirit, the wisdom and knowledge, understanding and counsel and strength, and all these things are part of our inheritance. And he says grace is able to give you, to obtain this inheritance that God has promised, because Jesus, Jesus died on the cross. There cannot be an inheritance without the death of the one who wrote the will, and he’s dead, folks. And he come back to alive, and so we, he has activated the will, and we can have our inheritance if we will embrace grace and let grace work in our life.
Can everyone be a light to the world, and what inheritance does grace give?
Acts 20:32: “So now, brethren, I commend you to God and to the word of His grace, which is able to build you up and give you an inheritance among all those who are sanctified.
Are you increasing in grace, or is your grace limited?

He says some Christians “just take favor, go to heaven, wait for the rapture,” while others “grow in grace” and so have more influence in “changing people’s lives and bringing them to Christ.” He asks, “are you increasing in grace, or is your grace limited?” and says grace “will change that and put a focus on Jesus and his focus on others.”
Are you increasing in grace, or is your grace limited?

See, why is it that some Christians are concerned about others, are concerned about, about going to church, and are concerned about growing? They’ve entered into a dimension of grace. See, that’s influencing them. Others, they just take favor, go to heaven, wait for the rapture, that’s it. They do what they want, they stay home, they don’t pray, they don’t, you know, they can’t win souls to Christ because they don’t know the word or anything else. But others, they respond to that grace, and they grow in grace, and the more they grow, the more influence they have in helping people and changing people’s lives and bringing them to Christ. My question, or the, I should say the Holy Spirit’s question to us this morning is: are you increasing in grace, or is your grace limited? If you don’t like things or you, you don’t want to do things, you just don’t do them. You got no influence of God to overcome your personal desires and wishes and laziness and attitude and beliefs. Everything’s got to be for you and focused on you. Grace will change that and put a focus on Jesus and his focus on others to come to him and grow in him.
He says “Receive means you accept it, you take it.”
What does he say it means to hold fast to the gospel?
He says “we hang on, we don’t give up, we don’t quit,” and that if you let it go, “it doesn’t do you any good.”
Does he say the Old Testament is still for today?
Yes. He says some churches say it is not, but “the Old Testament is still for today.”
Which days does he count for the burial and resurrection?
He says Jesus died on Friday, was in the grave on Saturday, and arose on Sunday, and he calls trying “to keep Jesus in the grave for three 24-hour periods” ridiculous.
How many people does he say saw Jesus after the resurrection?
He says “there’s over 500 people that witnessed Jesus alive and well on planet Earth after he died.”
He asks “What’s another word for labor? Work.” and says the grace of God was with Paul as he labored.
Does he say grace is only something given to us?
No. He says “it also is a power that moves us.”
How does he describe grace as a divine influence?
He says it is “the divine influence or power upon the heart,” and the heart is “The mind, the emotions, and the will.”
What does he say grace did for Peter?
He says “grace moved God to reach out to Peter and bring him back,” even though Peter had denied Him.
What does he say about Jesus increasing in grace?
He says “He increased in grace” with God and men, and that grace moved Him to please the Father and to touch people.
How does he say grace differs from a favor?
He says a favor “doesn’t change him,” but “if I influence him to change to a better man, that is what grace is about.”
Does he say grace is a free gift?
Yes. He says grace “is a free gift, but you got to accept it and use it.”
What does he say grace does for worship?
He says “Grace wants you to worship God,” and that when His presence comes, “you start taking on His nature.”
Does he say everyone can be a disciple?
Yes. He says “you may not be an apostle, but you can still be a light to the world. You can be a disciple of Christ.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power is a real experience separate from salvation and water baptism. He starts with John 7:38-39 and Jesus as the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches that the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power is a real experience separate from salvation and water baptism. He starts with John 7:38-39 and Jesus as the baptizer, covers prophecy, visions and the names of the Holy Spirit, then walks through the accounts in Acts of Pentecost, the believers in Samaria, Cornelius’s household and the disciples at Ephesus. He also speaks about unity in worship, mistakes in Spirit-filled churches, and the purpose of the Spirit’s power.
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

He says there is “an experience in God called the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power,” not just something at Pentecost, at salvation or at water baptism. He reads John 7:38-39 as a promise to believers, and says the criteria for having the Holy Ghost is “Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated.” The Spirit flows from “your belly, innermost being,” and “it’s not a ceremony, it’s not a ritual, it’s a real experience.”
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

They told me that Holy Spirit baptism was one time on the day of Pentecost, or it was when you get saved, or it was when you got water baptized. And you people need to know how to answer this stuff, and you also need to know that there is an experience in God called the baptism of the Holy Ghost with power that is vitally important to your life, to the church life, and what God is doing in the earth. Okay, and I’m going to give you biology this morning. Are you ready? John 7:38-39. It is a promise to believers. Now, the Holy Spirit is called the Holy Ghost, Holy Spirit, Spirit of Truth, Comforter, My Spirit, and we’re going to give you the facts of the Holy Spirit. All right, nothing but facts. “He that believes on Me.” Okay, how many of you believe on Jesus? Where’s the rest of you? Huh, now. Okay, John 3:16 says, “He that believes on Me shall not perish but have everlasting life.” Same statement here, but instead of everlasting life, He says, “As the Scripture has said, out of his belly shall flow rivers of living water.” And this spake He of the Spirit, which they that believe on Him should receive, for the Holy Ghost was not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified. He hadn’t died and risen again, and so the Holy Spirit hadn’t been poured out on all flesh yet. But what’s the criteria for having the Holy Ghost? Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated. All right, and where will we experience this Holy Ghost? Out of your belly, innermost being. You’re going to experience it in that inner man that you really are, that spirit that’s really inside that body. Let me just share with you here a minute. It said, “As the Scripture has said” in the Old Testament. In Job 32:18, Elihu said, “I am full of the matter, the spirit within me constrains me. Behold, my belly is as wine which hath no vent, it is ready to burst like new wine bottles.” See, in the Old Testament Scriptures God already said He was going to do this. All right, and it’s going to pour out of our innermost being. It’s not a ceremony, it’s not a ritual, it’s a real experience. In Isaiah 58:11: “You shall be like a watered garden and like a spring of water whose waters fail not.” Hallelujah. And so this is the promise of that in John 7:38.
What is the baptism of the Holy Ghost, and what does John 7:38-39 promise?

John 7:38-39: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” But this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in Him would receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified. John 3:16: For God so loved the world that He gave His only begotten Son, that whoever believes in Him should not perish but have everlasting life. Job 32:18-19: For I am full of words; The spirit within me compels me. Indeed my belly is like wine that has no vent; It is ready to burst like new wineskins. Isaiah 58:11: The LORD will guide you continually, And satisfy your soul in drought, And strengthen your bones; You shall be like a watered garden, And like a spring of water, whose waters do not fail.
Who baptizes in the Holy Ghost, what is the power for, and what does it mean to be a witness? (Luke 3:16; 24:49; Acts 1:8; 22:15)

He says “Jesus is the baptizer in the Holy Ghost,” who “shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire,” which is “what happened on the day of Pentecost.” He says “we are clothed with power when the Holy Ghost comes upon us,” and that the Holy Ghost coming upon you means “we put it on like a coat.” He adds that “a witness is someone who has seen or experienced facts,” and “we are proof that His salvation works.”
Who baptizes in the Holy Ghost, what is the power for, and what does it mean to be a witness? (Luke 3:16; 24:49; Acts 1:8; 22:15)

We find that Jesus is the baptizer in the Holy Ghost. All right, Luke 3:16: “I indeed baptize you with water, but One mightier than I comes,” this is John the Baptist talking, “the laces of whose shoes I am not worthy to unloose. He shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire.” And that’s what happened on the day of Pentecost, tongues of fire, baptism of the Holy Ghost. All right, so Jesus is the baptizer, Jesus is the sender. Luke 24:49: “I send the promise of My Father upon you, but you wait in Jerusalem until you be clothed with power from on high.” You see, we receive and we are clothed with power when the Holy Ghost comes upon us. Acts 1:8: “You shall receive power after the Holy Ghost is come upon you.” You see, the Scriptures don’t always use “baptized in the Holy Ghost” and “filled with the Holy Ghost.” It also uses a statement that the Holy Ghost comes upon you, so we put it on like a coat. “And you shall be witnesses unto Me.” Everybody uses that as we’re witnessing to the world, in Jerusalem, Samaria, Judea, and the uttermost parts of the earth, but it isn’t stated that way. It’s “witnesses unto Me.” Now, a witness is someone who has seen or experienced facts. And so “witnesses unto Me,” we experience His salvation, we see His truths, we experience the baptism of the Holy Ghost, we experience water baptism. Witnesses unto Him. Are you there? In Acts 22:15, God tells Paul, “You shall be His witnesses unto all men of what you have seen and heard.” Now here He’s saying, Paul, you’re going to go and be witnesses of what you’ve seen and heard. So Paul had the first what? See truth and hear truth, possess truth before he could go and be a witness to people that didn’t know the truth. Have you got it? See, first we’ve got to see, we’ve got to hear, we got to possess. That makes us witnesses unto Him. See, we are proof that His salvation works. We are proof, and then He sends us as witnesses to the world.
Who baptizes in the Holy Ghost, what is the power for, and what does it mean to be a witness? (Luke 3:16; 24:49; Acts 1:8; 22:15)

Luke 3:16: John answered, saying to all, “I indeed baptize you with water; but One mightier than I is coming, whose sandal strap I am not worthy to loose. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. Luke 24:49: Behold, I send the Promise of My Father upon you; but tarry in the city of Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high.” Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” Acts 22:15: For you will be His witness to all men of what you have seen and heard.
Who is the Spirit poured out on, and what does “prophesy” mean in Acts 2:17?

He reads Acts 2:17 and says the Holy Ghost is “God’s Spirit,” poured out “upon all flesh,” so “you can be baptized, filled with, have the Holy Ghost come upon you with power.” He says “prophesy” there “just simply means speaking by the inspiration of the Spirit,” and he asks who could use a tongue “spoke by the inspiration of the Spirit instead of the inspiration of your emotions.”
Who is the Spirit poured out on, and what does “prophesy” mean in Acts 2:17?

It is the Spirit of God with natural, supernatural signs. Okay, it is the Spirit of God. Acts 2:17: “It shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, I will pour out,” whose Spirit? My Spirit. So the Holy Ghost is whose Spirit? God’s Spirit. Are you with me? All right, “upon all flesh.” How many flesh? All. So you can be baptized, filled with, have the Holy Ghost come upon you with power. “Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy.” “Prophesy” there just simply means speaking by the inspiration of the Spirit. How many could use a tongue that’s spoke by the inspiration of the Spirit instead of the inspiration of your emotions? Yeah. See, this thing is important. This Holy Spirit is very important. “Your sons and daughters shall prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men shall dream dreams.” Now these are indications of the manifestations of the Spirit of God.
Who is the Spirit poured out on, and what does “prophesy” mean in Acts 2:17?

Acts 2:17-18: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy.
What is the difference between prophesying and predicting, and what kind of visions does he want? (Acts 21:9; 1 Corinthians 14:3)

He says Philip’s daughters prophesied as “they spoke by the inspiration of the Spirit,” and “there’s a big difference when you go into predicting” and claiming the office of a prophet: “if you miss one time, the Bible says you’re a false prophet.” He says “prophesying for edification, exhortation, and comfort is totally different.” On visions, he wants the kind Peter and Stephen had, “not pizza nightmares,” and of the pizza kind he says “there’s no message in it, there’s no edification in it.”
What is the difference between prophesying and predicting, and what kind of visions does he want? (Acts 21:9; 1 Corinthians 14:3)

In Acts 21:9, Philip had four daughters, virgins, which did prophesy. Okay, they spoke by the inspiration of the Spirit. Agabus, he was the office of a prophet. There’s a big difference when you go into predicting. You are saying, “I’m in the office of a prophet. I’m like Jeremiah, I’m like Isaiah, I’m like John the Baptist, I’m like Jesus, I’m like Paul,” and if you miss one time, the Bible says you’re a false prophet and we’re not to fear you. Now, prophesying for edification, exhortation, and comfort is totally different. And so somebody over there brought up a false prophet to me, and I said, “What name did you say?” And he repeated the name. I said, “That guy’s a false prophet. I know that guy.” I said, “He gives Spirit-filled people a bad name, and those guys with him are false prophets, because they miss.” And when you predict that something’s going to happen in your name and you miss, that’s it, it’s over. Could that be an amen? And Spirit-filled people need to stop being in fantasy land, thinking these guys have some kind of connection with God, and they are missing. They are prophesying and they are missing in the name of the Holy Ghost, and it does give us a bad name. Are you there? So, visions. Remember, Peter had visions that the Gentiles were not unclean, and he had a vision of an angel coming to him in jail and bringing him out. Stephen was full of the Holy Ghost, he had a vision of Jesus standing at the right hand of God and saw the glory of God. Folks, that’s the kind of visions that we need, not pizza nightmares. Most people come to me with visions, and I just tell them, “Listen, did you have pizza last night and have a pizza nightmare?” There’s no message in it, there’s no edification in it, there’s nothing but you trying to show your kind of spiritual nothing, that you think you’re something that’s not. The visions. Other names of the Holy Spirit.
What is the difference between prophesying and predicting, and what kind of visions does he want? (Acts 21:9; 1 Corinthians 14:3)

Acts 21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied. 1 Corinthians 14:3: But he who prophesies speaks edification and exhortation and comfort to men. Acts 10:9-16: The next day, as they went on their journey and drew near the city, Peter went up on the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour. Then he became very hungry and wanted to eat; but while they made ready, he fell into a trance and saw heaven opened and an object like a great sheet bound at the four corners, descending to him and let down to the earth. In it were all kinds of four-footed animals of the earth, wild beasts, creeping things, and birds of the air. And a voice came to him, “Rise, Peter; kill and eat.” But Peter said, “Not so, Lord! For I have never eaten anything common or unclean.” And a voice spoke to him again the second time, “What God has cleansed you must not call common.” This was done three times. And the object was taken up into heaven again. Acts 12:7-10: Now behold, an angel of the Lord stood by him, and a light shone in the prison; and he struck Peter on the side and raised him up, saying, “Arise quickly!” And his chains fell off his hands. Then the angel said to him, “Gird yourself and tie on your sandals”; and so he did. And he said to him, “Put on your garment and follow me.” So he went out and followed him, and did not know that what was done by the angel was real, but thought he was seeing a vision. When they were past the first and the second guard posts, they came to the iron gate that leads to the city, which opened to them of its own accord; and they went out and went down one street, and immediately the angel departed from him. Acts 7:55-56: But he, being full of the Holy Spirit, gazed into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God, and said, “Look! I see the heavens opened and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God!”
What does “Comforter” mean, and what is the Holy Spirit like? (John 14:16)

He explains “Comforter” as “a legal adviser, an advocate, a counselor, a helper.” He says the Holy Ghost is “not out to condemn you,” not “out to punish you,” but “out to change you and help you in your time of need,” and that “there’s nothing weird about the Holy Ghost.” He says the Spirit will not forsake you, and “He’s a Spirit of Truth, He only speaks truth and only drives you to truth.”
What does “Comforter” mean, and what is the Holy Spirit like? (John 14:16)

John 14:16: “I will pray the Father and He will give you another Comforter.” Okay, “Comforter” is a legal adviser, an advocate, a counselor, a helper. How many could use a counselor and a helper? Yes. And when it comes to God’s Word, could you use a little legal advice instead of men’s? Yes, this Holy Ghost is important. Okay, He’s the Comforter. He’s not out to condemn you, He’s not out to punish you, He is out to change you and help you in your time of need. There’s nothing weird about the Holy Ghost. Just because some people make it weird doesn’t mean the Holy Ghost is weird. “Now He will abide with you” for how long? Yeah, see, Jesus said, “I will never leave you or forsake you,” and the Holy Ghost won’t forsake you. He’s going to stick with you. And He’s called the Spirit of Truth. Is He ever going to lie to you? Would He ever give a false prophecy? No. You can’t give a false prophecy and say it’s from the Spirit or from God. He’s a Spirit of Truth, He only speaks truth and only drives you to truth.
What does “Comforter” mean, and what is the Holy Spirit like? (John 14:16)

John 14:16-17: And I will pray the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may abide with you forever— the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him; but you know Him, for He dwells with you and will be in you. Hebrews 13:5: Let your conduct be without covetousness; be content with such things as you have. For He Himself has said, “I will never leave you nor forsake you.”
Can people grieve, quench, resist or reject the Holy Ghost? (John 14:26)

Reading John 14:26, he asks “who has to really teach you? The Holy Spirit.” He says “we can grieve the Holy Ghost, we can quench the Holy Ghost, and we can resist the Holy Ghost,” and that you grieve Him “when you live a bad lifestyle.” He says you can be “a religious person and actually reject the Holy Spirit convicting you,” and shares that as a young man he would “just shove that Holy Ghost away” until “He got my attention, and it’s been a great life ever since.”
Can people grieve, quench, resist or reject the Holy Ghost? (John 14:26)

Okay, John 14:26: “The Comforter, which is the Holy Ghost, will teach you” what? “All things.” See, I can get up here and I can give you Bible knowledge, I can guide you through the Bible and teach you, but who has to really teach you? The Holy Spirit. You got to let the Holy Spirit enlighten you, open your spiritual understanding. So you can sit there and turn me off, you can sit there and turn the Holy Ghost off. In fact, I got up here, we can grieve the Holy Ghost, we can quench the Holy Ghost, and we can resist the Holy Ghost, and so many people resist Him. Why does he say unity in worship matters for God’s presence in a church? (Acts 1:14–2:2)

Now, the fulfilled part. Okay, we’re going to show you that it’s a separate event from water baptism, it’s a separate event from salvation. They were all in one accord in prayer and supplication. Okay, here’s how to get God’s presence in a church. We need to be in one accord and in worship. How do you stay in one accord? Who do you follow? The song leader. If the song leader claps their hands, you clap your hands. Song leader raises the hand, you raise your hand. See, that way we can be in unity. It’s that simple, church. It’s not a mystery. If the song leader asks you to stand, what do we do? Stand, unless there’s something physically wrong. There’s no problem if you physically can’t stand. And so when we join together, then people come in, and I’ve seen it in days past, not so much here because we’re all doing our little thing, but I’ve seen it in days past when the church was in unity, unbelievers come in and they, well, everybody’s got their hands up, I better raise my hand up, and God honors it. Acts 1:14: These all continued with one accord in prayer and supplication, with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers. He says all 120 in the upper room “were filled with the Holy Ghost, not just the apostles,” and they spoke with other languages “as the Spirit gave them utterance.” He says “they didn’t fake it” and “you don’t manufacture, God does it.” Asked how you know you are filled, he says “believe me, you will know,” because it is “a visitation of power, supernatural ability.” He adds that “without Him we’re just a social club.”
What happened on the day of Pentecost, and how do you know you have been filled? (Acts 2:2-4)

They were praying and they were supplicating, they were petitioning God for this Holy Ghost. Supplication is a petition. “A sound came from heaven as a mighty rushing wind, and it filled the house where they were sitting. There appeared unto them cloven tongues like as fire.” That’s what John said, He would baptize you with the Holy Ghost and with fire. That’s what happened on the day of Pentecost, and it sat upon each one of them. All right, and they were what? All filled. All 120 people in that upper room were filled with the Holy Ghost, not just the apostles. And they began to what? Speak. You see, I got it in red because this is a result of the Holy Ghost. He affects your tongue, and you’re going to learn how to speak from the Holy Spirit. And they spoke with other languages, okay, “as the Spirit gave them utterance.” They didn’t fake it, they didn’t pretend it like I saw in Pentecostal churches when I was a young believer. They would come up and tickle their chin and say, “Jibber jibber jib jra.” That ain’t it. I’m a young Christian and I know better than that. You don’t manufacture, God does it. Hallelujah. And someone asked me, “Well, how do you know when you’ve been filled with the Holy Ghost?” Believe me, you will know. It comes from your innermost being. All right, “the Spirit gave them utterance.” Do we want the Spirit to come in our church and speak? Amen, to build the church of God and touch people’s lives. Yeah, folks, without Him we’re just a social club. Don’t you get it? You take the Holy Ghost out of this, we just got a social club. You get the Holy Ghost in it, you got a church.

Acts 2:2-4: And suddenly there came a sound from heaven, as of a rushing mighty wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting. He says others teach “this communal living doctrine,” but Philip “had a house,” Simon “had a house,” and “they taught from house to house.” He says the early believers sold property because “they understood the abomination of desolation that was coming,” but “they kept their houses.” He says the apostles were “already believers,” and the Holy Ghost was “a separate experience from water baptism and salvation.” He also asks what do you do with the verse “forbid not to speak in tongues.”
What does he say about communal living and about not forbidding tongues? (Acts 2:44-45; 1 Corinthians 14:39)

Now, also over there they’re teaching this communal living doctrine. I haven’t heard that since the hippies. God, and I went down in Acts 2, it said they all had all things in common, and they sold the properties, and later, you know, no one said anything was their own. And I told the guy, I said, “Man, you’re a millionaire. You’re a graduate of Yale, and you say that is communal living?” I said, “Don’t you know that Philip had a house? Are you there? Simon had a house. They taught from house to house. These people still lived in a house by themselves.” And folks, they sold their properties for the, they understood the abomination of desolation that was coming. They understood that the property around Jerusalem was going to be worthless because Daniel’s abomination of desolation was coming, and so they sold all this other stuff and their investments because they knew it was not going to have any value, but they kept their houses. All right, and then they were persecuted and sent out all over. Okay, are they already believers? Yes. Okay, have they all been baptized? Yes, the apostles have been baptized. They were already believers, and now the Holy Ghost came, a separate experience from water baptism and salvation. That verse implies there’s going to be tongues, there’s going to be languages. Isn’t that right?” And he says, “Don’t stop it, just get it organized.”

Acts 2:44-45: Now all who believed were together, and had all things in common, and sold their possessions and goods, and divided them among all, as anyone had need. 1 Corinthians 14:39: Therefore, brethren, desire earnestly to prophesy, and do not forbid to speak with tongues.
What does he say tongues are a sign for, and what did being filled again do for Peter and the church? (1 Corinthians 14:22; Acts 4:8, 4:31)

He says tongues are “a sign for who? The unbeliever,” and to get an unbeliever’s attention, “let the Holy Spirit move in a language that you don’t know.” He lists “power to speak, power to smite the enemies, power to do miracles, power to convert souls.” In Acts 4:8 Peter “had already been filled with the Holy Ghost in Acts chapter 2” and is “filled again, as an individual,” speaking “a powerful word of God.” In Acts 4:31, the church prayed in one accord, “the place was shaken,” and they spoke “with boldness,” which he calls confidence: the Holy Ghost “will only allow you to speak truth, not your opinion.”
What does he say tongues are a sign for, and what did being filled again do for Peter and the church? (1 Corinthians 14:22; Acts 4:8, 4:31)

He also said that tongues are a sign for who? For who? The unbeliever. Oh, now that should jar a lot of us Pentecostal people, because we get in our little tongue-talking contest, and tongues are a sign for who? The unbeliever. You want to get unbelievers’ attention, let the Holy Spirit move in a language that you don’t know. It will get their attention if they know it. Power. Power to speak, power to smite the enemies, power to do miracles, power to convert souls. Acts 4:8: Peter, filled with the Holy Ghost. Now, Peter had already been filled with the Holy Ghost in Acts chapter 2, right? Now he’s filled again, as an individual, not a group. This one, this is an individual. He was filled with the Holy Ghost, the Holy Ghost came upon him, and he said unto the leaders that were angry because they healed that guy at the temple, he spoke a powerful word of God to them. So the result of the Holy Ghost coming on Peter was speaking. All right, chapter 4:31: “When they had prayed.” Okay, the church got together. They persecuted, they beat the apostles, the church got together and they prayed in one accord. Now, what’s being in one accord? Everybody doing the same thing at the same time. We worship, we pray, you know, that’s being in one accord. We pray for the what? We want God to do, and we pray together, we worship together. See, when they were in one accord praying, the place was shaken. Boy, how many would like to see this barn shake? Amen. Yeah, some of us need to see something shake. You know, we say we serve a supernatural God, then we take the supernatural out of Him. “And they were all filled.” How many? All that were in there with the Holy Ghost, “and they spoke the word of God with boldness.” Here there’s no tongues. They just spoke the Word of God with what? Confidence. Confidence. Are you confident when you speak the Word of God? The Holy Ghost will give you that confidence, because He will only allow you to speak truth, not your opinion, so you can speak confidently. And I try to tell young ministers, speak like it’s God’s Word. It’s truth. Don’t speak like it’s a suggestion, it’s your opinion. Speak like it is. It is truth. Amen.

Continual experience.” He says “they weren’t always filled with the Holy Ghost, but when the Holy Ghost wanted to do something, He come upon them.”

“Confidently, and with great power gave the apostles witness of the resurrection of Jesus. Great power, great grace was upon them all.” We told you that grace is to grow. There’s power in grace, and “great grace” was upon them, not a little bit of grace. So how many would like more grace? Yeah, it’s Bible to want more grace. Don’t believe these people that just, “You’re just favored and God just loves you no matter what.” There is divine enablement for greater things. Okay, this is the second time they were filled with the Holy Ghost. Acts 13:9. So that means they weren’t always filled with the Holy Ghost, but when the Holy Ghost wanted to do something, He come upon them, and out of their innermost being these words flow out and things happened. Yes, see, we get past the fear and into the force.

Acts 4:33: And with great power the apostles gave witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And great grace was upon them all. Acts 13:9: Then Saul, who also is called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, looked intently at him Acts 13:52: And the disciples were filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit. It happens when it happens. Okay, are they filled with the Holy Ghost? Not yet. Are they baptized in water? Yes. Are they filled with the Holy Ghost yet? No. Verse 14: Peter and John came down and prayed for them to receive the Holy Ghost, “as yet He was fallen upon none of them.” Now here they use the word “fallen.” See, come upon. “Only they were baptized in the name of the Lord.” Had they been water baptized? Had they been water baptized? The story is the story, church. Do you get it? Then they laid their hands on them and they received the Holy Ghost. A different experience from salvation, a different experience from water baptism. Already believers, they were already baptized. Okay, now separate event. You agree? Is that what the Scripture says? Yes. Say amen if you got it. Amen. All right, say it with fortitude. Amen. All right, now I believe you.

Acts 8:12: But when they believed Philip as he preached the things concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized. He says “everything is backwards here”: the Holy Ghost fell on people who “were unbelievers,” and “before he could have an altar call for salvation, God just filled them with the Holy Ghost.” He says the Jews with Peter “were astonished,” and that the Gentiles “spoke with tongues again and magnified God.” He gives the order: “First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized,” and calls it “separate experience from water baptism and the salvation of your soul.” He says God did it “because He knew these dumbbells in the future would twist the Scriptures and rob people of a real experience in God.”
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

Now, this one is really interesting. God really dazzles you when you come to Cornelius. All right, I mean, everything is backwards here. God just don’t fall into our little pattern all the time, and He does have a pattern, but He’s God, He can go outside His pattern. We’re not allowed to, but He’s God, He can do anything He wants when He wants. Okay, Cornelius is a Roman soldier, praying and fasting. An angel came, told him go down and get Peter to come up and preach to him. So he went down and got Peter, Peter come up and spoke, and as Peter spoke the Word of God, the Holy Ghost fell on all them which heard the Word. All these people came to Cornelius’s house. They were unbelievers. Peter had to come and preach the gospel to them. These were unbelievers, and before he could have an altar call for salvation, God just filled them with the Holy Ghost. How could He do such a thing? Because He knew these dumbbells in the future would twist the Scriptures and rob people of a real experience in God, a powerful experience in God, by their theological interpretations. And so here He really just messes everything up. They were filled with the Holy Ghost before a salvation call and before their water baptism, and they of the circumcision, the Jews that came with Peter, were astonished because on the Gentiles was poured out the gift of the Holy Ghost. They were just astonished. How can this be? You know, it’s us [unclear], no more. You know, it’s just us people, with the, we’re the people. Hallelujah. And God said He would pour out His Spirit on how many flesh? All flesh. You are a candidate for the Holy Ghost. “For they heard them speak with tongues.” Oh, tongues again. My gosh, how could God do such a thing? They spoke with tongues again and magnified God, or praised God. Remember, on the day of Pentecost they spoke the mighty works of God. Here they praise and enlarged, magnified God. Then commanded Peter that they be baptized in water in the name of the Lord. Amen. First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized. He’s God. He had definitely, this is a what? Separate experience from water baptism and the salvation of your soul. Unbelievers, not baptized, they got the Holy Ghost.
What does Cornelius’s household show about the order of salvation, the Holy Ghost and water baptism? (Acts 10:44-48)

All right, now we go to Acts 19. Here Paul comes to Ephesus, and Paul says, “Have you people received the Holy Ghost since you believed?” And of course they were in a group that didn’t teach the Holy Ghost. And see, when you don’t teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost, you are robbing the people of a powerful experience in God that will help them in daily life and help us reach the world for Christ. The unbeliever. Don’t forget that. Tongues are a sign for the unbeliever, prophecy is for the believer. Hallelujah.
What happened in Ephesus in Acts 19, and what does he say about churches that do not teach the baptism of the Holy Ghost?

Acts 19:1-7: And it happened, while Apollos was at Corinth, that Paul, having passed through the upper regions, came to Ephesus. And finding some disciples he said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” So they said to him, “We have not so much as heard whether there is a Holy Spirit.” And he said to them, “Into what then were you baptized?” So they said, “Into John’s baptism.” Then Paul said, “John indeed baptized with a baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe on Him who would come after him, that is, on Christ Jesus.” When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. And when Paul had laid hands on them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they spoke with tongues and prophesied. Now the men were about twelve in all.
What does he say about excesses and “funny things” in Spirit-filled churches, and the claim that the Holy Ghost is not for today?

He admits “us Pentecostals, we do make mistakes,” and that “babies in Christ” may “speak some silly things,” but compares them to children: “we don’t kick them out of the house and condemn them.” He says “these things hurt no one,” and asks “how does tongues hurt you?” He says teaching that the Holy Ghost “isn’t for today” hurts people because “you’re robbing them of a tremendous experience and truth in God,” and that being offended by it is “called pride.” He says “I would rather be in a Spirit-filled church with some funny things going on.”
What does he say about excesses and “funny things” in Spirit-filled churches, and the claim that the Holy Ghost is not for today?

Now, I tell these brethren, you know, us Pentecostals, we do make mistakes. Okay, we get too shaken, we slain in the Spirit, we fall for this stuff, and we even have babies in Christ that speak some silly things. Okay, me and Mr. Barnes heard some of that in one of the services. Didn’t bother us any, we just knew they were babies in Christ. And you know, children, they say strange things, and we just laugh and we don’t kick them out of the house and condemn them. These things hurt no one. I asked them, “How does tongues hurt you?” It doesn’t hurt you. There’s no physical harm, there’s no spiritual harm because somebody speaks in tongues. If somebody shakes and falls down on the ground, how does that hurt you? Why are you offended at that? That does no personal harm to you, does it? You’re only hurt because they’re not believing what you believe. That’s why you’re hurt. It’s called pride. But I said, “Now, let’s get to your end. You’re telling people that the Holy Ghost isn’t for today. That hurts them because you’re robbing them of a tremendous experience and truth in God. I said, are you over here, you’re telling them that they get the Holy Ghost when they were water baptized and they didn’t get anything. You’re robbing them. I said, who’s really doing the hurting here? You’re robbing people of an experience in God.” Amen. So we have a few funny things going on. I would, listen, I would rather be in a Spirit-filled church with some funny things going on, and believe me, I have the authority to control things. You don’t believe me, you watch funny things happen. Yeah, we don’t have to hurt people and step on them, we can just guide them. We can grow in this thing. How many, when you first got on a bicycle, didn’t crash it? Most of us wrecked the bike, don’t we? Okay, so we do some funny things with the Holy Ghost. They’re babies, we’re babies, we’re learning. Could that be an amen? Amen, yes. What we need is that power. We need that power that changes people’s life in our services.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)
