He concludes that the baptism of the Holy Ghost “is another spiritual miracle like salvation,” and that “you have to believe above your experience before you’re going to experience it.” He says it is “for a purpose,” not “for you to feel good,” and people need “power, freeing them from sin, Satan, and self.” He says “everything we do should be to build up the people of God,” and the church must “decrease and let God increase.” He says the Spirit “will drive you to the Word,” and “politicians need to hear the Word of God” too.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

Okay, they are believers, they are baptized. Clearly the Holy Ghost baptism is another separate experience. Amen. Now, conclusion: “Clothed with power,” “receive power,” “witnesses unto Me.” The baptism of the Holy Ghost is another spiritual miracle like salvation. Okay, the Bible says that, I don’t care what you believe, the Bible say you have to preach above your experience before you’re going to experience it. You have to believe above your experience before you’re going to experience it. Don’t take your experience and bring the Bible down to your lack of experience. You speak the Bible and He will bring your experience up to what you’re speaking and believing. Separate from water baptism and salvation, we saw it clearly, didn’t we? There’s nothing to interpret, is there? Power to speak, smite your enemies, do miracles, and win souls. Do we need that in the church at Mountainside? Yes. As John says, “I must decrease and He must increase.” How many of you realize we got to decrease and let God increase in this church? We got to get out of our opinions, we got to get out of our cultural antics, and we got to say, “God, arise,” if we want to see a visitation. And I guarantee you, when God starts moving, people will come. The Holy Ghost baptism is for a purpose, either in the assembly or individually, whether they’re filled, baptized, or the Spirit comes upon them. All right, it’s for a purpose. It’s not for you to feel good, and that’s not totally true. There are times of refreshing, you need to be refreshed, but not to where you have to roll around on the floor and shake and bake. And just that refreshing on the inner man, that strengthening in the inner man. You see, it’s for a purpose. He’s a Comforter, He’s a Spirit of Truth that teaches us all things. So I challenge this church today. People need power, freeing them from sin, Satan, and self, and they need refreshing from God. This is what I liked about the Spirit-filled churches when I went to them. You could feel God. He would penetrate your being. He would convict you that you’re wrong. I was always wrong. I hadn’t given my heart to Christ yet. I believed in God, but I wasn’t about to serve Him because I had plans, man, I had plans. But that presence comes, you can feel Him. It’s like putting gas in your tank. You know, we run out of gas, we run out of spiritual gas, we get refilled. It’s a refreshing, and people need that. And people need the Holy Ghost to convict them of sin, forgive them of sin, and cleanse them of sin, and encourage them. Remember, prophecy is for edification, exhortation, and comfort. People need that comfort, people need that building up. See, and Paul said in 1 Corinthians 14, “Let all things be done to edify.” Everything we do should be to build up the people of God, make them better people, and that’s what the ministry of the Holy Ghost is for. We’ve got to get the word out. They told me over there they send us to go to politicians, politicians is of the devil, you know, and all this stuff. I go, man, this world is still believing the lies of Satan in the garden when Satan told Jesus that all these kingdoms are given to me and I can give them to who I want. He’s lying through his teeth. The Bible plainly tells us over and over that the nations, the kingdoms, belong to the Lord. Amen. He was lying. Politicians need to hear the Word of God. Unbelievers need to hear the Word of God. Unlearned people, unlearned people, they’re believers but they’re unlearned, they need to hear this Word that God has given this church. And to whom much is given, much is required. Folks, we got to get this word out. We’ve got to buck up, we’ve got to get together and get this word out: printed, Internet, radio, TV, CD. You know, Christine and Mike were really good on a camera, I’ve noticed. They really have camera appeal. Me and Mr. Barnes, we don’t, you know, we don’t look so good on camera. And remember, the Holy Ghost will guide you into all truth. When you really get filled with the Holy Ghost, you will not only know because of the feeling. He will not allow you to be lazy in the Word of God, because it’s the Word that set you free. He will drive you to the Word, He will drive you to church to learn the Word. You will have a motivational factor in your life.
What is Holy Spirit baptism for, and what does he challenge the church to do? (John 3:30; 1 Corinthians 14:26; John 16:13)

John 3:30: He must increase, but I must decrease. 1 Corinthians 14:26: How is it then, brethren? Whenever you come together, each of you has a psalm, has a teaching, has a tongue, has a revelation, has an interpretation. Let all things be done for edification. Luke 4:5-7: Then the devil, taking Him up on a high mountain, showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. And the devil said to Him, “All this authority I will give You, and their glory; for this has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish. Therefore, if You will worship before me, all will be Yours.” Luke 12:48: But he who did not know, yet committed things deserving of stripes, shall be beaten with few. For everyone to whom much is given, from him much will be required; and to whom much has been committed, of him they will ask the more. John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come.
What teachings does he say he was told about Holy Spirit baptism?

He says, “They told me that Holy Spirit baptism was one time on the day of Pentecost, or it was when you get saved, or it was when you got water baptized.” He says “you people need to know how to answer this stuff.”
What does he say is the criteria for having the Holy Ghost?
He asks, “But what’s the criteria for having the Holy Ghost? Believe. Okay, it’s not complicated.” He says you will experience it in “that inner man that you really are.”
Who does he say baptizes in the Holy Ghost?
He says, “Jesus is the baptizer in the Holy Ghost,” and “Jesus is the sender,” reading Luke 3:16 and Luke 24:49.
Does he say prophesying and predicting are the same thing?
No. He says “there’s a big difference when you go into predicting,” and that “prophesying for edification, exhortation, and comfort is totally different.”
What does he say the Holy Ghost is not out to do?
He says, “He’s not out to condemn you, He’s not out to punish you, He is out to change you and help you in your time of need.”
What does he say about resisting the Holy Ghost as a young man?

He says, “I believed in God, but I had plans and I had purposes, and I would just shove that Holy Ghost away. I didn’t want to be convicted.” He says that “until finally He got my attention, and it’s been a great life ever since.”
What does he say about following the song leader in worship?
He says, “If the song leader claps their hands, you clap your hands. Song leader raises the hand, you raise your hand.” He also says, “if you don’t want to lift your hands, you don’t have to.”
What does he say about faking tongues?
He says of Pentecost, “They didn’t fake it, they didn’t pretend it,” and of his early experience in Pentecostal churches that “you don’t manufacture, God does it.”
How does he say you know you have been filled with the Holy Ghost?
He says, “Believe me, you will know. It comes from your innermost being. It is a visitation of power, supernatural ability.” He adds “tongues or no tongues, you will know.”
What does he say about speaking God’s Word with confidence?
He says, “speak like it’s God’s Word. It’s truth. Don’t speak like it’s a suggestion, it’s your opinion. Speak like it is.”
What does he say grace is?
He says, “grace isn’t just favor from God,” and “grace is divine enablement. There’s power in grace.”
What order does he give for Cornelius’s household?
He says, “First you got the Holy Ghost, then you got them believing, and then you got them water baptized.”
What bicycle illustration does he use?

He asks, “when you first got on a bicycle didn’t crash it? Most of us wrecked the bike, don’t we?” and says, “we do some funny things with the Holy Ghost. They’re babies, we’re babies, we’re learning.”
What does he say about politicians and the Word of God?
He says the Bible “plainly tells us over and over that the nations, the kingdoms, belong to the Lord,” and “politicians need to hear the Word of God. Unbelievers need to hear the Word of God.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer sets Jeremiah 31 and 32 in the middle of Israel’s captivity and shows the hope God gave there: a new, everlasting covenant in which God puts His Word in our hearts, forgives, and promises to do us good. He then lays out our part, to repent, believe the gospel, confess Jesus as Lord and receive Him, and uses the butterfly and 1 John 2 to describe growing from baby to child to young man to father in Christ.
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

He says Josiah was the last good king, but his son “burned the Scriptures” and did evil before God, the first captivity came, and later the king of Babylon burned Jerusalem and destroyed the temple. He says Jeremiah 32 was written about ten years after that, and asks, “If Israel had hope, do we have hope?”
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

Okay, we’re going to go to Jeremiah chapter 31 and 32, but we want you to understand and remember when these chapters were written. Okay? You remember a few lessons ago we showed you that Josiah was the last good king of Israel. All right, looks like Israel was going to avoid the captivity and everything, because Josiah really turned to God, got the nation to turn to God, reinstituted the feast and the things of God. But then his son came on the throne. How many of you had children that didn’t follow your ways? Jehoiakim came up. He reigned 11 years, and he burned the Scriptures, just burned them, and he did evil before God. He shed innocent blood. He committed abominations. Abominations is sexual immorality, homosexuality, idolatry, stealing, murder. In Proverbs 6:17, you remember, there’s seven things that the Lord, it’s called abominations: a lying tongue, a proud look, hands that shed innocent blood, he that devises wicked imaginations, feet that are swift to running to do evil, a false witness that repeats lies and speaks lies, and he that sows division among the brethren, and there’s many others. Okay? And he committed them. He committed them all. All right, he had wars, there were famine, there were plagues, and the first captivity came at the end of his term. Then [unclear] arose, and he was king, made king by the king of Babylon, and he only lasted three months, but the Bible just summed him up and said he did evil like [unclear] did. Now it was in this condition that chapter 31 was written. Hallelujah. I mean, we got serious calamity. America’s got calamities, but nothing this bad yet. So if Israel had hope, do we have hope? If Israel would have listened to Jeremiah, 31 and 32 could have saved them a lot of pain, and so can we. Hallelujah. Then we go down to Zedekiah. He reigned 11 years, and the second captivity came in the 11th year, and this time the king of Babylon destroyed and burned the city of Jerusalem, destroyed the temple. He imprisoned the preacher of righteousness, Jeremiah, and this is when Jeremiah 32 was written, okay, about 10 years later.
What was happening in Israel when Jeremiah 31 and 32 were written?

Proverbs 6:16-19: These six things the LORD hates, Yes, seven are an abomination to Him: A proud look, A lying tongue, Hands that shed innocent blood, A heart that devises wicked plans, Feet that are swift in running to evil, A false witness who speaks lies, And one who sows discord among brethren.
What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)

He says “a covenant is a contract,” like promising a lender to pay for a house: each side does its part. Of the new covenant he says, “this is God’s covenant, this is God’s contract, and this is God’s part,” and that God does it, not any preacher.
What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)

Now you got the picture. Things are really bad here, and the people keep being bad, they keep rejecting, and God keeps giving them hope. And this is what God says as we’re coming up. Remember, the false prophets are still prophesying falsely. How many of you know we got false prophets today, false teachers teaching their own doctrine? Temple leaders, the citizens, his own hometown tried to kill Jeremiah, tried to silence the Word of God. Everybody’s wanting to kill Jeremiah. The temple leaders tried to kill him, imprison him. And if you’re going to stand up for right, people are going to dislike you, and that’s one of the reasons we don’t stand up for right, is we don’t want people not liking us. Jeremiah 31:31: “The days come.” Here’s God talking in the midst of this, and watch, this is really simple. It’s just plain, clear English. This is what God says: “I will make a new covenant,” a fresh covenant, a fresh contract, “with Israel and Judah.” A covenant is a contract. If I go to buy a house, I promise the lender that I will pay the payments, I promise the government that I will pay the taxes, and they let me buy that house, live in it. If I don’t pay the payments or I don’t pay the taxes, they kick me out. See, they do their part, I have to do my part. So this is God’s covenant, this is God’s contract, and this is God’s part. This is what God says, this is what I will do. Who will do it? God. Not the Pope, not Billy Graham, not Martin Luther, not [unclear].
What is a covenant, and who keeps God’s part of the new covenant? (Jeremiah 31:31)
Jeremiah 31:31: “Behold, the days are coming, says the LORD, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel and with the house of Judah—
Will everyone in the new covenant know God, keep His commandments, and be forgiven? (Jeremiah 31:33-34)

He says God promises to put His law in the inward part, our spirit, and that “all shall know Me, from the least to the greatest,” which he ties to knowing God personally (John 17:3) and keeping His commandments. He says God also forgives the iniquity and will “remember your sin no more,” and asks, “If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves?”
Will everyone in the new covenant know God, keep His commandments, and be forgiven? (Jeremiah 31:33-34)

God says, “I’ll do this.” And how many would rather have God than any preacher that we’ve ever heard? Yes. “I will put My law in their inward parts and in their heart.” The inward part is that third part of us, that spirit. All of us have a spirit within us, and He says He’s going to put His Word in that spiritual man, that spirit man that’s in you, and in your mind: “I’ll put My law, I’ll put My Word in there.” And if He doesn’t, you don’t know nothing. Can I hear an amen? And He says, “I’ll do this.” I’ll do this next: “All shall know Me, from the least to the greatest.” All shall know Me. All right, as we’ve taught you before, the Bible says in John 17:3 that this is eternal life, that they may know God the Father and Jesus Christ His Son. Have a relationship with Him, a personal relationship. All right, a personal encounter. But not only that, it says in First John that we know that we know Him if we keep His commandments. See, all will know Me, all will keep My commandments, all will have a relationship with Me. Hallelujah, that’s powerful. From the least to the greatest, no matter how little you think you are, no matter how puny of a Christian you think you are, God says you’ll know Me, and you’ll keep My Word, to the greatest. Hallelujah. That’s your promise. Can God lie? No. All right, next: “I will forgive your iniquity,” your immoral, immorality I should say, and the punishment for immorality. You see, I will forgive it. The breaking of moral laws comes with a punishment. He said, “I’ll forgive it, I’ll render it zero, I’ll look at it like it never happened, and I will remember your sin no more.” And if God forgets our sin, shouldn’t we? Yeah, you got to. If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves? Yes. If God erases the sin and doesn’t bring it up again, shouldn’t we? Yeah. Hallelujah. Very powerful, very powerful.
Will everyone in the new covenant know God, keep His commandments, and be forgiven? (Jeremiah 31:33-34)

Jeremiah 31:33-34: But this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put My law in their minds, and write it on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people. No more shall every man teach his neighbor, and every man his brother, saying, ‘Know the LORD,’ for they all shall know Me, from the least of them to the greatest of them, says the LORD. For I will forgive their iniquity, and their sin I will remember no more.” John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent. 1 John 2:3: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments.
What does the covenant mean by “one heart and one way,” and what is the fear of the Lord? (Hebrews 8; Jeremiah 32)

He says Hebrews 8 repeats the covenant and adds that God will be “a God of supernatural power,” doing what humans can’t do. He says God promises “one heart and one way,” that “there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church,” and that the fear of the Lord is to “depart from evil and hate evil.”
What does the covenant mean by “one heart and one way,” and what is the fear of the Lord? (Hebrews 8; Jeremiah 32)

“I will be to them,” now Hebrews 8 repeats this in the New Testament, repeats it word by word, but adds this: “I will be to them a God of supernatural power, and they shall be My people.” Who needs a supernatural power? Hallelujah. I’ll do things that humans can’t do, “and they who come into covenant with Me, they will be My people.” Well, I like that. If God before us, who can stand against us? Amen. God’s on my side, even when I’m the least. Even when I’m the least, He’s on my side. He’s not going to keep me, the flea on the dog. Jeremiah 32:9: “I will give them one heart and one way.” One heart, one way. We got all these denominational Protestant churches and everybody thinks their little camp is the best. That Paul plainly says there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church. Amen. We got to get rid of these tags, and all of us have to line up to that. God, putting a name on your church building and saying, “Well, we believe this,” doesn’t count. All of us have the responsibility to line up to Him. I don’t care what the tag is out on your church. And He says, “I’m going to do that.” Do we need this one answered in America? Amen, and throughout the world, “that they may fear Me forever.” For how long? Forever. What is the fear of the Lord? Depart from evil and hate evil. That’s the Bible definition of the fear of the Lord. He said, “I will give you one heart and one way.” Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” He is the way. No man comes to the Father but by Me. All right, and He says, “I’ll do this so that you fear Me, you hate evil, and you depart from evil, and I’ll do this for the good of them and their children.”
What does the covenant mean by “one heart and one way,” and what is the fear of the Lord? (Hebrews 8; Jeremiah 32)

Hebrews 8:10: For this is the covenant that I will make with the house of Israel after those days, says the LORD: I will put My laws in their mind and write them on their hearts; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people. Jeremiah 32:39-40: then I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear Me forever, for the good of them and their children after them. And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from doing them good; but I will put My fear in their hearts so that they will not depart from Me. Ephesians 4:5: one Lord, one faith, one baptism; John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
Why does God want to do you good, and will He ever turn away from you? (Jeremiah 32:40)

He says “the whole thing is to do you good,” so that your neighbor sees God’s blessing, and that this is the last covenant: “there ain’t no other covenant coming.” He says God will not turn away from you “even in your despair, even in your stupidity and your rebellion,” and, like the prodigal son, you can remember the father’s house and go back.
Why does God want to do you good, and will He ever turn away from you? (Jeremiah 32:40)

See, the whole thing is to do you good. And the reason God wants to do you good is because the world looks at success. They measure everything by success. And so if God can get you to obey His covenant, He’s going to make you good. He’s going to bless your finances, bless your health, He’s going to bless your life. Why? Because He wants to get the attention of your neighbor, that they see it pays to what? Serve God. Now, “I will make an everlasting covenant with them.” So is there another covenant coming after this one? No. This is the what? Everlasting. There was the Adamic covenant, God’s covenant with Adam. There was the Noah covenant, God’s covenant with Noah. There was the David covenant, God’s covenant with David. There was the Moses covenant, God’s covenant with His people Israel. And now He says, “I’m going to bring in the last covenant, and it’s going to be forever.” So there ain’t no other covenant coming. This is it, and this is a good one. We don’t need another one. See that? “I will not turn away from them.” Man, that is so encouraging. How many of you ever just really messed up, to where you thought God didn’t hear you anymore, didn’t even like you anymore? Yeah. Well, the covenant says He will what? Not turn away from you, even in your despair, even in your stupidity and your rebellion. He’s going to be drawing you back to Him to bless you and do you good. And if you are like the prodigal son and you wake up in the pigpen, just remember what the father said. That’s what the prodigal son did. He remembered what the father said. He remembered what the house of the father was, and he went back to the house, back to the father, and the father restored it. And that’s exactly what God said He would do in this covenant. So never let Satan or people around you talk you into giving up. God is for you. And again, He won’t turn away from you, because He wants to do you good. “I will put My fear in their hearts.” There it is again: My fear in their hearts, I’ll do it. “And they shall not depart from Me.” You know, from the day I got saved, backsliding and going back to the world was never even a temptation with me, because I really met God, I really had a born again experience. “They shall not depart from Me.” Wow, I love it.
Why does God want to do you good, and will He ever turn away from you? (Jeremiah 32:40)
Jeremiah 32:40: And I will make an everlasting covenant with them, that I will not turn away from doing them good; but I will put My fear in their hearts so that they will not depart from Me.
Does God bring or allow calamity to correct His people? (Jeremiah 32:39-42)

He says nothing can separate us from God’s love, and that God is “out to do you good,” using the word “good” four times. He says God allowed plague, famine and conquest to correct Israel because “if He didn’t allow it, Satan can’t do anything, and nations can’t do anything,” but that if they return to the covenant He will “bring all the good upon them.”
Does God bring or allow calamity to correct His people? (Jeremiah 32:39-42)

See, nothing can separate us, Paul said, from the love of God which is in Christ. Nothing: principalities or powers, things to come, things behind, things here present, nothing. Jeremiah 32:39: “I will rejoice over them to do them good.” Here’s that word “good” again. That’s three times God’s out to do you good. Don’t you listen to this world, because God does you good. “I will plant them in this land.” His kingdom, His kingdom of righteousness, peace, and joy. His kingdom is what we enter into, and He said He will plant us. “Like as I have brought this great evil upon these people.” See, God corrected them. God brought, or allowed Satan to come and plague them with plagues, and the king of Babylon to conquer them in war. You see, famine, He allowed the famine to happen, because if He didn’t allow it, Satan can’t do anything, and nations can’t do anything. He’s the Lord of it all. “So will I bring upon them all the good that I have promised.” There’s that word “good” again. That’s four times. Is God wanting to do you good? Yeah, we get the hint. Following Him, you will wind up with a good life, I guarantee you. God will come and correct us, and God will allow your sins and your rebellion to bring corrections in your life. The Bible says their sin will correct them. Sin has a punishment, sin has a correction. You see, but He says if I do that, I will also what? Bring all the good upon them. All they got to do is get back to My covenant and I will forget all of that stuff and bless them again. Now that’s powerful, and it’s very clear, very clear. As you see the development of a butterfly here, is our part. This is our part, this is what we got to do. People say, “Not by works.” I’m sorry, not by works of the ceremonial shadow laws of the Bible, but you’ve got to apply the spiritual laws to get the spiritual answers. Are you with me?
Does God bring or allow calamity to correct His people? (Jeremiah 32:39-42)

Romans 8:38-39: For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord. Jeremiah 32:41-42: Yes, I will rejoice over them to do them good, and I will assuredly plant them in this land, with all My heart and with all My soul.’ “For thus says the LORD: ‘Just as I have brought all this great calamity on this people, so I will bring on them all the good that I have promised them.
What is our part in the covenant: repent and believe the gospel? (Mark 1:15; Luke 13:5; 1 John 1:9)

He says “this is our part”: repent, turn from your evil ways, leave sin behind and “believe the gospel,” trusting God the way astronauts trusted their spaceship. Citing Luke 13:5, he says our trust has to be in Jesus, “not a church, not a pastor, not our own opinions,” and that we must admit with our mouth that we were wrong so He forgives and cleanses.
What is our part in the covenant: repent and believe the gospel? (Mark 1:15; Luke 13:5; 1 John 1:9)

So this is what you got to do. This is what you got to put an effort in. Mark chapter 1:15: “Repent.” See, repent: turn from your evil ways, adultery, stealing, and turn to right ways. You got to turn, you got to leave sin behind, the drugs, all that stuff that Satan puts out there to try to lure you. You got to turn from it and “believe the gospel.” So you got to put your trust in the gospel. These astronauts that went into space to go to the moon, they had to trust that spaceship, the engineers that built it, the mechanics that put it together, the architects that drew it, and the scientists that studied all the laws that hindered them from getting into space and how to overcome. They had to trust them, and they didn’t know if it would work or not, and that’s the way it is here. You got to trust God. You got to put your life on the line. You got to trust Him, the gospel of Jesus Christ. Luke 13:5 says, “Except you repent, you shall all likewise perish.” Doesn’t say except you get baptized, doesn’t say except you witness. It doesn’t say that. It says except you what? Repent. You turn. See, and then also, “He that believes not shall be destroyed.” You see, so our trust has to be in Jesus, not a church, not a pastor, not our own opinions, and we’ve got to turn from our sins. Number two, 1 John 1:9: “If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” So I have to admit I was wrong. I have to admit that the things I was doing were wrong. I have to admit it with my mouth: “Lord, I’m wrong in this adultery, I’m wrong in homosexuality, I’m wrong in stealing, I’m wrong in lying.” You see, then He is faithful to forgive, and not only forgive, but wash it off, cleanse me of the contamination.
What is our part in the covenant: repent and believe the gospel? (Mark 1:15; Luke 13:5; 1 John 1:9)

Mark 1:15: and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand. Repent, and believe in the gospel.” Luke 13:5: I tell you, no; but unless you repent you will all likewise perish.” 1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
Why must you confess Jesus Christ as Lord, and not another name? (Romans 10:9)

He says besides confessing your sin, “you also have to confess the Lord Jesus Christ” with your mouth, and believe in your heart that God raised Him. He says the Bible tells us His name is Jesus Christ, “and that’s the name you’ve got to confess,” and that His death, burial, and resurrection “took my sin and gave me a new life.”
Why must you confess Jesus Christ as Lord, and not another name? (Romans 10:9)

Now number three, Romans 10:9. You can’t just confess your sin, you also have to confess the Lord Jesus Christ. Folks, I tell you, Muhammad does nothing for anybody, Buddha does nothing for anybody. So you got to confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus Christ. How many can say, “Jesus Christ is my Lord”? Let’s say it: Jesus Christ is my Lord. See, you got to say that. Not Buddha, not Muhammad, not Allah. The name is what? Jesus. Don’t you believe that nonsense that Allah is just another name for God. No. The Bible plainly tells us His name is who? Jesus Christ, and that’s the name you’ve got to confess. You got to speak it and give Him credit for you, and then the power comes, it works. Believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, so His death, burial, and resurrection took my sin and gave me a new life. That’s what he’s saying. Jesus Christ died for me, rose again. My old man of sin is dead. I come out of the water a new creature in Christ. You will be saved: delivered from sin, delivered from the lake of fire, and delivered from the kingdom of darkness.
Why must you confess Jesus Christ as Lord, and not another name? (Romans 10:9)
Romans 10:9: that if you confess with your mouth the Lord Jesus and believe in your heart that God has raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.
What does it mean to receive Christ and get power to become a son of God? (John 1:12)

He says we must not only confess our sins and confess Jesus but also say, “Jesus, come and live in my life,” and that “as many as accept Him and receive Him, to them gave He power” to become sons of God who obey His Word. He says when you put your trust in Christ, “He’s the engineer, He’s the architect,” the mechanic, the power and the fuel
What does it mean to receive Christ and get power to become a son of God? (John 1:12)

John 1:12: “As many as receive Him, to them gave He power,” supernatural ability, “to become the sons of God.” Isn’t that what it said in Jeremiah, that God will do this stuff? Huh? “I will put My Word in their heart. I will put My fear in them.” Ain’t that right? I will do this. “As many as receive Him.” Accept Christ, you see, and that’s what we got to do. We cannot only confess our sins and confess Jesus, but then we have to say, “Jesus, come and live in my life.” The Bible says we are the temple of God. “Jesus, come in. I accept You. I am Your kingdom. Come in, King, and rule in my life.” As many as accept Him and receive Him, “to them gave He power.” He gives us power to become the sons of God. The Bible says in First John that the sons of God obey His Word. See, “to them gave He power” to obey His Word, to them that trust Him. Say, when you put your trust in Christ, He will get you into orbit, get you into the heavenlies. He’s the engineer, He’s the architect,
What does it mean to receive Christ and get power to become a son of God? (John 1:12)
John 1:12: But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name:
How does the Word of God change us “from glory to glory”? (2 Corinthians 3:18)

He says as we behold the glory of the Lord in the Word of God “we are changed,” as a caterpillar into a butterfly, and that God will empower us to be like Jesus in character. He says this happens in stages, “from glory to glory,” “from faith to faith,” not by being “zapped” mature, so “don’t get down on yourself while He’s delivering you in one thing and you still got a problem in another area.”
How does the Word of God change us “from glory to glory”? (2 Corinthians 3:18)

He’s the mechanic, He’s the power, He’s the fuel, He’s everything to rocket us into the heavenly places. Now number five, 2 Corinthians 3:18: “We all,” how many of us all? All of us, “behold as in a glass the glory of the Lord.” That’s the Word of God. We see in the Word of God the glory, the honor that God, Jesus Christ has. “We are changed,” metamorphosed. From one being to another we are changed. You see, from one kind of creation to another kind of creation, just like this butterfly. Into the what image? Same image, His image. I don’t care how good my pastor is, I don’t care how good the megachurch minister is, I don’t care how good the Pope is, it’s not him that I want to imitate. My Bible tells me God will empower me to be like Jesus in character. Now, amen. And isn’t that what we need, the character of God? Yes. “From glory to glory.” So it’s going to be in stages, isn’t it? I’m not going to be zapped. Hallelujah, I’m mature. Hallelujah, glory to God. That’s what us old Pentecostals used to think. “Boy, we get the Holy Ghost, come up, feel that, hallelujah, man, I’m just totally, I’m totally mature now.” No, no, no. You go from what? Glory to glory, honor to honor. You see, the Bible says we go from faith to faith. Your faith starts out little, but your faith, your persuasion in God and His Word, grows. And the Bible says we go from salvation to salvation. You can’t forget this stuff. He delivers you from this thing, then He delivers you from another thing, then He delivers you from another thing. So don’t get down on yourself while He’s delivering you in one thing and you still got a problem in another area. Are you with me? And so we have
How does the Word of God change us “from glory to glory”? (2 Corinthians 3:18)
2 Corinthians 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord.
What does the butterfly teach about growing as a Christian, and what is a “baby” in Christ? (1 John 2:12)

He says God gave us a covenant “to make us like Himself,” so “we can’t be satisfied with staying where we’re at.” Using 1 John 2, he says babies are those whose sins are forgiven but who still have habitual sin, like the egg and caterpillar, and the church should understand what stage they are in and “keep feeding them, keep nourishing them.”
What does the butterfly teach about growing as a Christian, and what is a “baby” in Christ? (1 John 2:12)

metamorphosis, the changing from the egg to the cocoon to the beautiful butterfly that lays the egg, and it starts all over again. Hallelujah. And this is the message the American church has got to get. We can’t be satisfied with staying where we’re at when God has given us a covenant to make us like Himself and to do us good. 1 John 2:12 and 14 plainly lays it out to us. Babies. See, he talks about the babies: “Your sins are forgiven.” He tells us who babies are: your sins are forgiven. That’s it. And my sins are forgiven. They may have still, and most of them do have, habitual sin still in their life. See, this is the egg to the caterpillar. That caterpillar comes out and eats the egg. It goes back, turns back. You’ll see him, if you had have seen it, he crawled out and then he went back to that egg, that old life, and he partook of it. And this is what baby Christians do. They have habitual sins still in their life, and so that’s babies. So babies, when they’re making mistakes, church, understand what stage they’re in and keep feeding them, keep nourishing them, so they overcome these things. Amen. They grow. And then you got Christians that are 15 years old and claim to be mature, and they have habitual sins. How many of you know that’s not maturity at all? That is still baby level. They haven’t grown up. Remember, it only took three years for the tree in the Bible to produce fruit. This isn’t, you know, a lifetime thing. God said He would do a quick work.
What does the butterfly teach about growing as a Christian, and what is a “baby” in Christ? (1 John 2:12)

1 John 2:12-14: I write to you, little children, Because your sins are forgiven you for His name’s sake. I write to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, Because you have overcome the wicked one. I write to you, little children, Because you have known the Father. I have written to you, fathers, Because you have known Him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, Because you are strong, and the word of God abides in you, And you have overcome the wicked one.
What does it mean to be a “child” in Christ? (1 John 2:13)

He says children know the Father and are delivered from sin, but “not from bad doctrines”; “it’s the doctrines that children get tripped up on.” He says they may not be committing adultery or stealing, but their doctrine is “really lacking,” they “don’t know doctrine, they do stupid things,” and they haven’t made Jesus Lord of their life.
What does it mean to be a “child” in Christ? (1 John 2:13)

Number two, children. He mentions the children. He says, “Children, you know the Father.” See, you know the Father. “All shall know Me, from the least to the greatest.” They don’t know the Father yet. These know the Father. They’re delivered from sin now, but not from bad doctrines. “Be children no longer, tossed to and fro by every wind of doctrine.” It’s the doctrines that children get tripped up on. They may not be committing adultery and stealing and doing bad things, but their doctrine is really lacking. See, you see, they may not embrace the doctrine. “They that are planted in the house of the Lord.” Assemble yourself together, even the more so as you see the day approaching. “Where two or three are gathered together, I will be in the midst,” and when He’s in the midst, He builds, and He does things. And so, you know, they don’t know doctrine, they do stupid things, they haven’t made Jesus Lord of their life yet. They’re still running their life, they don’t read their Bible. They’re children.
What does it mean to be a “child” in Christ? (1 John 2:13)

Ephesians 4:14: that we should no longer be children, tossed to and fro and carried about with every wind of doctrine, by the trickery of men, in the cunning craftiness of deceitful plotting, Hebrews 10:25: not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching. Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
What marks a “young man” in Christ who has overcome the wicked one? (1 John 2:14)

He says these “young men” have conquered the doctrines, gone back to the apostles’ doctrines, and are “following and obeying those doctrines,” and that “the Word is how you overcome the wicked one.” He likens it to the cocoon stage, where “something is working inside of them,” and asks listeners, “Are you still a baby Christian?”
What marks a “young man” in Christ who has overcome the wicked one? (1 John 2:14)

And then he says, “I speak to you young men. You have overcome the wicked one. The Word abides in you, and you are strong.” See, these guys have conquered the doctrines, got back to the apostles’ doctrines, got back to following and obeying those doctrines, applying those doctrines, and they are strong, and they have overcome the wicked one. See, the Word is how you overcome the wicked one, and so they are strong. So this is the cocoon stage. This is the better-looking caterpillar stage. This is the ugly caterpillar stage, you wonder if they’re even saved. And then you got the cocoon, you see something is working inside of them. Hallelujah. Didn’t Paul say, “Was strengthened with might in the inner man”? And see, you can identify where you’re at today. Are you still a baby Christian, you know, because you got habitual sin in your life? You need to grow. Don’t know the doctrines of Christ, believe in false doctrines, believe in your own doctrines, you’re just a child.
What marks a “young man” in Christ who has overcome the wicked one? (1 John 2:14)
Ephesians 3:16: that He would grant you, according to the riches of His glory, to be strengthened with might through His Spirit in the inner man,
What is a spiritual “father” in Christ, and why must Jesus be Lord and Teacher, not only Savior?

He says fathers know Jesus from the beginning of the Bible to the end, love Him, and “can birth others” through the gospel, while “children can’t birth.” He says too many rely on the Savior stage, but “we got to have Jesus the rabbi, Jesus the teacher, and then Jesus the Lord.”
What is a spiritual “father” in Christ, and why must Jesus be Lord and Teacher, not only Savior?

You know the Bible and you overcome the wicked one. He can’t tempt you, test you, lead you astray. You’re just immune to it now. Satan is no problem. He just, “Get away from me, Satan. Get back. Get back off.” Not even a struggle for you. See, something’s going on inside of you, deep inside of you. See, that’s God working His work in you. And then the fathers. You see, fathers, you know Him. That’s Jesus from the beginning. You see, now they know God is Jesus. Now they know that Jesus was there at the beginning, to the end of the Bible, and they love Jesus, and they can birth others. See, fathers can birth others through Christ’s gospel. Children can’t birth. See, the father is married. The Bible says that Jesus is our Savior. That’s what babies rely on. But the Bible also says that He’s your Lord. See, are you there? He also says He is your rabbi, your teacher. These guys need to be taught the Word of God. Am I getting this across to you? See, too many people rely on the Savior stage. The Savior stage is the stage we got to go through. The caterpillar had to be hatched from the egg. It had to be done, but that wasn’t the goal. What was the goal of the egg? A beautiful butterfly. And so we got to have Jesus the rabbi, Jesus the teacher, and then Jesus the Lord. And these young men made Him Lord, so they studied the Word, they took time out for God, they did what God said to do, and they overcame the wicked one. They overcame the world, you see, by the Word of God, and a work was going on in them, transferring them to young adulthood, to fatherhood, into the image of Christ.
Can most Christians say what the new covenant is?

He says fathers make beautiful Christians out of non-believers, baby Christians and children by bringing them into the image of Christ. He says over 90% of Christians he asks cannot say what the new covenant is, and asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of, then summarizes the steps: turn from sin, confess it, trust Jesus’s death, burial and resurrection, confess Him as Lord, accept Him, and “I will do all these things.”
Can most Christians say what the new covenant is?

Fathers, you know Him, and you can birth others. And this is the image: they birth people in the image of Christ. They make beautiful Christians out of non-believers, out of baby Christians, out of children. They nourish them and they bring them into the image of Christ. Isn’t that powerful? Hallelujah. And that’s the covenant. That’s it, it’s that simple. Most Christians cannot tell me the covenant. Over 90% of them, if I ask them what is the new covenant, they have no idea. How can you live in something that you don’t have knowledge of? How can you inherit things that you have no knowledge of? How can you just be satisfied with just being a saved Christian and not know the promise of the covenant that God promised to you, if you would do these simple things: turn from your sin, confess your sin, put your trust in Jesus’s death, burial, and resurrection, confessing Him as Lord, accept Him in your life? Then He said, “I will do all these things.”
What does he say Israel’s kings did that led up to the captivities?

He says Josiah turned the nation to God, but his son “burned the Scriptures,” shed innocent blood and committed abominations, listing the seven things the Lord hates from Proverbs 6:17. He says the first captivity came at the end of that king’s term.
What is a covenant, according to this message?

He says “a covenant is a contract.” He compares it to buying a house, where you promise the lender and the government to pay, “they do their part, I have to do my part,” and says the new covenant is God’s contract with God’s part and ours.
Does he say God forgives and forgets sin?
He says God says, “I’ll forgive it, I’ll render it zero, I’ll look at it like it never happened, and I will remember your sin no more.” He asks, “If God forgives us, shouldn’t we forgive ourselves?”
What does he say the fear of the Lord is?
He says, “depart from evil and hate evil. That’s the Bible definition of the fear of the Lord.”
What does he say about denominational names on churches?

He says Paul “plainly says there is one Lord, one Savior, one body, one baptism, one church,” and that putting a name on your church building and saying what you believe “doesn’t count.” He says all of us have the responsibility to line up to Him.
Is there another covenant coming after the new covenant?
No. He says it is the “everlasting” covenant and lists the Adamic, Noah, David and Moses covenants before it: “there ain’t no other covenant coming. This is it, and this is a good one.”
Why does he say God blesses those who obey His covenant?
He says God wants to bless your finances, health and life “because He wants to get the attention of your neighbor,” so they see it pays to serve God.
He says “repent: turn from your evil ways, adultery, stealing, and turn to right ways,” leave sin behind, and “believe the gospel.”
What does he say Luke 13:5 tells us we must do?
He reads, “Except you repent, you shall all likewise perish,” and says it doesn’t say “except you get baptized” or “except you witness”; “it says except you what? Repent. You turn.”
How does he say we confess our sins?
He says “I have to admit it with my mouth” and name what is wrong, and then, citing 1 John 1:9, “He is faithful to forgive, and not only forgive, but wash it off, cleanse me of the contamination.”
Does he say a Christian becomes mature right away?
No. He says “I’m not going to be zapped,” and says old Pentecostals thought “I’m totally mature now,” but “no, no, no,” you go from glory to glory, faith to faith, and salvation to salvation.
How can you tell which stage of Christian growth you are at?

He says, “you can identify where you’re at today.” If you have habitual sin you are a baby; if you don’t know the doctrines of Christ or believe in your own doctrines, you are a child; if you know the Bible and overcome the wicked one, you are a young man; fathers know Him and can birth others.
What does he say about relying only on Jesus as Savior?

He says “the Savior stage is the stage we got to go through,” like the caterpillar hatching from the egg, “but that wasn’t the goal.” The goal is “a beautiful butterfly,” so we need Jesus as teacher and then as Lord.
How many Christians does he say can tell him what the new covenant is?
He says “most Christians cannot tell me the covenant,” and over 90% have no idea when he asks, then asks how you can live in or inherit something you have no knowledge of.

items.t: How Do We Know That We Know God?
items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear.…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from John 17:1–4 that eternal life is knowing the only true God and Jesus Christ, that only God gives it, and that we receive it in proportion to a hearing ear. He explains how to know that we know God: the Spirit within us, keeping His commandments, being born again, and growing in the word.
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?

He says John 17:1–4 is about knowing God and Jesus Christ, a very basic and powerful teaching of the Bible. He says God glorified Jesus through the virgin birth, His miracles, and mostly His death, burial and resurrection, and Jesus glorifies the Father “by reconciling people back to the father.”
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?

Now today we’re going to be talking about knowing God and Jesus Christ. This is a very very basic teaching of the Bible and very powerful. All right. Knowing— and Catholics and Protestants alike are ignoring this important doctrine. Okay. We open the book here and it’s John 17:1-4: “Father, the hour is come.” The time has come. Appointed time has come. A season has come. Okay. What time? What season? Okay. And then he explains what’s come. “Now glorify your Son, that your Son might also glorify You.” Now God glorified Jesus by him being born of a virgin, preaching the gospel, doing miracles, bringing many into the kingdom. But mostly his death, burial, and resurrection. That’s how God honored. Glorify means honored. He honored the son with the ability to give his life. No one could take it. He had to give up his life and then he took it back again. And then how does Jesus glorify the father? By reconciling people back to the father. You see, and the time is here. We’re in that season. Jesus died on the cross. He, he went into the grave, rose again, and for the forgiveness of sin for the cleansing of sin for the freedom of sin and that we might receive him and have him living in us.
What does “the hour has come” mean in John 17:1-4?

John 17:1-4: Jesus spoke these words, lifted up His eyes to heaven, and said: “Father, the hour has come. Glorify Your Son, that Your Son also may glorify You, as You have given Him authority over all flesh, that He should give eternal life to as many as You have given Him. And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent. I have glorified You on the earth. I have finished the work which You have given Me to do.

He says Jesus has authority over all flesh and gives eternal life to as many as the Father gave Him, so “nobody on earth can give you eternal life but God and Jesus Christ.” He says “The church is simply a messenger,” and he is a messenger who can’t give you anything.

That’s how God glorify Jesus. All right. Then Jesus in turn reconciles us back to God and gives honor to God. Number two, you’ve given him Jesus authority over all flesh. Okay? Jesus has been given authority over everybody and every nation and every language upon the earth. He is the one running the kingdoms. All right, that’s number two. The hour is here and it’s been here. This season’s been here before creation. Not just when Jesus came in the flesh, but he was given this before creation. He created everything. He has that kind of authority. Number three, that he give eternal life to as many as you’ve given him. Now, this is quite a statement. You see, he gives eternal life to as many as God has given him. So we see here that God and Jesus Christ are involved in the process of eternal life. Not your church, not your pastor, not some author, nobody on earth can give you eternal life but God and Jesus Christ. The church is simply a messenger. I am a messenger. I can’t give you anything. I know a lot of priests and the pope and everybody, they act like they have something to give. But nobody can give you anything in the Bible. God gives it. Think on that. We have the tendency because somebody has some speaking skills or charisma to think that they possess something and they can give it to us. They can’t. There is no one on earth that can give you eternal life. Muhammad cannot give you eternal life. Nor can the Muslim religion. Only Jesus Christ can give you eternal life. And it says so right here. Ain’t that right? Very powerful. And he gives it to as many as the father gives him. Wow. So both God and the father are involved in us possessing eternal life. Then number four he says this is eternal life.
John 17:2: as You have given Him authority over all flesh, that He should give eternal life to as many as You have given Him.
Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)

He says John 17:3 defines eternal life as knowing “the only true God,” and “There’s only one God,” not the same God in every religion. He says the Bible explains exactly who this God is, “when you deflect from anything that he is, you got the wrong God,” and that Christians seek eternal life, not enlightenment.
Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)

He gives a definition of eternal life that they may know you the only true God. The only true God. There’s only one God. And don’t give me this stuff that Buddha and Muslims and Hindus all lead to the same. No, the Bible explains exactly who this one God is. And when you deflect from anything that he is, you got the wrong God. Amen. See, we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life. The Buddhists are looking for some kind of enlightenment, an arena where they’re not reincarnated anymore. And the Muslims are looking for a harem in heaven, a— women. That is stupid. You got God in heaven and you want a woman. I mean, how secular, how fleshly can you get? Are you with me? See, that just nullifies their God. See, now let’s take a look at these four things. We already know that Jesus has already died on the cross, rose again. Okay, God has glorified him and he has glorified the father by obeying his word and reconciling people by his blood to God. We already know that, right? That’s just basic Bible. Now you have given him authority over all flesh. Let’s check and see if historically in the scriptures this is true that Jesus Christ has authority over all mankind.
Do all religions lead to the same God? (John 17:3)
John 17:3: And this is eternal life, that they may know You, the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom You have sent.
Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)

He cites Matthew 28:18, 1 Peter 3:22 and Daniel 7:14 to say Jesus has authority over the spirit world and the earth, and is “the leader and ruler of all of them.” He cites Matthew 9:38 and says the Lord of the harvest has to be involved, using a picture of grain ground and baked into bread. He says churches that skirt the Lord of the harvest just to fill their buildings are “wasting your time,” and “We are just messengers.”
Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)

Matthew 28:18: “All power is given unto me,” Jesus said, “in heaven and in earth.” In heaven is the spirit world. That’s where the angels are, the seraphims are, the demons are. Satan is. So he has authority over that whole spirit world and he has authority over the earth where humans are. Amen. And he has how much authority? All. 1 Peter 3:22: “Angels, authorities, and powers being made subject unto him.” Angels are in the spirit world. Authorities, Satan, and principalities and powers of darkness are in the spirit world. Governors and presidents and kings and so forth are in the earthly world, mayors and governors and so forth. And he is what? He is the leader and ruler of all of them. But Daniel says it the best. Daniel 7:14: “There was given unto him dominion, glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages should—“ what? “Serve him.” He has authority over all flesh. Matthew 9:38: “Pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest.” Jesus said, “The field is mankind.” The seed is the word of God, and the harvest is ripe, ready to be harvest. So, we need the Lord of the harvest to be involved in reaching people and harvesting them, don’t we? Yeah. It’s the Lord of the harvest that has the knowledge and the authority to plant the seed and make it grow and then cut it down and put it in the barn and then bring it out and thresh it so it to separate the stalk and the husk from the grain. And then he puts it to the grinder and has all those kernels of grain ground into one body, one [unclear], losing their identity. And he knows how to put yeast in it, his spirit, and impregnate that, and put it in his oven, his fiery trials, so that it bakes and makes bread for the master’s table. That’s the Lord of the harvest. And you try leading people into eternal life without going through the Lord of the harvest, you’re wasting your time. You get it? He does have this power. And too many churches and too many ministers are skirting the Lord of the harvest just trying to get the churches filled. Folks, that don’t work. The Lord of the harvest has got to be involved in this. He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers. Could that be true? And if we do our part and message right, he will do his part and save those that will believe. So we find that’s true. Now what authority does Jesus have to benefit mankind through his death, burial, and resurrection? See, what kind of authority does he have to benefit mankind? And he has authority over all flesh. It says in point number three that God gives people to Jesus to give them eternal life. And so I turned that around and I asked the question, how are you interested in how God’s going to do this? How does God give people to Jesus and then Jesus gives them eternal life?
Does Jesus have authority over all flesh, and why must the Lord of the harvest be involved? (Matthew 28:18, Daniel 7:14, Matthew 9:38)

Matthew 28:18: And Jesus came and spoke to them, saying, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth. 1 Peter 3:22: who has gone into heaven and is at the right hand of God, angels and authorities and powers having been made subject to Him. Daniel 7:14: Then to Him was given dominion and glory and a kingdom, That all peoples, nations, and languages should serve Him. His dominion is an everlasting dominion, Which shall not pass away, And His kingdom the one Which shall not be destroyed. Matthew 9:38: Therefore pray the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into His harvest.”
What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)

He cites Mark 4:23 on having “a hearing ear,” and says take heed means to understand, consider, apply and then experience the result. He uses a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that opens to something that looks like tomatoes, to show that we must open things up and find out what is really inside.
What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)

Have any interest in seeing the answer to that question? See, this is imperative for us. Mark 4:23: “If anyone has ears to hear, let him—“ what? “Hear.” So, we need what? A hearing ear. And then he explains what kind of hearing ear. He said to them, “Take heed what you hear.” Now that word take heed is a complex word meaning you got to understand, you got to consider it. You got to understand it, you got to apply it and then you experience the result of it. Okay? For instance, now I know you guys go to school and you’re really intelligent. What does it say on that can? Organic pumpkin. Organic pumpkin. All right. What does it say? Organic pumpkin. So, he was right. Right. Okay. So, what are we going to find when we open this can? Pumpkin. Organic pumpkin. But how are we going to know unless we what? Apply and find out what’s really in the can. Okay, here you go. You guys know how to use a can opener? There you go. Open that can up for me. Now, guys, is that pumpkin? No. No, it’s not. No, but the can says pumpkin. It looks like salsa. It looks like tomatoes. Huh? Yeah. Is it tomatoes? Maybe. Is that a tomato? No.
What does it mean to “take heed what you hear”? (Mark 4:23-24)

Mark 4:23: If anyone has ears to hear, let him hear.” Mark 4:24: Then He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given.
Should we dig deeper into what preachers tell us?

He says too many do not dig deeper to find out if what preachers say is true, so “we don’t experience the truth.” He says “a lot of people think they’re good on the inside until their inside is open.” He says a church leader has no authority to change what the Bible says: “You cannot change the word of God.”
Should we dig deeper into what preachers tell us?

Yes. Huh? That looks like it. Yeah, looks like tomato. You see, too many of us do not dig deeper and find out if what preachers are telling us is the truth. We don’t apply, we don’t put time into it, and so we don’t experience the truth. See, a lot of people think they’re good on the inside until their inside is open. All right? So, we need to put time in to what we’re hearing. Could that be an amen, church? You can’t just believe the pope. The pope just said that homosexuals is an acceptable thing. You know, the Catholic Church has got to change things for— The pope has no authority to do that.
What does “with what measure you mete” mean? (Mark 4:24)

He says measure means a standard of measure, and uses a teaspoon, a cup and a hose to show that the more time we put into seeking God, the more water we have to clean the house. He says Jesus said, “Out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow,” a continuous flow that can cleanse us, our house and “the whole nation.”
What does “with what measure you mete” mean? (Mark 4:24)

You cannot change the word of God. Amen. See, the can doesn’t have the right stuff in it. Now, “with what measure you mete”: measure means a standard of measure. See that’s like this cup here. This is the two cup— cup. This is a teaspoon. All right. What standard of measure you meet? Which means to give out— what measure you give out is going to be measured, [unclear] given back to you. So, we want to clean the barn. All right. So, we get a teaspoon. We get a teaspoon and we’re going to clean this barn. Doesn’t do anything, does it? Okay. We go back to God and say, “God, it didn’t work.” You know, he said, “Well, get a bigger measure.” Okay, so instead of putting two minutes a day into God, we put five. And so we get more water. And God says, “Now clean your house. Clean the house.” So we didn’t work. There’s not enough water to get the job done, is there? Okay, God, it didn’t work. What do I do now? Well, get a bigger measure. Okay. All right, God. I’m going to get a bigger measure. Here we go. And I want you to clean yourself. Hallelujah. Clean the house. It didn’t work. See, we put 15 minutes into the day of seeking God and we got more, but we don’t have enough to get the job done. So then God says, “Have you ever read in the scriptures out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow out?” Okay, God, I got it. I get a hose that has an endless supply of water. Now, can I clean the church? Yes. Yes. You see, we’re looking for teaspoons in cups. David said, “My cup runneth over.” Elijah filled the barrels with water. But Jesus said, “Out of your innermost being, rivers of water would flow.” A continuous flow of water that can not only cleanse us and our house and those around us, but the whole nation.
What does “with what measure you mete” mean? (Mark 4:24)

Mark 4:24: Then He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given. John 7:38: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.”
How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)

He says “To you who hear, more will be given,” and when we respond to what God gave, He gives us more, which is how “we grow in grace.” He says whoever has not a hearing ear, even what he has “will be taken from him,” including a little faith and a little grace because they are not growing.
How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)

It’s an endless supply. But then you got to put in more time to get that water. Are you there? You got to read the word and you got to understand the word. So this is how they give us eternal life. They become involved and they respond with the response that you respond back. To you who hear, more will be given. See, they that hear and then they take what God has given them. Though God gives back more than he gave them. And when they respond and give God back, he responds and gives us more. And that’s how we grow in grace and things. For whosoever has whosoever has what? Faith, grace, a big church, a little church. No. Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given. You see, we have to hear, understand, apply, and then we experience the results of what God said. Whosoever has not has not what? A hearing ear. Even that which he has will be taken from him. That little bit of faith that he has will be taken away. That little bit of grace that he has will be taken away because they’re not growing in faith. They’re not growing in grace. Now, isn’t that pretty clear? And that’s how God gets involved in our life and gives us eternal life by your response. Do we really know him? This is eternal life. The fourth principle was the fourth thing that we’re in the season of that they may know you, the only true God and Jesus Christ whom you have sent. That’s a powerful emphasis. Powerful. I can know God and I can know Jesus Christ. I can really know. See, these guys knew what was in the can when they opened the can. They knew it wasn’t pumpkin. They knew it was tomato.
How does hearing lead to more being given? (Mark 4:24-25)

Mark 4:24-25: Then He said to them, “Take heed what you hear. With the same measure you use, it will be measured to you; and to you who hear, more will be given. For whoever has, to him more will be given; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.” Mark 4:25: For whoever has, to him more will be given; but whoever does not have, even what he has will be taken away from him.”
How can I get to know God? (1 John 4:13, Ezekiel 36:27)

He says God promised we can know Him, and cites 1 John 4:13, “we dwell in him and he in us, because he hath given us his Spirit.” He cites Ezekiel 36:27, God putting His Spirit within us to cause us to “walk in my statutes.” He says “It’s not me trying to mentally make up my mind to do this,” but God providing the empowerment and desire to please Him.
How can I get to know God? (1 John 4:13, Ezekiel 36:27)

One of them said salsa. And that was close cuz salsa is made of tomatoes. And you can make some good salsa with what’s in that can. See that? But they knew it wasn’t pumpkin. And see, us Christians, we have got to dig deep enough to know what these preachers and these books are saying. We got to get understanding and we apply it. And if it doesn’t work, we know they’re wrong. And if it does work, we know that’s right. Now, we’re going to ask the question, how would I get to know God and Jesus? Well, God promised I could know him. How can I know him? 1 John 4:13. Hereby— by this we know that we dwell in him and he in us, because he hath given us his Spirit. This spirit that raises up a standard against our enemy. We know Jesus lives in us. And we live in him by that spirit. See, that spirit is involved. And it’s promised in Ezekiel 36:27. Hundreds of years before God promised that he would put his spirit within us. I will put my spirit within you. And what that spirit will cause you to walk in my statutes. Cause you to keep my judgments, cause you to do them. See, it’s God coming to my life that gives me the desire to obey his word to do that what’s pleasing to him. It’s not me trying to mentally make up my mind to do this. It’s him providing the empowerment, the desire, the compelling to please him. And see, when I make a mistake, that compelling picks me up and moves me on. I don’t stay in my mistake. I don’t stay in my failure. Why? Cuz the Holy Spirit’s there causing me to get up and keep pursuing his word, his righteous judgment, his righteous moral truths. Hallelujah. So, it’s important that I know God and God is spirit. See, so when God says, “I will put my spirit,” he’s going to he’s what?
How can I get to know God? (1 John 4:13, Ezekiel 36:27)

1 John 4:13: By this we know that we abide in Him, and He in us, because He has given us of His Spirit. Ezekiel 36:27: I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will keep My judgments and do them.
How can we know that we know Him? (1 John 2:3-4)

He cites 1 John 2:3–4, that we know we know Him if we keep His commandments, and says the Spirit within compels us to repent, ask forgiveness and tackle the sin again until it is broken. He says those who say “I know him” but do not keep His commandments are liars and “The truth is not in him.” He says a Christian who stumbles and gets back up is different from one who lives in habitual sin.
How can we know that we know Him? (1 John 2:3-4)

I’m going to put myself in you. 1 John 2:3-4. Here it is again: “Hereby— by this we know that we know him.” You see, we can know if we know God. We can know if we are participators of that promise to know God and Jesus Christ if we keep his commandments. Now Ezekiel just told us when God comes to us, he’s going to cause us to keep his commandments. It’s not going to be, you know, well, I just got to figure this out. I just got to grunt and do this on my own. No, no, no. There is a spirit within you. There is a force within you that keeps compelling you and driving you to keep his word. And so therefore, I know I know him. Why? Yes, I’ve messed up three times in this area and I’ve asked forgiveness three times and here I did it again. But that spirit what? Compels me to repent. Compels me to ask God to forgive me for compels me to ask God to cleanse me and free me from this. And I get back up and I tackle that sin again. And then one day, the spirit has given me authority over it. Set me free from it. That’s how I know I know God. He that says, “I know him,” and keeps not his commandments, is a what? Liar. You know, homosexuals that say they’re going to heaven, and they’re living in habitual sin, and prostitutes and incest people and pedophiles and all this, they say, “Well, you know, God loves me and all this.” Listen, God loving the world has nothing to do with where you’re going. If you don’t respond with a hearing ear, you’re going to be everything’s going to be taken from you, including eternal life. Isn’t that what we read? And look at this last part. The truth is not in him. The truth, you see it up there. Truth. The truth is not in him. John 16:13, when he, the Spirit of truth is come, he will guide you unto all truth. So what’s not in him? When truth is not in him, what’s not in him? The spirit. See, he doesn’t know God. The spirit’s not in him. And John 14:6, I am the way, the truth, and the life. Jesus is the truth. So, who is not in them? Jesus and the spirit’s not in them. And they know it because they live in habitual sin. They’re not Christians just stumbling and making mistakes and getting back up.
How can we know that we know Him? (1 John 2:3-4)

1 John 2:3-4: Now by this we know that we know Him, if we keep His commandments. He who says, “I know Him,” and does not keep His commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him. John 16:13: However, when He, the Spirit of truth, has come, He will guide you into all truth; for He will not speak on His own authority, but whatever He hears He will speak; and He will tell you things to come. John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.

He cites John 14:16–17, that the Father will send “another Comforter,” the Spirit of truth. He says the Holy Spirit is “a friend” who mends the brokenhearted, sets the captive free and encourages us when we think all is lost: “He comes as a comforter. He doesn’t come as a quitter.” He says the world cannot receive Him because it neither sees nor knows Him.

They habitually live in sin. Now, isn’t that clear? And we can know him. And this same chapter of John 14 tells us we know him. Okay, let’s go to verse 16 of John 14: “I will pray the Father, and he will send you another Comforter, that he may abide with you forever.” Now this Holy Spirit’s not only spirit of truth but he’s a comforter. He’s a friend. He’s there to mend up the brokenhearted, set the captive free. He’s there to encourage you when you think all is lost and there’s no hope. He comes as a comforter. He doesn’t come as a quitter. Might as well just quit. Give up. No, the Holy Spirit’s an encourager, an inspirer. “Even the Spirit of truth.” See, that’s what he’s talking about in John 14. The spirit of truth, the Holy Spirit. Whom the world cannot receive because it sees him not, neither knows him. And they know they don’t know him because they don’t keep his word. The comforter and the spirit of truth, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit’s all the same thing. But you know him. Oh, for he dwells with you and shall be in you.

John 14:16: And I will pray the Father, and He will give you another Helper, that He may abide with you forever— John 14:17: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him; but you know Him, for He dwells with you and will be in you.
What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)

He asks who was with the apostles when Jesus said the Spirit is with you and will be in you, and says it was Jesus, who is truth, with the pouring out of the Spirit still to come. He says “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one,” who identifies Himself as the Father, the Son, the Holy Spirit and the Word. He cites John 1:1 and John 7, rivers of life-giving water flowing from our innermost being from the Spirit, who had not come yet because Jesus had not been glorified.
What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)

You know him. Hallelujah. Now, what does he mean when he says he’s talking to his apostles and he says this Holy Spirit is with you. The spirit of truth is with you, but it’s going to be in you. Now, let me answer this by asking you this question. Who was with the apostles at the time he said this? Jesus, who is truth. The Spirit is truth. You see, God says, “I’ll pour out my Spirit.” It’s God’s Spirit. You know, the Muslims say that Christianity has three gods because they use the word trinity to try to express, you know, God. But the Muslims lying. Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one. And he identifies himself as the father, the son, the Holy Spirit, and the word. He identifies himself. So when we speak, we speak his identity. He’s the father. He’s the son. He’s the Holy Spirit. And he’s the word. Jesus said, “My word is truth.” In John 1:1, it says, “The word became flesh and dwelt amongst us. The word was with God and the word was God.” So the word is God. Jesus is God. God is God. And the Holy Spirit is God. Make no mistake, we worship one God. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Now Jesus is with them. So what is he talking about shall be in you? Well, he had told them to go and tarry in Jerusalem until they be clothed with power from on high. He had told them that there was going to be a pouring out of the Holy Spirit. When he was glorified, you see it says in John 7, he that believeth on me out of his innermost being what? Rivers of life-giving water would flow. This spake he of the spirit which had not come yet because he had not been glorified. He hadn’t died on the cross and rose again. So there is a promise of Jesus coming back and empowering us, filling us with his spirit.
What does “with you” and “in you” mean, and is God three gods? (John 14:17)

John 1:1: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God. Luke 24:49: Behold, I send the Promise of My Father upon you; but tarry in the city of Jerusalem until you are endued with power from on high.” John 7:38-39: He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” But this He spoke concerning the Spirit, whom those believing in Him would receive; for the Holy Spirit was not yet given, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?

He tells of a conversation with a Catholic priest he invited to speak, who said he had been filled with the Holy Ghost at a large spirit-filled Catholic convention. He says what the priest experienced was “his presence with us,” which anyone can have when they gather and acknowledge Christ, not the baptism of the Holy Spirit. He says “That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right.”
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?

But we also have him with us. Amen. Do you guys get this? Let me give you an illustration of this. I mingle a lot with other denominations and so especially when I was younger and I invited Father Fred, a Catholic priest in the community to come in and speak at the church. And he spoke a good message of faith and you know and in that message he said he’d been filled with the Holy Ghost. All right. And so after the service, me and him are talking, and he lights up a cigarette. And then he uses profanity like a truck driver. Blankly blanket this and blankly blanket that. And I go, “Uh, Father Fred, how did you get the Holy Ghost?” I said, “Number one, the first name of the spirit is holy. Holy Ghost. He said, “Well, I went down to the Anaheim Convention Center where the spirit-filled Catholics gathered together.” And if you haven’t been there, it was it’s powerful.
