These Catholics that were filled with the spirit 1968, God just visited denominational churches and just poured out his spirit on that. He didn’t ask anybody’s permission. He just did it. And so these Catholics would get together and they’d have a a big convention. I mean, there’s 10 or 12,000 down there, man. We walk in there and they’re worshiping Jesus and all that. The power of his presence is there. But see, that’s the presence with us. And that’s what he said. I walked into that and man, the spirit of God was just came all over me and I just felt God’s presence. And I said, “Father Fred, that is not the baptism of the Holy Ghost. That is his presence with us. Everybody can have that. When the church gets together, Jesus said, “I will be in the midst.” Presbyterians, Baptists, Methodists, Cath— I don’t care who you are. If you gather together and you acknowledge Christ, his presence will come. That doesn’t mean your doctrine’s right. I said, “Father Fred, Jesus said that the spirit would pour out of us.” I said, ‘You haven’t got the baptism of the Holy Spirit. You just experienced the first time the presence of God. And there’s a big difference. Hallelujah. And that’s what Jesus is telling his apostles. Now, there is some spirit-filled churches that believe if you don’t have the baptism of the Holy Spirit with speaking in tongues, you’re not saved and you’re going to hell.
What is the difference between God’s presence with us and the baptism of the Holy Spirit?
Matthew 18:20: For where two or three are gathered together in My name, I am there in the midst of them.”
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

He says some spirit-filled churches believe if you don’t speak in tongues you’re not saved, and tells of parents who told a daughter she was going to hell for that. He says “the Bible says not all speak in tongues,” and that in Acts 2 they spoke in languages while in Acts 4 they “spoke in their own language.” He says the parents stuck with their church doctrine over Scripture because they didn’t take time to find out.
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

And I’ve had to deal with these people. I’ve had to deal with parents, good parents, that told their child, they had two children. One got filled with the Holy Ghost and spoke in tongues, the other one didn’t. And they told this other daughter that she was going to hell. And I knew that girl. She was a fine Christian girl. And I’m pretty sure Mr. Barnes knows who I’m talking about. And I had to— you know, I had to deal with this thing. I can’t have this girl going through life thinking she’s going to hell because she don’t speak in tongues when the Bible says not all speak in tongues. My God, church. It doesn’t take a genius to figure this out, does it? Amen. In Acts chapter 2, yes, they spoke in languages. In Acts 4, they didn’t. They spoke in their own language. They didn’t speak in other languages. Are you with me? And that couple, as tremendous a couple as they was, and the guy was a successful businessman and they were very educated and knowledgeable, they stuck with their church doctrine over scripture because they didn’t take time to find out and get the understanding. See, that’s what Paul meant when he— or Peter meant when he said, “Unstable and unlearned people, twist the scriptures and bring destruction.” But I finally got to the young lady. Hallelujah. And she’s the one that needed to hear.
Do you have to speak in tongues to be saved?

1 Corinthians 12:30: Do all have gifts of healings? Do all speak with tongues? Do all interpret? Acts 2:4: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and began to speak with other tongues, as the Spirit gave them utterance. Acts 4:31: And when they had prayed, the place where they were assembled together was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and they spoke the word of God with boldness. 2 Peter 3:16: as also in all his epistles, speaking in them of these things, in which are some things hard to understand, which untaught and unstable people twist to their own destruction, as they do also the rest of the Scriptures.
What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

He says evangelicals, fundamentalists and spirit-filled churches agree God must be involved in salvation, not “head knowledge” or “getting your name on a church,” citing “you must be born again.” He says God is involved as you respond: if we confess our sins He is faithful to forgive and cleanse us, and John 1:12 gives power to “as many as receive him.” He says you must admit you’re wrong: “That’s the formula.”
What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

And when mom and dad’s wrong, they’re just what? Wrong. Now this is what evangelicals, fundamentalists, spirit-filled churches, they all believe that God must be involved in your salvation. Can’t just be head knowledge. Can’t just be, you know, getting your name on a church and joining some group. God has to be involved. And we all use this scripture that Jesus said, you must be born again. Unless a man is born of water and of the spirit, he can’t enter the kingdom of God. You see, this is what separates Protestants from other Protestants. And this really separates the Protestants from other Protestants from Catholics because Catholics have the tendency to believe because they join that church and they do the rituals. They’re going to heaven. And folks, you got to be born again. That’s what the scripture says. And that born again, you got to be born of the spirit. See, God’s got to be involved in your salvation. And he’s involved as you what? Respond. See, if we confess our sins, he’s what? Faithful and just to forgive our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness. Not just forgive us, but cleanse us, wash the sin away. He will set us free from sin. And John 1:12 says, “To as many as receive him, to them gave he power.” Now, this is God coming and dwelling with us. This is not the baptism of the Holy Ghost. He will give them power that receive him to become sons of God. See, sons of God, when you know the interpretation of the sons of God in the Bible, the sons of God live right. They live holy. And so he empowers us to keep the word is what he’s saying. So when you invite Jesus, that initial presence of God comes. Hallelujah. And so this is what being born again is. You admit you’re a sinner. If you [unclear] admit you’re a sinner, God can’t cleanse you. He can’t forgive you. You got to admit you’re wrong. Even Christians that need areas of their life straighten out have to admit they’re wrong. That’s the formula. Hallelujah. Then after we get saved, if we seek him and we seek the word, we will grow in the word.
What does it mean to be born again? (John 3:5, John 1:12)

John 3:5: Jesus answered, “Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born of water and the Spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God. 1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. John 1:12: But as many as received Him, to them He gave the right to become children of God, to those who believe in His name:
What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

He says a time and season has come: Jesus has already died for the sins of the world, we must confess we are sinners and come to Him for cleansing, and “No one can save you but Jesus.” He says this is the season to possess eternal life and to know God, in proportion to our hearing ear: “You have out of God what you put into God.” He says we know God by the Spirit in us and our hearing ear to keep His word.
What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

See, desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow by that. You’ve got to have the word to grow and you got to have the water, the spirit to grow. And unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow. So, you got to take heed what you hear. 1 Peter 1:23, born again by the word of God, which lives and abides forever. You see, we’re born again by the word of God. Remember Jesus said, “My word is spirit. The spirit is spirit. The word is spirit. All this is spirit.” All this is God’s involvement with us, folks. And he promised this is the season. You live in it. And if you’ll respond to me, I will respond to you. And if you respond more, I will respond more. So what’s the conclusion? There’s a time and season that has come. Jesus has already died on the cross for the sins of the world. But we have to confess we are sinners and come to him for cleansing. No one can save you but Jesus. All right? And if you will admit and come to him, invite him into your life, he will back it up and he’ll come to you, forgive you, cleanse you, and live in you. He will give you eternal life. This is the season to possess eternal life. Not only to live with him forever when you die, but to know him. This is the season you can know God. And we are given these promises and other promises in proportion to our hearing ear. That’s the conclusion. You have out of God what you put into God. That’s what Jesus said. We know. We know God by the spirit in us and our hearing ear to keep his word. We know we should be honest. We know we should be truthful. We know we should not be doing wrong. So, we know God is in us cuz he’s putting that in us. He’s compelling us. He is causing us to rise up. Rise up, son. We heard it Friday night. Rise up, son. And finish the race.
What is the conclusion? How do we know God?

1 Peter 2:2: as newborn babes, desire the pure milk of the word, that you may grow thereby, 1 Peter 1:23: having been born again, not of corruptible seed but incorruptible, through the word of God which lives and abides forever,
He says “Glorify means honored.” He says God honored the Son with the ability to give His life, and no one could take it.
What authority does he say Jesus was given before creation?

He says Jesus has authority over everybody and every nation and every language on the earth: “He is the one running the kingdoms.” He says this was given to Him before creation, and He created everything.
Can anyone on earth give you eternal life?
He says no: “There is no one on earth that can give you eternal life.” He says “Only Jesus Christ can give you eternal life.”
What is the difference between enlightenment and eternal life?
He says “we’re not looking for enlightenment. We’re looking for eternal life.” He says eternal life is defined as knowing the only true God.
What does he say the Lord of the harvest can do?

He says the Lord of the harvest has the knowledge and authority to plant the seed and make it grow, cut it down, thresh it and bake it for the master’s table. He says “He’s the one that can do the job. We are just messengers.”
What was the can illustration about?

He opens a can labeled “Organic pumpkin” that looks like tomatoes, and says “too many of us do not dig deeper and find out if what preachers are telling us is the truth.” He says we need to put time into what we hear.
Who does he say gets more from God?
He says it is not faith, grace, a big church or a little church: “Whosoever has ears to hear, more will be given.”
Is obeying God just my own effort?
He says no: “It’s him providing the empowerment, the desire, the compelling to please him.” He says when he makes a mistake, that compelling picks him up and “I don’t stay in my mistake.”
What does he say happens when a Christian keeps messing up in an area?
He says the Spirit “compels me to repent” and ask God to cleanse and free him, and he gets back up and tackles the sin again. He says one day “the spirit has given me authority over it.”
Are the Comforter and the Spirit of truth the same?
He says “The comforter and the spirit of truth, the Holy Ghost, the Holy Spirit’s all the same thing.”
Does he say Christians believe in three gods?
He says no: “Us Christians do not believe in three gods. We believe in one.” He says “Make no mistake, we worship one God.”
How does he say we grow after we are saved?

He says we “desire the sincere milk of the word that you may grow,” and you’ve got to have the word and the Spirit. He says “unless you go to church and get in Bible studies and you’re not going to grow.”

items.d: In “How to Have No Fail Success,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the new covenant promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 — one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing by the word, and the covenant of…
p: In “How to Have No Fail Success,” Pastor David G. Kincer walks through the new covenant promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 — one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing by the word, and the covenant of peace that makes believers priests — and shows where the New Testament says the same. He teaches that God says “I will” and does the changing, while we must respond, seek Him and apply ourselves. He closes with accounts of early martyrs and the deathbed words of well-known unbelievers.
What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?

He says we should know the covenant, even have it memorized, because “this is powerful.” In Ezekiel 11 God says “I will gather you,” and he ties this to the church being the called-out ones, brought out of the power of Satan into a spiritual land, not a natural one.
What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?

So this is a very important thing. You got to know the covenant. You really do. You should have this memorized, basically. You need to pray about the covenant, you need to get this in your brain, because this is powerful. Okay, the new covenant, Ezekiel 11:16-21. First of all, He introduces the topic like Jeremiah does: “I will gather you from the people.” And in the New Testament we actually find that the church, the word church, means the called-out ones. Okay, and in Acts 26:18 the Bible says that Jesus came to turn people from darkness to light, from the power of Satan to the power of God. So He’s bringing us out from under the authority and the power, the kingdom of darkness and Satan, and placing us in, He isn’t bringing us into a natural land, He’s bringing us into a spiritual land. Got it?
What is the new covenant promise in Ezekiel 11, and why should we know it?

Ezekiel 11:16-21: Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “Although I have cast them far off among the Gentiles, and although I have scattered them among the countries, yet I shall be a little sanctuary for them in the countries where they have gone.” ’ Therefore say, ‘Thus says the Lord GOD: “I will gather you from the peoples, assemble you from the countries where you have been scattered, and I will give you the land of Israel.” ’ And they will go there, and they will take away all its detestable things and all its abominations from there. Then I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them, and take the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh, that they may walk in My statutes and keep My judgments and do them; and they shall be My people, and I will be their God. But as for those whose hearts follow the desire for their detestable things and their abominations, I will recompense their deeds on their own heads,” says the Lord GOD. Acts 26:18: to open their eyes, in order to turn them from darkness to light, and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who are sanctified by faith in Me.’
Why does he say there is only one pastor and one church?

He says Ezekiel’s “one heart” matches Jesus saying there will be one fold and one shepherd, and that no pastor on earth can be your pastor because there is only one, Jesus Christ. He says that following one shepherd in one direction impresses unbelievers, and he points to the one accord of Pentecost.
Why does he say there is only one pastor and one church?

Number two, He said, “I will give them one heart.” Same thing Jeremiah said. If you see the italics up here, it’s exactly what Jeremiah said. “I will give them one heart.” Now in John 10:18 Jesus said there will be one fold and one shepherd. Hallelujah. There is no pastor on earth that can be your pastor. We are strictly delegated ministers of the gospel. There is only one pastor, one shepherd, and that is Jesus Christ. Do we understand that? And you better be under Him. You know, don’t go around saying, “My pastor is Dave Kinzer.” No, your pastor is the Lord Jesus Christ. He better be. In John 17:21 Jesus prayed this prayer: “Father, make them one, that the world may believe and know that You have sent Me.” See, us having one pastor, following one direction, impresses the unbeliever so much that they will believe and know, and it’s imperative that we strive to be one in God. Can I hear an amen? And in America we got so many denominations and so many voices and so many books and so many ways of doing things. There’s only one shepherd, one way, one truth, one baptism, one church in the Bible. Can I hear an amen? And we need to remember that. And that’s our promise from the Old Testament and in the New. And remember, in Acts one, on the day of Pentecost they were in one accord.
Why does he say there is only one pastor and one church?

Ezekiel 11:19: Then I will give them one heart, and I will put a new spirit within them, and take the stony heart out of their flesh, and give them a heart of flesh, John 10:16: And other sheep I have which are not of this fold; them also I must bring, and they will hear My voice; and there will be one flock and one shepherd. John 17:21: that they all may be one, as You, Father, are in Me, and I in You; that they also may be one in Us, that the world may believe that You sent Me. Acts 2:1: When the Day of Pentecost had fully come, they were all with one accord in one place.
What does “a new spirit within you” mean, and is the Holy Spirit with us or in us?

He says Jesus told His apostles that the Spirit of truth was with them and would be in them, and he links John 7:38 with John 3:16, saying both come as a package. He says that when you accept Christ He comes in you, but there is also an infilling of the Holy Ghost of power, and these are “two different things.”

When the wind blew and the tongues of fire came and they spoke the mighty works of God, they were one. So He fulfilled that. Number three in Ezekiel, describing the new covenant: “I will put a new spirit within you.” When we go to the New Testament, John 14:17 it says the Spirit of truth, “He dwells with you and shall be in you.” You see, Jesus backs it up and says, listen, and He’s talking to His apostles, listen, the Holy Spirit’s with you, because Jesus was with them, but He said, “My Spirit’s going to be in you,” because the day of Pentecost was coming, when He would pour out of their innermost being that Holy Spirit and that river of life-giving water. Are you with me? I wish we’d stop arguing about the Holy Ghost and just get it. I really would. I, I ah. And in John 7:38, this is the scripture that I get all the people that oppose the Holy Ghost with. And “this spake He of the Holy Ghost,” which was to come and be what? In us. He’s with us, but He’ll be in us. Hallelujah. So how can you take John 3:16 and say, “Yeah, boy, if I believe, I’ll have eternal life,” and then you go to John 7:38 and you go, “No, no, no, no, no, believing on Jesus, that’s not for today”? You can’t do that. They both come as a package. Can I hear an amen? Hallelujah. That Holy Ghost is very important, folks. He says a stone has no feelings or sensitivity, and he says many American Christians have a heart of stone and are stubborn in thinking and spirit. A heart of flesh senses and can respond, and he says Jesus wants to give us that sensitive heart.

sensitivity. And that’s a lot of us American Christians. We don’t have any sensitivity. We got a heart of stone. We are stubborn in our thinking, we are stubborn in our spirit, and we need Jesus to come along with His jackhammer and break that [unclear] up. Amen. He wants to give us a heart of flesh. He says the reason is that we may walk in His statutes and keep His ordinances, and he links it to John 14:23. We obey, he says, not as robots but because we love Him and want to please Him.

pain. Hallelujah. And if I love something, I want to what? Embrace it, feel that love. And so He says, “I will take the stony heart out of their flesh. He says God will hold accountable those whose hearts walk after detestable things and abominations, and “bring problems and pain” into their lives to correct them. He says believing, grace, paying tithes and helping the poor “isn’t going to cut it” if we do the things God detests.

rewards. Hallelujah. Now number five: “They shall be My people and I will be their God.” That’s exactly what Jeremiah said, the exact statement. Verse 21: “As for them whose heart walks after the heart [unclear] their detestable things and their abominations,” those things that God hates, “I will recompense their way upon their own head, says the Lord.” Believing isn’t going to cut it. In Ezekiel 36 he reads that God will sprinkle clean water on them and cleanse them from their filthiness and idols, and says it is God doing the cleansing. He says the word “not only causes us to grow and delivers us and heals us, but it also cleanses us,” and he calls it “God’s soap,” which is why we need to read it, study it and hear it preached.

you. Are you there? He says Ezekiel 36:31 shows another side of repentance in the New Testament, feeling sorry as well as turning. that we really feel bad that we would hurt God and we would do such a thing and hurt people. But we also need to what? Turn from the sin. heard the gospel from John, was 86 years old when they were going to burn him at the stake, and his last words were, “86 years I’ve served Jesus Christ and He’s never done me the least wrong. Uh, he goes on to say, “We Christians are fixed in our minds not to change from good to evil, but for me it would be good to be changed from evil to good.” Isn’t he describing the Christian life? We’re in a process of being changed from evil to good, and here they’re going to kill him. Now this is the one I really like. Perpetua was a wife and a mother. I can’t find her husband, but they said she was a wife and a mother of a nursing baby. She’s 22 years old, she just accepted Christ, and she’s going through catechism, she’s learning the basic scriptures over there in North Africa. And the governor, the government comes in and arrests them in the Bible study, and they told her if you denounce Christ you will live, and if you don’t you’re going to die. They took her baby from her. And how many, you know, for a woman who’s got a little baby, and the heart that a natural mother has for a baby, would be a big temptation to renounce Christ. And she wouldn’t do it. So they came and took the baby from her. Her father came and tried to put a guilt trip on her: “What are you doing? Your baby needs you. Renounce Christ and live your life and take care of this baby.” She still would not budge. Now, folks, that new covenant is working, and she’s a baby Christian. She’s not been saved very long at all. So they take her to the arena when the governor was going to be there, put him on display. They stripped her naked and beat her before all the people, and she would not give in at all. And then they put her in an area where there was a cow with rabies, a wild cow, and that cow just chased them and gored [unclear], and she’s wounded. And then the gladiators would come over and do the job, but the gladiator, when he came over, he was so taken by this woman standing for Christ, and she took his sword and put it up to her neck, and then the gladiator cut her throat and she died. Now, folks, that’s a powerful story that the new covenant works. Thomas Paine, on the other hand,
What does he say about the deathbed words of well-known unbelievers?

After the martyrs, he says “on the other hand” and recounts what he says were the last words of several famous skeptics, who he says cried out in fear of hell. These are the speaker’s own historical accounts, not checked by this site.
What does he say about the deathbed words of well-known unbelievers?

1809, the leading atheist writer in the American colonies, wrote the pamphlet Common Sense, which really stirred America to fight the Revolutionary War and become independent. On his deathbed, this is his words: “Stay with me, for God’s sake stay with me. I cannot bear to be left alone. Oh Lord, help me. Oh God, what have I done to suffer so much? What will become of me hereafter? I would give worlds, if I had them, that The Age of Reason had never been published.” That’s a book he published that put down Christianity. Now there’s some good things in that book. He brought out the ridiculous things in the church, the things done in the church that we shouldn’t be doing, but he also ridiculed the church, God and Jesus in it. “The Age of Reason had never been published. Oh Lord, help me. Christ, help me.” Look at that word, Christ. He didn’t call on Allah. “No, don’t leave, stay with me. Send even a child to stay with me, for I’m on the edge of hell here alone. If ever the Devil had an agent, I have been that agent.” That’s his deathbed cry after reading The Age of Reason. In 1757 Benjamin Franklin wrote, “I would advise you not to attempt unchaining the tiger, but to burn this piece before it’s seen by any other person, whereby you will save yourself a great deal of mortification from the enemies that may raise up against you, and perhaps a good deal of regret and repentance. If men were so wicked as we now see them with religion, what would they be without it?” Did you catch that? Powerful. David Hume, the famous agnostic atheist, in 1776 when he died, his cry was, “I am in flames, I am in flames.” Voltaire, the famous atheist, wrote that book that everybody reads in college. 1778: “I’m abandoned by God and man. I’ll give you half of what I’m worth if you give me six months of life. I’ll give you half of my wealth.” The doctor replied and said it could not be done. “Then I shall die and go to hell,” Voltaire said. And his nurse said, “For all the money in Europe I don’t want to see another unbeliever die.” All night long he begged for
What does he urge us to do about the new covenant?

He urges us to get the new covenant “out of the New Testament and the Old Testament,” pointing to Hebrews 6 and 8, to pray about it, and to remember it is God’s promise to us. He says God will be involved and do it, “divine enablement,” but that we got to put some effort into it.
What does he urge us to do about the new covenant?

forgiveness, and like Esau, God didn’t show up. Now, folks, I would really beseech you, this new covenant is so important. You need to get it out of the New Testament and the Old Testament. It’s in Hebrews 6 and Hebrews 8 in the New Testament, very plain, very clear. You need to pray about this. This is God’s promise to you, and He said He will be involved. This is the grace of God, that He will be involved and do it, divine enablement, but we got to put some effort into it.
What is the new covenant, according to this message?

He walks through the promises in Ezekiel 11, 36 and 37 and says they are the new covenant: God gathers us, gives one heart, a new spirit, a heart of flesh, cleansing, and an everlasting covenant of peace.
He says the word church means the called-out ones, and ties it to Acts 26:18, where Jesus turns people from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God.
Can a pastor on earth be my pastor?
He says no: he says we are “strictly delegated ministers of the gospel” and there is only one pastor, one shepherd, Jesus Christ.
What does Jesus pray about being one?
He reads Jesus praying, “Father, make them one, that the world may believe and know that You have sent Me,” and says having one direction impresses the unbeliever.
Does he connect John 3:16 and John 7:38?

He says both promise something to whoever believes, eternal life in one and rivers of living water in the other, and that “they both come as a package.” He says John 7:38 speaks of the Holy Ghost, who would be in us.
Is there more to the Holy Ghost than receiving Christ?
He says that when you accept Christ, He comes in you, but there is an infilling of the Holy Ghost of power, and they are two different things.
Why does he say we are not robots when we obey?
He says Jesus gives us a heart to fall in love with Him, so we obey because we care, love and appreciate Him, not because of “thou shalt not.” He says His word also brings rewards.
Does God hold believers accountable for doing detestable things?
He says that if you do the things God detests, He will come and hold you accountable, bringing problems and pain to correct you.
What does he mean by “God’s soap”?

He means the word of God, which he says keeps washing and cleansing us. He points to Ephesians 5:26, the washing of the water by the word, and says we need to read it, study it and listen to Bible studies.
What does God promise about daily needs in Ezekiel 36?
He says that in the verse about calling for the corn and laying no famine on them, God is saying He will bless your daily life, income, food, clothing and shelter.
What are the two sides of repentance?
He says one is turning and the other is feeling sorry or bad for what you have done, and that we need both.
Why does he say God blesses us?
He says God’s ultimate goal is the unbeliever, and God blesses us so He can reach our neighbors, parents and other people.
What could priests do under the covenant of peace?
He says they had authority to come into the very presence of God and minister to God, and to minister to the people, and could go in and talk to God directly.
Who does the changing: God or me?
He says “the ‘I will’ will do it” and not to try to do it on our own, but also, near the end, that we have to put some effort into it.
Can I have these promises here on earth?
He says you don’t have to wait for the rapture. If you give God time, he says, He will transform you into a priest who can minister to Him and to people and possess His promises.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says America has its own idols in entertainment and compares them with the gods of ancient Corinth. He walks through 1 Corinthians 8, where Paul answers those who rely on…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer says America has its own idols in entertainment and compares them with the gods of ancient Corinth. He walks through 1 Corinthians 8, where Paul answers those who rely on human knowledge about food offered to idols, and explains the weak conscience and the stumbling block. He then connects idolatry to spiritual adultery and to 1 Corinthians 10, where Paul says to flee from idolatry and uses communion as an illustration.
Do we have idols in America today?

He says in America “we do not have a tradition or custom to really worship” carved images, “but we do have our own idols.” He points to American Idol, where someone is made into a musical idol whom teenagers “adore,” and says music and TV develop the minds of most young people, who “imitate their idol.”
Do we have idols in America today?

Today in America, we do not have a tradition or custom to really worship and--and uh--follow idols, images created into gods. But we do have our own idols. American Idol is called American Idol. Why? Because they’re trying to make someone into a musical idol where the teenagers especially will adore them, wear the clothes that they wear, wear the hairstyle that they wear, and embrace the message that they’re trying to get across. These three judges, Steve Tyler, claims to be a Catholic, but he lives with women, and he aborted a five-month-old son and all kinds of other debauchery, drugs, sex, and everything else. You think he cares about the moral condition of these people coming to be the next American Idol? No, he doesn’t care about the moral condition. He can call himself a Catholic all he wants. The Bible says, “You know them by their fruits.” Jennifer Lopez. She was raised in a Catholic home. She was a Buddhist a few years ago and now she switched over to Scientology. She’s just, you know, smorgasbord. She has no problem playing nude scenes in movies and uh all kinds of other uh immoral things. Randy Jackson is from a Catholic family, but on the show he wears voodoo beads. He is from Louisiana and voodoo is big down there. Are you there? You think these judges care about whether these people wind up good or not? Or what they told him about this [unclear] fella, this young teenage rapper. They said, “Boy, you you you you win and you’re going to get all the girls you want.” This is what the judges told this young teenager. See, the focus is on sex, pleasure, partying, drinking, just a loose life. See, it’s idolatry. And they got the show pegged right. American Idol. Now, that’s not the only reality show. There’s other ones. The Kardashians is one, and I’ve never seen it, but wouldn’t want to see it, but I read about in the newspapers all the time, and other things. You see, we don’t have idols. We have living people that are idols. We have entertainment that we idolize. You know what develops the minds of most young people in America today? Music. You know what the second development of minds of most young people today? TV. The media. Absolutely. And that’s why kids dress like they dress, wear their hair like they do, and so forth. They imitate their idol. So idolatry in America is very prevalent, but we don’t have these images and stuff like Corinth had. Here is just a few of their idols, their gods. Okay. Now, all of these idols were served with sacrifices, whether plants or meat, incense, music, prayers. They were common to all.
Do we have idols in America today?
Matthew 7:16: You will know them by their fruits. Do men gather grapes from thornbushes or figs from thistles?
What gods did people worship in ancient Corinth?

He lists gods such as Aphrodite, Poseidon, Apollo, Hermes, Fortuna and Isis, and the Pantheon where “any God you wanted to worship was there.” He says all idols were served with sacrifices, incense, music and prayers, and that Paul faced this “along with all the other debauchery going on,” including temple prostitution.
What gods did people worship in ancient Corinth?

And the participators got to eat the best part of the sacrifice. Both Rome and Greek religions had a view of the afterlife after you’re dead. The Rome you went, if you were good, you went to the Milky Way. Now, I don’t know what you’re going to do up the Milky Way, dance from star to star or whatever. And the Greek, you went to Hades. Yeah, not a very good place. But uh you see the gods up here, Aphrodite, uh the Roman counterpart was Venus, the love goddesses, beauty, love, sex, and they included temple prostitution in their worship. You could go there in the temple and have sex uh both men and women. They had men prostitutes in the temple, they had women prostitutes in the temple. And you could get mar-- a sacred marriage there, you know, and there’s religions today that teach you you can have a sacred marriage. Uh, Poseidon is the next one, the God of the sea. Apollo, the sun God. Hermes, the messenger of the God. His counterpart was Mercury. Uh, Fortuna, the Roman goddess of luck and chance. If you’re going to go down and gamble at the casinos, you go and [unclear] drop in at the uh goddess of luck and chance so that you win money. Okay. Isis, the Egyptian God of motherhood. Pantheon, uh up at the top there, that’s where you could go and any God you wanted to worship was there. Okay? You didn’t have to go to a specific temple. You could go to the pantheon and all the gods were there and you could just go to that God and do your thing. Then you had uh you know the God of the waters and the healing God and so forth. And this is what Paul was facing at Corinth along with all the other debauchery going on. Here is a layout of the city of Corinth downtown. And uh in this area here is where the Pantheon was, the temple of uh Poseidon and Apollo and Hermes and a lot of temples. Right here over here was shops and in the middle of this shop was the God of wine. You know, uh Corinthians were big on wine. They drank wine from sun up to sun down.
What does “things offered to idols” mean in 1 Corinthians 8?

He says Paul’s subject is “the meat and the sacrifices, the prayers and all that involved in idolatry.” In Corinth you could talk to a medium or oracle, he says, “but see, in America, we don’t do that. We just make idols out of music, Hollywood, entertainers, athletes.”
What does “things offered to idols” mean in 1 Corinthians 8?

A lot of alcoholics there. And then you have Apollo big temple over here and one over here and other temples. So downtown and this area right here was where you could go and you could you could talk to a a medium uh an oracle, a person that could tell you what God is saying directly. All right. So, it was a big thing back then. But see, in America, we don’t do that. We just make idols out of music, Hollywood, entertainers, athletes, we just make idols out of them. And so here in 1 Corinthians 8 verse 1, Paul starts out by saying, “Now as touching things offered to idols,” okay, his subject is the meat and the sacrifices, the prayers and all that involved in idolatry offered to idols he’s going to talk about.
What does “things offered to idols” mean in 1 Corinthians 8?
1 Corinthians 8:1: Now concerning things offered to idols: We know that we all have knowledge. Knowledge puffs up, but love edifies.
Why does knowledge puff up but love edify? (1 Corinthians 8:1)

He says Paul first addresses people who “through natural human knowledge deal with idolatry.” Knowledge “brings pride,” he says, but “when love communicates it’s there to build up,” while knowledge can be “me showing you what I know.”
Why does knowledge puff up but love edify? (1 Corinthians 8:1)

But he’s going to talk about it as Paul does. Paul is a very very good speaker, great communicator. He’s going to approach it. He’s going to address those who through natural human knowledge deal with idolatry. Okay? There were people in the Corinthian church who had it all figured out through human knowledge just like today. And so Paul’s going to tackle that first. All right. He says, “We know that we all have knowledge.” Isn’t that true? Anybody in here brainless? See, we all have knowledge. We all have some understanding. He says, “We also know that knowledge puffs up. It makes us proud.” You see, and you can tell that when when somebody gets knowledge of something, they want to go pass it on. Did you hear? Did you know? See why, man? And I got something that you know other people don’t have and I got to tell them. So knowledge brings p brings pride. He says but what love edifies. See love see when love communicates it’s there to build up. But when knowledge communicates it can just be me showing you what I know. Look how smart I am. Look what I know. And it may be something stupid, but to you it’s big deal. He says, “We know that.” And in Isaiah 5:21, it says, “Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes.” In Isaiah 47:10, “Your knowledge says, I and no one else besides me.” I’ve got it. If you don’t agree, you ain’t got it. Paul’s slick. He knows his Bible. He’s been to the third heaven and he’s filled with the Holy Ghost. He knows what he’s talking about. And he knows how people think and how people respond. And he’s going to neutralize this human thinking factor in trying to find solutions to spiritual problems. Romans 12:16, “Do not be wise in your own conceit, your own eyes, and your own opinions.” And so Paul is simply stating what the Bible already says. If any man thinks, verse two, that he knows anything, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know.
Why does knowledge puff up but love edify? (1 Corinthians 8:1)

Isaiah 5:21: Woe to those who are wise in their own eyes, And prudent in their own sight! Isaiah 47:10: “For you have trusted in your wickedness; You have said, ‘No one sees me’; Your wisdom and your knowledge have warped you; And you have said in your heart, ‘I am, and there is no one else besides me.’ Romans 12:16: Be of the same mind toward one another. Do not set your mind on high things, but associate with the humble. Do not be wise in your own opinion.
What does it mean to think you know something but know nothing? (1 Corinthians 8:2)

He says “we think we know something and we haven’t searched out the full ramifications of the topic and we give slanted information.” Quoting 1 Timothy 6:3, he says a person who does not consent to Jesus’ words and the doctrine according to godliness is proud and knows nothing, and “living to please God is the final measuring stick of anything you believe.”
What does it mean to think you know something but know nothing? (1 Corinthians 8:2)

You know, and that is a true statement. We think we know something and we haven’t searched out the full ramifications of the topic and we give slanted information and we believe a slanted part of that knowledge. Are you there? Oh, it’s true. It’s true. We don’t take time to search it all out. And so he’s really and he says we know this stuff. He says all of you know this stuff. And then in 1 Timothy 6:3 the Bible says if any man teach otherwise and consent not to the wholesome words even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ and consent not to the doctrine which is according to godliness. And what is the definition of godliness? Pleasing God, not pleasing your friend, not pleasing your spouse, not pleasing some political party, but pleasing God. He says, “If anyone doesn’t consent to the words of Jesus and the doctrine according to godliness to live right and please God, he is what? Proud. And he what? Knows nothing. Just like he said, if somebody thinks they know something, they really don’t know anything if they haven’t searched out the total facts on the issue and come up with Jesus’s words. And living to please God is the final measuring stick of anything you believe.
What does it mean to think you know something but know nothing? (1 Corinthians 8:2)

1 Corinthians 8:2: And if anyone thinks that he knows anything, he knows nothing yet as he ought to know. 1 Timothy 6:3: If anyone teaches otherwise and does not consent to wholesome words, even the words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine which accords with godliness,
Does God know you if you say you know God? (1 Corinthians 8:3)

He says “anybody can say, I believe in God. I know God. I know Jesus. But does God know you?” He points to the sons of Sceva in Acts, who “thought they knew God,” and the demon answered, “but who in the world are you?”
Does God know you if you say you know God? (1 Corinthians 8:3)

Now, that was good. See, he’s got them. He’s got them. If any man love God, the same is known of him. What is he saying? Anybody can say, I believe in God. I know God. I know Jesus. But does God know you? And where is that in the book of Acts? See the sons of Sceva they wanted to cast out demons like Paul did. So they come and said in the name of Jesus that Paul preaches you know come out. And the demon said what Paul I know you know Jesus I know but who in the world are you? See they thought they knew God. They thought they believed in God. They thought they were followers of God, but God didn’t know them. Isn’t that good? That’s a good place for an oh me. Not an amen, but oh me. See, the key is does God know you? You’re talking about human knowledge and you’re acting like you’re in contact with God and getting it from God. But go does God even know you. Isn’t that a good point? Yeah. Now verse four, 1 Corinthians 8, Paul says, “Now as eating things offered to idols.” All right, watch his skillfulness.
Does God know you if you say you know God? (1 Corinthians 8:3)

1 Corinthians 8:3: But if anyone loves God, this one is known by Him. Acts 19:14-15: Also there were seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did so. And the evil spirit answered and said, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know; but who are you?”
Is an idol really nothing? (1 Corinthians 8:4 and Psalm 115)

He says Paul’s readers were saying “an idol is nothing,” and he points to Psalm 115:4 that idols are “the works of men’s hands” and that those who worship them become like them. He says “there’s only one God. There is no other gods,” but “there is not in all men this knowledge that an idol is nothing.”
Is an idol really nothing? (1 Corinthians 8:4 and Psalm 115)

We know that an idol is nothing. And that’s what these people were saying. An idol is nothing. So if I eat something, sacrifice to an idol, doesn’t matter. It’s what they were saying. Psalms 115:4, idols are the works of men’s hands. They have mouths but speak not, eyes and hear not see not, ears and hear not, nose and smell not, hands and they can’t handle anything, feet and they can’t walk. Neither can they speak through their throat. They that make them are like them. So is everyone that trust is in them. See, they that are idol worshippers can’t see, they can’t hear, they can’t talk, they can’t walk. And even when you are worshiping American idol, you become like them. You’re blind. You’re deaf. See, you can’t walk in the moral standards of God. And so, he’s just quoting what the Old Testament said about idols. Idols are what? Nothing. We know that there’s only one God. There is no other gods. Oprah’s wrong. There isn’t any other way to God but God’s way. But there is not in all men this knowledge that an idol is nothing. Are you following it? See, he’s approaching those who decided with human wisdom what they could do with idolatry and that they could go and eat meat and be partakers in those temples because the idol is nothing.
Is an idol really nothing? (1 Corinthians 8:4 and Psalm 115)

1 Corinthians 8:4: Therefore concerning the eating of things offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world, and that there is no other God but one. Psalm 115:4-8: Their idols are silver and gold, The work of men’s hands. They have mouths, but they do not speak; Eyes they have, but they do not see; They have ears, but they do not hear; Noses they have, but they do not smell; They have hands, but they do not handle; Feet they have, but they do not walk; Nor do they mutter through their throat. Those who make them are like them; So is everyone who trusts in them. 1 Corinthians 8:7: However, there is not in everyone that knowledge; for some, with consciousness of the idol, until now eat it as a thing offered to an idol; and their conscience, being weak, is defiled.
Does food have anything to do with spirituality, and what is a stumbling block? (1 Corinthians 8:8-9)

He says Paul says food “does not commend us to God,” and “food has nothing to do with it.” Citing Romans 14:1, he says “it’s backed up in the Bible,” but “not everyone has this knowledge,” so Paul now appeals to the conscience, that “what you do can hurt other people.”
Does food have anything to do with spirituality, and what is a stumbling block? (1 Corinthians 8:8-9)

Okay? Through human knowledge. But everybody doesn’t have this knowledge that an idol is nothing. He says we know food does not commend us to God. If we eat it, are we the better? Nor if we do not eat it, are we the worst? Food has nothing to do with it. You can have all your diet stuff and all your healthy stuff. It has nothing to do with spirituality. So get over it. If you really want long life, honor your parents and keep your tongue from evil and your lips from speaking lies, the Bible says will give you long life. The Bible says if you obey my word, it will be health unto you. So if you want to be healthy, focus in on the Bible because God can go beyond your diet. Are you there? And so he points this out. You know, food’s nothing. Whether that food has been offered to sacrifice, it doesn’t matter. It’s nothing. It It has nothing to do with spirituality. See, now he’s setting them up. I don’t know if you know this or not, but he’s setting these intellectual people up. Romans 14:1 says, “He that is weak in the faith, re receive, but do not but don’t receive them to questioning and judgments and all that. For one believes that he may eat all things, another who is weak eats herbs.” He’s vegetarian. Do not him let him that eats despise him that eats not, and let not him which eats not judge him that eats. See, it’s backed up in the Bible. Food has nothing to do with spirituality. Okay? But he says, “Not everyone has this knowledge.” And we know the idol is nothing and food is nothing. Has nothing to do with anything. But take heed that this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to them that are weak. See, now he’s appealing to not their mental understanding of the not at the idol is nothing. Not the mental understanding that the food sacrifice to idols is nothing. But now he’s appealing to their conscience that what you do can hurt other people.
Does food have anything to do with spirituality, and what is a stumbling block? (1 Corinthians 8:8-9)

1 Corinthians 8:8: But food does not commend us to God; for neither if we eat are we the better, nor if we do not eat are we the worse. Romans 14:1-3: Receive one who is weak in the faith, but not to disputes over doubtful things. For one believes he may eat all things, but he who is weak eats only vegetables. Let not him who eats despise him who does not eat, and let not him who does not eat judge him who eats; for God has received him. 1 Corinthians 8:9: But beware lest somehow this liberty of yours become a stumbling block to those who are weak.
Why does Paul warn about eating in an idol’s temple? (1 Corinthians 8:10)

He says Paul calls those who do not see that an idol is nothing “weak,” and that the intelligent ones were not only buying sacrificed meat but “going to the temple” to eat. He says “your action is going to cause someone that knows better to follow you and then they have sinned.”
Why does Paul warn about eating in an idol’s temple? (1 Corinthians 8:10)

All right? Be a stumbling block. Calls them to fall and he calls these people weak. Now he’s saying these people that don’t understand an idol is nothing and the meat is nothing. He’s calling them weak. Now why do you think he’s calling them weak? To make these mentally intelligent people that’s figured all this out feel more important. We love it. We like to be the one that’s better. But wait till he gets done with it. Are you with me? Is this clear so far? For if any man see you sit at meat in the idol’s temple. These guys were not only going to homes and going to the meat market and buying meat that have been sacrificed to idols. They were going to the temple. In the temple, they had rooms you could rent and all this where you could do your sacrifice and eat. You’d bring your friends or your family in and you just have a nice big party there. And so these guys, because they knew an idol was nothing and meat sacrificed to idol was nothing, they were going into the temple of the idol and eating the meat there, not just at home and in an idolater’s home. Are you there? Shall not the conscience of him which is weak be emboldened or be built up to eat those things which are offered to idols? You see, your action is going to cause someone that knows better to follow you and then they have sinned.
Why does Paul warn about eating in an idol’s temple? (1 Corinthians 8:10)
1 Corinthians 8:10: For if anyone sees you who have knowledge eating in an idol’s temple, will not the conscience of him who is weak be emboldened to eat those things offered to idols?
Who is the real “weak” one, and how do we sin against Christ? (1 Corinthians 8:11-13)

He says that if you read the chapter right you would know “who’s really the weak one,” and that “through your knowledge shall the weak brother perish for whom Christ died.” We need to think “from the Holy Ghost, from the word of God, not our human intellect,” he says, and “when you sin so against the brethren and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.”
Who is the real “weak” one, and how do we sin against Christ? (1 Corinthians 8:11-13)

Now, right quick, you ought to know who is the real weak one here. See, if you really read this chapter right, you’d quickly know, hm, who’s weak? Who’s really the weak one? And through your knowledge shall the weak brother perish for whom Christ died. You are the source for him going to hell because he violated a consciousness that Paul has not brought up yet. Are you there? Paul hasn’t brought this up yet. He’s just brought up their human thinking. And this is what most Christians do. They read passages in the Bible and they come up with human thinking instead of the mind of the spirit. Doesn’t the Bible says to have the mind of the spirit? Didn’t Paul said, “I have the mind of the spirit.” Yeah. And see, we need to think from the Holy Ghost, from the word of God, not our human intellect to come up with spiritual answers. Can I hear an amen on that? But when you sin so against the brethren and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ. And we learned last week that we’re all part of the body of Christ. So when you sin and hurt someone that is a follower of Christ, you’re sinning against Christ. Very good argument. Wherefore. Wherefore. When you see wherefore, you see, you figure out what it’s there for. For this reason, if meat makes my brother to offend, I will eat no meat while the world stands.
Who is the real “weak” one, and how do we sin against Christ? (1 Corinthians 8:11-13)

1 Corinthians 8:11: And because of your knowledge shall the weak brother perish, for whom Christ died? 1 Corinthians 8:12-13: But when you thus sin against the brethren, and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ. Therefore, if food makes my brother stumble, I will never again eat meat, lest I make my brother stumble.
What did the “weak” believer understand? (the Ten Commandments)

He says the weak person understood the Ten Commandments, including “You shall have no other gods before me” and the command not to make or bow down to graven images. That is why “his conscience was offended” when he saw the other believer eating meat sacrificed to idols.
What did the “weak” believer understand? (the Ten Commandments)

Least I make my brother to offend. And he’s talking about meat sacrificed to idols. He’s not talking about all food. Are you there? And he says, “You human thinking people don’t do that.” What he’s saying is you guys don’t do that. You just do your thing. You don’t care who it hurts. Don’t we have that in the church world today? People through human understanding come up with crazy ideas that gives them liberty to do a lot of things that are against the Bible. And uh causes people to be offended. Causes people, especially young Christians that haven’t learned the Bible yet. Now, this is what the weak person understood. It’s right in the Ten Commandments. Duh. The Ten Commandments was the big deal in the Bible for millenniums. You shall have no other gods before me. This is what the weak person understood. Are you there? See, that’s why they were offended when they saw the other guy doing something that violated the first two commandments. You shall not make any graven image of anything that is heaven above, earth beneath, or in the water under under the earth. You shall not bow down to them, nor what? Nor what? Serve them. You see, the weak believer knew this. And that’s why his conscience was offended when he saw this human thinking guy going into the temple and eating meat sacrificed to idols.
What did the “weak” believer understand? (the Ten Commandments)

Exodus 20:3-5: “You shall have no other gods before Me. “You shall not make for yourself a carved image—any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is in the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth; you shall not bow down to them nor serve them. For I, the LORD your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generations of those who hate Me,
Who is really weak, and will people always be offended?

He says “who’s really weak? The human thinker,” and that the other person was only weak because he “hadn’t grown enough in God to know the scriptures enough to just stand for scripture no matter what these other yo-yos do.” Recalling his white buck shoes, afro, motorcycle and sideburns, he says people took offense at each, and “no matter what I do, I’m going to offend.”
Who is really weak, and will people always be offended?

So who’s really weak? The human thinker. And the only thing that made the other guy weak was he hadn’t grown enough in God to know the scriptures enough to just stand for scripture no matter what these other yo-yos do. Is that clear? Isn’t he good? Isn’t he good at explaining it? Now, how many preachers do you know that explain it this way? No. In fact, we used it. I back in the old days, I wore white buck shoes and people were offended at that. And I grew my hair into an afro once cuz I told some people my hair I could grow into an afro. Afro were popular. And I said to the hippies, you know, I can grow an afro. It’s all in how I dry my hair when I get out of the shower. They go, “Oh, get her an afro. We want to see you. Get an afro.” They push me. So, I do an afro. It offended a lot of people that I had an afro. Then I got a motorcycle because it was cheap and also it was cheap entertainment. Me and Mr. Barnes, I had a on street off-road motorcycle and we could go off-roading and then I could drive back and forth to the church cheaply cuz they weren’t paying me much anyway. 600 bucks a month even back then wasn’t much. That offended a lot of people. And uh I grew some sideburns down to here that offended a lot of people. Finally, I go, you know, no matter what I do, I’m going to offend.
What does the Bible say to do about other people’s gods? (Exodus 23:24)

He says he came to the conclusion “I’m just going to do what I know is right. And if they get offended, that’s their problem,” which was “a big freedom.” Reading Exodus 23:24, “Do not bow down to their gods,” he says to “overthrow them through the gospel and through your life. Destroy that mentality of idolatry,” and he says the church in America embraces whatever Hollywood says is okay.
What does the Bible say to do about other people’s gods? (Exodus 23:24)

And they go to this chapter. That offends me. That offends me. He’s talking about idols, folks. And he’s talking about how to rationalize things in the spirit mind rather than the human mind. Can I hear an amen? And I finally had to come to the conclusion, I’m just going to do what I know is right. And if they get offended, that’s their problem. And that was a big freedom. Hallelujah. But that’s what we do with our human mind. Exodus 23:24, “Do not bow down to their gods. Do not serve their gods, nor do according to their works that they do with their gods, which is prayers and music and and uh sacrifices and so sexual immorality right there in the temple. Don’t do any of those things. In fact, he says, “Break down their sacred pillars. Overthrow them through the gospel and through your life. Destroy that mentality of idolatry.” Amen. Exodus 34:15, “Do not make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land.” And see, this is what the church is doing in America. Whatever Hollywood says is okay, we’re just embracing. Whatever Oprah says is okay, millions of women are just embracing. She is the Messiah of this generation of women worldwide. I mean, she’s big time. She’s way bigger than American Idol. She’s way bigger than the Kardashians and and all these other reality shows. She is worldwide. And when she’s got money, she’s got billions of dollars. She could start orphanages and and a place for battered women and and you know, when you do good to people, they think good of you.
What does the Bible say to do about other people’s gods? (Exodus 23:24)
Exodus 23:24: You shall not bow down to their gods, nor serve them, nor do according to their works; but you shall utterly overthrow them and completely break down their sacred pillars.
Why does the Bible call idolatry spiritual adultery?

He says “idolatry is also called adultery, sexual immorality. It’s spiritual adultery in the Bible. Why? Because you’re attaching yourself to another God.” He says “when you come up with your own religion, you’re committing spiritual adultery,” and that Scripture says not to eat of their sacrifices: “Don’t have anything to do with idolatry.”
Why does the Bible call idolatry spiritual adultery?

But her message is eternal damnation to them. Don’t play the harlot with their gods. You see, idolatry is also called adultery, sexual immorality. It’s spiritual adultery in the Bible. Why? Because you’re attaching yourself to another God. See, it’s like a man or a woman married to someone and then they have relationships outside. It’s called adultery. You see, and God says idolatry is adultery. When you come up with your own religion, you’re committing spiritual adultery. And it goes on, he says, do not make sacrifices to their gods. And if they invite you, do to eat of his sacrifices, do not do it. Do not what? Eat of the sacrifices. Don’t have anything to do with idolatry. It is sexual ad. I mean it is spiritual adultery. Now see, the weak-minded ones knew this and they couldn’t understand how these other ones thinking through their human brain that the idol is nothing and food sacrificed is nothing had the freedom to go into these temples and go to the meat market and buy food sacrificed to to to the idols and go to neighbors houses where they were throwing a a a party, a a a festival in the name of their God and eating that food. You see, the weak ones knew this.
Why does the Bible call idolatry spiritual adultery?

Exodus 34:15-16: lest you make a covenant with the inhabitants of the land, and they play the harlot with their gods and make sacrifice to their gods, and one of them invites you and you eat of his sacrifice, and you take of his daughters for your sons, and his daughters play the harlot with their gods and make your sons play the harlot with their gods.
What does Paul conclude about idols, and what does “flee from idolatry” mean? (1 Corinthians 10:14)

He says “the conclusion of this approach to idols is not to partake of idols nor food sacrificed to idols.” In chapter 10 Paul “switches abruptly back to idolatry” with “flee from idolatry.” He says Israel in the wilderness shows that “just because you have the presence of God and you read the Bible does not mean you are pleasing to God.”
What does Paul conclude about idols, and what does “flee from idolatry” mean? (1 Corinthians 10:14)

The conclusion of this approach to idols is not to partake of idols nor food sacrificed to idols. That’s his conclusion, isn’t it? And he approached it from the human intellectual standpoint. Now, as Paul’s style is, he’s going to give another approach to the idol question. The next chapter deals with ministry. He’s establishing himself as ministry. The next chapter deals with Israel in the wilderness proving that just because you have the presence of God and you read the Bible does not mean you are pleasing to God. And in chapter 10 he switches abruptly back to idolatry. Chapter 10 verse 14. Wherefore, when you see wherefore, you got to take note what it’s there for. For this reason, flee from idolatry. What’s he saying? What’s he saying directly now? Flee from idolatry. Okay. For what reason? He’s going to give it to us. First, he’s going to butter us up and tell us, I speak to wise men. Judge you what I say. You guys are a bunch of intelligent people. You can judge this. Here he is telling us to judge what he’s saying. And what’s America big on? Judge not, let you be not judged.
What does Paul conclude about idols, and what does “flee from idolatry” mean? (1 Corinthians 10:14)
1 Corinthians 10:14: Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry. 1 Corinthians 10:15: I speak as to wise men; judge for yourselves what I say.
What does communion teach about partaking with idols? (1 Corinthians 10:16-21)

He says the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom, so believers can make a judgment. When we take the cup and the bread, “we are fellowshipping with the blood and with the body of Jesus Christ. We are in partnership. We are partakers.” Israel’s offerers were “partakers of the altar,” and what the Gentiles sacrifice “they sacrifice to devils, not to God.”
What does communion teach about partaking with idols? (1 Corinthians 10:16-21)

No, don’t make any judgments. God forbid that you make any good decisions in this world. That you pass any judgments on evil. Here he’s telling us again to what? Make a judgment. Okay. Now the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. How many of you fear the Lord Jesus. You invited him into your life. Raise your hand. Okay. Then you have some what? Wisdom. You You don’t have total wisdom, but you got some. You got the beginning of it. All right. Now, so you can make a judgment. Now, here he goes. Here he gives with his phenomenal way of explaining things. The cup and bread are the communion of the blood and body of Christ. We’re going to be taking communion this morning. Okay. When we take the cup of the Lord and we eat of the bread, we are fellowshipping with the blood and with the body of Jesus Christ. We are in partnership. We are partakers. They can’t argue that, can they? That that’s not true. Isn’t that true? Okay. We’re partakers. He says, “We being many are one bread. We’re the body of Christ and one body. All partakers of that one bread.” Can’t argue with that. Jesus is that bread that we partake of. And we are partners with each other in partaking of his bread, his body. Then he switches to another spiritual illustration. Israel after the flesh means their sacrifices, their shadow laws, all that stuff that pointed to the real thing. He says, “Are not they which eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar? When they went to the temple to offer the burnt offering, the atoning offering, did they partake of that sacrifice and the results of that sacrifice? Atonement for sin.” And the people had to say, “What?” Yes, they were partakers. He’s got them in the communion table now. He’s got him in the Israel of old. What am I saying then? That the idol is anything? No, we know the idol is nothing. Or the food sacrificed to idols or their music or whatever is anything? No. No. We’ve got knowledge that that’s nothing. But we also have knowledge that when we partake of the communion table, we’re partaking of the body and blood of Jesus Christ. When Israel of old partook of the sacrifices and the and the shadow laws that God had them to partake of to illustrate spiritual things to come, they were partakers. Now he’s going to hit them when the iron is hot. [Unclear]. But I say the things which the Gentiles sacrifice, they sacrifice to devils, not to God. And I would not that you should have what? Fellowship participators with devils. He’s got them and he’s got you.
What does communion teach about partaking with idols? (1 Corinthians 10:16-21)

Proverbs 9:10: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom, And the knowledge of the Holy One is understanding. 1 Corinthians 10:16-17: The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not the communion of the blood of Christ? The bread which we break, is it not the communion of the body of Christ? For we, though many, are one bread and one body; for we all partake of that one bread. 1 Corinthians 10:18: Observe Israel after the flesh: Are not those who eat of the sacrifices partakers of the altar? 1 Corinthians 10:19-20: What am I saying then? That an idol is anything, or what is offered to idols is anything? Rather, that the things which the Gentiles sacrifice they sacrifice to demons and not to God, and I do not want you to have fellowship with demons.
What does he say American Idol shows about idolatry?

He says the show tries to “make someone into a musical idol where the teenagers especially will adore them.” He says “the focus is on sex, pleasure, partying, drinking, just a loose life. See, it’s idolatry.”
What does he say shapes the minds of young people the most?
He says music is first and TV, “the media,” is second, and “that’s why kids dress like they dress, wear their hair like they do.”
What did the Romans and Greeks believe about the afterlife?
He says for the Romans, if you were good, “you went to the Milky Way,” and for the Greeks, “you went to Hades.”
He says it was “where you could go and any God you wanted to worship was there,” so you did not have to go to a specific temple.
Why does Paul begin by talking about knowledge?
He says some in the Corinthian church “had it all figured out through human knowledge just like today,” so Paul tackles that first, and notes that “knowledge puffs up. It makes us proud.”
How does Paul deal with human thinking about spiritual problems?

He says Paul “knows his Bible,” and “he’s going to neutralize this human thinking factor in trying to find solutions to spiritual problems,” citing what the Bible already says about not being wise in your own eyes.
What does he say godliness is?
He says godliness is pleasing God, not pleasing your friend or your spouse. He says “living to please God is the final measuring stick of anything you believe.”
Does he say there is more than one way to God?
No. He says “there is no other gods” and “there isn’t any other way to God but God’s way.”
Does what you eat make you more spiritual?
He says food “has nothing to do with spirituality,” including diet and healthy eating, and that if you honor your parents and obey God’s word, he says the Bible promises long life and health.
What does Romans 14 say about eating?

He reads that one believes he may eat all things while another who is weak eats herbs, and that the one who eats should not despise the one who does not, and “let not him which eats not judge him that eats.”
What is a stumbling block in 1 Corinthians 8?

He says Paul is appealing not to their mental understanding but to their conscience, “that what you do can hurt other people,” and that your liberty can become a stumbling block to those who are weak.
Why does Paul call some believers weak?
He asks, “why do you think he’s calling them weak?” and answers that it is to make them “feel more important. We love it. We like to be the one that’s better. But wait till he gets done with it.”
What does he say most Christians do when they read the Bible?
He says “they read passages in the Bible and they come up with human thinking instead of the mind of the spirit.”
What does he conclude about people being offended?
He says he finally decided “I’m just going to do what I know is right. And if they get offended, that’s their problem. And that was a big freedom.”
Does he say Christians should never judge?

He says Paul tells them to judge what he is saying: “Here he is telling us to judge what he’s saying.” He contrasts that with “Judge not, let you be not judged,” and says the fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom.
