p: In this second part Pastor David G. Kincer explains that the Old Testament has civil laws, spiritual laws and shadow laws that point to Jesus, using the shadow of a cross. He ties this to communion, assembling, praise and baptism, explains why people were stoned, and says Jesus fulfilled the shadow laws and is the only way.
What are the three kinds of laws in the Old Testament?

He says there are civil laws (like “Thou shalt not murder”), which carry a punishment; spiritual laws (like seek the Lord and pray); and shadow laws. He says critics are “confused about the difference between civil, spiritual, and shadow laws.”
What are the three kinds of laws in the Old Testament?

What people don’t understand is there’s three kinds of laws in the Bible in the Old Testament. Are you ready? There’s civil laws. All right? Thou shalt not murder. That’s a civil law and it has a punishment if you break it. Then there are spiritual laws. Seek the Lord your God and you will find him. Pray, you know, come before him and sing. See that’s spiritual laws. And then there is shadow laws. As we heard earlier, shadow laws. Say the word shadow. Yeah. And this is what these people are confused about the difference between civil, spiritual, and shadow laws.
What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)

He cites Hebrews 10:1, the law is a “shadow of good things to come,” and uses a shadow of a cross: from the shadow alone you cannot tell its color or material, but following it leads you to the real cross. In the same way, shadow laws “point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ.”
What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)

Now don’t look at me like that. I’m telling you the truth. Hebrews 10:1: “For the law having a— what? Shadow of good things to come.” Say it. Shadow of good things to come. “And not the very image of the things can never with these sacrifices which they offer year by year make those who approach perfect.” But you see, they pointed to Jesus who can make you perfect. Now, you see up there on the screen a shadow of a cross. Now, because you’re an intelligent society, you know that’s a cross, isn’t it? But can you tell me the color of that cross? Can you tell me the dimensions of that cross? Can you tell me if it’s made of metal, wood, plastic, stone? No, all you can tell me is what? It’s a cross. And if I follow the shadow, I will get to what? The real cross. And I’ll see its color. I’ll know its dimensions. I’ll know its purpose. And so, you can’t understand the details of God’s words by following shadow laws. They point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ. Amen. Now, folks, that’s good stuff. And this is what Mr. Savage and Mr. Bush and Mr. Obama and Oprah has got all mixed up.
What does he mean by “shadow laws”? (Hebrews 10:1)

Hebrews 10:1-2: For the law, having a shadow of the good things to come, and not the very image of the things, can never with these same sacrifices, which they offer continually year by year, make those who approach perfect. For then would they not have ceased to be offered? For the worshipers, once purified, would have had no more consciousness of sins.
What does he say happens when people bash the Bible?

He says Jesus came to make us new people, so “old things passed away,” and he lists adultery, homosexuality, stealing, murder and hatred as the old things. He says “when you bash the Bible who points to Christ, you are bashing Christ” and removing the force that can change your life.
What does he say happens when people bash the Bible?

They don’t know their Bible. And they’re trying to tell people what the Bible says when they don’t know their Bible. Mr. Obama, I read my Bible. I know my Bible. And I know you’re wrong. Do you guys see that clearly? Yeah, it’s very clear. Did Jesus come to make us new people? Old things passed away. Isn’t that right? What’s our old things? Adultery, homosexuality, stealing, murder, hatred. You see, Jesus came and he has the power to fulfill what God destiny is for us. And when you bash the Bible who points to Christ, you are bashing Christ and you’re eliminating the force in your life that can change your life and change society.
What does he say happens when people bash the Bible?
2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.

He cites Isaiah 1:11 and says God did require the sacrifices, but “his goal wasn’t the shadow”; the people embraced the example and did not do what it said. He says the shadow laws were there “to remind them to treat people right, to live right, and to do right.”

So these are shadow laws, Mr. Savage. They have nothing to do with anything except to remind people in the Old Testament to live holy and right. Even in the Old Testament, Mr. Obama, God told him that he didn’t want these things. He told him that shadow laws were reminders to live right. Isaiah 1:11: “What purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to me? I don’t delight in the blood of bulls and lambs and goats when you come to me. Who has required this?” Well, he required it. He’s the one said to offer lambs. He’s the one said to burn incense. He’s the one said to take the Sabbath day off and worship God and meet together and come into the— He said all that. But see, his goal wasn’t the shadow. His goal was good. And they were embracing the shadow, the example, and not doing what the example said to do. Are you with me? And we read on and we see it. Bring no more worthless sacrifices. Incense is an abomination to me. New moon, Sabbath, feast. My soul hates when you spread your hands and make many prayers. I will hide my eyes from you and I will not hear you. And then he says what those shadow laws are for. Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean. Put away the evil of your doings from my eyes. Cease to do evil and learn to do good. You see, the shadow laws were there to remind them to treat people right, to live right, and to do right. And they were caught up in the shadow laws.

Isaiah 1:11-13: “To what purpose is the multitude of your sacrifices to Me?” Says the LORD. “I have had enough of burnt offerings of rams And the fat of fed cattle. I do not delight in the blood of bulls, Or of lambs or goats. “When you come to appear before Me, Who has required this from your hand, To trample My courts? Bring no more futile sacrifices; Incense is an abomination to Me. The New Moons, the Sabbaths, and the calling of assemblies— I cannot endure iniquity and the sacred meeting. Isaiah 1:16-17: “Wash yourselves, make yourselves clean; Put away the evil of your doings from before My eyes. Cease to do evil, Learn to do good; Seek justice, Rebuke the oppressor; Defend the fatherless, Plead for the widow.
How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?

He says the Lord’s table reminds us that Jesus died for our sins and gives new life, and we miss the point if we take communion but “don’t go to the real thing.” He says we assemble to be “stirred up to love one another” and do good when we leave, not for music or drama.
How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?

See, they embraced the shadow. Is this clear to you? Now, watch this. Let’s bring it up to date. The Lord’s table. Jesus said, as of— do you do this in what? Remembrance of me. It reminds us that he died for our sins that we can get forgiveness even as a Christian. And he gives us that new life, that resurrection. That’s what the communion table’s for. But when we just take communion and embrace communion and don’t go to the real thing, we live any way we want, don’t we? Let’s take another one. Assembling together. The Bible says, “Assembling yourself together, even the more so as you see the day approaching, stirring up one another to love and to good works.” See, that’s why we come together is to remind ourselves that we are to go out and be a light to this world that they may see our good works. That’s the purpose of assembling. It’s not music. It’s not drama. It’s not some prophet or priest. It’s we are supposed to be stirred up to love one another, not hurt one another, and do good when we leave. It’s not having a bell ringing message and you know some athlete come in and give their testimony or whatever. We should come to church too like the old the New Testament church when the Roman leaders wrote to each other about the church.
How do the Lord’s table and assembling together work as reminders?

Luke 22:19: And He took bread, gave thanks and broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is My body which is given for you; do this in remembrance of Me.” Hebrews 10:24-25: And let us consider one another in order to stir up love and good works, not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the manner of some, but exhorting one another, and so much the more as you see the Day approaching.
How are praise and baptism reminders, not substitutes?

He says praise and worship is a sacrifice, citing the “sacrifice of praise, the fruit of your lips,” and that “if your worship isn’t stirring you to live good, then you’re not worshiping.” He says baptism “reminds you that Jesus died on the cross for your sins” and made you a new man.
How are praise and baptism reminders, not substitutes?

They get together on Sunday and they make a vow not to do wrong. Every Sunday they kept repeating the vow. Why? Because they messed up sometimes and they had to change and they had to recommit to doing right. Have any of you Christians ever messed up? Yeah. You see? Hallelujah. Praise and worship. My gosh. You know, when I got saved, praise and worship was taboo. Like the Holy Ghost baptism, man. If you were filled with the Holy Ghost, you were in a church on the other side of the street and everybody looked down on you. And if you praise and worship God, lifting your hands and dancing and, you know, being outwardly demonstrative, man, that’s horrible. Now everybody’s doing it. But folks, praise and worship is a sacrifice. In Hebrews, it says, “Bring therefore the sacrifice of praise, the fruit of your lips, giving thanks to his name.” That’s our sacrifices. But the sacrifice is not what we embrace. We embrace who the sacrifice brings us to. And that’s the presence of Jesus. And Jesus wants us to live right. Isn’t that right? So it reminds us again to what? Live right, do good. And if your worship isn’t stirring you to live good, then you’re not worshiping. You’re enjoying music. That’s all. Hallelujah. H2O means water baptism in case you didn’t know that. You know, people got their baptism or certificate. Baptism doesn’t mean a hill of beans. Baptism reminds you that Jesus died on the cross for your sins, rose from the grave and made you a new man and an overcomer of sin.
How are praise and baptism reminders, not substitutes?
Hebrews 13:15: Therefore by Him let us continually offer the sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of our lips, giving thanks to His name.
Where do most American Christians put their confidence? (1 Samuel 15:22)

He asks whether Christians embrace the shadow or the reality, saying “We’re putting confidence in our church. We’re putting confidence in our baptism.” He cites 1 Samuel 15:22, “to obey is better than sacrifice,” and says God wants us to listen to Him, respond and live for Him.
Where do most American Christians put their confidence? (1 Samuel 15:22)

He put away sin. The old man is dead. So every time we see someone baptized, we are reminded that we’re new creatures. Sin no more has control over us. See, it’s a reminder. But what do most American Christians embrace? Do they embrace the shadow of the thing or do they really get the reality of the thing? See, we’re putting confidence in our church. We’re putting confidence in our baptism. We’re putting confidence and I take communion on Sunday when it should be pointing us to Jesus Christ and living for him. And that’s a good place for an amen. Now, these people are just wrong. Here it is again. 1st Samuel 15:22. Has the Lord a great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to listen better than the fat of rams. God wants us to listen to him and respond to him and live for him. And the sacrifices were there to direct us to that. Amen. Now I want to focus in on a very significant shadow law. This is important for you. You young Christians, you need to get this in your cranial vacuum. You old folks need to shake the cobwebs out of your head here and get this in there. Are you ready?
Where do most American Christians put their confidence? (1 Samuel 15:22)

1 Samuel 15:22: So Samuel said: “Has the LORD as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, As in obeying the voice of the LORD? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, And to heed than the fat of rams.
Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)

He cites John 7:19, “Moses gave you the law, yet none of you keep it,” and says it was impossible because they were constantly unclean and “spent all their life trying to get clean.” He says the Jews embraced the shadow instead of what it pointed to, and warns we are in danger of doing the same.
Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)

John 7:19, “Moses gave you the law, yet none of you keep it.” Why didn’t they keep it? Because it was impossible. Them guys were unclean every day. If they had sex with their spouse, they were unclean. If a bug landed on their— a bug landed on their plate or whatever, they were unclean. Every time you turn around, they’re unclean. They’re unclean. They spent all their life trying to get clean. The the shadow laws were impossible to keep. And yet the Jews embraced the shadow instead of what the shadow pointed to. And today we are embracing the shadow and to what the shadow points to. We’re in danger of that. Hallelujah.
Why couldn’t they keep the shadow laws? (John 7:19)
John 7:19: Did not Moses give you the law, yet none of you keeps the law? Why do you seek to kill Me?”
Why do some groups want you to follow them instead of Christ? (Galatians 6:13)

He cites Galatians 6:13 and says certain churches have you do certain things because “they glory in your flesh,” and that “they’re not wanting you to follow Christ.” He says the holy water that matters “is the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the word of the Lord.”
Why do some groups want you to follow them instead of Christ? (Galatians 6:13)

Galatians 6:13: “Neither they who are circumcised keep the law, but desire to have you circumcised so they may glory in your flesh.” Why does the Catholic Church have holy water there and all that and all this [unclear] and all this? So they can glory. That’s a Catholic. It does nothing. The holy water does nothing. The holy water is the baptism of the Holy Ghost and the word of the Lord. That’s the holy water. That’s the real thing. Can I hear an amen? Amen. See, why does certain churches have you do the certain thing? They glory in your flesh. Why does Dan Savage try to get you to believe the Bible’s full of BS so he can glory in your flesh turning from the Bible? Yeah. Yeah, I got through. See, they want you to follow them. They’re not wanting you to follow Christ. They want you to follow them, their group, their church. Now, that’s good preaching right there. And who are we to follow? And what word are we to follow? His word, right? Psalms 14 makes it even more clear. The Lord looked down from heaven to see if any understood who seek God. And his conclusion was they’ve all turned aside together. They’ve become corrupt. None does good. No, not one. You see, we mess up with these requirements of God. We mess up. But look at here. Us Christians make mistakes. Us believers make mistakes.
Why do some groups want you to follow them instead of Christ? (Galatians 6:13)

Galatians 6:13: For not even those who are circumcised keep the law, but they desire to have you circumcised that they may boast in your flesh. Psalm 14:2-3: The LORD looks down from heaven upon the children of men, To see if there are any who understand, who seek God. They have all turned aside, They have together become corrupt; There is none who does good, No, not one.
What is the importance of the shadow law, and why do we all make mistakes?

He says the shadow laws were impossible to keep because “they pointed to a requirement of God that was impossible without God for you to live up to.” He says believers make mistakes too, and that people who criticize the church can “always find” fault because we are “coming into maturity.”
What is the importance of the shadow law, and why do we all make mistakes?

I I’m a believer and I make mistakes. How many believers say, you know, I make mistakes? I made them in the past. I’ll probably make them tomorrow. Yeah. You see, this is the importance of the shadow law. The shadow laws were impossible to keep. Why? Because they pointed to a requirement of God that was impossible without God for you to live up to. It’s impossible. And this is the importance of the shadow law. The biggest biggest one. Now listen to this. Have all your workers of iniquity no knowledge? Who eat up my people as they eat bread and do not call on the Lord? See, this guy has the audacity to lambaste our Bible. A lot of these students walked out. When he started bashing the Bible, they walked out. Others applauded. And see, these people oppose us. Yes, they can find fault with us because we’re coming into maturity. We’re coming into his image. They can always find. You can’t be good enough for people that are trying to find something to criticize the church about. Ain’t I right? But see, us Christians know that Jesus is the answer for us and our mistakes. And you shouldn’t be messing around with this church. You should not be messing around with this church, even with their flaws. You don’t want to mess around with God’s people.
What is the importance of the shadow law, and why do we all make mistakes?
Psalm 14:4: Have all the workers of iniquity no knowledge, Who eat up my people as they eat bread, And do not call on the LORD?
Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?

He begins to address homosexuality by saying the food and clothing laws were “examples of living holy,” and that nobody was stoned in the Bible for the woman who lied about being a virgin: “Zero.” He says the one man stoned for working on Saturday was “an example of the judgment of God,” and that the real issue is an eternal price.
Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?

Now, let me address homosexuality. Now, we we address the food, the clothing, the different clothing. It was all examples of living holy. Okay? The virgin or the woman that wasn’t a virgin on her [unclear] night, she got stoned because she said she was a virgin. They didn’t put that in there and she wasn’t. She lied and and she went into a marriage with a lie and deception. And you know how many people were stoned for that in the Bible? Zero. Interesting, isn’t it? Why? It’s a shadow law. God didn’t put it there for us to go around killing people that sinned. It’s a shadow law. How many people were stoned for picking up sticks on the Saturday? One. One for working on Saturday and that was in in Exodus to give us an example of the judgment of God. You see there God is coming to judge and there is a judgment. But Jesus said, “I’ve not come to destroy sinners but to what? Save them.” See, God’s in his saving timetable right now. But when he comes again, folks, he’s going to judge. And stoning the people that messed up back there in the Bible is not the issue. It’s you are going to pay an eternal price.
Why weren’t people stoned for breaking the shadow laws?

Deuteronomy 22:20-21: “But if the thing is true, and evidences of virginity are not found for the young woman, then they shall bring out the young woman to the door of her father’s house, and the men of her city shall stone her to death with stones, because she has done a disgraceful thing in Israel, to play the harlot in her father’s house. So you shall put away the evil from among you. Numbers 15:32-36: Now while the children of Israel were in the wilderness, they found a man gathering sticks on the Sabbath day. And those who found him gathering sticks brought him to Moses and Aaron, and to all the congregation. They put him under guard, because it had not been explained what should be done to him. Then the LORD said to Moses, “The man must surely be put to death; all the congregation shall stone him with stones outside the camp.” So, as the LORD commanded Moses, all the congregation brought him outside the camp and stoned him with stones, and he died.
Who does he say was actually stoned in the Bible?

He says there is an eternal punishment “if you flagrantly disobey,” but most people stoned in the Bible were innocent: Nabal killed over a vineyard, prophets, and Stephen, all by those using the shadow law. He says people twisting the Scriptures “destroy people’s lives,” and “America’s buying it.”
Who does he say was actually stoned in the Bible?

That is what the shadow laws are trying to tell you. There’s an eternal punishment to pay if you flagrantly disobey. Hallelujah. Do you know what most people were stoned for in the Old Testament and in the New Testament? I didn’t think you did. Nabal was an innocent man. They wanted his vineyard and they used the shadow law to kill an innocent man. Prophets were innocent people. They used the shadow law to kill and stone prophets. Stephen was an innocent man. They use stoning. The Jews did the shadow law to kill Stephen. It’s these sinners like this Dan Savage that are twisting the scriptures to destroy people’s lives.
Who does he say was actually stoned in the Bible?

1 Kings 21:1-3: And it came to pass after these things that Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard which was in Jezreel, next to the palace of Ahab king of Samaria. So Ahab spoke to Naboth, saying, “Give me your vineyard, that I may have it for a vegetable garden, because it is near, next to my house; and for it I will give you a vineyard better than it. Or, if it seems good to you, I will give you its worth in money.” But Naboth said to Ahab, “The LORD forbid that I should give the inheritance of my fathers to you!” Acts 7:58-60: and they cast him out of the city and stoned him. And the witnesses laid down their clothes at the feet of a young man named Saul. And they stoned Stephen as he was calling on God and saying, “Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.” Then he knelt down and cried out with a loud voice, “Lord, do not charge them with this sin.” And when he had said this, he fell asleep.
What do Christians do when they sin?

He says if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess our sins “he is faithful and just to forgive our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” He says the shadow law points to someone who can do the impossible: “He’s the real deal.”
What do Christians do when they sin?

You get the point? Hallelujah. And America’s buying it. They are buying it hook, line, and sinker. See, this is what Christians know. If we say we have no sin, we deceive ourselves and the truth is not in us. You know, you say you’re Mr. Perfect, you’re lying through your teeth. You’re not looking at yourself good. Ask somebody that works with you. Ask somebody that lives with you in your home. They’ll tell you you got some problems. We can think real high and mighty of oursel, but the Bible says it’s not good for one to boast of himself. Let another boast of you. Let another who can see you right tell you the truth. And there might might not be much boasting there. But if we confess our sins, he is faithful and just to forgive our sins and cleanse us from all unrighteousness. See, we know that. We know the shadow law points to somebody that can do the impossible in our life. That which the law couldn’t do. The shadow laws could not do, Jesus can do. And so when we sin, we confess he’s reliable. He’s faithful. He forgives. And we go on. That’s what Mr. Savage and these people need to understand. And Jesus isn’t the shadow. He’s the real deal. If we say we have not sinned, we make him a liar and his word’s not in us. See, that’s the importance of the shadow law. The superior shadow law is is impossible to live by.
What do Christians do when they sin?

1 John 1:8: If we say that we have no sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us. 1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness. 1 John 1:10: If we say that we have not sinned, we make Him a liar, and His word is not in us. Proverbs 27:2: Let another man praise you, and not your own mouth; A stranger, and not your own lips.
Does the Bible say anything about masturbation?

He says shadow laws “bring us to Christ” and have “nothing to do with eating shellfish or not eating shellfish.” He says he has read the Bible 121 times and “there is nothing in the Bible about masturbation,” and asks if a critic is wrong about that, “could he be wrong about homosexuality?”
Does the Bible say anything about masturbation?

Just like it is impossible for you to live by God’s laws of righteousness, but through Christ who strengthens us, who quickens us by might in the inner man, who comes and gives us empowerment to do all things through Christ. We can do these things. And if we mess up, we can get up and get going again. Shadow laws bring us to Christ. It’s got nothing to do with eating shellfish or not eating shellfish. And never nowhere. He said the Bible is wrong on masturbation. Folks, I’ve read that Bible 121 times. I’ve studied it for hours. There is nothing in the Bible about masturbation. Zero. You have to fabricate it. To make a scripture talk about masturbation. You have to dream it up. See, he’s totally wrong. And I submit to Dan Savage, if he’s wrong in this elementary thing about the Bible, could he be wrong about homosexuality? The law was our school master to bring us to Christ. The only way I am come, Jesus said, to destroy the law, not to destroy, it should say, I’m come not to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfill them. Okay. Who fulfilled the shadow laws? [unclear] He plainly— Jesus plainly said he did.
Does the Bible say anything about masturbation?

Philippians 4:13: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. Galatians 3:24: Therefore the law was our tutor to bring us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith. Matthew 5:17: “Do not think that I came to destroy the Law or the Prophets. I did not come to destroy but to fulfill.
Is Jesus the only way, and what does he say about Muslims?

He says Jesus fulfilled the shadow laws, so “you don’t need to sacrifice animals anymore,” and quotes “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” He says Muslims do not believe Jesus died, rose, or is the Son of God, that “there’s no truth outside of Jesus,” and that we need to reach Muslims, homosexuals and all people.
Is Jesus the only way, and what does he say about Muslims?

You don’t need to sacrifice animals anymore. He did the sacrifice. You don’t need to give incense. You can pray right to him. You can go directly to God. You see, you don’t need to all do these shadows anymore. You got the real deal. Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life.” No one Muslims. President Bush said Muslims and non-believers were going to heaven. Did you hear that? President Bush said Muslims and non-believers are going to heaven. Mr. President, you’re totally wrong. Muslims do not believe Jesus died on the cross. Muslims do not believe he rose from the grave. Therefore, Muslims do not believe that he is the only begotten son of God. He was God in the flesh and Jesus said, “I am the only way.” President Bush, you’re wrong. Oprah, you’re wrong. Obama, you’re wrong. Jesus is the only way. And his word, the scriptures show us the way to him. Can I hear an amen? That’s good for you guys to know this so you have answers for people out there. We need answers for people. We need to be able to answer them back. There’s no truth outside of Jesus. There’s no life outside of Jesus. And he’s the only way to the father. And the father is God. And that’s why we need to reach the Muslims. That’s why we need to reach the homosexuals. That’s why we need to reach all people. Bring them to Christ. He can straighten them out. Now folks, some of these students [unclear]. Mothers, I submit to you today, would your child have walked out, or would your child have applauded this bashing of the Bible? Mothers, fathers, would you have applauded or would you have walked out?
Is Jesus the only way, and what does he say about Muslims?
John 14:6: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through Me.
Can you understand God’s word by following the shadow laws?
He says no: “you can’t understand the details of God’s words by following shadow laws. They point to the real thing, and that is Jesus Christ.”
Did Jesus come to make us new people?
He says yes: “old things passed away,” and Jesus “has the power to fulfill” God’s destiny for us.
What does he say the shadow laws were for in Isaiah 1?
He says after rejecting the empty sacrifices, God says, “Wash yourselves. Make yourself clean,” and “Cease to do evil and learn to do good.”
Why does he say we assemble together?
He says it is “to remind ourselves that we are to go out and be a light to this world that they may see our good works.” He says, “It’s not music. It’s not drama.”
What does he say the early church did every Sunday?
He says Roman leaders wrote that Christians “get together on Sunday and they make a vow not to do wrong,” and “Every Sunday they kept repeating the vow.”
What does he say baptism means?

He says a baptism certificate alone “doesn’t mean a hill of beans”; baptism reminds you that Jesus died for your sins and made you a new man. Whenever we see someone baptized, we are reminded that “we’re new creatures.”
What does he say about people who look for fault in the church?
He says “You can’t be good enough for people that are trying to find something to criticize the church about.” He says, “You don’t want to mess around with God’s people.”
How many people does he say were stoned for picking up sticks on Saturday?
He says one, “to give us an example of the judgment of God.” He says God is in “his saving timetable right now” but will judge when he comes again.
What does he say about people who say they are perfect?
He says if you say you’re “Mr. Perfect, you’re lying through your teeth,” and suggests asking somebody who works with you or lives with you in your home.
What does he say happens when a believer sins and confesses?
He says “The shadow laws could not do, Jesus can do,” and that when we sin and confess, “He’s reliable. He’s faithful. He forgives. And we go on.”
What does he say Jesus said about the law and the prophets?
He says Jesus came “not to destroy the law or the prophets, but to fulfill them,” and that “Jesus plainly said he did.” He adds that “The law was our school master to bring us to Christ.”
Why does he say we need these answers?
He says, “We need to be able to answer them back,” and that we need to reach all people and “Bring them to Christ.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer answers the claim that men wrote the Bible by walking through Ezekiel’s allegory of Jerusalem as a “she” and the death of Ezekiel’s wife, which he says shows the…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer answers the claim that men wrote the Bible by walking through Ezekiel’s allegory of Jerusalem as a “she” and the death of Ezekiel’s wife, which he says shows the difference between religion and reality. He then connects it to Sarah and Hagar in Galatians 4, the heavenly Jerusalem “coming down,” the church as the bride, grace as divine enablement, and God’s goal of a glorious church.
Why does Ezekiel call Jerusalem a “she”?

He says Ezekiel gives the month, the day and the year that Babylon started its siege, and refers to Jerusalem as “a she, as a female,” which he says is “very important.” He calls it a bloody city killing innocent people that “has wearied herself with lies.”
Why does Ezekiel call Jerusalem a “she”?

And you can see a picture on your screen of the old-time Jerusalem. The wall facing you is east, and the reason I know that is because the temple entry was from the east, so you’re looking at the eastern wall, the eastern gate of Jerusalem. He begins to talk about Jerusalem, and he tells us what month, what day of the month, and what year of the captivity that Babylon came and started their siege against Jerusalem. Now remember, Ezekiel is the prophet on the other side of the captivity. He is in Babylon. Jeremiah was in Jerusalem, in Judah, and, uh, they’ve already been carried away captive once. God already came and corrected them one time, but they didn’t learn their lesson. Okay, so Ezekiel, by the Spirit of God, lifts up his voice, and he brings up the topic of Jerusalem. He goes on to keep talking about Jerusalem, and he refers to Jerusalem as a she, as a female, and that’s very important. He goes on to describe it as a bloody city. They are killing innocent people. All right, they’re persecuting and killing and hurting innocent people. Then he says she, the city, she has wearied herself with lies. Her— feminine— she, feminine, likened to Jerusalem as a female, a she. That’s very important.
Why does Ezekiel call Jerusalem a “she”?

Ezekiel 24:1-2: Again, in the ninth year, in the tenth month, on the tenth day of the month, the word of the LORD came to me, saying, “Son of man, write down the name of the day, this very day—the king of Babylon started his siege against Jerusalem this very day. Ezekiel 24:12: She has grown weary with lies, And her great scum has not gone from her. Let her scum be in the fire!
Did men write the Bible, or is it from God?

He tells young believers who hear that “men wrote the Bible” and that it is “just a bunch of myths” that Ezekiel is “another example that man did not write this book.” He says, “Only God could do these amazing things and then fulfill them.”
Did men write the Bible, or is it from God?

And you young people, and you young believers, who hear this nonsense that men wrote the Bible, and, you know, the Bible’s just a bunch of myths and just a bunch of nonsense, and, as a homosexual activist said, just a bunch of BS, I want to show you— here’s another example that man did not write this book. Only God could do these amazing things and then fulfill them, talk about them and then fulfill them, and make it clear to us. Are you with me? He goes on to continue to talk about her condition, which is already bloody and lies. All right, “in your filthiness is lewdness,” or in your loose conduct, your loose plans, is uncleanness, including sexual immorality and immorality of all kinds. He says that’s your condition, and he’s talking to his people. His people, he’s saying, are liars; they’re hurting innocent people.
Did men write the Bible, or is it from God?

Ezekiel 24:13: In your filthiness is lewdness. Because I have cleansed you, and you were not cleansed, You will not be cleansed of your filthiness anymore, Till I have caused My fury to rest upon you.
Can you be “clean by faith” and still live in sin?

He says God told Ezekiel’s generation, “I have purged you, and you’re not purged,” and compares America’s church saying “I’m clean by the blood” while living in sin. He asks, “what good is it do me if I’m only cleaned by faith,” and says “It’s absolutely no good,” because God judges your ways, not what you believe.
Can you be “clean by faith” and still live in sin?

And they conduct themselves very loose, sexual immorality and all other kinds of immorality going on, “because I have purged you.” I’ve cleansed you, “and you were not purged.” He already came one time and brought correction and brought the prophet’s message. Jeremiah, we gave it to you, it was very powerful, the new covenant and the promises He gave, and these people did not listen to Jeremiah. So God raises up Ezekiel to come and tell them the same thing. And the condition of America’s church is exactly what Ezekiel says. They have been purged by faith, but they’re not purged. Everybody in America, “Oh yeah, I’m clean by the blood, I’m clean by the blood.” They’re shacking up with people, they’re taking drugs and getting drunk and doing all kinds of debauchery, but “I’m clean by the blood.” This is exactly what God spoke through Ezekiel: “I have purged you, and you’re not purged.” The blood hasn’t worked in your life. You’re just believing you’re clean by faith, and you’re not clean. Isn’t America like that right now? And who gets the credit for it? These ministers, these mega churches, these people that are out to sell books and just flatter the people and be popular. They are propagating this message that only cleans by faith. Folks, what good is it do me if I’m only cleaned by faith, clean by faith, and I don’t change my life? It’s absolutely no good. I’m just like any other religion. No other religion on earth can give you cleansing of the body, soul and mind. “You shall not be cleansed from your filthiness anymore till I’ve caused My fury to rest upon you.” He says, “I’m coming with another correction. I’m coming with another judgment. I’m coming with another punishment to get your attention to change your ways.” And it’s just two years away. He’s prophesying in the ninth year of Zedekiah, the king of Israel. And Jerusalem was started to be surrounded by Babylon’s army this day, and just less than two years away they’re going to be carried away captive, and the city’s going to be destroyed, and the temple’s going to be destroyed. This time— I mean, last time God left the temple and the city; this time He’s going to destroy it all. Are you there? He said, “I purged you once, I came and I got your attention, and you didn’t listen, so I’m coming again.” And that is where America’s church is right now. The end result, verse 14: “I the Lord have spoken it; it shall come to pass, and I will do it. I will not go back, neither will I spare, neither will I repent. According to your” what? “Ways.” Not your faith. It is over and over and over again. It’s not what you believe. “Well, I believe this is okay.” It doesn’t matter if you believe something is okay if your ways are wrong according to God’s ways. He’s going to judge you and your doings. Do we get the message now? This God has promised us, “if any man be in Christ, he is a new creature, old things are passed away.” We’ve been promised change in our life, but when it doesn’t happen real quickly, then we start justifying, because God doesn’t do things real quickly, but He’s always on time. He’s just amazing. He’s always on time. And when things don’t happen the way we want them to happen, and in the time we wanted to happen, we start trying to solve the thing ourself.
Can you be “clean by faith” and still live in sin?

Ezekiel 24:13-14: In your filthiness is lewdness. Because I have cleansed you, and you were not cleansed, You will not be cleansed of your filthiness anymore, Till I have caused My fury to rest upon you. I, the LORD, have spoken it; It shall come to pass, and I will do it; I will not hold back, Nor will I spare, Nor will I relent; According to your ways And according to your deeds They will judge you,” Says the Lord GOD.’ ” 2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new.
How can the Bible be written by men and still be from the Holy Spirit?

He says nobody “could dream this stuff up,” and that this Book “was written by men through the Spirit of God.” They “wrote what the Spirit made them write,” and he says they were “a bunch of hardheads like us.”
How can the Bible be written by men and still be from the Holy Spirit?

So God says, “I’m not going to repent. I’m not going to turn back from judging you. It’s your ways and your doings that I’m after. I came once and I punished you, I corrected you, and I’m coming again.” All right, then here’s this amazing allegory introduced. Amazing. And these people say the Bible’s just written by men. You’ve got to be kidding. Nobody could dream this stuff up that God has hidden in these Scriptures that only the Holy Ghost can expose to you. Are you there? And you young believers need to know that this Book was written by men through the Spirit of God. They didn’t write what they wanted to write; they wrote what the Spirit made them write. They were a bunch of hardheads like us, but the Spirit made them right. How many would like the Holy Ghost to make you live right? Yeah, this is what God has promised us.
Why did God tell Ezekiel not to mourn his wife’s death?

He says God told Ezekiel He would take away “the desire of your eyes,” his wife, and that he must not mourn, but put on traveling clothes instead of mourning clothes. When the people asked what it meant, he says they knew “it was an allegory,” and God answered that He would profane His sanctuary.
Why did God tell Ezekiel not to mourn his wife’s death?

“Son of man,” verse 16 and 17, “Look, I take away from you the desire of your eyes with a stroke.” He’s talking to Ezekiel personally now. He said, “Ezekiel, I’m going to take away the desire of your eyes with one sweep. Yet neither shall you mourn nor weep for the dead.” Wow. He’s talking personally to Ezekiel and says, “Ezekiel, you desire something with your eyes, and I’m going to take it away, and you’re not going to mourn about it.” So Jerusalem is likened to Ezekiel’s wife, as we will see here. Remember, Jerusalem was a she. Right, hello, church? All right, now he gets down to the nitty-gritty. Your wife, and that was the desire of Ezekiel’s eyes, was his wife. He loved his wife. Man, how would you like to be married to him? And God comes to illustrate, “You’re dead, you’re gone. Bye.” She died early because God had an illustration. But see, death in God is not like we see death. “At evening my wife died”— that was the desire of his eyes— “and I did in the morning as I was commanded.” He didn’t mourn, he didn’t put on mourning clothes. He was instructed, “Don’t you put on mourning clothes; you put on traveling clothes.” And so we see here a picture of Ezekiel, and his wife’s dead, and these people are coming to him and go, “What? You know, why ain’t you mourning? Why? You know the custom, the culture. You mourn, you, you know, you’re sorry.” Oh, so these people knew something was up. So the people came to Ezekiel and said, “Will you tell us what these things are to us that you do?” They knew Ezekiel had been prophesying for several years now, and they knew he had been given illustrations for several years, so they come and say, “Okay, what are you trying to tell us now? Your wife died, you’re not mourning, you’re dressed in traveling clothes.” They knew that it was an allegory. They knew, they wanted to know what God was telling them. “Thus saith the Lord.” He tells them, this is what the Lord is saying through my wife’s death, through Jerusalem being an allegory of a female: “Behold, I will profane My sanctuary.” Now, where was His sanctuary back then?
Why did God tell Ezekiel not to mourn his wife’s death?

Ezekiel 24:16-21: “Son of man, behold, I take away from you the desire of your eyes with one stroke; yet you shall neither mourn nor weep, nor shall your tears run down. Sigh in silence, make no mourning for the dead; bind your turban on your head, and put your sandals on your feet; do not cover your lips, and do not eat man’s bread of sorrow.” So I spoke to the people in the morning, and at evening my wife died; and the next morning I did as I was commanded. And the people said to me, “Will you not tell us what these things signify to us, that you behave so?” Then I answered them, “The word of the LORD came to me, saying, ‘Speak to the house of Israel, “Thus says the Lord GOD: ‘Behold, I will profane My sanctuary, your arrogant boast, the desire of your eyes, the delight of your soul; and your sons and daughters whom you left behind shall fall by the sword.
What is the difference between religion and reality?

He says the temple and city were the desire of the Jews’ eyes: “We’ll die for that city, we’ll die for that temple, but we won’t die to live right.” He says Ezekiel’s wife died so God could illustrate “the difference between religion and reality,” and that the majority of Christians in America are living in sin and thinking they’re okay.
What is the difference between religion and reality?

In the temple in Jerusalem. That’s where God dwelt, on the cherubim, between the cherubim on the ark of the covenant. Are you there? See, that was the [unclear]. That’s where God dwelt. And that was the desire of the Jews’ eyes: that temple and that city. They were obsessed with it. They’re committing adultery, they’re lying, they’re killing innocent people, but boy, don’t you talk about that temple, and don’t you talk about that city. Don’t you touch that temple, don’t you touch that city. We’ll die for that city, we’ll die for that temple, but we won’t die to live right. Are you there, church? Very powerful, didn’t it? And Ezekiel’s wife died so God could illustrate in an allegory the difference between religion and reality. Okay, “My sanctuary,” the temple, Jerusalem, “the excellency of your strength, the desire of your eyes.” That’s what the people’s desires was, “and that which your soul pities.” See, when bad things happened to Jerusalem or the temple, they felt so bad for it. Oh, but it did— they didn’t feel bad at all sinning and breaking God’s Word. And that’s exactly where America’s church is, on the most part. Not everybody, but the majority of Christians in America are living in sin and thinking they’re okay. Am I right? Absolutely. Jerusalem likened to Ezekiel’s wife. He said, “Then your sons and your daughters whom you have left shall fall by the sword.” Who’s paying the price for adults in America living loosely? The children. Everybody’s talking about the problems with our kids, but nobody is putting the blame where it belongs, and that is the adults need to buck up and be adults and stand for morality and live right at the cost of their own pain. You stay married, you get married, you raise that kid, you do what’s right. Here is Sarah and Hagar, an amazing allegory made clear in Galatians, the New Testament, 4:21. This amazing allegory, I think it’s just amazing. It’s extraordinary.
What do Sarah and Hagar teach about doing things God’s way?

He explains the shadow laws as illustrations of what Christ would do, and says Abraham and Sarah doing it their way instead of waiting for the promise is “religion.” He says the American church does the same when it brings in “psychology,” 12-step programs and other secular programs “because they won’t wait for God’s promise.”
What do Sarah and Hagar teach about doing things God’s way?

He says in 4:21 of Galatians, “You that desire to be under the law, do you not hear the law?” Now, the law he’s talking about is the shadow laws, the laws that were an illustration of the truth He was going to perform and bring into reality when He came to earth, born of a virgin and dying on the cross. That’s what the shadow laws are. The civil laws are still with us— there’s a difference— the spiritual laws are still with us, but these Jews, they were obsessed with the shadow laws. See, Jerusalem was an illustration of what He was going to do. The temple was an illustration, an allegory of what He’s going to do, and they were obsessed with the illustrations. “For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one by a bond woman,” a slave, a bond slave; she sold herself into servanthood. “The other by a free woman.” Sarah was the free woman. “He who was of the bond woman was born after the flesh.” And here’s where America is. Abraham and Sarah, after 10 years God promised them a son. It didn’t happen. Sarah came up with the idea, said, “You know, why don’t you go into my handmaiden Hagar, have sex with her and have a son by her, ‘cause God’s moving a little slow here, and I’m not sure He’s going to do anything. We don’t have an heir.” And Abraham, the dumb guy, like dumb men do, listened to his wife. He said, “Oh, Sarah, oh, what a great idea! Oh man!” It probably didn’t hurt that Hagar was pretty good-looking either. So he goes in, has sex. See, that’s of the flesh. When you do it your way, that’s religion. You’re doing it your way. You don’t wait for the promise; you get anxious and you do it your way. “He of the free woman was by promise.” You see, God promised Sarah and Abraham a son. He didn’t say when. Abraham was 90 years old; he’s going to be 100 years old; 10 years have gone by. “Man, we’ve got to help God out.” And that’s what the American church is doing. They’re bringing in psychology, and they’re bringing in the 12-step programs, and the, uh, uh, divorce recovery program and the alcohol recovery program, the secular programs they’re bringing in. Why? Because they won’t wait for God’s promise and seek Him until He comes and does it. Galatians 4:24, he goes on to talk about two Jerusalems. There’s the old Jerusalem, here’s the new Jerusalem, “which things are an” what? Allegory. I told you there was an amazing allegory, and I told you you can only call things an allegory when God calls it an allegory. “These are two covenants.” How many covenants? Two. “One from Mount Sinai,” that law that he spoke about, the shadow laws.
What do Sarah and Hagar teach about doing things God’s way?

Galatians 4:21-24: Tell me, you who desire to be under the law, do you not hear the law? For it is written that Abraham had two sons: the one by a bondwoman, the other by a freewoman. But he who was of the bondwoman was born according to the flesh, and he of the freewoman through promise, which things are symbolic. For these are the two covenants: the one from Mount Sinai which gives birth to bondage, which is Hagar—
Who is the “mother of us all”: the church of religion or the Jerusalem above?

He says the religious church will “birth them into bondage,” while those born of the Spirit are free from sin, judgment and darkness. He points to “the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all,” and says the earthly city and temple were an allegory of the real thing.
Who is the “mother of us all”: the church of religion or the Jerusalem above?

“Is Hagar, which births to bondage.” And that’s what the religious church does. They birth them into their church and they birth them into bondage. We’re supposed to be birthed into the Spirit and into the living church. Amen. Born again by the Spirit, and over in the epistle, by the Word, born again. “She answers to Jerusalem which is now.” This is this Jerusalem, the Jewish religion, the Jerusalem in Ezekiel, in bondage to sin. They’re not purged, they’re shedding innocent blood, they’re lying, they’re obsessed with their Jewish religion. They are obsessed with their city, they’re obsessed with the temple, all the illustrations of what God would do. In truth, they’re obsessed with it. “Jerusalem which is now is in bondage with her children.” See, her children, that’s what he told. They’re her children, the offspring, and the Christians that these false churches are producing, they’re destroying them, as Jesus said, “You make them two times the child of hell than you are.” That’s what religion does. But see, the blind lead the blind. People want religion; they don’t want the truth. Are you there? You’ve got to decide: do you want the real thing, or do you want religion number two? “But the Jerusalem which is above is free, which is the mother of us all.” Powerful. See, mothers are producers; they’re birthers. The Jerusalem from above is free. See, the people birthed by the real church are free: free from sin, free from the judgment, free from the kingdom of darkness. They’re free, they’re liberated, they’re new creatures. Yes, it takes a process. Yes, God has a little timetable between His promise and His provision, but it will come if you do what He said. “The mother of us all.” What a statement. Did you catch that statement? Jerusalem from above is the mother of us all. The natural city of Jerusalem, the natural temple in the city, was nothing but an allegory, an illustration of the real thing. But the Jerusalem from above is the real thing, and that Jerusalem, that temple, that city births every one of us. That’s why the city was referred to as a female, and that’s why the church is referred to as a female. God keeps the continuity all the way through the Bible. Don’t you tell me that Bible was written by men and just a bunch of myths and all that. This Bible is real.
Who is the “mother of us all”: the church of religion or the Jerusalem above?

Galatians 4:25-26: for this Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and corresponds to Jerusalem which now is, and is in bondage with her children— but the Jerusalem above is free, which is the mother of us all. Matthew 23:15: “Woe to you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! For you travel land and sea to win one proselyte, and when he is won, you make him twice as much a son of hell as yourselves.
Is the “foursquare city” literal, or is the New Jerusalem the bride of Christ?

He says the New Jerusalem “comes down out of heaven from God,” that the foursquare city is “an illustration,” and that “the city is the bride.” He says, “Give me Jesus, my husband, that I can have a relationship with,” and that he needs the heavenly Jerusalem now rather than waiting for the rapture.
Is the “foursquare city” literal, or is the New Jerusalem the bride of Christ?

Amen. “Mother of” [unclear]. What is the mother of [unclear] then? And how, here we got the new Jerusalem, and we got the bride over here. Revelation 3:12: “The name of the city of My God is” what? “New Jerusalem.” The city of God is the new Jerusalem, which is the mother of us all, “which comes down out of heaven from God.” It what? Comes down. Well, that’s talking about the end time when that foursquare city comes out. They’ve been lying to you. That is an illustration, folks. Ain’t no foursquare city. Good grief, grow up, get into college Christianity. Don’t get drooling over symbols; get the reality of the symbols. And he’s talking about this foursquare city with its 12 gates and all that. What you got to understand here is this city, the heavenly Jerusalem, is coming down. It’s not staying up there. See, it comes down today, it’ll come down tomorrow, it came down yesterday. You get it? You know, don’t tell me I got to wait for the rapture and all this stuff. I need the heavenly Jerusalem now. How about you? I need to be birthed now. I can’t wait for some rapture and silly end-time idea you have. I need a God that’s powerful now and can change my life now, and that’s the God we serve. Revelation 21:2: “I, John, saw the holy city.” John said, “I saw it, New Jerusalem, the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down from God out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.” He said, “I saw it coming down.” It came down on the day of Pentecost. It came down just a few chapters over, when they come and prayed together and the building shook. See, and God has been coming down “prepared as a bride adorned for a husband.” And you see the bride here, which is the city. Now, which one do you want to be, a city or you want to be the bride of Christ? Yeah, the city is the bride. Don’t give me this foursquare nonsense; that’s the illustration. Give me Jesus, my husband, that I can have a relationship with, and I can produce because I have a relationship with Him. That’s the new Jerusalem I need. Hallelujah. And so you understand it, 2 Corinthians 11:2: “I have engaged you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ.” The church is the bride. He says again in Romans 7:4, “You should be married to another, even to Him who is raised from the dead.” Who is that? Jesus. “That we should” what? “Bring forth fruit.” So it’s imperative that I have a relationship with Jesus, that heavenly Jerusalem, so I can bring forth the fruit of love and a joy and a peace and so forth. Amen. It’s out of the relationship that fruit is naturally produced. The church comes to and is the heavenly Jerusalem.
Is the “foursquare city” literal, or is the New Jerusalem the bride of Christ?

Revelation 3:12: He who overcomes, I will make him a pillar in the temple of My God, and he shall go out no more. I will write on him the name of My God and the name of the city of My God, the New Jerusalem, which comes down out of heaven from My God. And I will write on him My new name. Revelation 21:2: Then I, John, saw the holy city, New Jerusalem, coming down out of heaven from God, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband. 2 Corinthians 11:2: For I am jealous for you with godly jealousy. For I have betrothed you to one husband, that I may present you as a chaste virgin to Christ. Romans 7:4: Therefore, my brethren, you also have become dead to the law through the body of Christ, that you may be married to another—to Him who was raised from the dead, that we should bear fruit to God.
Have Christians already come to the heavenly Jerusalem?

He says Hebrews 12:22 is “talking to the saints”: “You are come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God.” He says they didn’t go to heaven; “they came to the church, heard the message and touched God,” and “we are that heavenly city when that heavenly city touches us.”
Have Christians already come to the heavenly Jerusalem?

See, we come to the heavenly Jerusalem, and we are the heavenly Jerusalem when we connect with heaven. Hallelujah. When we’re not connected with heaven, we are the Jerusalem below, which now is religious. Watch this: Hebrews 12:22, talking to the saints, talking to the believers: “You are come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God.” And what was the name of the city of the living God? New Jerusalem, the heavenly Jerusalem. He explains it: “You’ve come to the heavenly Jerusalem.” Well, you know, they didn’t go to heaven; you know, they came to the church, heard the message and touched God. Am I right? Yeah. Why do we fantasize and put all this stuff off into the future? I need a God now that will come down to me. “To an innumerable company of angels, the general assembly, the church of the firstborn.” Now, who’s the church of the firstborn? We are. We come out from among the nations, we come to Jesus. That’s what church means: the assembled, the ones that gather out, coming out of. That’s what the church is. So see, we come to the heavenly city, and we are that heavenly city when that heavenly city touches us.
Have Christians already come to the heavenly Jerusalem?

Hebrews 12:22-24: But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, to an innumerable company of angels, to the general assembly and church of the firstborn who are registered in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect, to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling that speaks better things than that of Abel.
What does “on earth as it is in heaven” mean?

He asks what the Lord’s Prayer means by “Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven,” and says it is the real city of God, the real church, “coming down and touching His people.” He says on the day of Pentecost and all through Acts heaven “kept coming down,” and warns against getting hung up on one visitation of God.
What does “on earth as it is in heaven” mean?

We become that heavenly city on earth. What do you think in the Lord’s Prayer, He said, “Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven”? What do you think that means? Did you ever ask God about that? What in the world are you talking about? He’s talking about the real city of God, the real church, the real temple coming down and touching His people and making it as the real church on earth as it is in heaven, because the real thing come down and changed them, “which are written in heaven, to God the Judge of all, to the spirits of just men made perfect, to Jesus the Mediator of the new covenant.” So where’s God? In Jesus. Where’s God in Jesus? The heavenly Jerusalem that comes down. If the city comes down and the heavenly temple comes down, who comes down with them? Who is living in the heavenly Jerusalem? Jesus. Yeah, God and Jesus. So when they come down and we’re gathered together, the church becomes the heavenly Jerusalem on earth, and people can touch the real thing. So we see clearly that the heavenly Jerusalem, the heavenly temple, the heavenly city must be in contact with the earthly one before any results are going to happen. We need the heavenly coming down to us on earth. And that’s what happened on the day of Pentecost. That’s what happened when they prayed and the place was shaken, and all through the book of Acts heaven was coming down. It kept coming down, it kept coming down, it kept coming down, and it expressed Himself differently every time He came down. And that’s one of our problems: we get hung up on one visitation of God, we want to propagate it the rest of our life. There’s all kinds of things to acquiring God. How many want them all? Yeah.
What does “on earth as it is in heaven” mean?
Matthew 6:10: Your kingdom come. Your will be done On earth as it is in heaven.
What is the New Jerusalem like: crystal, light and the nations?

He says “the condition of the new Jerusalem is not like the old Jerusalem,” quoting Revelation 21:10 about a light “clear as crystal,” a stone with all impurities out. He says when we connect with it “we get transformation in our life,” so people can be saved from sin, judgment and darkness.
What is the New Jerusalem like: crystal, light and the nations?

The condition of the new Jerusalem is not like the old Jerusalem. Revelation 21:10: “He showed me that great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God.” The what? Glory. The honor of God. “And her light was like a stone most precious, clear as crystal.” How many of you know crystal has all the impurities out of it? When you look through it, there’s no impurities. Everything’s been, it’s been heated up to such a level there’s not one little speck of impurity, and when you thump it, it has that ring. See, He says, “I put a new song in your heart, even praise unto our God, and many shall see it and turn and put their trust in the Lord.” When we get like the crystal, and we get [unclear], we don’t hate back. There’s a song that comes out of us that people want to have what we have. “And the glory of God did lighten it, and the Lamb is the light thereof.” And who’s the Lamb? Jesus. You see, Jesus and His Word is the light, and when the heavenly thing comes down and we connect with it, then we have the real light, we have the real Jesus, and we get transformation in our life. The results: “The nations of them which are saved shall walk in the light of it.” See, what’s the whole purpose of Him doing this? So people can get saved from their sin, saved from the judgment, saved from the power of darkness, saved from alcohol habits and drug habits and cigarette habits and whatever. They can be delivered, they can be set free. What? By the power of Jesus Christ and His Father, God and our Father.
What is the New Jerusalem like: crystal, light and the nations?

Revelation 21:10-11: And he carried me away in the Spirit to a great and high mountain, and showed me the great city, the holy Jerusalem, descending out of heaven from God, having the glory of God. Her light was like a most precious stone, like a jasper stone, clear as crystal. Psalm 40:3: He has put a new song in my mouth— Praise to our God; Many will see it and fear, And will trust in the LORD. Revelation 21:23-24: The city had no need of the sun or of the moon to shine in it, for the glory of God illuminated it. The Lamb is its light. And the nations of those who are saved shall walk in its light, and the kings of the earth bring their glory and honor into it.
Who gets written in the Lamb’s Book of Life?

He says “there is a move of God coming before Christ comes that’s going to revolutionize this whole earth,” because God is “after the nations.” He says believing in Jesus is “one requirement,” and that you also turn from lying and the works God hates for your name to be written in the Book of Life.
Who gets written in the Lamb’s Book of Life?

“They will bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it.” You see, I’m telling you, there is a move of God coming before Christ comes that’s going to revolutionize this whole earth, ‘cause God is after the nations. His death on the cross wasn’t for a puny few million. His death on the cross was a big thing. It’s powerful, and He’s after the nations, and He has to change you to reach them. “There shall not enter anything that defiles, lies, or works in abomination, but they which are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” And I submit to you, if that statement is true, then what do you got to do to get written in the Lamb’s Book of Life? “But I believe in Jesus. I believe in Jesus. I’m in the Lamb’s Book of Life.” That’s one requirement.
Who gets written in the Lamb’s Book of Life?

Revelation 21:26-27: And they shall bring the glory and the honor of the nations into it. But there shall by no means enter it anything that defiles, or causes an abomination or a lie, but only those who are written in the Lamb’s Book of Life.

He reads Ephesians 3:7 and asks whether it sounds like “grace is just the unmerited favor of God.” He says no: “There’s a power working in grace,” and this “shows that grace is divine enablement, not just a little favor.”

What’s the requirement here? That I turn from lying, I turn from those things that God hates. Abominations, I stop doing the works of them. Then my name is written in the Book of Life. The church, the heavenly Jerusalem, was a mystery from the beginning of time. Ephesians 3:7: “I was made a minister according to the gift of the grace of God given unto me by the effectual working of His power.” Now, does that sound like grace is just the unmerited favor of God, free gift, and pop, that’s it? No. There’s a power working in grace, and that grace made him a minister. And all Americans have is grace that somehow is going to get me to heaven no matter what I do.

Ephesians 3:7-8: of which I became a minister according to the gift of the grace of God given to me by the effective working of His power. To me, who am less than the least of all the saints, this grace was given, that I should preach among the Gentiles the unsearchable riches of Christ,
What is the mystery hidden from the beginning of the world?

He says the mystery, “a secret, something hidden,” is the church, hidden since God created all things by Jesus Christ. He says the purpose was that “spiritual powers in heavenly places” might know the many different kinds of the wisdom of God, and that the plan started before He said let there be light.
What is the mystery hidden from the beginning of the world?

This is just one place that shows that grace is divine enablement, not just a little favor: the working of His what? Power. “Unto me, who am less than the least of the saints, is this grace given” into me, “that I should preach” this grace. I preach the gospel to all people so all men may see “what is the fellowship of the” what? Say that word: mystery. That’s a secret, something hidden. Well, what’s hidden? “This mystery from the beginning of the world.” When did this mystery start? Yeah, when God said, “Let there be light.” This mystery started. It has been hidden, “God who created all things by” who? Jesus Christ. Now, why did He do that? “To the intent”— to the purpose— “that now unto the principalities and powers in heavenly places,” spiritual powers. The purpose is that spiritual powers in heavenly places “might be known by the church the many different kinds of the wisdom of God.” So what’s the mystery? The church. See, “I’ve come to the heavenly Jerusalem, the city of God, to the church of the firstborn.” His purpose was to build a church from the time He said, “Let there be light.” In fact, it was before that. Jesus died before the foundation of the world. His whole plan started before He said, “Let there be light.”
What is the mystery hidden from the beginning of the world?

Ephesians 3:9-11: and to make all see what is the fellowship of the mystery, which from the beginning of the ages has been hidden in God who created all things through Jesus Christ; to the intent that now the manifold wisdom of God might be made known by the church to the principalities and powers in the heavenly places, according to the eternal purpose which He accomplished in Christ Jesus our Lord,
What is God’s goal for the church?

He says the promise is “I will build My church,” and the goal is a glorious church “not having spot or wrinkle.” He says the Second Coming is not just around the corner (“no way”), because God must still fulfill these promises and bring the nations in, and that Jesus is able to keep you from falling by divine enablement.
What is God’s goal for the church?

Hallelujah. And it was the church, and the many different kinds of wisdom. How many want the full wisdom of God, not just one little corner? Yeah, I mean, come on, church, we got to go for it. We got to go for this stuff. God’s goal for His church in the heavenly Jerusalem: the promise, Matthew 16:18, “I will build My church.” That’s the promise. Okay, the goal: “The gates of hell shall not prevail against it.” You know why Satan is running Christians’ lives in America? Because they don’t understand this revelation of what the new Jerusalem really is, the city of God really is, and the people, that the Jesus and God in that city that comes down and touches us and transforms us. The goal, Ephesians 5, “that He might present it to Himself a” what? “Glorious church.” You think the American church, on the most part, is glorious right now? No way. So you think the Second Coming is just around the corner? No way. He’s got to fulfill these promises, He’s got to bring these nations in, He’s going to do everything He said He would do. “Not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that it should be holy and without” what? “Blemish.” That’s the goal. That’s the promise. Now unto Him, Jude 24, and who’s Him? Jesus. “Unto Him that is able to” what? “Keep you from falling.” Does that sound like grace is just a, a flattering thing, a favor? He can keep you from that. That’s divine enablement. He comes by His divine power and encourages you and strengthens you and builds you up by might in the inner man, as the Bible says, and you little by little, line upon line, you become a person that walks in truth. We have great hope, folks. We have a great promise. And this is one of the most powerful messages you can hear. It’s been hidden for decades, but God revealed it when Christ came: the church. You are the apple of His eye. You, He wants to make into a crystal with a sound that gets people’s attention. A—
What is God’s goal for the church?

Matthew 16:18: And I also say to you that you are Peter, and on this rock I will build My church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it. Ephesians 5:27: that He might present her to Himself a glorious church, not having spot or wrinkle or any such thing, but that she should be holy and without blemish. Jude 24: Now to Him who is able to keep you from stumbling, And to present you faultless Before the presence of His glory with exceeding joy,
Where were Ezekiel and Jeremiah when Jerusalem was under judgment?

He says Ezekiel was the prophet “on the other side of the captivity,” in Babylon, while Jeremiah was in Jerusalem, in Judah. He says they had already been carried away captive once and God had corrected them, “but they didn’t learn their lesson.”
Why does he say the condition of America’s church matches what Ezekiel says?

He says people say “I’m clean by the blood” while living in sin, which he says is exactly what God spoke through Ezekiel: “I have purged you, and you’re not purged.” He says ministers who flatter people and are “out to sell books” spread this message that only cleans by faith.
What was coming to Jerusalem in less than two years?

He says Jerusalem was being surrounded by Babylon’s army, and in less than two years the people would be carried away captive and the city and temple destroyed. He says, “this time He’s going to destroy it all.”
Does it matter what you believe if your ways are wrong?

He says, “It doesn’t matter if you believe something is okay if your ways are wrong according to God’s ways.” He says we are promised change in our life, but when it doesn’t happen quickly we start justifying and trying to solve it ourselves.
Were the people who wrote the Bible perfect?
He says they were “a bunch of hardheads like us, but the Spirit made them right.” He asks how many would like the Holy Ghost to make them live right and says this is what God has promised.
Where did God dwell in Ezekiel’s day?

He says it was in the temple in Jerusalem, “on the cherubim, between the cherubim on the ark of the covenant.” He says that temple and city were what the people were obsessed with while committing adultery, lying and killing innocent people.
Who does he say pays the price when adults live loosely?

He says “the children” do, and that the adults need to “buck up and be adults and stand for morality and live right at the cost of their own pain.” He says nobody is putting the blame where it belongs.
What does he mean by the “shadow laws”?

He says they are “the laws that were an illustration of the truth He was going to perform and bring into reality when He came to earth, born of a virgin and dying on the cross.” He says the civil laws and the spiritual laws are still with us, but the Jews were obsessed with the shadow laws.
How many covenants does Galatians 4 describe, and what are they?

He says there are two: one from Mount Sinai, “that law,” the shadow laws, which is Hagar and bears children into bondage; and the Jerusalem which is above, which is free. He says you can only call things an allegory when God calls them an allegory.
Why does he say the city and the church are referred to as a female?
He says the Jerusalem from above is “the mother of us all,” and the natural city and temple were an allegory of the real thing. He says, “God keeps the continuity all the way through the Bible.”
Does he say we have to wait for the rapture to experience the heavenly Jerusalem?

He says the heavenly Jerusalem “comes down today, it’ll come down tomorrow, it came down yesterday,” and “I need a God that’s powerful now and can change my life now.” He says he can’t wait for some rapture and end-time idea.
What does it mean that the church is the bride of Christ?

He cites 2 Corinthians 11:2 and Romans 7:4 and says “the church is the bride,” married to Christ so that we “bring forth fruit.” He says it is imperative to have a relationship with Jesus, and that “it’s out of the relationship that fruit is naturally produced.”
What does he say “the church of the firstborn” means?
He says it is us: “we come out from among the nations, we come to Jesus.” He says that is what church means, “the assembled,” and that we come to the heavenly city and become it when it touches us.
Why does he compare believers to crystal?

He says crystal has all the impurities out, heated until “there’s not one little speck of impurity,” and when you thump it, it has that ring. He says that when we get like crystal, “we don’t hate back,” and “there’s a song that comes out of us that people want to have what we have.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 1:3-4 that believers are called to be partakers of the divine nature. He traces the first promise in Genesis 3:15, the woman’s seed bruising Satan’s…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from 2 Peter 1:3-4 that believers are called to be partakers of the divine nature. He traces the first promise in Genesis 3:15, the woman’s seed bruising Satan’s head, and says Jesus and His church have rendered Satan powerless. He then uses the parable of the wheat and the tares in Matthew 13 to explain why the good and bad seed grow together, and how behavior shows who are children of God and who are children of the devil.
What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)

He says 2 Peter 1:3-4 gives “exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature.” “We’re not a fan sitting in the stand watching the Super Bowl game; we are out there on the field playing the game.” He says Christians tend to look elsewhere, but being participators in God’s nature “needs to be a high priority in our life.”
What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)

In 2 Peter 1:3-4: “As Jesus the divine power has given us all things,” “whereby by these things are given us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature.” Okay, participators of the divine nature. We’re not a fan sitting in the stand watching the Super Bowl game; we are out there on the field playing the game. We’re participants. Okay, now American Christians have a tendency to look for the second coming, a prosperity, purpose, positive confessions, focusing on the poor instead of the divine nature, or phenomenal-- Miracles and so forth. We have a tendency to look for gifts and all that, and a lot of groups focus on different areas, uh, some on soul-winning and so forth, but God very strongly puts in His Word that there are promises that we can be participators in the divine nature, God’s nature, and so that needs to be a high priority in our life. Could that be true? Okay, now we have to ask ourself, what are these promises that I through them can become a participator of God’s divine--
What does it mean to be a partaker of the divine nature? (2 Peter 1:3-4)

2 Peter 1:3-4: as His divine power has given to us all things that pertain to life and godliness, through the knowledge of Him who called us by glory and virtue, by which have been given to us exceedingly great and precious promises, that through these you may be partakers of the divine nature, having escaped the corruption that is in the world through lust.
What is the first promise in the Bible? (Genesis 3:15)

He says the first promise was “to declare war on Satan and Satan’s seed.” In Genesis 3:15, “I will put war between you and the woman, between your seed and her seed,” and her seed “shall bruise your head,” your chief part, your authority. Read with “he,” he says, it is Jesus who bruises Satan’s head and Satan who bruises His heel.
What is the first promise in the Bible? (Genesis 3:15)

Nature? This seed has been impregnated with good nourishment, and it will produce nourishing fruit. Okay, John 8:44: “You are of your father the devil.” You see, “he does not stand in the truth.” That is positive identification. When people don’t stand up for truth, they are the seed of who? Satan. It’s not saying, “I’m a Christian, I got a baptismal certificate.” When you stand up for truth, that shows you’re God’s seed, and when you don’t stand up for Truth, it shows that you’re of Satan. Is that positive identification? Yeah, okay. Let’s go again.
