When you rule and reign in this life, you’re way above the Navy SEALs. Hallelujah. You think that Kobe and these basketball players are hot stuff? They don’t even come close to the people that are ruling and reigning in this life. Hallelujah. Oh, if I could just be wealthy like Billy Gates. Listen, if you got control over your spirit, you are much better off than Billy Gates. He’s an atheist. Money is not the answer, fame is not the answer. The real people are people that let Christ rule and reign in them, and they rule and reign in earth. Amen. That’s the real heroes.
What does it mean that Jesus made us kings and priests?

Revelation 5:9-10: And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy to take the scroll, And to open its seals; For You were slain, And have redeemed us to God by Your blood Out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation, And have made us kings and priests to our God; And we shall reign on the earth.” Proverbs 16:32: He who is slow to anger is better than the mighty, And he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city.
Can I really do all things through Christ who strengthens me?

He says yes: Christ strengthens and empowers you with supernatural power to do what the world cannot do, so we can labor to reach this fulfillment of the righteousness of the law and attain it. He ends that we are more than conquerors, nothing can separate us from the love of God, and “we need Christ reigning in us, and we need to start reigning now in this life.”
Can I really do all things through Christ who strengthens me?

“I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me.” Is it possible that we can labor to reach this fulfillment of the righteousness of the law of God and attain it? Yes. Why? Because I can do all things through who? Christ. He will get me there. Yes, hallelujah. My trust is in Him, my hope is in Him, everything I have is in Him, my future is in Him. He is Jesus Christ, the only God, and I can do this stuff. He strengthens me. What does Christ do? He strengthens you, He empowers you, supernatural power to do what the world cannot do. Philippians 4:13, I mean Romans 8:37, “We are more than conquerors,” overcomers. Nothing can separate me from the love of God. He says there’s nothing: principalities, powers, things not seen, things that are seen, plagues, famines, you know, economic crisis, nothing can shake me from Jesus Christ, nothing. Hallelujah. I submit to you today that we need Christ reigning in us, and we need to start reigning now in this life.
Can I really do all things through Christ who strengthens me?

Philippians 4:13: I can do all things through Christ who strengthens me. Romans 8:37-39: Yet in all these things we are more than conquerors through Him who loved us. For I am persuaded that neither death nor life, nor angels nor principalities nor powers, nor things present nor things to come, nor height nor depth, nor any other created thing, shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
He says it is sin, and the strength and power of sin is the law. He gives Romans 6:23 on the wages of sin being death.
If I have a bad thought, have I sinned?
He says no: “don’t beat yourself up if you’re not activating the thought. Relax.” The sin is when you activate the wrong desire.
He says it is the lake of fire, another death besides the body dying that everyone must confront. He says it is the eternal death, “when that eternal body will be eternally punished forever.”
He says it is Jesus Christ and those saints of old coming out of the grave when He came out of the grave. If you take part in it, he says, the second death has no power over you.
Does he take the thousand years in Revelation literally?

He says you can get into the thousand years all you want, but he would be careful about making it a real thousand years, because other things in the Scriptures did not happen in the time period God said. “The key here is not the thousand years”; it is reigning and ruling with Christ.
How can God’s law be the strength of sin?
He says it threw him at first, and explains that the law not only reveals that the things I am doing are bad but also brings a punishment for them.

He says lust “just means a desire,” and the word isn’t an evil word in itself: “it’s the way you take it, it’s the direction you use it.” The same lust can work toward things you shouldn’t do or things you should.
Are we free to throw out the law because we are under grace?
He says no: the law is spiritual, and people who say we’re not under law, we’re under grace, “to such an extreme that they just throw out all the laws of God,” are being ridiculous.
Did Paul struggle with sin like we do?
He says Paul’s description of doing what he hates is him, even after he was saved: “I knew that was wrong but I did it anyway.” He says Paul is separating sin as a separate segment of your life.
What does it mean that Jesus “condemned sin in the flesh”?
He says “condemn” means He put to death that sin working in my flesh, and that Jesus can destroy sin in my life without destroying me.
Can I work my way into salvation?
He says you cannot work your way into that initial salvation, which is a free gift, but if you are going to grow in God you have to put effort into it and apply yourself.
What is “the old man” that I am supposed to put off?

He says the old man lied, stole, got angry and got bitter, and gave harmful talk; that was my old sinful nature, and we put away that kind of thing and put on kindness, forgiveness, patience and humbleness.
Does shaking or rolling on the floor change how you live?

He says some in Pentecostal and charismatic circles look for a spirit that will do everything for them, and then “they live the same way they lived before,” because they are not putting off and not letting the Holy Spirit and the Word bring them to discipline the old man.
Why lift your hands when you do not feel like it?
He says it is a breaking of the outward man, the old man, and “that’s how you put on the new man.” God honors that humble response.
What does he say about psychology and Paul’s teaching?
He says “we need more Paul teaching in this American church and less psychology,” and “in fact we don’t need psychology.” He says to put on self-control.

items.d: In this first message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer begins from the idea that people with charts and predictions missed Jesus’ first coming and may be wrong about the second. He asks what…
p: In this first message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer begins from the idea that people with charts and predictions missed Jesus’ first coming and may be wrong about the second. He asks what the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5 is, then starts the four horsemen: the white horse and whether it is the Antichrist, what the Bible says about “antichrist,” the rider of Revelation 19:11, and the red horse, closing with Mark 13:7 on wars and the end.
Why does he say we can be wrong about the second coming the way people were wrong about the first?

He says the Jews and the preachers who had “their charts” at Jesus’ first coming “missed every point,” because they looked for a son of David to restore the kingdom from Rome, and “the Messiah wasn’t coming to restore the natural kingdom from Rome to them. He was coming to put a kingdom in people’s lives.” He says “we can be wrong today,” and “they did not know the Messiah was God Himself when He came the first time.”
Why does he say we can be wrong about the second coming the way people were wrong about the first?

Seriously, okay, we’re going to get into the Bible this morning, and we are talking about the book of Revelation, and today we’re going to be talking about six of the seven seals. Now, the approach to Revelation is strictly from the book of Revelation, and you’ve got to remember this, please. Get this in your cranial vacuum what I’m going to say. The Jews and the preachers, when Jesus came, had their charts. They had it all figured out what was going to happen, how it was going to happen, and they missed every point. Do you realize that? You see, the Jews had it wrong the first time Jesus came. They were looking for a son of David to restore the kingdom to them from Rome, and the Messiah wasn’t coming to restore the natural kingdom from Rome to them. He was coming to put a kingdom in people’s lives. See, they were totally wrong, and we can be wrong today. They did not know the Messiah was God Himself when He came the first time. They didn’t have that in their charts and their predictions. They did not know.
What does he say defiles us, and what did the religious teachers of Jesus’ day miss? (Mark 7:15; Matthew 11:14)

He says “it is things within that defile us, and not what we eat or what we wear,” and “it’s what comes out, those words and those actions, that’s what defiles us and condemns us.” He says they “had doctrines of clothing, Sabbath day’s journey,” and “the washing of hands and dishes,” and of the Sabbath rule says “it’s not in the Bible, they made it up.” He says they “didn’t know that John the Baptist was Elijah that was to come in the spirit,” and “they wanted and tried to kill Jesus, God Himself.”
What does he say defiles us, and what did the religious teachers of Jesus’ day miss? (Mark 7:15; Matthew 11:14)

It is things within that defile us, and not what we eat or what we wear. See, Seventh Day Adventists, they’re still into the food program. The holiness people are into no jewelry and no makeup, and you know, look pale and don’t go to hell. You know, and it’s not what we eat. We can eat pork, we can eat what, it has nothing to do with our character and nothing to do with our spiritual man and nothing to do with sin. See, it’s what comes out, those words and those actions, that’s what defiles us and condemns us. They had doctrines of clothing, Sabbath day’s journey, you can only go so far on the Sabbath day, it’s not in the Bible, they made it up, the washing of hands and dishes and all this stuff. You see, they had all of these doctrines, and when Jesus came, they missed it totally. They didn’t know that John the Baptist was Elijah that was to come in the spirit, the forerunner of Jesus, and they cut off his head. They wanted and tried to kill Jesus, God Himself, which violated the Ten Commandments they claim to believe in. Amen. And a lot of these theoretical people about the second coming, they don’t balance their checkbook, they don’t stay married, they violate the very book that they say that they believe in, but yet they got this second coming all figured out.
What does he say defiles us, and what did the religious teachers of Jesus’ day miss? (Mark 7:15; Matthew 11:14)

Mark 7:15: There is nothing that enters a man from outside which can defile him; but the things which come out of him, those are the things that defile a man. Matthew 11:14: And if you are willing to receive it, he is Elijah who is to come.
What does he say about preachers who predict the end time and the day or hour? (Matthew 24:36)

He says preachers “have made millions of dollars selling you a bill of goods, claiming to know the inside of the end time, when Jesus Himself and God Himself said twice, no man knows the day or the hour.” He says they “still predict the day,” yet “Nobody knows but God Himself.” He says some in Jesus’ day thought He was an old prophet risen from the dead, and “this is what happens with the second coming teaching. We wind up leaving Jesus Himself, the most important person in the Bible, the goal of the Bible, and get into our petty little doctrines that mean nothing.”
What does he say about preachers who predict the end time and the day or hour? (Matthew 24:36)

And let me tell you something: preachers have made millions of dollars selling you a bill of goods, claiming to know the inside of the end time, when Jesus Himself and God Himself said twice, no man knows the day or the hour. They still predict the day, they still, still, still predict the year and the month and everything else, and it says plainly, what? Nobody knows but God Himself. And you buy their books, and you got the book to read yourself, and they’re making a fortune. Literally, some believed Jesus was an old prophet risen from the dead. Look at that doctrine they conjured up. Well, this is one of them old prophets, I don’t know which one, but it’s one of them that raised from the dead. And they believed Jesus was a sinner. They called Him a sinner, and He’s God, and God cannot what? Sin. The Bible says there was no sin in Him. And this is what they said: if we leave Jesus alone, all will believe on Him. Well, duh, that’s the whole point. We’re supposed to be believing and trusting in and following Jesus Christ, but they wanted people to believe in their group, their doctrine, and leave Jesus. And this is what happens with the second coming teaching. We wind up leaving Jesus Himself, the most important person in the Bible, the goal of the Bible, and get into our petty little doctrines that mean nothing.
What does he say about preachers who predict the end time and the day or hour? (Matthew 24:36)
Matthew 24:36: “But of that day and hour no one knows, not even the angels of heaven, but My Father only.
What did the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand about Jesus? (Matthew 16:22; 17:4; 11:2-3)

He asks, “if they missed the first time, could it be possible we don’t know beans about the second time?” He says “even the apostles did not understand that Jesus was going to die,” that Peter said “you can’t die,” that they “wanted to be number one,” and wanted to build three tabernacles at the transfiguration: “these are the apostles, the chosen twelve.” He adds that John the Baptist later sent his disciples to ask “Are You the One?” and asks, “just because we hear something, does that mean we got it?”
What did the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand about Jesus? (Matthew 16:22; 17:4; 11:2-3)

Are you with me now? My point is this: if they missed the first time, could it be possible we don’t know beans about the second time? See, they knew the Messiah was coming, just as we know Jesus is what? Coming again. We know that it says over and over He’s coming the second time. And so with that introduction, we’re going to be studying this book of Revelation. Even the apostles did not understand that Jesus was going to die. He told them He’s going to die, and they still didn’t get it. Isn’t that right? So just because we hear something, does that mean we got it? No. No, in fact, Peter said, “Well, you can’t die. We’re not going to let you die.” They wanted to be in charge of others, the first, you know, they wanted to be number one. They wanted to build three tabernacles when Jesus was transfigured. They wanted to build one for Jesus, one for Moses, and one for Elijah. See, they got it all wrong, and these are the apostles, the chosen twelve. John the Baptist, after declaring that Jesus was the One to come and take away the sins of the world, check this out. After John the Baptist declared and baptized Jesus, then a little bit later he sends his disciples to Jesus and said, “Are You the One?” And yet in this day and hour, these guys are proclaiming they got all this knowledge.
What did the apostles and John the Baptist misunderstand about Jesus? (Matthew 16:22; 17:4; 11:2-3)

Matthew 16:22: Then Peter took Him aside and began to rebuke Him, saying, “Far be it from You, Lord; this shall not happen to You!” Matthew 17:4: Then Peter answered and said to Jesus, “Lord, it is good for us to be here; if You wish, let us make here three tabernacles: one for You, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” Matthew 11:2-3: And when John had heard in prison about the works of Christ, he sent two of his disciples and said to Him, “Are You the Coming One, or do we look for another?”
What does he say about prophecy writers who keep revising their predictions?

He says the author of a popular end-time book “has changed his theory twelve times that I know of, because he predicted some things that did not happen, so he had to rewrite his book, and people bought it again.” He then introduces today’s topic, “six of the seven seals,” and notes that Daniel “was told to shut up the words and seal the book.”
What does he say about prophecy writers who keep revising their predictions?

And the guy that wrote The Late Great Planet Earth, Hal Lindsay, has changed his theory twelve times that I know of, because he predicted some things that did not happen, so he had to rewrite his book, and people bought it again. And they just keep buying it, like Hal Lindsay got some kind of personal insight that no one else has. Are you with me? So with that in our cranial vacuum, we don’t have a cranial vacuum anymore, we got something in there, you know, let’s just keep this thing simple. All right, what are we teaching on today? Six of the seven seals. You remember in the book of Daniel, Daniel himself, that they use to twist Scriptures and get these ideas, was told to shut up the words and seal the book.
What does he say about prophecy writers who keep revising their predictions?
Daniel 12:4: “But you, Daniel, shut up the words, and seal the book until the time of the end; many shall run to and fro, and knowledge shall increase.”
Could we be hearing Revelation without understanding it, like Daniel? (Daniel 12:8)

He says Daniel said, “I heard, but I understood not,” and asks, “could it be possible, when we read the book of Revelation, we are hearing but we’re not getting much understanding out of it?” He says “we don’t always understand things, and there’s nothing wrong with it.” When Jesus came the first time, “they started understanding as things happened,” and “all their charts didn’t amount to anything,” so at His second coming “we may be totally wrong in saying how He’s going to do it.”
Could we be hearing Revelation without understanding it, like Daniel? (Daniel 12:8)

Are you there? And in the last chapter, when the angel is talking to Daniel, Daniel says, “I heard, but I understood not.” Could it be possible, when we read the book of Revelation, we are hearing but we’re not getting much understanding out of it? And Daniel, who was one of the three heroes of the Old Testament, did not understand what the angel was saying. Could it be possible we don’t always understand things, and there’s nothing wrong with it? And this is the point: when Jesus came the first time, they started understanding as things happened, the virgin conceiving and having a child. See, then as it was preached and as it happened, then they started what? Getting understanding. All their charts didn’t amount to anything, all their programs and all their ideas they come up with had to be thrown out when it started happening. And it could be the same way when Jesus comes the second time. When He starts doing something, we’re going to go, “Oh, that’s what that is! Oh, that’s what that is!” Because God is doing something again, and we can identify it as He does it, and we may be totally wrong in saying how He’s going to do it. Could that be a good amen? Hallelujah.
Could we be hearing Revelation without understanding it, like Daniel? (Daniel 12:8)
Daniel 12:8: Although I heard, I did not understand. Then I said, “My lord, what shall be the end of these things?”
What is the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5, and what other books does the Bible mention? (Revelation 5:5; 20:12; Isaiah 29:11)

He calls this “a college course. This isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching.” He reads Revelation 5:5 about the Lion of the tribe of Judah who “hath prevailed to open the book and to loose the seven seals thereof,” and says the Bible tells us “about eight books in the Bible itself,” including the Book of Life and the book of our works in Revelation 20:12, where “everything we did, everything we say is written there.” He then rules out the Scriptures themselves and the judgment book of Israel and Babylon, and raises the sealed book Isaiah saw.
What is the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5, and what other books does the Bible mention? (Revelation 5:5; 20:12; Isaiah 29:11)

And with that in your head, I told you this is a college course. This isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching. You know, in college you listen to the professor and then you got to go home and study for hours to get it. Are you there? So we got a bunch of non-wimps in here this morning. You came to hear this tough teaching, hard to sit there. Okay, we got a picture of the Lamb, and the seven seals are open, there, of the book in Revelation 5:5: “The Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, hath prevailed to open the book and to loose the seven seals thereof.” What book? The Bible tells us about eight books in the Bible itself. The Book of Life, you know, if our name’s in there, we go to heaven, if it’s not, we’re in trouble. The book of our works, in Revelation 20:12, everything we did, everything we say is written there, and if we’re in the Book of Life, we’re not judged out of the things in the book of works. Hallelujah. Anyway, we know it’s not that book. We certainly know it’s not the Scriptures, the Bible itself, because Jesus opened understanding to them. We know it’s not the judgment book of Israel and Babylon and Jeremiah, because that was to them. We know that the sealed book that Isaiah saw could be it. This is a sealed book. Isaiah saw a sealed book, but it was sealed, it wasn’t opened, and so it just goes on. He saw a sealed book and that’s it.
What is the book with seven seals in Revelation 5:5, and what other books does the Bible mention? (Revelation 5:5; 20:12; Isaiah 29:11)

Revelation 5:5: But one of the elders said to me, “Do not weep. Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has prevailed to open the scroll and to loose its seven seals.” Revelation 20:12: And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their works, by the things which were written in the books. Isaiah 29:11: The whole vision has become to you like the words of a book that is sealed, which men deliver to one who is literate, saying, “Read this, please.” And he says, “I cannot, for it is sealed.”
Could the book be Isaiah’s, Ezekiel’s or Daniel’s sealed book, or the book of remembrance? (Ezekiel 2:9-10; Daniel 12:4; Luke 21:20; Exodus 17:14)

He considers whether it is the sealed book Isaiah saw, the book of woe in Ezekiel, or Daniel’s sealed book, and says “there’s a lot of woes when this book starts getting opened.” He says that in Luke, “when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh,” so “the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD was the fulfillment of Daniel,” and “some of Daniel’s book was open, so I doubt it’s Daniel’s book.” He also considers the book of remembrance in Exodus 17:14 and says, “I doubt it’s that book, because people have been sinning ever since.”
Could the book be Isaiah’s, Ezekiel’s or Daniel’s sealed book, or the book of remembrance? (Ezekiel 2:9-10; Daniel 12:4; Luke 21:20; Exodus 17:14)

The book was locked up and stayed locked up, so maybe that could be it. The book of woe in Ezekiel that Ezekiel saw could be, because there’s a lot of woes when this book starts getting opened, there’s a lot of woes. And then the sealed book of Daniel that I told you about earlier, seal the book, all those things he saw, he said seal it up until the last days, but we got some revelation of Daniel’s sealed book. When Jesus came, Jesus said that the abomination of desolation, when you see that, you know that the time is nigh, in Matthew 13:14 and in Mark. But in Luke it says, “When you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that the desolation thereof is nigh.” So we know that the destruction of Jerusalem in 70 AD was the fulfillment of Daniel. We know that, so at least part of Daniel’s sealed book was opened up, if not all of it, then. And so Daniel’s book could have been fulfilled during Jesus’s birth, death, and resurrection, and the church period, the early church period. Are you with me? Because we have some insight that some of Daniel’s book was open, so I doubt it’s Daniel’s book. Hallelujah. And we also know that Jesus came and all that in that book of Daniel. And then you got the book of remembrance. In Exodus 17:14, Amalek came and attacked Israel and picked on the stragglers and the weak ones, and God says, “I’m going to have a book of remembrance for him.” And a few hundred years later, sure enough, God says, “Okay, it’s time to judge Amalek for what he did back there to Israel and the weak ones and the straggling.” He picked on the stragglers and the weak ones, and He had Saul to rise up and destroy that nation and that king. Are you there? And so I doubt it’s that book, because people have been sinning ever since
Could the book be Isaiah’s, Ezekiel’s or Daniel’s sealed book, or the book of remembrance? (Ezekiel 2:9-10; Daniel 12:4; Luke 21:20; Exodus 17:14)

Ezekiel 2:9-10: Now when I looked, there was a hand stretched out to me; and behold, a scroll of a book was in it. Then He spread it before me; and there was writing on the inside and on the outside, and written on it were lamentations and mourning and woe. Matthew 24:15: “Therefore when you see the ‘abomination of desolation,’ spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in the holy place” (whoever reads, let him understand), Luke 21:20: “But when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation is near. Exodus 17:14: Then the LORD said to Moses, “Write this for a memorial in the book and recount it in the hearing of Joshua, that I will utterly blot out the remembrance of Amalek from under heaven.”
What does he say the book in Revelation is, and how can a record in the book of remembrance be erased?

He says “most likely the book in Revelation is its own book. It’s the book of wrath. It’s a book that explains God’s day of wrath that already has been explained throughout the Scriptures. It’s not a fresh new revelation.” He says “when you do things, God remembers,” but you can get it erased by repenting: “That’s the power of the blood. The power of the blood is endless, and there is nothing it can’t cleanse.”
What does he say the book in Revelation is, and how can a record in the book of remembrance be erased?

Eve. And yes, there’s a book of remembrance, and He does come to correct and deal with that. Most likely the book in Revelation is its own book. It’s the book of wrath. It’s a book that explains God’s day of wrath that already has been explained throughout the Scriptures. It’s not a fresh new revelation. Are you with me? I wanted you to know there’s eight books in the Bible. See, there is a book of remembrance. When you do things, God remembers. All right, you can get it erased by what? Repenting. Absolutely. “I was wrong.” That’s the power of the blood. The power of the blood is endless, and there is nothing it can’t cleanse. Don’t ever forget that. And a simple humbling yourself and admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness and cleansing gets it done.
Who rides the first horse in the seven seals, and does the Bible say it is the Antichrist? (Revelation 6:1-2)

He says “we feel like we got to interpret the stuff, and this is where we get into our problem.” The first horse is “a white horse with a rider that has a crown and a bow,” going “conquering and to conquer.” He says most interpreters say it is the Antichrist, but “it never says in the Bible that the Antichrist rides a white horse.”
Who rides the first horse in the seven seals, and does the Bible say it is the Antichrist? (Revelation 6:1-2)

Hallelujah, that’s the bottom line. Now, let’s go. Okay, here we are, the four horsemen. The seven seals are going to be opened here. And here comes the interpretations of all these things. We feel like we got to interpret the stuff, and this is where we get into our problem. All right, we get four horses. The first one is a white horse with a rider that has a crown and a bow, and this horse and rider, they go conquering and to conquer. See, now they say that this is a war horse and rider, or most of them say this is the Antichrist. It never says in the Bible that the Antichrist rides a white horse.
Who rides the first horse in the seven seals, and does the Bible say it is the Antichrist? (Revelation 6:1-2)

Revelation 6:1-2: Now I saw when the Lamb opened one of the seals; and I heard one of the four living creatures saying with a voice like thunder, “Come and see.” And I looked, and behold, a white horse. He who sat on it had a bow; and a crown was given to him, and he went out conquering and to conquer.
What does he say the Bible teaches about “antichrist”? (1 John 2:18; 4:2-3)

He says “it never says that the Antichrist is some one person that’s going to rise up in the earth,” and “we conjure up these things and then we go to the Scripture to fit them in, and this is our problem.” He says the apostle John “said there are many antichrists” because “they oppose Christ,” saying “Christ hasn’t come in the flesh, He wasn’t the Word that came in the flesh, He wasn’t God.” He says “the Jews who do not believe Jesus has come the first time, they are what? Antichrist,” and adds, “That’s the truth. They oppose Jesus.”
What does he say the Bible teaches about “antichrist”? (1 John 2:18; 4:2-3)

Never. It never says that the Antichrist is some one person that’s going to rise up in the earth. Never says that anywhere. We conjure up these things and then we go to the Scripture to fit them in, and this is our problem. You see, John, the apostle John himself, said there are many antichrists. You see why? Because they oppose Christ. They say Christ hasn’t come in the flesh, He wasn’t the Word that came in the flesh, He wasn’t God. That’s antichrist. That’s opposing Christ. And so the Jews who do not believe Jesus has come the first time, they are what? Antichrist. Oh, you can’t say that, that’s intolerance. That’s the truth. They oppose Jesus, and God was
What does he say the Bible teaches about “antichrist”? (1 John 2:18; 4:2-3)

1 John 2:18: Little children, it is the last hour; and as you have heard that the Antichrist is coming, even now many antichrists have come, by which we know that it is the last hour. 1 John 4:2-3: By this you know the Spirit of God: Every spirit that confesses that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is of God, and every spirit that does not confess that Jesus Christ has come in the flesh is not of God. And this is the spirit of the Antichrist, which you have heard was coming, and is now already in the world.
Who is the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11, and what about the crowns and the bow? (Revelation 19:11-15; 4:10)

Reading Revelation 19:11, he says “now we got somebody on a white horse,” called “Faithful and True,” and answers the objection about one crown versus many: “when the elders bow before Him, they cast their crowns. He put them back on His head.” He says “you find Jesus came also with a bow and with an arrow,” and “the bottom line is it doesn’t tell us who this white horse rider is.” He says the messages to the seven churches tell them to “be overcomers.”
Who is the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11, and what about the crowns and the bow? (Revelation 19:11-15; 4:10)

Jesus. Amen. That’s what the Scripture says, and that’s all the authority we have to preach, is what the Scripture says. But now we do have a Scripture in Revelation that tells us about a white horse. In Revelation 19:11, there was a white horse, and “he that sat on him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness he doth judge and make war. And on his head were many crowns, and out of his mouth goes a sharp sword, with it he shall smite the nations that war against him and his army.” Now we got somebody on a white horse, but they say, “Well, the one here is one crown, and over there it’s many crowns.” Well, dummy, when the elders bow before Him, they cast their crowns. He put them back on His head. That’s as good a theory as yours. You think you’re going to get any honor when you stand before Jesus Himself? You’re going to give it back to Him. Why? You wouldn’t have any honor if it wasn’t for Him. So yeah, He’s going to wear your crown, because He’s the one empowered you to get your crown. Hallelujah. He says, “Well, He’s got a bow and not a sword.” Yes, but if you go through the Scriptures, you find Jesus came also with a bow and with an arrow. All right, so He can use the sword, the bow and arrow, they’re both the Word of God. But the bottom line is it doesn’t tell us who this white horse rider is. That’s the bottom line, it just says this guy. Now, does Jesus, is Jesus conquering? Yes. Is He going to conquer? Absolutely. It describes Him in the messages to the seven churches. Did He tell all of them to rise up and be conquerors? Yeah, be overcomers.
Who is the rider on the white horse in Revelation 19:11, and what about the crowns and the bow? (Revelation 19:11-15; 4:10)

Revelation 19:11-15: Now I saw heaven opened, and behold, a white horse. And He who sat on him was called Faithful and True, and in righteousness He judges and makes war. His eyes were like a flame of fire, and on His head were many crowns. He had a name written that no one knew except Himself. He was clothed with a robe dipped in blood, and His name is called The Word of God. And the armies in heaven, clothed in fine linen, white and clean, followed Him on white horses. Now out of His mouth goes a sharp sword, that with it He should strike the nations. And He Himself will rule them with a rod of iron. He Himself treads the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of Almighty God. Revelation 4:10: the twenty-four elders fall down before Him who sits on the throne and worship Him who lives forever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying: Revelation 2:7: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’
What does he say about conquering and overcoming through Christ?

He says “how do we overcome? Through Jesus Christ,” and asks how many “have conquered things in your life through Christ.” He says “that’s the King of kings and the Lord of lords riding on His white horse. He is conquering, He is going to conquer, and He has conquered.” He says “the Bible never says the Antichrist rides a white horse, or the Antichrist has a crown, or the Antichrist has power to conquer people for God and win people to Christ.”
What does he say about conquering and overcoming through Christ?

Hallelujah. And how do we overcome? Through Jesus Christ. Amen. How many of you are conquering? Have conquered things in your life through Christ? How many things are being conquered right now? They’re not quite down, but they’re being conquered, and how many of you go looking tomorrow for some other things to be conquered in your life? Yeah, that’s the King of kings and the Lord of lords riding on His white horse. He is conquering, He is going to conquer, and He has conquered. Amen. That’s as good a theory as them things that the Antichrist, where do you get that from? Because you’re wanting to build a theory you already wanted to reach, and so you’re grabbing for things, and you just say it means that. You cannot just say it means that when the Bible doesn’t say that. And the Bible never says the Antichrist rides a white horse, or the Antichrist has a crown, or the Antichrist has power to conquer people for God and win people to Christ. Are you with me?
What does he say about the red horse and God “smiting” the nations? (Revelation 6:3-4; Acts 2:37)

He asks, “Is God wanting to smite the nations, the people? Isn’t that what He did on the day of Pentecost? Their hearts were smitten.” He describes the second horse as “a red horse with a huge sword” given “power to take peace from the earth so that men slaughter one another,” and says “He isn’t slaughtering anyone, they’re slaughtering what? One another.” The theory people, he says, “call this anarchy, the absence of government.”
What does he say about the red horse and God “smiting” the nations? (Revelation 6:3-4; Acts 2:37)

Now, hallelujah. Is God wanting to smite the nations, the people? Isn’t that what He did on the day of Pentecost? Their hearts were smitten. Amen. How many of you had your heart smitten? Yeah, about Christ. Yeah, a change of heart. Absolutely. That fits way more into this Antichrist thing. Can I hear an amen? Amen. Now, the second horse is a red horse with a huge sword. Empowered, he’s been given power to take peace from the earth so that men slaughter one another. He isn’t slaughtering anyone, they’re slaughtering what? One another. The theory people call this anarchy, the absence of government, the disorder and the lawlessness that’s coming.
What does he say about the red horse and God “smiting” the nations? (Revelation 6:3-4; Acts 2:37)

Revelation 6:3-4: When He opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying, “Come and see.” Another horse, fiery red, went out. And it was granted to the one who sat on it to take peace from the earth, and that people should kill one another; and there was given to him a great sword. Acts 2:37: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, “Men and brethren, what shall we do?”
Does he say wars and earthquakes are signs that the end has come? (Mark 13:7-8)

He says wars and killing have been “going on since the beginning,” and reads Mark 13:7 that such things “must needs be, but the end is not yet.” He says people call wars, earthquakes, volcanoes and hurricanes “the sign of the end,” but “Jesus said just the opposite.” In his words, “that’s no indication of the second coming,” and when people tell us what to believe, “we interpret the Bible to believe what they told us to believe, and yet Jesus Himself said just the opposite.”
Does he say wars and earthquakes are signs that the end has come? (Mark 13:7-8)

But let me submit to you, this has been going on since the beginning. People killing one another, hurting one another, it’s been going on ever since the earth started. In Mark 13:7 it says, “When you hear of wars and rumors of wars, be not troubled. Such things must needs be, but the end is not yet. For a nation will rise against nation, kingdom against kingdom, and there will be earthquakes in different places, and there will be famines and troubles. And these are the beginning of sorrows.” But the what? End is not yet. Did you hear that? And what do they say? “Oh, all these wars and earthquakes and volcanoes exploding and hurricanes, that’s the sign of the end.” Jesus said just the opposite. He said, [unclear], wars and rumors of war were going to happen, but what? The end, the second coming, is not yet. In other words, that’s no indication of the second coming. Are you out there? But see, when they tell us what to believe, and when we read the Bible, we interpret the Bible to believe what they told us to believe, and yet Jesus Himself said just the opposite. Are you there? You see, and so people have been killing people ever since.
Does he say wars and earthquakes are signs that the end has come? (Mark 13:7-8)

Mark 13:7-8: But when you hear of wars and rumors of wars, do not be troubled; for such things must happen, but the end is not yet. For nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be earthquakes in various places, and there will be famines and troubles. These are the beginnings of sorrows.
What does he say people got wrong at Jesus’ first coming?

He says “the Jews had it wrong the first time Jesus came,” looking for “a son of David to restore the kingdom to them from Rome,” and “they did not know the Messiah was God Himself when He came the first time.”
Does he say anyone can know the day or hour of the second coming?
No. He says Jesus and God “said twice, no man knows the day or the hour,” and “it says plainly what? Nobody knows but God Himself.”
What does he say Peter said when Jesus spoke of dying?
He says, “Peter said, ‘Well, you can’t die. We’re not going to let you die.’” He says the disciples “wanted to be number one.”
Does he say Daniel understood what he heard from the angel?
No. He says that in the last chapter Daniel says, “I heard, but I understood not,” and that Daniel “did not understand what the angel was saying.”
What does he expect people to say when Jesus begins acting at the second coming?

He says, “When He starts doing something, we’re going to go, ‘Oh, that’s what that is! Oh, that’s what that is!’” and that “we can identify it as He does it, and we may be totally wrong in saying how He’s going to do it.”
How does he describe this teaching?
He says, “I told you this is a college course. This isn’t for wimps. This is serious teaching,” and that in college “you got to go home and study for hours to get it.”
What does he say the Book of Life and the book of works are?

He says, “The Book of Life, you know, if our name’s in there, we go to heaven, if it’s not, we’re in trouble. The book of our works, in Revelation 20:12, everything we did, everything we say is written there.”
How does he say what God remembers can be erased?
He asks, “You can get it erased by what? Repenting.” He says “a simple humbling yourself and admitting you’re wrong and asking forgiveness and cleansing gets it done.”
Does he say the Bible describes the Antichrist as one person?
No. He says, “It never says that the Antichrist is some one person that’s going to rise up in the earth,” and that John “said there are many antichrists.”
What does he say about honor when we stand before Jesus?
He says, “You think you’re going to get any honor when you stand before Jesus Himself? You’re going to give it back to Him. Why? You wouldn’t have any honor if it wasn’t for Him.”
Does he say wars and earthquakes are the sign of the end?
No. He says people say “that’s the sign of the end,” but “Jesus said just the opposite,” that “the end, the second coming, is not yet.”
What does he say about letting others tell us what to believe from the Bible?
He says, “when they tell us what to believe, and when we read the Bible, we interpret the Bible to believe what they told us to believe, and yet Jesus Himself said just the opposite.”

items.d: In this second message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer works through the third horse, the black horse with scales and the price of wheat and barley, and argues from Mark 6:37 that it does not…
p: In this second message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer works through the third horse, the black horse with scales and the price of wheat and barley, and argues from Mark 6:37 that it does not describe a famine. He then covers the fourth seal and the pale horse named Death, Satan’s limited authority, the fifth seal martyrs and the martyred number, and the sixth seal with its earthquake, darkened sun, blood-red moon and rolled-up sky.
How does he open this message, and how does he introduce the black horse? (Revelation 6:5-6)

He says Chicago and Washington, D.C., “are the murder capitals of the United States of America,” that “it’s not the gun that kills people, it’s the one pulling the trigger,” and “if you change the heart of a person, you have control.” He then moves on: “the third horse is a black horse, and its rider has a pair of scales.”
How does he open this message, and how does he introduce the black horse? (Revelation 6:5-6)

He says Satan is “ready and willing any time God will let him, but he only has power over one-fourth.” He says, “Don’t give him that much credit.”
What does he say about hope despite our flaws?
He says, “Yes, there is hope, because right here we see you have a 75 percent chance of making it in spite of your flaws.”
What does he say a martyr is?
He says, “That martyr means they were killed because they followed Jesus and served Jesus and served His Word. That’s a martyr.”
Why does he say Jesus has not yet returned?

He says, “He has a number, and when that number is reached, guess what? Jesus is coming. That’s one of the reasons why He can’t come today, and He didn’t come yesterday, because the martyrs haven’t reached the number.”
What does he say happens to the sky in the sixth seal?
He says, “there was a great earthquake, the sun was black,” and “the moon like blood,” and that the sky is “rolled up like a scroll.”

p: In this third message on six of the seven seals, Pastor David G. Kincer finishes the sixth seal, connecting it to Joel in Acts 2:16, Matthew 24:29 and Isaiah 34:4. He then previews the seventh seal with the sealing of God’s servants in Revelation 7, teaches that believers are sealed by the Holy Spirit, and gives reasons for a delay in the second coming: the martyr number, the sealing, and the great harvest of the multitude no one could count.
What does he say the sixth seal does to the earth, and why does everyone hide? (Revelation 6:14-17)

He says, “Every mountain and island was dislodged, removed out of its place,” and ties it to the Bible’s promise that “He’s going to renovate the earth.” He says “everybody’s hiding. Why? They see Him.” He then challenges the rapture idea: “These people that say, you know, Jesus comes and raptures the church and people are wondering what happened. Well, good grief, even in your theory the graves were open and they’re wondering what happened.”
What does he say the sixth seal does to the earth, and why does everyone hide? (Revelation 6:14-17)

Every mountain and island was dislodged, removed out of its place. Hawaii is at the Antarctica, Tahiti is in the Arctic, everything’s moved around. Boy, that sure messes up the evolution science theories. Huh? Mount St. Helens is in the ocean now, we don’t know where it is, it’s removed, it’s moved. There’s a drastic change here, isn’t that right? All right, which the Bible talks about, He’s going to renovate the earth. Okay, all hid from Him on the throne and the wrath of the Lamb. Everybody’s hiding. Why? They see Him. These people that say, you know, Jesus comes and raptures the church and people are wondering what happened. Well, good grief, even in your theory the graves were open and they’re wondering what happened.
What does he say the sixth seal does to the earth, and why does everyone hide? (Revelation 6:14-17)

Revelation 6:14-17: Then the sky receded as a scroll when it is rolled up, and every mountain and island was moved out of its place. And the kings of the earth, the great men, the rich men, the commanders, the mighty men, every slave and every free man, hid themselves in the caves and in the rocks of the mountains, and said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb! For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
What does he say popular rapture stories have done to the church’s reputation? (Revelation 6:13; Matthew 24:32)

He says “we just believe these little movie stories and these little books that they give us,” and that “this second coming thing is really given us a black eye in the world. People with any intelligence know something’s wrong here.” He says, “It’s made us look bad, we need to get this thing right.”
What does he say popular rapture stories have done to the church’s reputation? (Revelation 6:13; Matthew 24:32)

Are you there? But see, we just believe these little movie stories and these little books that they give us, you know, there are plane pilots flying and one goes and the other’s left, you know, or somebody’s driving a car down the freeway and he’s gone and his car wrecks. How many of you seen those pictures? Yeah. Oh, that really, you know, this second coming thing is really given us a black eye in the world. People with any intelligence know something’s wrong here. Are you there? Hallelujah. It’s made us look bad, we need to get this thing right. Stars drop like shaking figs, and Jesus said, “Behold the fig tree.” Anyway, just thought I’d pass that out. May not be all hid from Him on the throne and the wrath of the Lamb.
What does he say popular rapture stories have done to the church’s reputation? (Revelation 6:13; Matthew 24:32)

Revelation 6:13: And the stars of heaven fell to the earth, as a fig tree drops its late figs when it is shaken by a mighty wind. Matthew 24:32: “Now learn this parable from the fig tree: When its branch has already become tender and puts forth leaves, you know that summer is near.
Has the great day of His wrath already happened? (Revelation 6:16-17)

He says the people hide “Because they’re seeing Him. They’re afraid, they know they’ve messed up.” He asks about “the great day of His wrath” and who can stand, and says the verse is “talking about a day when it will happen,” so as with the conquering, slaughter, famines and plagues, “this is a promise of something going to happen. It hasn’t happened yet.” He says he will show why next week “when we get to the seven trumpets and the seven bowls.”
Has the great day of His wrath already happened? (Revelation 6:16-17)

Why? Because they’re seeing Him. They’re afraid, they know they’ve messed up. “For the great day of His wrath has” what? The great day of His wrath is what? Come, “and who is able to stand?” Before the day of His wrath, and stand before Jesus Christ. Now, according to this verse, it has what? Happened. But we know these statements were made throughout the Bible, and it hasn’t happened, it’s talking about a day when it will happen. Amen. And I submit to you, just like the conquering and the slaughtering of men and the famines and the plagues and all that are happening, will happen, that this is a promise of something going to happen. It hasn’t happened yet, and I’m going to prove it to you next week why it hasn’t happened when we get to the seven trumpets and the seven bowls.
Has the great day of His wrath already happened? (Revelation 6:16-17)

Revelation 6:16-17: and said to the mountains and rocks, “Fall on us and hide us from the face of Him who sits on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb! For the great day of His wrath has come, and who is able to stand?”
What do Acts 2:16 and Joel say about the last days? (Acts 2:16-21; Joel 2:28-32)

He reads Acts 2:16, “This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel,” and says it was “addressed before” on Pentecost when “they spoke the wonderful works of God.” He reads Joel’s words, including “The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and notable day of the Lord.” He says, “He is saving people to the day He comes. Prophesying and preaching the Word of God is going to happen to the day He comes.”
What do Acts 2:16 and Joel say about the last days? (Acts 2:16-21; Joel 2:28-32)

Fair enough, it’s just simple. Acts 2:16, “This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel.” Are you with me? See, this has been addressed before. On the day of Pentecost the Holy Ghost moved, and they spoke the wonderful works of God, they spoke in languages, and they were filled with power and everything else. And the Bible says this is what the prophet Joel prophesied: “It will come to pass in the last days that I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh. Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, your young men will see visions, and your old men will dream dreams. On My servants and on My handmaidens I’ll pour out My Spirit, and they will prophesy. I will show wonders in the heaven above, signs in the earth beneath, blood, fire, and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness and the moon into blood before the great and notable day of the Lord. And it shall come to pass that whosoever shall call on the Lord shall be” what? Saved. Folks, He is saving people to the day He comes. Prophesying and preaching the Word of God is going to happen to the day He comes. Amen.
What do Acts 2:16 and Joel say about the last days? (Acts 2:16-21; Joel 2:28-32)

Acts 2:16-21: But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel: ‘And it shall come to pass in the last days, says God, That I will pour out of My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your young men shall see visions, Your old men shall dream dreams. And on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days; And they shall prophesy. I will show wonders in heaven above And signs in the earth beneath: Blood and fire and vapor of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved.’ Joel 2:28-32: “And it shall come to pass afterward That I will pour out My Spirit on all flesh; Your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, Your old men shall dream dreams, Your young men shall see visions. And also on My menservants and on My maidservants I will pour out My Spirit in those days. “And I will show wonders in the heavens and in the earth: Blood and fire and pillars of smoke. The sun shall be turned into darkness, And the moon into blood, Before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. And it shall come to pass That whoever calls on the name of the LORD Shall be saved. For in Mount Zion and in Jerusalem there shall be deliverance, As the LORD has said, Among the remnant whom the LORD calls.
What does he say about a seven-year tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

He says good and powerful things go on “till the day He comes. But we turn this into some kind of great seven-year tribulation period, which is ridiculous nonsense.” He says, “Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation, nowhere. They have to manufacture it out of Daniel.” He reads Matthew 24:29 and says, “Immediately after what? The great tribulation, these things are going to happen, along with the prophesying and the preaching.”
What does he say about a seven-year tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

Aren’t you glad good things are going on until the day He comes? Powerful things are going on till the day He comes. But we turn this into some kind of great seven-year tribulation period, which is ridiculous nonsense. Are you with me? Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation, nowhere. They have to manufacture it out of Daniel. Hallelujah. Jesus spoke the same thing in Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days shall the sun be darkened, and the moon shall not give her light, and the stars shall fall from heaven, and the powers of heaven will be” what? Shaken. Immediately after what? The great tribulation, these things are going to happen, along with the prophesying and the preaching and great things happening, God doing great things in the earth.
What does he say about a seven-year tribulation? (Matthew 24:29)

Matthew 24:29: “Immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened, and the moon will not give its light; the stars will fall from heaven, and the powers of the heavens will be shaken.
What does Isaiah 34:4 add, and what does he say about the seals being thousand-year periods? (Isaiah 34:4; 2 Peter 3:10)

He reads Isaiah 34:4 and says, “it was Isaiah spoke it way before John said it,” and “it is something that’s going to happen, it didn’t happen.” He criticizes a timeline that “starts with the first seal”: “The Bible doesn’t say each seal is a thousand-year period. The Bible says this seal is about a book proclaiming the day of wrath, ain’t that right? A one-time period.” He reads 2 Peter 3:10 and says, “It’s not happened yet, but will happen in the future.”
What does Isaiah 34:4 add, and what does he say about the seals being thousand-year periods? (Isaiah 34:4; 2 Peter 3:10)

Isaiah 34:4: “All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll, and all their host shall fall down as the leaf falls from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree.” See, it was Isaiah spoke it way before John said it. Are you with me? It is something that’s going to happen, it didn’t happen. Here is my point, do you get it? Because they got a timeline, and this timeline starts with the first seal, and they got an Antichrist, you know, the [unclear] have the seven seals as seven 1,000-year periods. We get so ridiculous. The Bible doesn’t say each seal is a thousand-year period. The Bible says this seal is about a book proclaiming the day of wrath, ain’t that right? A one-time period. 2 Peter 3:10: “The day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens shall pass away with a great noise, and the elements shall melt with fervent heat, the earth also and the works that are therein shall be” what? Burned up. Just as many other Scriptures talk of something coming to pass ahead of us, so is John. It’s not happened yet, but will happen in the future. Okay, I’m going to save this for next week.
What does Isaiah 34:4 add, and what does he say about the seals being thousand-year periods? (Isaiah 34:4; 2 Peter 3:10)

Isaiah 34:4: All the host of heaven shall be dissolved, And the heavens shall be rolled up like a scroll; All their host shall fall down As the leaf falls from the vine, And as fruit falling from a fig tree. 2 Peter 3:10: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will melt with fervent heat; both the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.
What does he say about a rebuilt temple, and how does he introduce the seventh seal? (Acts 7:48; Revelation 7:3)

He says of a built temple, “the Bible plainly says God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, and yet they got to have a temple built because it’s got to fit into their theory.” He introduces the seventh seal: “This is the last one, and the last one is a long one, as we will see next week.”
What does he say about a rebuilt temple, and how does he introduce the seventh seal? (Acts 7:48; Revelation 7:3)

This is their chart. They got to have a temple built, and the Bible plainly says God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands, and yet they got to have a temple built because it’s got to fit into their theory. All right. Okay. Now we come to the seventh seal. How many seals are there? Seven. This is the last one, and the last one is a long one, as we will see next week. All right, previews of coming attractions. Revelation 7:3, the seventh seal is coming, but before the seventh seal comes, he says,
What does he say about a rebuilt temple, and how does he introduce the seventh seal? (Acts 7:48; Revelation 7:3)

Acts 7:48: “However, the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands, as the prophet says: Revelation 7:3: saying, “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees till we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.”
What does the sealing of God’s servants before any harm mean? (Revelation 7:1-3; Ezekiel 9:4-6)

He reads that no harm is to be done to the earth, the sea or the trees “until we have sealed the bond servants of our God on their forehead,” and says, “you never hear preaching on that. It’s always 666.” He says God says to “delay everything until I’m done sealing My people.” He connects it to Ezekiel 9:4-6: “Put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations.”
What does the sealing of God’s servants before any harm mean? (Revelation 7:1-3; Ezekiel 9:4-6)

“Don’t harm the earth, the sea, nor the trees until we have sealed the bond servants of our God on their forehead.” Don’t do any destruction until the people of God are sealed by God. Now, you never hear preaching on that. It’s always 666, can’t buy and sell, 666, number of men, tick, tick, tick. We think Revelation was a revelation of 666. Well, here God seals His people, and He says delay everything. Say it: delay everything until I’m done sealing My people. Woo, woo. “After this I saw four angels stationed at the four corners of the earth, firmly holding back the four winds of the earth so that no wind could blow on the earth, on the sea, or on any tree. Then I saw a second angel coming up from the east, carrying a seal of the living God, and with a loud voice he cried out to the four angels who had been given authority and power to hurt the earth and the sea.” And he says, “Don’t you hurt anything till we have sealed the bond servants of our God in their foreheads.” Ezekiel 9:4-6, Ezekiel saw it: “Put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations that are done in My temple.” And to the others He said in my hearing, “Go after him through the city and kill, and do not let your eyes spare nor have any pity. Utterly slay all the young men and the maidens and the little children and the women. Do not come near anyone on whom is the mark of God.”
What does the sealing of God’s servants before any harm mean? (Revelation 7:1-3; Ezekiel 9:4-6)

Revelation 7:1-3: After these things I saw four angels standing at the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, that the wind should not blow on the earth, on the sea, or on any tree. Then I saw another angel ascending from the east, having the seal of the living God. And he cried with a loud voice to the four angels to whom it was granted to harm the earth and the sea, saying, “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees till we have sealed the servants of our God on their foreheads.” Ezekiel 9:4-6: and the LORD said to him, “Go through the midst of the city, through the midst of Jerusalem, and put a mark on the foreheads of the men who sigh and cry over all the abominations that are done within it.” To the others He said in my hearing, “Go after him through the city and kill; do not let your eye spare, nor have any pity. Utterly slay old and young men, maidens and little children and women; but do not come near anyone on whom is the mark; and begin at My sanctuary.” So they began with the elders who were before the temple.
What does it mean to be sealed by God, and does he say believers must be raptured out of tribulation? (Ephesians 1:13; 2 Corinthians 1:22)

He says, “if God has given me a seal, I don’t have to be raptured out of the tribulation period. Man, I can handle it. Why? He’s sealed me.” He reads Ephesians 1:13 and 2 Corinthians 1:22, that we are sealed and given the Spirit “as a guarantee,” a guarantee “that He will finish the good work He’s begun in us.” He says, “as long as I serve Him and seek Him, He’s going to get me there, and I don’t have to worry about my flaws now and my weaknesses and my problems now.”
What does it mean to be sealed by God, and does he say believers must be raptured out of tribulation? (Ephesians 1:13; 2 Corinthians 1:22)

Are you there? Now, if God has given me a seal, I don’t have to be raptured out of the tribulation period. Man, I can handle it. Why? He’s sealed me. Amen. Ephesians 1:13 says you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise. 2 Corinthians 1:22: “You also He has sealed and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee,” a guarantee of what? That He will finish the good work He’s begun in us. Jeez, when I heard that, when God opened that to me as a young Christian, I just exploded. You’re looking at me like, so what? He guarantees me He will get me to my destiny. Now, folks, that takes it out of my hands. As long as I serve Him and seek Him, He’s going to get me there, and I don’t have to worry about my flaws now and my weaknesses and my problems now. He will heal those problems, get me out of those problems, and He will get me to the goal, because He guarantees that it’s His seal to me, and it’s that Holy Spirit that witnesses it in me.
What does it mean to be sealed by God, and does he say believers must be raptured out of tribulation? (Ephesians 1:13; 2 Corinthians 1:22)

Ephesians 1:13: In Him you also trusted, after you heard the word of truth, the gospel of your salvation; in whom also, having believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise, 2 Corinthians 1:22: who also has sealed us and given us the Spirit in our hearts as a guarantee. Philippians 1:6: being confident of this very thing, that He who has begun a good work in you will complete it until the day of Jesus Christ;
Why does he say there is a delay in the second coming, and what is “the mark of God”?

He says “there are multitudes in this world that God wants to save and seal,” so there is a delay: “He is out to win people to Himself and seal them.” He says, “The real focus is on the mark of God, not the mark of the beast,” and “with the mark of God, nothing can touch me.”
Why does he say there is a delay in the second coming, and what is “the mark of God”?

Amen. So I can serve my God with all the zeal and the fortitude that I have in me. And just like the martyrs, He hadn’t finished the martyrs yet, and, you know, hasn’t finished sealing God’s people yet. There are multitudes in this world that God wants to save and seal. Could that be an amen? So there’s a delay. There’s the delay of this stuff, the heavens rolled back like a scroll and the moon turned to blood and the sun going down and all that. There’s a delay. Why? He is out to win people to Himself and seal them. Man, that’s good stuff. And so this second coming is a powerful thing, very powerful. The real focus is on the mark of God, not the mark of the beast. Can I hear an amen? With the mark of God, nothing can touch me, and without it, huh, I’m worthless.
What reasons for the delay does he give, and what is the great harvest? (Revelation 7:9)

He says, “First we find the delay because of the martyr quota hasn’t been reached. Second, we find there’s a delay because the saints of God have got to be sealed.” He gives another reason: “Remember I keep telling you that there’s going to be a great harvest in these last days? Right here it is.” He says of the multitude no one could count, “Give me a break,” rejecting the idea that it comes out of a seven-year period.
What reasons for the delay does he give, and what is the great harvest? (Revelation 7:9)

So there’s a delay. First we find the delay because of the martyr quota hasn’t been reached. Second, we find there’s a delay because the saints of God have got to be sealed. Okay. And here is another reason for the delay. Remember I keep telling you that there’s going to be a great harvest in these last days? Right here it is. Right here it is. “After this I saw a multitude no one could count.” Is this big? Yeah. They say, “Well, this is the one that comes out of the great tribulation period.” Give me a break. A multitude that no one could count coming out of seven years, and then you preach that’s going to be hard to get a, accept Christ, and, you know, you tell us it’s hard and the Spirit’s taken from the earth and all this, then you tell me, give me a break. Are you, you understand what I’m saying?
What reasons for the delay does he give, and what is the great harvest? (Revelation 7:9)

Revelation 7:9: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands,
What does he say about predictions that Russia, China or others will attack, in light of Revelation 7:9?

He says, “if He’s bringing people out of every nation, kind, and tribe, and tongue,” then of those who predict a nation will destroy Israel, “they’re picking on a nation that God wants to save.” He says, “He’s out to bring out a people for Himself out of all these nations,” and “He doesn’t dislike Russians because they’re Russians.”
What does he say about predictions that Russia, China or others will attack, in light of Revelation 7:9?

Okay, a multitude no one could number come out of great tribulation, out of every nation, kind, and tribe, tongue, and people, and “there stood before the throne and before the Lamb.” Now listen, if He’s bringing people out of every nation, kind, and tribe, and tongue, these people that said Russia’s going to come down and destroy Israel and blah, blah, blah, they’re picking on a nation that God wants to save. When they say China’s going to do it, and the, you know, the Muslims are going to do it, the Arabs and all that, they’re picking on a nation that God wants to save. He’s out to bring out a people for Himself out of all these nations. Let’s stop picking this, let’s stop bringing this. You know, the symbol of Russia was the bear, and so it says over there in Ezekiel the bear, and so forth, so they connect the symbol with the, God didn’t need a symbol back there to tell us what the bear was. He didn’t need a symbol today that Russia has to tell us who the bear is. And He doesn’t dislike Russians because they’re Russians. You cannot judge of people to die and persecute the Jews because they’re born Russian. What if you were born in Russia? Would that be good news to you? You’re doomed to come down and be destroyed. Amen.
What does he say about predictions that Russia, China or others will attack, in light of Revelation 7:9?

Revelation 7:9-10: After these things I looked, and behold, a great multitude which no one could number, of all nations, tribes, peoples, and tongues, standing before the throne and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, with palm branches in their hands, and crying out with a loud voice, saying, “Salvation belongs to our God who sits on the throne, and to the Lamb!”
Who does he say the people in white robes are? (Revelation 7:11-14; John 16:33)

He reads Revelation 7:13-14 about those “clothed in long white robes” who “have washed their robes and made them white in the” blood of the Lamb. He says, “these people came from earth, and they were made white by what? The blood of the Lamb, not the persecution, not the tribulation.” He says, “we don’t have to be raptured out, we can handle this thing,” and quotes Jesus, “In this world you will have” tribulation.
Who does he say the people in white robes are? (Revelation 7:11-14; John 16:33)

Now these cried, saying, “Salvation to our God who is seated on the throne and to the Lamb.” Here they are worshiping again, and all the angels were standing around the throne and around the elders and the four living creatures, and they all fell prostrate before the throne and worship God. Here’s a lot of worship going on in Revelation, and they cried, “Blessing and glory and majesty and splendor and wisdom and thanksgiving and honor and power and might to our God forever and ever.” All right. Now, those people in white robes, this innumerable number of people that came out of the great tribulation. Verse 13 says one of the elders said to me, “Who are these clothed in long white robes, and from where have they come?” And I replied, “Sir, you know.” And he said to me, “These are they which have come out of the great tribulation, the great persecution, and have washed their robes and made them white in the” what? Blood of the Lamb. Jesus said, “In this world you will have” what? Tribulation. How many found that out? You know, if you’re twenty years old, you find you’re in a world that’s got a lot of conflict and trouble in it, and you are one of your biggest sources of trouble, aren’t you? Yeah, the guy you look at in the mirror. So these people came from earth, and they were made white by what? The blood of the Lamb, not the persecution, not the tribulation. You see, we don’t have to be raptured out, we can handle this thing. Are you with me? Are you with me? And it says “a number of,” so the blood of the Lamb is going to bring a powerful lot of people into the kingdom of God. Hallelujah, and you’re one of them.
Who does he say the people in white robes are? (Revelation 7:11-14; John 16:33)

Revelation 7:11-12: All the angels stood around the throne and the elders and the four living creatures, and fell on their faces before the throne and worshiped God, saying: “Amen! Blessing and glory and wisdom, Thanksgiving and honor and power and might, Be to our God forever and ever. Amen.” Revelation 7:13-14: Then one of the elders answered, saying to me, “Who are these arrayed in white robes, and where did they come from?” And I said to him, “Sir, you know.” So he said to me, “These are the ones who come out of the great tribulation, and washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. John 16:33: These things I have spoken to you, that in Me you may have peace. In the world you will have tribulation; but be of good cheer, I have overcome the world.”
What does he say about the 144,000 and the twelve tribes? (Revelation 7:4-8)

He says, “He lists twelve tribes and 12,000 out of each one,” but “Joseph is listed as one of the twelve tribes,” Ephraim “is not even mentioned,” and “Dan, who was one of the original twelve tribes, is not mentioned.” He says, “it has nothing to do with anything,” and “there ain’t just 144,000 going to heaven like the Jehovah’s Witnesses said.” He says “there’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven” and the twelve tribes “illustrate the sealing of God’s people.”
What does he say about the 144,000 and the twelve tribes? (Revelation 7:4-8)

Now, going back to the sealed people. Say, well, you know, there’s 144,000 people sealed. Well, give me a break. He lists twelve tribes and 12,000 out of each one. The problem here is Joseph is listed as one of the twelve tribes, but if you know your Bible, there’s really thirteen tribes now, because Ephraim was picked to be one of Jacob’s children and be one of the tribes, and so Ephraim got the birthright and everything, and Ephraim is not even mentioned in these twelve tribes. Dan, who was one of the original twelve tribes, is not mentioned. Hello? Now, God is so confused He don’t even know the names of His tribes. No, because it has nothing to do with anything. There ain’t just 144,000 going to heaven like the Jehovah’s Witnesses said, they’re a bunch of baloney. There’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven. Amen. And He’s just using these twelve tribes to illustrate the sealing of God’s people. Hallelujah. So is there a delay? Why? The martyr quota hasn’t been reached.
What does he say about the 144,000 and the twelve tribes? (Revelation 7:4-8)

Revelation 7:4-8: And I heard the number of those who were sealed. One hundred and forty-four thousand of all the tribes of the children of Israel were sealed: of the tribe of Judah twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Reuben twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Gad twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Asher twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Naphtali twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Manasseh twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Simeon twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Levi twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Issachar twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Zebulun twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Joseph twelve thousand were sealed; of the tribe of Benjamin twelve thousand were sealed.
Why does he say we should want the harvest to come in before the Lord returns?

He says, “if you’re one of these that’s praying, ‘Oh, come, Lord Jesus, get me out of this mess,’ you don’t see the harvest,” and urges, “Stop being selfish and let’s get the vision of the harvest.” He asks whether Jesus’ blood is “big enough to save billions of people,” and says “what God wants to do is way beyond our capabilities.” He concludes, “it’s not about the beast and the troubles and the seven years of tribulation. It’s about the conquering Jesus and the harvest that His blood has power to bring in.”
Why does he say we should want the harvest to come in before the Lord returns?

God isn’t finished saving souls and sealing them, and the harvest hasn’t been brought in yet. Now, if you’re one of these that’s praying, “Oh, come, Lord Jesus, get me out of this mess,” you don’t see the harvest. If you put yourself in the shoes of someone in China that they won’t even allow him to hear the gospel, and it’s very hard to hear it, you wouldn’t want Him coming now. You would want to hear the gospel first, isn’t that right? Stop being selfish and let’s get the vision of the harvest. Hallelujah. Is the blood of Jesus, the sacrifice of Jesus, big enough to save billions of people in this last day? We got almost 7 billion people in this world. You talk about a harvest, we have a potential harvest, and that’s why we need to fast and pray and seek God, because what God wants to do is way beyond our capabilities. We need Him to arise in us, we need Him to arise in the world and accomplish what He promised to accomplish. Amen. And the second coming is about the power of Jesus Christ, the revelation of Jesus Christ, and what He can do in the earth. It’s not about the beast and the troubles and the seven years of tribulation. It’s about the conquering Jesus and the harvest that His blood has power to bring in. Now, I don’t know about you, but that’s good news.
What does he say happens to mountains and islands in the sixth seal?
He says, “Every mountain and island was dislodged, removed out of its place,” and “There’s a drastic change here, isn’t that right?”
What does he say about popular second-coming stories and books?
He says, “this second coming thing is really given us a black eye in the world,” and “It’s made us look bad, we need to get this thing right.”
Which prophet does he say Acts 2:16 points to?
He reads Acts 2:16, “This is that which was spoken by the prophet Joel,” and says it is what happened on the day of Pentecost.
Does he say the Bible mentions a seven-year tribulation?
No. He says, “Nowhere in the Bible does it say there’s seven years of tribulation, nowhere. They have to manufacture it out of Daniel.”
Does he say each seal is a thousand-year period?
No. He says, “The Bible doesn’t say each seal is a thousand-year period.”
What does he say about God dwelling in temples?
He says, “the Bible plainly says God doesn’t dwell in temples made with hands.”
What does he say is delayed until God’s servants are sealed?
He says, “Don’t do any destruction until the people of God are sealed by God,” and that God says, “delay everything until I’m done sealing My people.”
What does he say a seal from God guarantees?
He says it is “a guarantee of what? That He will finish the good work He’s begun in us,” and “He guarantees me He will get me to my destiny.”
What two reasons does he first give for the delay?
He says, “First we find the delay because of the martyr quota hasn’t been reached. Second, we find there’s a delay because the saints of God have got to be sealed.”
What does he say made the robes white?
He says, “they were made white by what? The blood of the Lamb, not the persecution, not the tribulation.”
Does he say only 144,000 people go to heaven?
No. He says, “there ain’t just 144,000 going to heaven,” and “there’s an innumerable group of people up there in heaven.”
What does he say about praying for Jesus to come and get us out of this mess?
He says, “if you’re one of these that’s praying, ‘Oh, come, Lord Jesus, get me out of this mess,’ you don’t see the harvest,” and “Stop being selfish and let’s get the vision of the harvest.”

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Jeremiah 3 that in the midst of God’s judgments there are promises for those who repent: God is married to His people, gives shepherds who feed with…
p: In this message Pastor David G.
