He says God had one plan, implemented at the beginning through Jesus Christ, and the Bible says His blood was shed “before the beginning of the world.” Then when He became flesh and dwelt among us, that “came to pass.”
How does he explain one God and the plural “us”?

He says there is one God, but when God says “let us make man in our image,” the word “us” is plural. He says Jesus, part of God who is still one God, was the first thing of God’s creation and then became flesh and dwelt among us.
What does he say separates Christianity from the rest of the religions?
He says, “this is what separates Christianity from the rest of the religions. Jesus Christ is God.” He says Jesus was God manifest in the flesh who died on the cross for the sins of the world.
Who does he say Christians are really fighting?

He says the Bible says we wrestle not against flesh and blood, and that Christians forget “we’re not really fighting our relatives that don’t want God.” We’re fighting the source of that mentality, the source of that teaching which comes from the heavenly places.
Should we run to a “mighty man of God” for a magical prayer?
He says people want to run to a mighty man of God “and some kind of magical prayer,” but “we are supposed to come before God. We are supposed to go directly to his throne of grace.”
What does he say about the idea that Russia will surround Jerusalem?
He says people have been led to think that Russia is going to surround Jerusalem, when instead “there is a warfare going on in the heavenlies that brings results to the earth.”
Who does Jesus say He will fight with the sword of His mouth in Revelation 2:16?

He says Revelation 2:16, “repent or I will come to you quickly and fight against them,” is about people in the church committing idolatry and sexual immorality who believed but lived in sin. Jesus will fight them with the “sword of my mouth.”
Why does he say Jesus could not have had a tattoo?

He says “Jesus cannot violate scripture,” and in Old Testament laws you could not have tattoos. He says Jesus “had to be a lamb without blemish,” just as He could not have been intoxicated and still die for the sins of the world.

items.ser: The War of The Word · Part 2
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer finishes Revelation 19, arguing that the supper of the great God, the horses and the sword from His mouth show a spiritual war of the word rather than a natural war. He gives Bible examples of the war of the word, from the flood, Sodom, Egypt, Babylon and the ark, to angels fighting for believers, and then turns to present-day suffering, morality and the question of which side of the word you are on.
What is the “supper of the great God” in Revelation 19, and why do the birds gather?

He reads Revelation 19:17, the angel “standing in the sun” crying to the birds to gather “into the supper of the great God.” He says Jesus used eagles and vultures as an illustration of the coming at the end of the world, citing “wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together.”
What is the “supper of the great God” in Revelation 19, and why do the birds gather?

And angels, verse 17, standing in the sun. Now you try standing in the sun, see how long you last. “Cried to all the birds, the fowls of heaven, gather yourselves together into the supper of the great God.” Now, we know that in the book of Daniel and in other books in the Bible, when there were national wars, physical people were killed, and the vultures actually would come and gather together and eat the dead flesh. Right? All right. We also know that angels— I mean, I’m sorry, we also know that eagles were used by Jesus to describe the second coming in Matthew 14 and in Luke and in John and Mark. Where one would be taken and the other left, and they said, “Where, Lord? Where are these people going to be taken?” And He says, “Wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together.” So we know that Jesus used these fowl, these vultures, as an illustration of the coming at the end of the world. Are you there? Hallelujah. In Luke 17:36 it said, “Two men will be in the field; one shall be taken, the other left.” And they answered, “Where, Lord?” “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together.” See, where the dead carcass is, the eagles, the vultures— the eagle is a vulture, he feeds on dead bodies and lights on [them].
What is the “supper of the great God” in Revelation 19, and why do the birds gather?

Revelation 19:17-18: Then I saw an angel standing in the sun; and he cried with a loud voice, saying to all the birds that fly in the midst of heaven, “Come and gather together for the supper of the great God, that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, both small and great.” Matthew 24:28: For wherever the carcass is, there the eagles will be gathered together. Luke 17:34-37: I tell you, in that night there will be two men in one bed: the one will be taken and the other will be left. Two women will be grinding together: the one will be taken and the other left. Two men will be in the field: the one will be taken and the other left.” And they answered and said to Him, “Where, Lord?” So He said to them, “Wherever the body is, there the eagles will be gathered together.”
Why does he say the horses in Revelation 19 show this is a spiritual war and not a natural one?

He says the birds eat the flesh of kings, captains, mighty men, horses and riders, “both free and bond, both small and great.” He says if this took place in our day, “we don’t use horses for war,” so “this is not a natural war. This is a spiritual war.”
Why does he say the horses in Revelation 19 show this is a spiritual war and not a natural one?

And so we know that this is illustrated as part of the second coming. Okay, and it’s the supper of the great God, and the birds were to eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and the people that sat on the horses, and the flesh of all men, both free and bond, both small and great. So these fowls are going to what? Eat the dead carcasses of everybody, including the horses. Now, the horses here tell you something. That’s why it’s in red. If this takes place in our day, as these prophets claim is going to be, we don’t use horses for war. You don’t win wars with horses anymore. You got to have tanks, you got to have airplanes, you got to have, uh, uh, aircraft carriers, I mean. So that tells us what? This is not a natural war. This is a spiritual war.
Why does he say the horses in Revelation 19 show this is a spiritual war and not a natural one?

Revelation 19:18: that you may eat the flesh of kings, the flesh of captains, the flesh of mighty men, the flesh of horses and of those who sit on them, and the flesh of all people, free and slave, both small and great.”
Will armies of the earth really fight Jesus when He returns?

He says God’s war of the word is “with everyone on earth,” small and great, bond and free. Of Revelation 19:19 he says people on earth will hide in the rocks and caves from a spirit coming out of heaven with angels, and “you’re going to run” rather than fight them with atomic bombs and missiles.
Will armies of the earth really fight Jesus when He returns?

Amen. And the fact that it says small and great, both free and bond, he’s talking about all people. People not even in the war. And is God’s war dealing with all nations? His war of the word, is He dealing with the small and the great? The Bible tells us that, doesn’t it? See, the bond and the free, He’s dealing with everyone. God’s spiritual war is with everyone on earth. Verse 19: “The beast, the kings of the earth, and their armies gathered together to war against Him that sat on the horse and against His army.” And this, again, is just ridiculous. Jesus comes riding out of heaven on a white horse with angels behind Him. They, people on earth, are going to do exactly what it said before this: they’re going to hide in the rocks and the caves and the— from the one who’s what? Coming. You see a spirit coming out of heaven, and angels, spirits, coming out of heaven, and you’re going to get your atomic bombs and your missiles and try to fight them? Uh-huh, honey, you’re going to run, just like He told, said, they’re going to run. They’re going to want to hide from this one who’s coming out of the heavens. Are you there? So this is obviously what? A spiritual war. Amen. But they got us thinking Russia’s coming and China’s coming and all this natural stuff, and, you know, and we don’t read the Bible enough to even know if they’re telling us the truth or not.
Will armies of the earth really fight Jesus when He returns?

Revelation 19:19: And I saw the beast, the kings of the earth, and their armies, gathered together to make war against Him who sat on the horse and against His army. He says “they got us thinking Russia’s coming and China’s coming and all this natural stuff,” and that “we don’t read the Bible enough to even know if they’re telling us the truth or not.”
Who is taken captive in the battle of Revelation 19?
He says the beast and the false prophet are taken captive, and “it’s a spiritual war in the spiritual realm.” They are cast alive into the lake of fire burning with brimstone.
What happens when the word of God comes to us?
He says “we can accept it or we can reject it.” If we accept it we live forever and are given eternal life; if we reject it we are called dead in trespasses and sins, even though we are alive.
Does God always give people a way out?
He says yes: “He’s God, He gives you a way out.” He says God sent Noah to preach, and the rest of the world rejected it and died in the judgment.
What could Egypt’s sorcerers do compared to Moses?

He says Egypt had sorcerers and people into witchcraft who also turned sticks into snakes, water into blood and brought out frogs. He says they could only do what God allowed them to do, so spiritual power in the world is “very limited.”
Do Christians have to be raptured to be safe?
He says God’s people were separated in Egypt and were safe, and “they didn’t have to be raptured to be safe.” He says “God can keep us right here.”
What did Israel do after leaving Egypt, and how did God respond?

He says Israel came out of Egypt serving idols and committing sexual immorality, and God said, “I’ll come and I’ll punish you for these things.” He says God brought famine and armies against them to correct them because they were breaking His word, until they went into captivity in Babylon.
What did Gideon’s father say when people wanted to kill Gideon for tearing down the idol?

He says Gideon’s father told the people of the city, “if your idol is really a God, let him defend himself.” He asks if Jesus is big enough to defend Himself and answers, “Yes, He’s the all-powerful One.”
What happened to the people who kept the ark of the covenant?
He says God sent a plague and “they started dying like flies,” with boils coming out on them. They said they had to get rid of the ark, sent it back, and God stopped the plague.
What does he say the lake of fire was created for?

He says it was created to handle Satan and his angels, “the wicked powers of the spiritual world,” in that great clash at the last day. He says Jesus said those who did not follow Him and live right would be cast into it.
What does he say God is aiming for in the final days?

He says a demonstration of the word will bring a tremendous harvest, “just like Egypt” with its mixed multitude, and that God is “moving to win as many as He can to Himself.” He says God is not out to kill them but to put them to death to sin and alive to righteousness.
Did Jesus use a sword or his fists when He preached?

He says Jesus used the word for three and a half years and did not take up a sword or hit anyone, and that “the word made people glad.” He says it is the war of the word, “destroying the principalities and powers in heavenly places.”

p: In “Three Revelations Part 1,” Pastor David G. Kincer introduces the book of Revelation through its opening verse, saying it gives three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and the revelation of the church. He teaches that Revelation is written to all of God’s servants, uses Romans 2 and Revelation 20 to show judgment by works and the Book of Life, and begins the revelation of the church as the body of Christ from Romans 16 and Ephesians 3 and 5.
Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?

He says John was banished to the isle of Patmos after being tarred and feathered for preaching the gospel, and that on the island, in that affliction, he received the book of Revelation. He says that when somebody pays a price like that, “we need to listen to them.”
Why does he say we should listen to John, who wrote Revelation on Patmos?

This John got this on the isle of Patmos. He was banished by the local authorities to the isle of Patmos after he had been tarred and feathered and somehow survived for preaching the gospel. I mean, if you really want to go out and preach the gospel, people aren’t going to like you. It is not like the church in America today where we flatter people. And this is what you’re going to find in the book of Revelations, these guys that really went out and preached the gospel, they were [unclear], they were in prison, they were beaten, I mean they were subject to abuse all the time. Today, not so, because we’re really not preaching the gospel. We’re preaching a very flattering message that doesn’t challenge anyone, doesn’t shake up anyone. Most, now not all the church, but the majority of the church, and the majority of the church is on TV and radio, because you want numbers and you want money, you have to water down the message. You don’t want to hurt anybody’s feelings. But John wasn’t like that. He preached the gospel, he was tarred and feathered, and they banished him, and on that island, in that kind of affliction, he got this book of Revelation. And so when somebody pays a price like that, we need to listen to them. Could that be an
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?

He says the book is the revelation of Jesus Christ, not of the beast or Satan, and that there are three revelations: of Jesus Christ, of the eternal judgment, and of the church. He says that if you read the Bible without looking for Jesus, “you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible.”
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?

amen? Revelations 1:1, it starts out by saying “the revelation of Jesus Christ.” Not the beast, not the revelation of Satan, not the revelation of the [unclear] sitting on the seven mountains. Are you hearing me? It’s the revelation of who? Jesus Christ. This book is going to tell us about Jesus Christ. Revelation means to disclose, to reveal things, even things that have not been seen before. Okay, and so we’re going to have the revelation, the revealing, the disclosure of Jesus Christ. And we find that there’s three revelations in the New Testament. That’s the revelation of Jesus, the Lion, the Lamb, the Captain of the host, the Head of the church. I mean, He’s the big guy, He’s the chief honcho in the Bible, and when you read the Bible, if you’re not looking for Jesus, you’re going to miss the whole point of the Bible. Secondly, it’s the revelation of the judgment. The Bible tells us there’s a revelation of the eternal judgment, and you don’t hear this message much anymore, that you’re going to be held accountable for what you say and do, and God is going to sentence you by what you say and do. You don’t hear this much anymore. When I was a kid you heard it all the time. They scared the hell out of you. I mean, man, you wanted Jesus and you wanted to get to heaven. But then we got into the love thing, everybody’s okay. And then the revelation of the church. I meet very few American Christians that even understand the basic revelation of the church. They think it’s a building with people in it. And I’d submit to you today, you don’t know it.
What are the three revelations in the book of Revelation?
Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,
Is the church just a building with people in it?

He says no: the Bible calls the church the body of Christ, each member with a particular function, and that it is also a flock, an army, and a house, a temple of God. He says that seeing what the church really is “should revolutionize” how you use your time and approach God.
Is the church just a building with people in it?

Because if you did, it would change your life. It would change the way you do things. When we get through with the book of Revelation and you see what the church really is, it should revolutionize the way you schedule your time and you approach your God. It will make all the difference in the world, because the church isn’t some building with people in it. The Bible refers to it as the body of Christ. You see all those heads? See, we are the body of Christ and each one a member in particular, with a particular function. We have a function. Your little finger has a function. The smallest in God’s church has a function, a purpose and an objective. We are a flock, we follow the Shepherd, we need His protection, but we’re also an army, and we’re also a house, a temple of God. But we will get into that later, and this is what the Bible speaks of, these three revelations.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

He says Revelation 1:1 gives the revelation of Jesus Christ from God, things shown to “his servants,” which is all believers and not only the seven churches in Asia, and things that must shortly come to pass. He says we must pray for understanding of the scriptures because the Spirit is the only one who can open them to us.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

Now Revelations 1:1 has three points in it. Number one, the revelation of Jesus Christ, as we talked about, which God gave to Him. Who gave this to Him? God. All right. It’s not like Muhammad, it’s not like Joseph Smith. Those are imitators, as we’ll show you a little later. And you got to be [unclear]. You got to know truth if you want to be free and you want others to be free. It’s the truth that sets you free. Free from what? Your traditions, your unbelief, your [unclear] doctrines, your doctrines of men. It sets you free from these things. Amen. And sin. Now number two, “to show unto His servants things.” Okay, He’s going to show us things, and it’s not just to the seven churches in Asia. To show unto His servants, all of us who accepted Christ. Christ is the King and we are His servants, and so He wants to show everybody, not just the seven churches of Asia. This is directed to everyone, isn’t that true? And He’s going to show us things. How many want your eyes open to the things He wants to show? Yeah. You got to pray. One of your main prayers is not only wisdom, but you need to pray that God gives you understanding of the scriptures, because the Spirit is the only one that can open the scriptures up to you. That’s what the Bible says, they are spiritually discerned. The Spirit has to do it. See, we can use our human intellect, but it is the Spirit that really bursts the truth in us.
What are the three points in Revelation 1:1, and how do we get understanding?

Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John, John 8:32: And you shall know the truth, and the truth shall make you free.” 1 Corinthians 2:14: But the natural man does not receive the things of the Spirit of God, for they are foolishness to him; nor can he know them, because they are spiritually discerned.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?

He says no, because it says it was written to God’s servants, all of us. He says we do need preachers and teachers, but “they’re not the ones to follow,” and our faith should be in Jesus Christ and His truth, not in any man or man’s teaching.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?

Amen. And number three, read this last one with me: “which must shortly come to pass.” Read it again: “which must shortly come to pass.” Now I submit to you, it’s 2,000 years. Shortly? It doesn’t sound very shortly, does it? Hallelujah. These words, Revelations 22, now we’re at the last chapter of the book, all right: “These words are faithful.” You can count on them. The words of Revelation, they are truth. They’re just like all the other books in the Bible. “The Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants.” There we are again, to show who? His servants, all of us. Do we need some special prophet opening the book of Revelation to us? No. Why? Because He wrote it for all of us. You see, only in America do we have this mentality, we need the gurus, we need Osteen, we need Joyce Meyer, we need somebody. Why? ’Cause that’s what they tell us, they preach we need them. But here it says this is to who? All of us. Is God partial? We just taught on it. Do you have every right to every inheritance just like anybody else? Absolutely. Do we need preachers and teachers? Yes, we do, but they’re not the ones to follow, and they’re not the ones to worship. They should be leading us to the One, and our faith should not be in any man or any man’s teaching. Our faith should be in the Jesus Christ and His truth.
Do we need a special prophet or teacher to explain Revelation to us?
Revelation 22:6: Then he said to me, “These words are faithful and true.” And the Lord God of the holy prophets sent His angel to show His servants the things which must shortly take place.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?

He says the book plainly says these things must shortly come to pass, and that end-time prophets twist and stretch scriptures to make it fit our last days. He warns that what you believe determines your behavior, and says there are people making up their own doctrine today.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?

Amen. The things which must what? Shortly come to pass. He emphasizes it again. And what do all these end-time prophets do with Revelation? They twist and stretch all kinds of scriptures to get it to fit into our last days. Am I right? I am right. And it says plainly, these things must what? Shortly come to pass. Wow, you youngins got that? He says you need to take heed. Jesus told him, take heed, beware of the doctrine of the scribes and the Pharisees. Why? What you believe is what will determine your behavior. And the Pharisees had made up their own doctrine, and the Sadducees had made up their own doctrine, and have, you know, there’s people today making up their own doctrine, and people will try to please a church group in their doctrines of faith rather than please Christ and His book of faith. Could that be true? Now you young people understand this now. This is good stuff. This is deep stuff. This is not for the weak-hearted.
What does he say about “shortly come to pass” and end-time prophecy teachers?
Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John,
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?

He uses an illustration of being shipwrecked on an island with only the book of Revelation, and says to use other true scriptures to confirm it. He compares it to a book about aerodynamics that mentions turbulence: the book is about how airplanes fly, and Revelation is about the revelation of Jesus Christ, not the other things it mentions.
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?

This stuff is meat. It will get into your innards and work powerful in your life. So these three things: revelation of Jesus, He’s going to show His servants things, and it’s going to be brought about what? Shortly. Shortly. Okay, let’s look at the revelation of the righteous judgment of God in Romans chapter 2. Now we’re going to use the book of Revelations as the book. We’re going to pretend that we’re on an island, we got shipwrecked, and we’re on an island, and we were just a dumb sinner before that, and then this book comes floating in on shore, somehow it got in the ocean and it washed up on shore, and we got one book and it’s the book of Revelation. We’re only going to use other true scriptures to confirm the book of Revelation. Is that fair enough? Are you with me? How many of you know, a book of aerodynamics, it states in the introduction and all the rest, this is a book on aerodynamics, how airplanes may fly. Okay, so what’s the book going to be about? How airplanes fly. Now in the book they talk about electric storms in the heavens, and they talk about, uh, what they call that when it plain shakes? Turbulence. Now is the book about storms and turbulence, or is it still about aerodynamics? Aerodynamics. Okay, this book is about the revelation of Jesus Christ, and if He talks about other things, the book isn’t about those other things. It’s about what? The revelation of Jesus
How does he say we should study the book of Revelation?
Romans 2:5: But in accordance with your hardness and your impenitent heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
What is the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and how will we be judged?

He says the New Testament gives three revelations, and the second is the judgment to come, “a day of wrath and the unveiling of the righteous judgment of God.” He says God renders to each one according to his deeds, not according to his faith, his grace, or the church he attends.
What is the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and how will we be judged?

Christ. And so the New Testament gives us three revelations: the revelation of Jesus Christ, the revelation of the judgment to come. See, the book isn’t complicated, it’s not 20 revelations, it’s how many? Three. “With your hardness and unrepentant heart you’re treasuring up wrath in the day of wrath.” Is there a day of wrath? Yes. “And the revelation of the righteous judgment of God.” So the two are synonymous, the two are happening at the same time. There’s a day of wrath and the unveiling of the righteous judgment of God. Now isn’t that easy to see? See, it’s not complicated. You don’t need the Hebrew and Greek, and you don’t need somebody on TV telling you what it says. It says what it says. Amen. “Who renders to each one according to his”, faith? Is that what it says? No. According to his grace? No. According to the church he goes to? No. According to your deeds, your work, your lifestyle, how you speak and how you act. You young people got that? That’s why the Bible says in Ecclesiastes, remember the Lord thy God in the days of thy youth before the evil day comes. Obey God, live right in your youth, because there’s a penalty coming. Eternal life. Then He tells us what’s going to happen by our
What is the revelation of the righteous judgment of God, and how will we be judged?

Romans 2:5-6: But in accordance with your hardness and your impenitent heart you are treasuring up for yourself wrath in the day of wrath and revelation of the righteous judgment of God, who “will render to each one according to his deeds”: Ecclesiastes 12:1: Remember now your Creator in the days of your youth, Before the difficult days come, And the years draw near when you say, “I have no pleasure in them”:
Did Judas believe in Jesus, and what does he say about believing and living right?

He says Judas believed, preached, healed and cast out demons, yet was a thief and, in his words, did not go to heaven or find repentance. He says the gospel works no matter who preaches it, and that you get eternal life by believing, but if you believe on Jesus and live like Judas did, “you’re going to hell.”
Did Judas believe in Jesus, and what does he say about believing and living right?

deeds. You say, did Judas believe in Jesus? You’re looking at me like you’re afraid to answer. Absolutely, he did. Did Judas preach the gospel? Yes. Did Judas heal the sick? Yes. Did Judas cast out demons? Yes. Was Judas a thief the whole time? Yes. Jesus said, “I’ve chose you 12 and one of you is a thief.” Jesus knew who Judas was when He picked him, and He picked him because He knew his heart, and he would fulfill what the scriptures had designated to be fulfilled, and there was a lot of Judases that day, He just picked this one. Are you out there, church? So because someone’s preaching the gospel and the gospel works, does that mean they’re great? No. It means the gospel’s great. Do you young ones get that? See, the gospel works no matter who’s preaching it. Because the gospel just works. Hallelujah. So He’s going to tell us what’s going to happen because of our works and our deeds. When our works are right, we get eternal life: “to those who by patience and continuing in doing good.” They patiently serve God whether things are good, whether things are bad, whether people serve God or whether the people don’t, they just stay faithful, they patiently serve God doing good things. Amen. And they get what? Eternal life. But I’m going to get eternal life because I believe on Jesus. That’s the step. But you believe on Jesus and you live like Judas did, you’re going to hell. Did Judas go to heaven? No. Did Judas find repentance, by the way? No. Are you there? See, it’s best to just serve God all the days of your life. And then there’s wrath to those who are self-seeking, who do what they want to do. They just do what they want to do. Their life’s about them. Everything they do is something to their advantage. What do I get out of it? Most of the church world in America have no compassion for the lost. They don’t weep in their prayers for the lost. You know, we got a lot of teenagers coming in here on Friday night who need our weapons of warfare exercised so that the kingdom of darkness’ hold on them is broken, but people don’t care. The kids are coming in, let them have fun, let them play games, you know, “I’ll just stay away.” Uh, you know, no. See, we don’t understand the

Romans 2:7-8: eternal life to those who by patient continuance in doing good seek for glory, honor, and immortality; but to those who are self-seeking and do not obey the truth, but obey unrighteousness—indignation and wrath,
What does he say the church is for when it comes to young people and spiritual warfare?

He says getting people to church is not the goal; the goal is getting the darkness broken off them, getting Jesus into them, and seeing them transformed. He says we are in a spiritual warfare and must exercise weapons of warfare that are not fleshly to tear down strongholds, and that coming to church alone doesn’t do it.
What does he say the church is for when it comes to young people and spiritual warfare?

church. Just getting them here isn’t it. It’s getting the darkness broken off of their light. It’s getting the Jesus into them. It’s getting them transformed into another kind of person that lives right, their mind changed, thinking right. And parents don’t care, they just drop them off. The church members don’t care, they just stay home and watch TV. Why? Because we don’t understand these things. We don’t understand that we’re in a spiritual warfare, and this is a serious thing. And my prayers and my compassion for those kids, and my touch and not loving them and putting my arm around them and listening to them, is important for them to make it in. We have weapons of warfare that aren’t fleshly, and we have to exercise them to tear down the strongholds of the enemy. Just coming to church doesn’t do
What does he say about the way Revelation is taught on TV and radio?

He says you never hear this kind of message from them because “they’re in it for money and sensationalism sells,” and he says some of these teachers make a fortune. These are his own opinions about other teachers, whom he does not name here.
What does he say about the way Revelation is taught on TV and radio?

it. Amen. Now is this good? Now you never hear this out of the book of Revelations when they teach it on the TV and the radio and all that and the little books that come out. Why? ’Cause they’re in it for money and sensationalism sells, and darkness sells. You know, the tribulation sells. You tell people there’s a glorious church, they’re not interested. You tell them there’s seven years of tribulation, “What? 666, it’s going to be tattooed on your forehead? Oh yeah, you got my attention.” And these guys make a fortune. They live in million, multi-million dollar homes, they have two or three of them, they drive the best cars, and have their own
What good is believing the gospel if you don’t apply it?

He says we have just as much right to go to the book and to Christ as anyone, and that we need to understand John’s revelation by opening the book and reading it. He says believing truth without obeying it does no good, just as believing medicine can cure you does no good if you do not take it.
What good is believing the gospel if you don’t apply it?

airplanes. And we have just as much right to go to the book and go to Christ as anybody does, and we’ve let them trick us and seduce us into thinking they have some great revelation. John’s got the revelation. I don’t need the revelation, I need to understand John’s revelation. Could that be an amen? Could that be an amen? I just need to get off my lazy butt, open the book and start reading it and learning it. Could that be an amen? Wrath to the self-seeking, those that disobey truth. See, you can believe in truth, but if you don’t obey it, what good does it do? Am I right? That you can believe in working to supply your own needs, but if you don’t go to work and just still live off welfare, what good does it do? You can believe that medicine can cure you, but if you don’t go to the doctor and take it, what good does it do? And it’s the same way with the gospel. You may believe in this gospel, in this book, but if you don’t apply it, it doesn’t work for
Will everyone stand before God and be judged?

He says yes, small and great, and it doesn’t matter how great or how small you think you are. He reads that the books were opened and the dead were judged by their works, and says the other books record everything we say and do.
Will everyone stand before God and be judged?

you. Amen. So there’s wrath to those who hear it and don’t do it and obey unrighteousness. People just want to sin. Some people just want to sin. That’s a bottom line. Now Revelations 20:12. See, John backs it up. We got to make sure everything John tells us is backed up by the rest of the scriptures. That’s how we know that it’s real truth. Revelation says, and He’s going to open it up with more detail, “I saw the dead, small and great, stand before God.” Is everyone going to stand before God? Yeah. It doesn’t matter how small you think you are, and a lot of us, we feel like the wimps of the kingdom, we’re the flea on the dog, you know, and some of us think we are just the greatest thing this earth has ever, you know, had. It doesn’t matter how great you are and how small you are, all of us are going to stand before God. “And the books were opened, and another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.” So what’s in these other books? Everything we say and
Will everyone stand before God and be judged?

Revelation 20:12: And I saw the dead, small and great, standing before God, and books were opened. And another book was opened, which is the Book of Life. And the dead were judged according to their works, by the things which were written in the books.
What is the Book of Life, and how do sins get out of the books?

He says that having your name in the Book of Life should ignite us to praise and thank God. He says that as a believer, you go to Christ, admit the sin, and ask Him to cleanse you, and 1 John 1:9 says He is faithful and just to forgive, so your book has blank pages again.
What is the Book of Life, and how do sins get out of the books?

do. The Book of Life, is your name in the Book of Life? You get your name in the Book of Life, and Jesus said you thank God and praise God because your name is written in the Book of Life, and people still refuse to thank Him and praise Him. They’ll just come to church and stand there. What, that’s self-willed. You’re doing what you want to do. But the Book of Life is so important, it should ignite us to praise God and thank God. Through His death on the cross I can be forgiven, I can be cleansed, and my name written in His book. But there’s other books, and these other books record everything I do. Now how do I get rid of the recording in those books as a believer? Let’s say, you know, I lied. It’s written down. How can I get that out of the book? I go to Christ, I admit I lied, I ask Him to cleanse me, and the Bible says in 1 John 1:9 He is what? Faithful and just to forgive and cleanse me of all sin. So now it’s blotted out and my book has blank pages again. Are you glad for that principle of repentance
What is the Book of Life, and how do sins get out of the books?
1 John 1:9: If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
What is the “revelation of the church” and the mystery kept secret?

He says there was something kept secret until Jesus came, and that it is now revealed to His apostles and prophets by the Spirit: that the Gentiles should be heirs of the same body, which is the church. He says the church is not just a building or a denomination, but His body, which God has chosen to be the messenger of His message.
What is the “revelation of the church” and the mystery kept secret?

for the power of the blood that works for Christians as well as unbelievers? Yeah. Amen. But if we don’t repent, see, if we don’t use our weapons of warfare, then it stays in the book. So, revelation of the church. Romans 16:25, “the revelation of the mystery kept secret since the world began, now made plain by the prophetic scriptures.” Okay, there was something kept secret till Jesus came. All right, what was it? Ephesians 3:3, “by revelation He made known to me the mystery,” “in other ages not made known to men.” Here it is again: “but now it’s revealed to His apostles and prophets by the Spirit.” See, I told you things, you get truth by the Spirit revealing it to you. So that means you got to study, you got to read, you got to go to Bible studies, you got to apply the things so the Spirit can open it up to you. And just because it’s in your mind, does it mean it’s in your inner man? “But now revealed to His apostles and prophets by the Spirit, that the Gentiles should be heirs of the same body,” body, the church. See, the Bible says His body is His church. They’re synonymous terms, so we understand what he’s talking about. “And partakers of His promise.” Hallelujah. So see, the church is one of the revelations. It’s not in the Old Testament in clarity. It is there in parables. Now that we have the revelation, we can see the church all through the Old Testament, but before Jesus came and revealed the church, we didn’t get it. And the church was revealed. So the church is very important, and it’s not just a building with people in it or an association like the Southern Baptist or the Northern Baptist or the South Baptist or the West Baptist or whatever, the Catholic. It’s not that. The church is His body, many-membered body of Christ. We are a powerful group on the earth that God has chosen to be the messenger of His message. We have the power to bring down strongholds, to stop the enemy. We have all these things, as we will
What is the “revelation of the church” and the mystery kept secret?

see. This is a great mystery, Ephesians 5:32. Here it is again, the word mystery: “But I speak about Christ and His” what? Church. So see, the church is a serious revelation, and we need to understand it. How many would raise your hand and say, “Man, I want to understand this church”? See, we are so narrow-minded in our thinking of the church. All right. Now Revelation 21:3, another scripture in Revelations: “The tabernacle of God is with men.” See, the Bible says we are His house, we are His building. “The tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them.” Wow. “And they shall be His people, and God Himself shall be with them and be their God.” Now this is just one verse in Revelations about the church. God said He would be with us. Should we settle for anything less? Absolutely not. Do we just need good speakers in the church? No, we need Him in the church. He promised that He would live with us, He would be here. In fact, Jesus said, “You’re the vine,” or “I am the vine and you are the branches, and without Me you can do nothing.” So is He the most important ingredient? Absolutely. Revelation 21:3: And I heard a loud voice from heaven saying, “Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and He will dwell with them, and they shall be His people. Where did John get the book of Revelation?
He says John got it on the isle of Patmos, where he was banished after being tarred and feathered for preaching the gospel.
He says it means to disclose or reveal, even things that have not been seen before, and this book is the revelation of Jesus Christ.
Who is the book of Revelation written to?
He says it is not just for the seven churches in Asia but for all of God’s servants, everyone who has accepted Christ.
How do we get understanding of the scriptures?
He says to pray, not only for wisdom but that God gives you understanding of the scriptures, because the Spirit is the only one who can open them to you.
What does he say sets us free?
He says it is the truth that sets you free, from your traditions, your unbelief, your doctrines of men and sin.
He says it isn’t complicated and isn’t 20 revelations, just three, and that you don’t need the Hebrew and Greek or someone on TV to tell you what it says.
Is judgment according to faith, grace or deeds?
He reads that God renders to each one according to his deeds, and says that means your work, your lifestyle, how you speak and how you act.
Who gets eternal life, according to this message?
He reads that eternal life goes to those who by patience and continuing in doing good patiently serve God, and says the first step is believing on Jesus.
Does the gospel work no matter who preaches it?
He says someone preaching the gospel and the gospel working does not make the preacher great; it means the gospel is great, because the gospel works no matter who’s preaching it.
Who does he say faces wrath?
He says there is wrath for those who are self-seeking, who do what they want, and for those who hear and don’t do it.
What does he say about weapons of warfare?
He says we have weapons of warfare that aren’t fleshly and we have to exercise them to tear down the strongholds of the enemy.
What good is believing in truth without obeying it?
He says you can believe in truth, but if you don’t obey it, it does no good. He says the gospel doesn’t work for you if you don’t apply it.
Why is the Book of Life important?
He says it should ignite us to praise God and thank Him, because through His death on the cross we can be forgiven and cleansed and our name written in His book.
What does 1 John 1:9 do for the record of our sins?
He says that when you admit the sin and ask Christ to cleanse you, it is blotted out and your book has blank pages again. He adds that if we don’t repent, it stays in the book.
Is the church a denomination or association?
He says the church is not a building or an association but His body, a many-membered body of Christ, chosen by God to be the messenger of His message.

items.d: In “Three Revelations Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues through the opening of Revelation, saying we need a hearing ear, that the book came from Jesus through an angel to all of His servants, and that…
p: In “Three Revelations Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues through the opening of Revelation, saying we need a hearing ear, that the book came from Jesus through an angel to all of His servants, and that angels do not give conflicting messages. He teaches that the blessing in Revelation 1:3 and 22:7 comes to those who read and keep the book, and then lays out what he calls sound doctrine, the foundational doctrines of Hebrews 6 and the mature doctrines of adding to faith.
Why is “he who has an ear, let him hear” repeated seven times, and how do we get a hearing ear?

He says the repetition shows the message is that we need an ear to hear, and that besides wisdom and knowledge we should pray for a hearing ear. He says God is always talking to His church, but we haven’t been taught to come to hear Him; instead we have been taught to come for an inspirational message and an offering.
Why is “he who has an ear, let him hear” repeated seven times, and how do we get a hearing ear?

“He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the” what? Churches. He repeats this seven times. Now what’s the message he’s trying to get across if he repeats it seven times? That we need an ear to hear. In your prayer, besides wisdom and knowledge, do you ever ask for a hearing ear? These are priority prayers. See, I need a hearing ear. Why? ’Cause God’s talking to His church. He’s always talking to His church. But we don’t come to hear Him talk, because we haven’t been taught to come to hear Him talk. We’ve been taught to come and let the guru, the mighty man of God, bless us with a great inspirational message and maybe touch us and pray for us, and if we give him an offering, great things will happen. That about sum it up? Don’t forget that offering. It’s like you got to buy your way into the blessing. Hallelujah. And we fall for it. I go into homes and I see Channel 40 Bibles and so-and-so’s book, a coach of life book. Where in the Bible does He say, “I placed into the body coaches of life”? It’s not there. It’s just absolutely not there. And anyone being my coach other than Jesus, I’m going to fall way short. Could that be an amen?
Why is “he who has an ear, let him hear” repeated seven times, and how do we get a hearing ear?
Revelation 2:7: “He who has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches. To him who overcomes I will give to eat from the tree of life, which is in the midst of the Paradise of God.” ’

He says it came directly from an angel sent by Jesus to His servant John, and that Jesus is directly involved in Revelation. He says it is a message to the churches, so it is for all of us.

Now this came directly from an angel, and Jesus Christ, God, Jesus are the same. He, Jesus, “sent and signified it by His angel unto His servant John.” Okay, going to the last book of the Bible again, of Revelations: “I, Jesus, have sent My angel to testify unto you these things in the churches.” Now here’s Jesus talking directly to John and telling John, “I have sent My angel to testify unto you these things,” unto who? The churches. So is this message for all of us? Yes. Is Jesus directly involved in Revelations also?

Revelation 1:1: The Revelation of Jesus Christ, which God gave Him to show His servants—things which must shortly take place. And He sent and signified it by His angel to His servant John, Revelation 22:16: “I, Jesus, have sent My angel to testify to you these things in the churches. I am the Root and the Offspring of David, the Bright and Morning Star.”

He says no: Galatians 1:8 says if we or an angel from heaven preach any other gospel than the one preached, let him be accursed. If someone sees an angel and the angel gives different doctrines, he says we should not follow that person.

Absolutely. Now we got to be careful of these imitators of angels. Remember, Galatians 1:8 says, “If we or an angel from heaven preach any other gospel unto you than which we have preached, let him be accursed.” Did you hear that? If we, apostles, or an angel from heaven preach any other gospel than that which we have preached, that was preached unto you, let him be accursed. So if I see an angel and he gives me different doctrines, should I follow that person that had that angelic visitation? Should I get all hyped up because someone saw an angel? No. Okay, what’s the point I’m getting at? I’m getting at

Galatians 1:8: But even if we, or an angel from heaven, preach any other gospel to you than what we have preached to you, let him be accursed.

He says angels cannot have different, conflicting messages. He compares claimed angelic visits to the founders of other religions with what the Bible says of the angel Gabriel, concludes the conflict shows the source is wrong, and calls one of those religions “a false religion.” These are his own views about other religions.

I guarantee, I’m still working on it. Now let’s summarize what we learned in the first few verses of Revelation. It is the revelation of who? Jesus Christ, not the beast.
What does he conclude about the first verses of Revelation?

He says Revelation is the revelation of Jesus Christ, not the beast or Satan, along with the judgment to come, which calls for the fear of God because everyone will give an account to Jesus Christ. He says the message is for all of God’s servants, that angels speak the same thing, and that those whose revelations conflict with God’s word are wrong; he ends by calling the church to commit to reading and keeping the Bible.
What does he conclude about the first verses of Revelation?

Hallelujah, not Satan, it’s Jesus we’re looking for here. The revelation of the judgment to come. We need to fear that. We need to have the fear of God in us. We got to stand before Him. It’s going to happen, folks. I don’t care if you’re a Catholic or Protestant or a Muslim, it’s going to happen. You’re going to give an account to God, not to your rabbi, not to the leader of the Muslim church or the Mormon church. You’re going to give an account to Jesus Christ. And the church. Oh church, I wish you could see what God intends for you, and I hope you can see it before this is over. We are a powerful, powerful thing in the earth, and we’re living way below our potential. Let me raise your hand and say, “I, that’s me.” Yeah, you are so powerful that the Bible says, if we lost the battle and we were all wounded, every one of us, that we would rise up and we would destroy the enemy, because God’s with us. Isn’t that powerful? So those of you who feel wounded and hurt and cast down, rise up. Us cripples are better than they are. Amen. That’s just a sample of things to come. And can God lie? No, God cannot lie. All right, things shortly to come to pass. How fast are these things wanting to be done? Quickly. The point is, this is God wanting to do these things quickly in your life, or is it going to take a lifetime and beyond? He wants to do it what? Quickly. Very important, these things that He wants us to learn and obey, we can quickly get them. He emphasized that it was written for all of God’s servants, not the pastors, not the ministers, not the popes and not the priests, it’s for all of us. The churches need an ear to hear, and that’s what we’re going to sing, “Open my eyes, Lord, open my ears, Lord.” We’re going to pray that prayer. It’s a prayer song, the hippies wrote it somewhere back there, it’s a great song. Angels speak the same thing. And when churches are contradicting the word of God, it’s the church’s problem, it’s not God. And when the Muslims and the Jehovah’s Witnesses and the Mormons and all these people who are supposed to have some kind of spectacular revelation from an angel and insight, and it’s conflicting, they are just wrong. And that’s when He says in Revelations, “Come out from among them.” Get into the real doctrine, get into the real thing. Can I hear an amen? “Blessed are those who read and keep the words of this book.” If you’re willing to commit to reading the Bible and keeping the Bible, if you’re willing to commit to saying, “God, open my eyes and my ears. I want to be what You said I could be, and I want to inherit these things You said I can inherit,” if you’re willing to do that, will you can stand with me.
What does he conclude about the first verses of Revelation?

Revelation 18:4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues. 2 Corinthians 6:17: Therefore “Come out from among them And be separate, says the Lord. Do not touch what is unclean, And I will receive you.” Revelation 1:3: Blessed is he who reads and those who hear the words of this prophecy, and keep those things which are written in it; for the time is near.
What is the message of “he who has an ear, let him hear”?
He says that since it is repeated seven times, the message is that we need an ear to hear, and that we should pray for a hearing ear.
Do we need a guru or a “coach of life”?
He says the Bible never says God placed “coaches of life” in the body, and that anyone being his coach other than Jesus would make him fall way short.
Is the book of Revelation for everyone?
He says yes: Jesus sent His angel to testify these things to the churches, so the message is for all of us.
What does Galatians 1:8 say about angels?
He reads that if we or an angel from heaven preach any other gospel than the one preached, let him be accursed.
He says no, angels don’t need to change their messages; they already have the right one. He says it is men who have to change.
Why did he wait to preach on Revelation?
He says God had him not preach on it for years until he could get real truths in the book through his “cranial vacuum,” because he had been tainted by what he heard.
He reads that he who reads and those who hear the words of this prophecy and keep what is written in it are blessed, for the time is near.
Can a famous preacher’s prayer bring blessing without reading and obeying?
He says no: God doesn’t break His principles for anybody, and people want the blessing without reading or obeying the book.
He says it is the blood of Christ that forgives sins, and that you have to come to Him personally and get it.
Which laws does he say we are not under?

He says the “we’re not under law” doctrine refers to the ceremonial laws, such as animal sacrifices, wearing only wool or linen, and planting mixed seeds, which pointed to truth and were fulfilled by Jesus. He says we are still under righteous laws.
Does “I’m not under law, I’m under grace” mean I can sin?
He says no: sound doctrine is righteous doctrine.
What kind of faith does he say we should have?
He says it is faith that God has the power to perform what He promised, not faith in our faith. He gives an example of someone whose faith in his faith had not fixed his finances.
He says the mature doctrines of adding to your faith, virtue, knowledge, self-control, perseverance and brotherly kindness, are higher than faith because we are building on faith.
Who will we give an account to?
He says we are going to give an account to Jesus Christ, not to a rabbi or the leader of another religion’s church.
Who does he say Revelation was written for?
He says it was written for all of God’s servants, not the pastors, ministers, popes or priests, but for all of us.
