If you go to the Catholic group, they’re telling you that the Protestants are this. That’s a fact, yeah. Lu— Martin Luther was the Antichrist, you know, mark 666. They found out how to calculate his name to 666. This nonsense has been going on because we look at things in the natural, when it plainly is talking about what? The spiritual. And somehow they leave that word out of there.
Are the seven mountains of Revelation the seven hills of Rome?
Psalm 125:2: As the mountains surround Jerusalem, So the LORD surrounds His people From this time forth and forever.
What are the mountains of Jerusalem, and what is spiritual fornication?

He says Jerusalem is founded around mountains and the Bible names six of them, and that God’s foundation is in the holy mountains. He says that when Jehoram made high places, the people committed fornication by worshiping God the way they wanted, not the way God said. He says the world’s fornication is spiritual, not sexual: serving God the way God said not to and living a lifestyle God said not to live.
What are the mountains of Jerusalem, and what is spiritual fornication?

And Jerusalem is founded around mountains. Are you aware of that? The Bible names six of them, plainly named six of them. Now, his foundation is in the— what? —holy mountains. Jesus Christ, God’s foundation is in the holy mountains. 2 Chronicles 21:22 [Editor’s note: the passage he reads is 2 Chronicles 21:11.]: Jehoram, the king of Judah, made high places in the mountains of Jerusalem and caused the people to commit— what’s the word? Fornication. They weren’t out there having sex; they were out there worshiping God the way they wanted to worship him, not the way God said. Are you with me? And these, the world, is committing fornication with this. It is not a sexual fornication; it is a spiritual fornication. They are serving God the way God said not to serve him, and they’re living a lifestyle that God said not to live.
What are the mountains of Jerusalem, and what is spiritual fornication?

Psalm 87:1: His foundation is in the holy mountains. 2 Chronicles 21:11: Moreover he made high places in the mountains of Judah, and caused the inhabitants of Jerusalem to commit harlotry, and led Judah astray.
Why did Pastor Kincer preach on the two mothers of Revelation for Mother’s Day?

He says he had to jump over a lesson in his Revelation series to get to this one so he would have it for Mother’s Day, and that next week he will go back and pick up the chapter that was missed. He says there are two mothers in Revelation, and he had already gone through one of them.
Is the woman in Revelation 12 a natural mother?
No, he says. He calls her obviously not a natural mother but a spiritual one, which he says is the church and God’s people, having Christ birthed in them.
Is it a bad sign if Satan dislikes you?

He says it is a big plus for you. If you do not live godly, Satan does not care about you, but if you choose to follow Christ and live right he will come after you, and he says it is a good sign when people do not like the right you are doing.
What should I do when I am going through a wilderness season?
He says to relax, because God has a place prepared and will take care of you there. He says those times of troubles and problems are an important time in which God is shaping us up.
What does he say about the marriage supper of the Lamb?
He says that when we accept Christ we become the bride of Christ, and then there is a big marriage supper up in heaven. He says the Lamb’s wife making herself ready refers to the real believers.
What does blasphemy mean in this message?
He defines blasphemy as speaking evil of God, evil of the Bible, evil of truth and evil of right. He says it shows the beast with the names of blasphemy is connected with Satan.
What does he say the word abomination means?

He says it is a word for a disgusting thing, a hateful thing, and that the Bible calls idolatry and sexual immorality abominations. He says it is not some magical word saying you are worse than anybody else in the world, but a word that means God hates it, despises it and looks down on it.
What does it look like to want only the name of Christ?

He points to Isaiah, where seven women take hold of one man and say they just want his name, with no responsibility or accountability. He says that is what a lot of Christians in America are like: they want to be called Christians, with no relationship, accountability or responsibility.
What does Samson show about why the second woman is a woman?

He says Samson was brought down twice, not by an army or a Philistine hero in battle, but by two women. He says the strongest man who ever existed was caused by a woman, through sexual intimacy, to break God’s laws, lose his eyes and go into captivity, and that the feminine illustration pictures our lust and desires overcoming our common sense and commitment to truth.
What does it mean that the beast “was, and is not, and yet is”?

He says it means the beast, which the Bible uses for a nation, government, ruler or kingdom, existed, then died, then existed again. He says the first beast was the same way, and that this beast ascends out of the bottomless pit, which is Satan’s domain.
Why does the Bible call God’s people Sodom or Egypt?

He says that when God’s people were bad, God referred to them as Rahab, Egypt, and the prophets related to them as Sodom. He says the key word in Revelation 11 is “spiritually,” because the great city that is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt is where the Lord was crucified.
Is the beast of Revelation only an end-time figure?

He says no: the beast was active before John got the revelation and is not some beast that will just be activated at the end time. He says most of it had already happened before John got the revelation, and the bottom line is that it is happening in every generation.

items.d: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues his teaching on the harlot and the beast of Revelation 17, saying Babylon is not the Catholic Church and that the waters, nations and…
p: In “Two Mothers of Revelation Part 2,” Pastor David G. Kincer continues his teaching on the harlot and the beast of Revelation 17, saying Babylon is not the Catholic Church and that the waters, nations and tongues describe a spiritual condition found in every nation. He says believing in Jesus and using his name while living your own way is spiritual fornication, explains John 8:41, and says Jesus calls his people, who are still here on earth, to come out of false religion and come to him. He closes with a Mother’s Day word to mothers and fathers about leading children well.
What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?

He says Babylon is called a destroying mountain in Jeremiah: a nation, a group of people destroying other people for all the evil done in Zion, which he says is the church, the people of God. He says they lead astray not just Christians but people who do not believe in Jesus, and that the shepherds in Jeremiah 50:6 lead people astray on the mountains, serving God the way they should not, so that they forget their resting place, Jesus Christ.
What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?

Shepherds cause my people, in Jeremiah 50:6, to go astray on the what? Mountains. And what are they doing on the mountains? Serving God the way they shouldn’t be serving. And they forget their resting place. Who is our resting place? Jesus Christ. Jeremiah 51:24: “I’m against Babylon, O destroying mountain.” [Editor’s note: the words “destroying mountain” are in Jeremiah 51:25; verse 24 speaks of the evil done in Zion.] So Babylon is referred to as a what? Destroying mountain. A nation, a group of people that are destroying other people for all the evil done in Zion. Zion is the church, the people of God, and destroying all the earth. They don’t just lead Christians astray and people who believe in Jesus astray; they lead people who don’t believe in Jesus astray. Are you there? Hallelujah.
What does the Bible mean by Babylon, the “destroying mountain”?

Jeremiah 50:6: “My people have been lost sheep. Their shepherds have led them astray; They have turned them away on the mountains. They have gone from mountain to hill; They have forgotten their resting place. Jeremiah 51:24-25: “And I will repay Babylon And all the inhabitants of Chaldea For all the evil they have done In Zion in your sight,” says the LORD. “Behold, I am against you, O destroying mountain, Who destroys all the earth,” says the LORD. “And I will stretch out My hand against you, Roll you down from the rocks, And make you a burnt mountain.
Is Babylon in the book of Revelation the Catholic Church?

He says it is not the Catholic Church at all, and that he has debated this with fundamentalist pastors. He says he has met good Catholics, good Baptists and good Pentecostals, and lousy ones too, after ministering in almost every denomination.
Is Babylon in the book of Revelation the Catholic Church?

It’s not the Catholic Church at all. And I’ve debated this with my fundamentalist pastors and all the rest. It’s got nothing to do. I have met good Catholics, folks. I have met good Baptists. I have met good Pentecostals. I’ve met a lot of good people in a lot of churches that I’ve ministered in. I’ve ministered in almost every denomination there is. And I’ve also met lousy ones. Ain’t that right? Their lifestyle and their own way of serving God just really comes up short.
Who are the called, chosen and faithful with the Lamb?

He says the ten spiritual horns make war with the Lamb for one hour, and the Lamb defeats them with those who are called, chosen and faithful. He says that is us: Jesus called us to himself, he chose us when we accepted his sacrifice, and we are faithful when we keep pursuing him and living a lifestyle that pleases him.
Who are the called, chosen and faithful with the Lamb?

There’s ten horns are going to be ten kings for one hour with the beast. Now, obviously, these are ten spiritual horns, and for one hour they’re going to make war with the Lamb. And the Lamb is going to defeat him. And he has some people following with him, and defeats him with him, and they are called “chosen and what? Faithful.” “With him are those called, chosen, and faithful.” Didn’t Jesus call us to himself? Yes. And when we accepted his sacrifice on the cross for our sins, admitted we were sinners and accepted forgiveness and deliverance from our sins because of him, did he choose us? Yes. And when we follow up and we pursue him and learn of him and keep living a lifestyle, we keep growing in a lifestyle pleasing him, isn’t that being faithful? Yeah, that’s us. So if that’s true, we’re still here.
Who are the called, chosen and faithful with the Lamb?

Revelation 17:12-14: “The ten horns which you saw are ten kings who have received no kingdom as yet, but they receive authority for one hour as kings with the beast. These are of one mind, and they will give their power and authority to the beast. These will make war with the Lamb, and the Lamb will overcome them, for He is Lord of lords and King of kings; and those who are with Him are called, chosen, and faithful.”
Will Christians be taken out of the earth before the difficult times?

He says the theory has Christians going out of this earth before these events, but he says he has shown in every chapter that we are still here. He says a God who could only forgive sins but could not keep us when difficult times come would be worthless, and a powerful God can also deliver us from the influence and control of sin.
Will Christians be taken out of the earth before the difficult times?

I’m just letting it sink in. You see, the theory has got us going out of this earth before all this happens. But I’ve showed you in every chapter where we’re still here. And it makes sense. Jesus can only save us and forgive us of sins, and he cannot keep us when the difficult times come? What kind of God is that? He’s a worthless God. A powerful God can not only save us from hell and forgive us for sins, he can deliver us from the influence and control of sin. That is a God that’s got some worth, amen. And Revelation shows us that God has got a people that show in their lifestyle and serving him his power.
What happens to the harlot and the beast in Revelation 17?

He says the ten horns hate the harlot, make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh and burn her with fire, which he says is obviously spiritual since no human being could do that. He says the ten will destroy the beast themselves, and the spiritual beast goes into perdition, a spiritual place of destruction, as Matthew 25:41 speaks of eternal fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
What happens to the harlot and the beast in Revelation 17?

The ten horns hate the [unclear], make her desolate, naked, eat her flesh, and burn her with fire. Now, I’d like to see a human being do that. You see, obviously this is what? Spiritual. And see, these ten are going to destroy the beast themselves, and it’s obviously spiritual. The beast shall go into perdition. Matthew 25:41 says there’s an eternal fire prepared for the devil and his what? Angels, you see? And so she’s going to go there, or the beast is going to go there; it’s talking about the beast. So that spiritual beast is going to go to a spiritual place of destruction.
What happens to the harlot and the beast in Revelation 17?

Revelation 17:16: And the ten horns which you saw on the beast, these will hate the harlot, make her desolate and naked, eat her flesh and burn her with fire. Matthew 25:41: “Then He will also say to those on the left hand, ‘Depart from Me, you cursed, into the everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels:
What do the waters in Revelation 17 mean, and is it about the United Nations or Europe?

He says the waters where the harlot sits are people, multitudes, nations and tongues, so trying to match the beast to the United Nations or a group of European nations misses it. He says this beast is in every nation, about 190 of them, and that God has no prejudice or preference toward any nation.
What do the waters in Revelation 17 mean, and is it about the United Nations or Europe?

Now listen to this. The waters where the [unclear] sits are what? People, multitudes, nations, and tongues. So when they want to go try to get the United Nations, or, you know, the Atlantic Treaty Organization, or the ten European nations, or whatever they were that bound together over there in Europe to get the euro, their own money, and all that, they’re missing it. This beast — and this is in every nation. There is 190— approximately 190 nations. They’re in every one of them. Can I hear an amen? But the theorists have us pondering these little packs of nations, and they always take the industrial nations. Well, you know, God loves Uganda. God loves Paraguay. God loves all these nations everywhere on the earth. He has no prejudice. He has no preference. All are the same. And every nation and every people and every language is important to him. Can I hear an amen? But they don’t make the news. It’s these bigger nations that make the news.
What do the waters in Revelation 17 mean, and is it about the United Nations or Europe?
Revelation 17:15: Then he said to me, “The waters which you saw, where the harlot sits, are peoples, multitudes, nations, and tongues.
What does “tongues” mean in Revelation 17, and what are the two mothers?

He says tongues means languages, and wherever there is a language this beast is right there, because it is a spiritual condition, not a particular nation. He calls it false religion, saying this is the right way when it is not, which is why the feminine illustration is used, and says that of the two mothers, one is really good and one is not so hot. He adds that the kingdom of God is itself a culture and a tradition we are to learn and keep.
What does “tongues” mean in Revelation 17, and what are the two mothers?

So the prophetic theorists use them. Now, there’s 6,000— over 6,000, about 6,500 languages in the earth. You see, this word tongues means languages. And so wherever there’s a language, where is this beast and this— They’re right there. You see, it is a spiritual condition that John is talking about. Can I hear an amen? It’s saying this is the right way, and it’s not. It’s saying they believe in Jesus, and they don’t believe in Jesus. It’s false religion. That’s why the woman is used. That’s why the feminine illustration is used. And when we identify with that, we’re committing spiritual fornication. Amen. So these two mothers, one is really good and one is not so hot. Hallelujah. And there’s just as many cultures as there is languages in this world. As Juliana found out, she went back to where I came from and found out, “Boy, things are different back there.” I said, “Yeah, you got it. Us Southerners, we have our own way of doing things.” But how many, you know, some things in cultures need to change. See, not everything in a culture should be kept. And how many know the kingdom of God is a culture, a tradition, and we’re to learn that and keep that tradition and culture?
Did Jesus give Satan authority over the nations?

He says that when Satan showed Jesus all the kingdoms in the third temptation and offered them for worship, Satan was lying, because Jesus is the Lord of the whole earth and Satan can do nothing without Jesus’s permission. He says Jesus had all the authority but delegated the nations to Satan, a limited delegated authority.
Did Jesus give Satan authority over the nations?

All right. “The woman is the great city which rules over the kings of the earth.” Now, the Bible tells us in the garden that Jesus was tempted by Satan. And the third temptation, he came and showed him all the kingdoms of the earth and said, “Hey, these kingdoms are given to me to give to whomsoever I want. And if you’ll worship me, I’ll give you the whole earth. You’ll be the king of the earth, and all the prosperity and everything that goes with it.” Well, Satan was lying there, because Jesus is the Lord of the whole earth, and Satan cannot do anything without Jesus’s permission. And I mean, this is, you know, be like me going to President Obama and telling him, “Hey, man, I’ll give you all the conservative vote in America and Republican votes, you know, if you just follow my way.” Well, he’s the one that’s got all the authority. He’ll just say, “Who are you?” And that’s the way it is with Jesus. See, Jesus had all the authority. He had all the power, but he delegated the nations to Satan. A limited delegated authority. Are you with me?
Did Jesus give Satan authority over the nations?

Revelation 17:18: And the woman whom you saw is that great city which reigns over the kings of the earth.” Matthew 4:8-9: Again, the devil took Him up on an exceedingly high mountain, and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their glory. And he said to Him, “All these things I will give You if You will fall down and worship me.”
Why does God allow Satan to do evil if God cannot do evil?

He says God cannot do evil, so any evil done in the earth is done by what the Old Testament calls the waster, whom he says God created to do what God has no character to do. He says God cannot lie and cannot reject you if you come to him, while Satan can tempt and test you, but if you follow Christ you will overcome, and there are only two roads, the wide road to hell and the narrow road to heaven.
Why does God allow Satan to do evil if God cannot do evil?

Because — okay, did you guys hear that? Why would he give it? Because God cannot do evil. Okay? So any evil done in the earth, he created what the Old Testament calls the waster to destroy. He created Satan to do what God has no character to do. See, there’s things God cannot do. Are you aware of that? Like, God can’t lie. Ain’t that right? God can’t reject you if you come to him. People say, “Well, God can do anything.” No, there’s things that God can’t do. Why? Because God is good. He can’t do evil. See, God can’t lie. And the Bible says when we come to him, he will not what? Cast us away. When we come to Christ, I don’t care how big a sinner you think you are, Jesus cannot reject you. It’s not in his nature. Does that answer that? But see, Satan can’t. And so Satan comes and he can tempt you. He can test you. He can put little things in your mind to do wrong and all the rest. But if you follow Christ, you’ll overcome that. See, Satan is there trying to lead you away from right. Jesus is there trying to lead you away from wrong. And the darkness and the light are at war. This is where the war is. You know, there’s only two roads. There’s only two spiritual kingdoms, dark and light, right and wrong. There’s only two roads: one, the wide road to hell; the other one, the narrow road to heaven. This is not a complicated Bible. Amen.
Why does God allow Satan to do evil if God cannot do evil?

Matthew 7:13-14: “Enter by the narrow gate; for wide is the gate and broad is the way that leads to destruction, and there are many who go in by it. Because narrow is the gate and difficult is the way which leads to life, and there are few who find it.
What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?

He says the woman used wrongly illustrates the kingdom of darkness, people who choose their own way of religion, and that we commit spiritual fornication when we follow them. He says the Jews of John 8:41 were believers who read the scriptures and had legitimate parents, but created their own way of serving God. He says Jesus told them that if God were their father they would love him, since love does no harm, and that they were harming others by leading them astray.
What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?

So it’s obvious this woman and this beast is connected to which kingdom? Satan’s kingdom. The kingdom of darkness. And when we listen to these people, follow in this way, we become like them. We commit spiritual fornication. John 8:41. Now, I want to prove this to you. Here we go. You ready? I’m trying to back up that the woman used rightly is the illustration of God’s people, the church. The woman used wrongly is an illustration of the kingdom of darkness. They that choose their own way of religion, whatever it may be. These Jews were believers, isn’t that right? Here’s Jesus talking to the Jews. They were believers. They read the scriptures. They went to the synagogue, and they talked to Jesus and say, “We’re not born of fornication.” What’s the word? Fornication. And they weren’t. They had legitimate parents. They weren’t adulterous parents. They could say that. But spiritual fornication is different. See, they created their own way of serving God. Even though they used the scriptures, even though they used God, they had their own way of doing it. And they said, “We’re not born of fornication,” but they were. “We have one father” — who is the father? God. See, they thought they were okay. And Jesus said to them, “If God were your father, you would what? Love me.” See, love in the Bible would do no harm. You’d do nothing to harm me. You do nothing to harm others. You are harming others, because you’re leading them astray from me. And then he says these powerful words: “You are of your father the devil.” Because why? “The works of your father you do.”
What is spiritual fornication, and what did Jesus say to the Jews who said they were not born of fornication?

John 8:41: You do the deeds of your father.” Then they said to Him, “We were not born of fornication; we have one Father—God.” John 8:42: Jesus said to them, “If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I proceeded forth and came from God; nor have I come of Myself, but He sent Me. John 8:44: You are of your father the devil, and the desires of your father you want to do. He was a murderer from the beginning, and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he speaks a lie, he speaks from his own resources, for he is a liar and the father of it.
Is it possible to believe in Jesus and still go to hell?

He says yes: if you start using his name to worship your own way and live your own way, that is spiritual fornication, which is what the beast and the woman are about. He says it is not the Catholic, Baptist or Presbyterian church or the people who come to Christ, but anyone in them who decides to take his name and not live his way and serve him his way.
Is it possible to believe in Jesus and still go to hell?

Are you out there? See, this is the masculine illustration, and in Revelation we have the feminine illustration. Hallelujah. So is it possible to believe in Jesus and go to hell? Yes. If you start using his name to worship your own way and live your own way, that is spiritual fornication. And that’s what this on the beast is all about. And it’s that simple. It’s not the Catholic Church. It’s not the Baptist church. It’s not the Presbyterian church or any of these people that come to Christ. It is anyone in them that decides to take his name and not live his way and serve him his way. Amen. Moms. Amen.
Should you read the Bible before you reject it?

He says that, talking with people with their own dreamed-up religion who never read the Bible, he asked how many know you cannot condemn a book until you read it and cannot say it does not work until you apply it. He says many Christians have not read the book either and just believe everything on radio and TV, which he says tells a lot of lies, and he asks, in the natural, what kind of mother or parent are you.
Should you read the Bible before you reject it?

You say, “What’s that got to do with Mother’s Day?” Well, what kind of mother are you? See, in the natural, are we leading our kids right, or we got our own way? I mean, I just talked to people Friday night that had their own dreamed-up religion. They never read the Bible. They just come up with ideas from hearing TV and talk show people and all the rest. And we had a great discussion there. At least I did. How many of you know you can’t condemn a book until you read it? And you can’t say a book doesn’t work until you read it and you applied it. Yeah. And they were failing on all parts. And how many you know, many Christians haven’t even read the book yet. They just believe everything on radio and TV, which are telling you a lot of lies. I guarantee you, you won’t hear this on the book of Revelation on radio and TV.
What does “Come out of her, my people” mean in Revelation 18?

He says Babylon, the city that rules over the kings of the earth, has fallen and is inhabited by evil spirits, with the kingdom of darkness the main force of influence in it, and the call is to come out from this false Christianity. He says the call goes to God’s people, who are still on earth, not raptured out, and Jesus is inviting everyone to come out of their own opinions and ideas and come to him, not religion.
What does “Come out of her, my people” mean in Revelation 18?

So the [unclear] is judged. She is Babylon that rules over the kings of the earth. The mother of abominations, and martyrs and the saints. She sits on seven mountains, sits on the nations. Ten kings hate and destroy her. And Revelation 18:2, it goes on to say that Babylon, this city, this is fallen, and it’s inhabited by evil spirits. So the word fallen doesn’t mean it’s totally destroyed. It’s fallen. It’s deteriorated, and the kingdom of darkness is the main force of influence in it. Are you with me? All right. All nations, kings, merchants commit fornication with her. They’re rich through her delicacies. Here it is: “Come out from what? Her— who? The—“ Come out from this false Christianity. Who is he saying to come out? “My people.” So where are they still? Where is the people? On earth. See, they got us in this dream world of rapturing out of here and all this bad stuff happening. But Revelation has us here handling it, because Jesus is the King of Kings and the Lord of Lords, and he is all powerful, and he keeps his people. Amen. And he’s saying, “My people, don’t have anything to do with that kind of religion.” They’re still here. And he’s inviting everyone today to come out from your own opinions, to come out from your own ideas, to come out from your friends’ ideas and their opinions, and come to him. He’s still saying, “Come unto me, all ye that labor and heavy laden, and I will give you rest. As many as come to me, I will in no wise cast out.” Jesus is still calling out to the world through the word and through the Spirit: “Come to me,” not religion. Catholic can’t get you to heaven. Baptists can’t get you to heaven. Pentecostals can’t get you to heaven. They can’t give you wisdom and knowledge and understanding and peace and love. “I can give it all to you. Come out, my people.” And that’s what every church should be preaching: come to him. Hallelujah.
What does “Come out of her, my people” mean in Revelation 18?

Revelation 18:2: And he cried mightily with a loud voice, saying, “Babylon the great is fallen, is fallen, and has become a dwelling place of demons, a prison for every foul spirit, and a cage for every unclean and hated bird! Revelation 18:4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues. Matthew 11:28: Come to Me, all you who labor and are heavy laden, and I will give you rest. John 6:37: All that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out.
If I have made spiritual mistakes, can I correct them?

He says yes: if we have made the mistake we can correct it, in the natural or in the spiritual. He says he made a lot of mistakes as a young Christian, thinking it was spiritual when it was not, and that Jesus is still the forgiver, the deliverer and the one who can save you, but you have to recognize the differences so you are not a partaker of her sins and plagues.
If I have made spiritual mistakes, can I correct them?

So, see, if we’ve made the mistake, can we correct it? Absolutely. In the natural, if we’re sexual immoral people or thieves and liars and so forth, can we come out and correct the natural? If in the spiritual we’re wrong, can we correct the spiritual? Yes. Thank God, I’d have been killed a long time ago, [unclear] I’ve been cast out a long time ago. I made a lot of mistakes as a young Christian, thinking it was spiritual and it wasn’t. And you can raise your hand and say, “Yeah, I can relate.” See, both in the natural and in the spiritual, he is crying, “Come to me. I’m still the forgiver. I’m still the deliverer. I’m still the one that can save you. I’m still the one that can get you to the goal.” But you got to recognize the differences to be able to make that decision, so you don’t be a partaker of her sins and of her plagues.
If I have made spiritual mistakes, can I correct them?
Revelation 18:4: And I heard another voice from heaven saying, “Come out of her, my people, lest you share in her sins, and lest you receive of her plagues.
Why does the Bible use a mother to picture the church?

He says it is the mother who carries, nourishes and finally gives birth to the child, while the man conceives it and gives it life. He says what the mother eats and does in the natural affects the child being born, and how she teaches it and lives before it affects it afterward, so mothers must keep the responsibility until the child is a responsible adult with good character and discipline.
Why does the Bible use a mother to picture the church?

The Bible uses the mother because it’s the mother that carries and nourishes and finally gives birth to that child. The man conceives it. He gives it life. It takes on his nature. But the mother nourishes it. And this is why the church is illustrated as a woman. See, what you eat, what you do with your body in the natural is going to affect that child being born. And after it’s born, how you teach it, the life you live before it is going to affect that child. And so, mothers, you’re very important not to just birth the child, but to keep that mother responsibility to see that that child gets to twenty years old, an adult that’s responsible, has good character, discipline in their life.
How should parents raise their children, according to this message?

He says the woman driven into the wilderness reproduced children with great character who had the testimony of Jesus and obeyed the word of God, and that dads are included because these are spiritual decisions. He says parents should stay, support the child and the home, live as an example, and bring children to church so they see them worshiping God, and he remembers his own mother’s voice keeping him from wrong.
How should parents raise their children, according to this message?

And that’s what the woman that was driven into the wilderness had. She reproduced children with great character. They had the testimony of Jesus, and they obeyed the word of God. Wow. So, moms, have we been doing that? And can we improve on that? And dads, if you think you can escape this message, I’m going to connect you, because it says spiritually. We’re talking about spiritual decisions. And so it’s not just the woman now, but the men need to make the same decisions. Can that be an amen? You don’t just give life to a child because you like to have sex and then just run off on it and leave it. That’s horrible. But you hang in there and you support that child. You support that home. You live an example to that home. Amen. Like Mike said, you bring them to church so they get the word of God in them from another source, not your own. Your own’s confirmed. They see you worshiping God. They don’t see you dropping them off at church and then going back home to watch the Lakers on TV or whatever. They see you right there with them. They see you are concerned about the things of God. And see, that’s the way my mom was. And I wound up just like her. Hallelujah. And sometimes when I was a teenager and I was doing bad things, it wasn’t God bringing me under conviction; it was my mom’s voice. David, now don’t get me wrong, God used my mom’s voice to bring me in conviction. But it was my mom [unclear] that said, “Don’t you do that.” I noticed one of my older brothers was saying, “Man, mom told me three things.” And one of the things is, you know, you don’t have sex outside of marriages and have kids that you don’t raise and all that. And though he’s in his seventies, he said, “Man, if I did anything wrong, I would remember that voice.” And I said, “I’m with you. I remember that voice.” Hallelujah. So it pays for moms to follow through on being a mom, and dads to follow through. And this morning Jesus is offering, still, for us to come out from among our own way, our own beliefs, our own religion, and embrace his
How should parents raise their children, according to this message?
Revelation 12:17: And the dragon was enraged with the woman, and he went to make war with the rest of her offspring, who keep the commandments of God and have the testimony of Jesus Christ.
Does he say there are good and bad people in every church?

He says he has met good Catholics, good Baptists and good Pentecostals, and lousy ones too, in the many denominations where he has ministered. He says their lifestyle and their own way of serving God comes up short in those cases.
What does it mean to be chosen and faithful?

He says Jesus called us to himself, and when we accepted his sacrifice, admitted we were sinners and accepted forgiveness and deliverance, he chose us. He says that when we pursue him, learn of him and keep growing in a lifestyle pleasing him, that is being faithful.
What does he say about the theory that Christians leave the earth first?

He says the theory has us going out of the earth before all this happens, but in every chapter he has shown that we are still here. He says Revelation has Jesus keeping his people here, handling it, because he is the King of Kings and Lord of Lords and is all powerful.
Does God love every nation equally?

He says God loves Uganda and Paraguay and all the nations everywhere on the earth, and has no prejudice and no preference. He says every nation, people and language is important to him, even though the smaller ones do not make the news.
How many languages does he say there are?

He says there are over 6,000, about 6,500 languages in the earth, and that wherever there is a language this beast is right there. He ties the word tongues to languages, and says the beast is a spiritual condition.
Is the kingdom of God a culture?

He says there are as many cultures as languages, and not everything in a culture should be kept. He says the kingdom of God is a culture and a tradition, and we are to learn that and keep that tradition and culture.
Can God lie or turn away someone who comes to him?

He says God cannot lie and cannot reject you if you come to him, because God is good and cannot do evil. He says that when we come to Christ, however big a sinner we think we are, Jesus cannot reject us, because it is not in his nature.
Does he say there are only two spiritual roads?

He says there are only two spiritual kingdoms, dark and light, right and wrong, and only two roads: the wide road to hell and the narrow road to heaven. He says Satan tries to lead you away from right and Jesus tries to lead you away from wrong, and the darkness and the light are at war.
How do we commit spiritual fornication, according to this message?

He says it happens when we listen to people who follow the kingdom of darkness and follow them in their way, and we become like them. He says it means choosing your own way of religion while using the scriptures and God’s name, as the Jews did when Jesus spoke with them.
What does he say love looks like in this passage?

He says love in the Bible would do no harm: you would do nothing to harm him and nothing to harm others. He says the Jews were harming others by leading them astray from Jesus, and he points to Jesus’s words that the works of your father you do.
Are dads included in this message to mothers?

He says that if dads think they can escape this message he is going to connect them, because it says spiritually and these are spiritual decisions. He says it is not just the woman but the men who need to make the same decisions, and that you do not give life to a child and then run off and leave it.
What does he say about his mother’s influence on him?

He says that when he was a teenager doing bad things, it was his mother’s voice he heard, and God used her voice to bring him under conviction. He says one of his older brothers, now in his seventies, said he would remember that voice if he did anything wrong, and he says he remembers it too.

items.d: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters…
p: In this message Pastor David G. Kincer teaches from Isaiah 43 that God’s people are victorious in afflictions because God created, formed, redeemed and called them by name, and will be with them in the waters and the fire. He ties the waters to baptism, teaches that grace says no to ungodliness, and warns that living for Christ brings conflict. He ends with the hindrances to victory (not calling on God, impatience, forgotten offerings) and the invitation to “state your case” to God.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

He goes to Isaiah 43:1–3 and says God “directly makes four statements himself that explain, totally explain, why Christians are victorious in afflictions.” He defines afflictions as “misery, pain,” and says they can come through sickness, poverty, persecution, acts of war, acts of God, or be self-inflicted.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

Isaiah 18. Why God’s people are victorious in afflictions. We’re going to go to Isaiah chapter 43, verses 1 through 3, and we’re going to see there that God makes four statements. He directly makes four statements himself that explain, totally explain, why Christians are victorious in afflictions. Afflictions is misery, pain. And in the Bible, afflictions can come through sickness, poverty, persecution, acts of war, acts of God, or self-inflicted. How many you know, a lot of us go through our own afflictions, we self-inflict them. And so, but God’s people are going to be victorious in these things. Verse 1.
Why are God’s people victorious in afflictions?

Isaiah 43:1-3: But now, thus says the LORD, who created you, O Jacob, And He who formed you, O Israel: “Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; You are Mine. When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned, Nor shall the flame scorch you. For I am the LORD your God, The Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I gave Egypt for your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place.
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

He says the first statement, “created and formed you,” is in the New Testament “being born again”: “God personally comes to us when we come to him, and he births us by the Spirit and by the word.” He says Jesus is forming us into “the likeness, the character of Jesus Christ,” and “therefore we can handle afflictions.”
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

Number one, “Thus saith the Lord who,” number one, “created and formed you.” I created you. In the New Testament we call it being born again. “Anyone in Christ,” if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creature, a new creation, “all things are passed away, all things are made new.” Why? Because God personally comes to us when we come to him, and he births us by the Spirit and by the word, and we become a new creature, and therefore we can be victorious in afflictions. In Galatians 4:19, “I labor in birth again till Christ is formed in you.” You see, Jesus is forming us, and the Bible says in Corinthians that we come into the same image of Christ. “By the Spirit of the Lord” we are changed, transformed, metamorphosed into the same image of Christ. See, he’s fashioning us into his image, not your pastors, not the great mighty man of God in the earth, but we are fashioned unto the likeness, the character of Jesus Christ. And so therefore we can handle afflictions when they come, pain and poverty, whatever, whatever faces us, we can handle it, be victorious, because he, number one, has created us, and he, number two, has fashioned us and formed us. Then he says the second reason is, “Fear not.” Don’t be afraid, “for I have redeemed you.” Now I remember when I first read the Bible through, and I came to Isaiah, I understood a little bit about chapter one, I didn’t understand beans till I got to Hezekiah
What does it mean that God created and formed you?

2 Corinthians 5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, he is a new creation; old things have passed away; behold, all things have become new. Galatians 4:19: My little children, for whom I labor in birth again until Christ is formed in you, 2 Corinthians 3:18: But we all, with unveiled face, beholding as in a mirror the glory of the Lord, are being transformed into the same image from glory to glory, just as by the Spirit of the Lord.
What does it mean that God redeemed you and called you by name?

He says “I’ve purchased you,” and compares it to taking care of a car you bought: “we’re his property.” He says God “personally called you by my name,” so “Satan is not my problem… I belong to Jesus, and nobody’s big enough to mess with him.”
What does it mean that God redeemed you and called you by name?

and the 185,000 getting killed, because I already read that in the book of Kings. But when I came to chapter 43, I understood that I needed this. I was going through things that I needed answers for, and this part of Isaiah just exploded to me. And uh, one of the things here, he not only formed us and created us, but he says, “Don’t be afraid, Dave. Don’t be afraid, church. I’ve redeemed you.” I’ve purchased you. Anyone that purchases something, when you purchase a car, you take care of it because it’s an investment for you. You purchase a gun, you take care of it, it’s an investment. You don’t lay it out in the rain, let it rust, and all that. You know, you take care of things. So God’s going to want to take care of us, he’s purchased us, we’re his property. Amen. And that just really just ignited my, my spiritual growth when I was younger. “I have called you,” number three, “by your name. You are mine.” He, again, “I’ve redeemed you, you belong to me, you’re my property, and I have personally come to you, Dave Kincer, and revealed myself to you, drawn you to me. I personally called you by my name, Dave Kincer, come, come over to the kingdom of light.” Aren’t you glad God’s a personal God? Hallelujah. Yes, I belong to him. Satan is not my problem, the kingdom of darkness is not my problem, I belong to Jesus, and nobody’s big enough to mess with him. Number four, “When you pass through the waters I will be with you, and through the rivers they shall not overflow you.” And this is what was happening in my first year of, of salvation. I was struggling
What does it mean that God redeemed you and called you by name?
Isaiah 43:1: But now, thus says the LORD, who created you, O Jacob, And He who formed you, O Israel: “Fear not, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; You are Mine.
Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?

He reads 1 Peter 3:20–21 and asks, “How can you tell me that baptism has nothing to do with salvation?” He says “water baptism is just as important as the sinner’s prayer,” that “people will defend their denominational doctrine above scriptural truth,” and that for him baptism was “my signature on the contract.”
Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?

a lot of times because I didn’t understand things, and a lot of times because people didn’t want anything to do with me, uh, my old friends. After I changed, they left me, and I had to learn to let them go, and it was painful, I didn’t want to lose friends, but I had to make a choice. I had to keep serving God. And so I needed, I needed this verse, this chapter in Isaiah to confirm and ignite me as I went through these things. The waters is talking about, 1 Peter 3:20, “In the days of Noah, eight souls were saved by water. The like figure, baptism, now saves us, not the putting away of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God by the resurrection of Jesus Christ.” Now, when I was in China, I asked a lot of questions, and one of the questions I asked is how quick someone should be baptized, and over there they waited six months to a year to baptize them. Folks, that is not Bible. And a lot of people teach that baptism has nothing to do with salvation. This verse tells you different. Let’s read it again. “In the days of Noah, eight souls were saved by,” what? Water. “In like model and like example, baptism. Water baptism now,” what? “Now saves us.” How can you tell me that baptism has nothing to do with salvation? Did John the Baptist say, “Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin”? Were there two things that needed to be done? Yes. Jesus, when he came along, did he say, “Repent and be baptized for the remission of sin”? Two things had to be done, and he added one thing to it: “I believe the gospel.” Do we need to believe the gospel, trust in the gospel? Yes. You see, people will defend their denominational doctrine above scriptural truth. And so, and water baptism is just as important as the sinner’s prayer. You ask God to repent, and then you get baptized, bam. And so I had a big debate with him all the time over there about water baptism. I said, “You’re robbing the people. You are robbing the people with your ignorance of the Scripture. Baptism is a powerful work.” Now, in this scripture he’s talking about “not the putting away the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God by the resurrection of Christ.” He’s talking about coming out of the water, the resurrection of Christ, we have a good conscience. And see, I understood as a young Christian that water baptism was my signature on the contract, and Jesus’s signature on the contract, the new covenant. And so when I went through anything, I could go back to my baptism and I could say, “No, God’s going to finish the good work he began in me. God’s gonna, he’s gonna keep forgiving me, he’s going to keep cleansing me, I am going to make it, because I’ve been water baptized, I put my signature on the contract, and he always keeps his word.” Can I hear an amen? Water baptism is very important.
Does baptism have anything to do with salvation?

1 Peter 3:20-21: who formerly were disobedient, when once the Divine longsuffering waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was being prepared, in which a few, that is, eight souls, were saved through water. There is also an antitype which now saves us—baptism (not the removal of the filth of the flesh, but the answer of a good conscience toward God), through the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?

He says the “waters” are the Red Sea and the “rivers” the Jordan, and “both baptisms delivered them from the affliction.” He says “passing through the Red Sea is a model of water baptism,” and “if you haven’t been baptized, I’d get baptized next Sunday.”
What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?

And that first year I was going through a struggle, Mike hit it last week, well, you know, the king of Egypt could come after, and he didn’t want him serving God even after he’d let him go, he still was after his people. And that’s what Satan did. “You had nothing really happened, you weren’t really born again, you know, you’re just making a fool out of yourself.” How many went through that as a young Christian? Man, I don’t believe that. I don’t believe that only a few of us went through that. I know this book, and I know Satan, how he works. Now, the waters, of course, is talking about the Red Sea here, in Isaiah. Egypt was after them, they were afflicted in Egypt, okay, and “through the rivers” is talking about the river of Jordan, 40 years later they had to go through the river of Jordan. The Red Sea parted and they went through it, river of Jordan piled up in heaps in the north until Israel got across, and they were afflicted by the wilderness, and see, both baptisms delivered them from the affliction and the pain of what they had been going through. Are you there? Hallelujah. And so I learned that. You know, these afflictions, they’re going to be, but God is going to deliver me out of every one of them, and I learned this in Isaiah, and then I found it all through the Scriptures. 1 Corinthians 10:1-2, “Our fathers were under the cloud, they passed through the Red Sea and were all baptized.” See, passing through the Red Sea is a model of water baptism. Noah’s judgment of water was an example of water baptism. Are you there? Water baptism is very important, and people that don’t get immediately baptized, they’re just missing it, and people that don’t believe that you need to get baptized as part of your salvation plan, they are just wrong. So if you haven’t been baptized, I’d get baptized next Sunday. I’m serious. The thing that helped me, an old man in the Assembly God church led me to Christ, and he knew how to do it, took me right through the Scriptures. I knew what was happening, the power of God through the word that he was bringing to me and making me read delivered me. I got, say, I got born again that night, that load of sin went off of me that I didn’t even know I had. I didn’t know I had a burden of sin, it was gone. He said, “Son, you got to get baptized next Sunday.” “Well, okay, whatever.” What’s next? Whatever. The first thing was good, second thing, huh, whatever. I didn’t even, they didn’t even, they didn’t tell me what a baptism was. I tell people what baptism is so they understand. I got in that baptismal pool and the power of God came all over me, the presence of God just flooded me, but they didn’t teach, you know, other than tongue, some kind of, they didn’t teach you about the power and the presence of God. But see, they came under the cloud, that’s the presence of God, and through the sea, the waters, the water baptism. The presence of God in water baptism is a powerful thing, church. And the Red Sea parting, the Bible says, was a model of water baptism. Hallelujah. And if nothing today, get your baptism doctrine right. You know, we pass on error to other people, we read error and we pass on error without really finding out and experiencing these powers in God, these principles. So, I’m delivered from the afflictions of sin. See,
What do the Red Sea and the Jordan teach about baptism and deliverance?

Isaiah 43:2: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; And through the rivers, they shall not overflow you. When you walk through the fire, you shall not be burned, Nor shall the flame scorch you. 1 Corinthians 10:1-2: Moreover, brethren, I do not want you to be unaware that all our fathers were under the cloud, all passed through the sea, all were baptized into Moses in the cloud and in the sea,
How does Jesus bring us out of the “furnace” of affliction?

He says Pharaoh was Israel’s slave master and “sin is also a slave master,” and “Jesus comes and delivers us from those slave masters.” He says the iron furnace in Deuteronomy 4:20 is Egypt, and “we can be victorious through afflictions because he created us, he formed us, he called us by our name.”
How does Jesus bring us out of the “furnace” of affliction?

Pharaoh, see, was the master, the slave master of Israel, afflicting them. They’re going through afflictions and pain and misery. Sin is also a slave master, and Jesus comes and delivers us from those slave masters, and part of it is not just being born again but being baptized. It’s a package. Could I hear an amen? “Let God be true and every man a liar.” Yeah, we need to get back to the Bible. All right, now, “When you walk through the fire you shall not be burned, neither shall the flame kindle upon you, for I am the Lord thy God.” Okay, now, Deuteronomy 4:20, “The Lord brought you out of the iron furnace.” Out of where? Who is the iron furnace? Egypt. You see, that 400 years of affliction, that slave masters’ control over their life. He said, “I brought you out of the iron furnace,” a furnace is a place where there is a fire, right? “And I brought you out to be my people and my inheritance.” Isaiah 43:10, “Behold, I have,” 48:10, “Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver. I have tested you in the furnace of,” what? Affliction. So the furnace of affliction was this furnace in Egypt. Who had them in slavery? Who were making their lives miserable and caused them to call upon God to deliver them? So plainly he’s talking about the afflictions of God’s people. Amen. And we can be victorious through afflictions because he created us, he formed us, he called us by our name specifically, and he gets us through these things, he redeemed us, we’re his property, and we’re going to get through these afflictions. I don’t care if it’s financial, physical, spiritual, mental, emotional, you’re going to get through, and you’re going to be victorious. Is that a good amen? Yes. And that just changed my life that day when I hit this verse. I didn’t understand the rest of it before that, but I sure got this one, and it really came at a good time in my life. Now,
How does Jesus bring us out of the “furnace” of affliction?

Deuteronomy 4:20: But the LORD has taken you and brought you out of the iron furnace, out of Egypt, to be His people, an inheritance, as you are this day. Isaiah 48:10: Behold, I have refined you, but not as silver; I have tested you in the furnace of affliction.
Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?

He says people told him “nothing’s going to happen to you,” but “a couple of weeks after being saved I had more problems than I’d ever had before.” He cites 1 Thessalonians 3:3, “we are appointed to this,” and Psalm 34:19, “Many are the afflictions of the righteous,” and says Paul testified “God delivered me.”
Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?

1 Thessalonians 3:3, “No one should be shaken by these afflictions. You know that we are appointed to this.” We’re appointed to what? Afflictions. We’re appointed to what? Afflictions. Now, when I got saved, everybody was saying, “If you believe in Jesus, nothing’s going to happen to you. You’re going to roller skate right into him. You’re going to skate through life, no problem.” You know, a couple of weeks after being saved, I had more problems than I’d ever had before, because now I see who I really am. Are you there? I didn’t know I was so bad. I wasn’t murdering people and committing adultery and, uh, you know, joining gangs and all that, but you’re still bad. “There’s none righteous, no, not one.” You come into his life, man, I got a lot of changing to do. Isn’t that right? And see, if we really get born again, we get into this thing, this is exactly how it works. You just join a church, you don’t know beans, you just say a little mechanical sinner’s prayer, you got nothing, born again. Don’t ever laugh at it, people laugh at it, don’t let them laugh at it. That’s how we become a new creature. And I don’t care if you’re a Catholic, a Baptist, a Pentecostal, a Lutheran, a Jew, I don’t care what you are, you get born again, you’re going to become a new creature, old things are going to pass away and all things are going to [unclear], got nothing to do with denominationalism. Can I hear an amen? Thank you. Psalm 34:19, “Many are the afflictions of the righteous.” How many? Many. Man, they were teaching me wrong back there, the faith camp. They were just totally out of it. “You’re going to prosper and everything’s going to be, nothing bad is going to happen.” The other, read the life of Jesus. Did bad things happen to him? Do you ever read the life of the twelve apostles? Did bad things happen to them? Yeah. Were they afflicted? Yes. Paul said God delivered me out of all my affliction, and he lists them. I had, I had afflictions with, with robbers, that affliction with countrymen, I was, I was stoned twice, and I was, you know, been in jail and beaten in prison. He had all kinds of afflictions, but Paul said God delivered me. How? Out of how many? All of them. And you live for Christ and you really preach the gospel, and people will afflict you because you are a threat to them. They want to justify their low level of Christianity as a high level, and you get to a high level, they don’t like you because you exposed them.
Does believing in Jesus mean nothing bad will happen to you?

1 Thessalonians 3:3: that no one should be shaken by these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we are appointed to this. Psalm 34:19: Many are the afflictions of the righteous, But the LORD delivers him out of them all.
Why does living for Christ bring conflict with others?

He says if you live your life for Christ, “you’re going to be in conflict with those who don’t,” including believers who do not pursue righteousness. He cites 2 Thessalonians 1:6, “It is a righteous thing with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you,” and says “Don’t mess with the church.”
Why does living for Christ bring conflict with others?

Are you there? Conflicts. Now he’s going to deal with conflicts. Two conflicts here: conflicts of right and wrong, and the conflicts of right people doing wrong, contradictory. Isaiah 43:3, [unclear], “I gave Egypt for your ransom.” I gave Ethiopia, the nation just below Egypt, for your [unclear], and Seba, a province next to Egypt in Ethiopia, for your [unclear]. And remember, Moses married an Ethiopian woman when he was down in Egypt, so Ethiopians were prominent in Egypt, they were right next door, and they came over and they were part of the Egyptian population. Do you understand that? Okay. Did God destroy Egypt? Did it kill a lot of people? Did he kill a lot of Egyptians? Yes, he did. “I will give men for you and people for your life.” Hallelujah. 2 Thessalonians 1:6, “It is a righteous thing with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you.” Wow. Don’t mess with the church. The church that follows and pursues righteousness, not just a believer, and, and in China we met all kinds of people. We may have disagreements in other doctrines, but every one of them, Mr. [unclear] can attest to this, had that pursuit of righteousness. They had the high mark plan, and it was beautiful, right, Mr. [unclear]? It was beautiful. You know, we don’t have to agree on every jot and tittle, but we need to agree on Jesus Christ saving us from his sins, making us new creatures, and we pursue righteousness. Amen, that’s the thing. Now, he goes on to say in Proverbs 28:4, “Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, but to keep the law oppose them.” You say, “You don’t have to go out and witness door-to-door or anything.” That we need to, don’t get me wrong, but if you live your life for Christ, you’re going to be in conflict with those who don’t. You’re going to be in opposition, and I’m talking about believers also. Believers who don’t pursue the high mark of the calling of God, to love Jesus, which is keeping his commandments, doing right, they’re going to be in conflict with you. And so you live your life, you’re going to, all you have to do is go through the day, live in your life for Christ, and you’re going to be at war with the enemy. Isn’t that beautiful? Hallelujah. Yeah, you may be too timid, like me, to share Christ with anybody. I broke that within a year, but, but you know, just living, just making that decision for Christ, you’re in conflict with people. Ah. Now, in Noah’s day, did God destroy the whole earth and save Noah? Did he give people that Noah might live? Are you out there? Okay. Job, was he afflicted? Yeah. Lot, did God destroy Sodom and Gomorrah, kill all the inhabitants, babies, children, everyone
Why does living for Christ bring conflict with others?

Isaiah 43:3-4: For I am the LORD your God, The Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I gave Egypt for your ransom, Ethiopia and Seba in your place. Since you were precious in My sight, You have been honored, And I have loved you; Therefore I will give men for you, And people for your life. 2 Thessalonians 1:6: since it is a righteous thing with God to repay with tribulation those who trouble you, Proverbs 28:4: Those who forsake the law praise the wicked, But such as keep the law contend with them.
Will God judge the world to defend his church?

He says “there’s a time coming before Christ returns that this world is going to be shaken by the power of God and his jealousy for his church,” and “he’s going to show the world his church is glorious.” He points to Noah, Lot, the 185,000 Syrians, Herod and the sorcerer on Cyprus as places where God struck enemies and delivered his people.
Will God judge the world to defend his church?

and delivered Lot to live? Yeah. Are you understanding this scripture? I’m telling you, there’s a time coming before Christ returns that this world is going to be shaken by the power of God and his jealousy for his church. And Isaiah is making this very plain. That’s why Christ isn’t coming today, that’s why he isn’t coming tomorrow, that’s why he isn’t coming when these people predict it. They don’t know when he’s coming, but he’s going to manifest himself before he comes, and he’s going to show the world his church is glorious. Hallelujah. Amen. And the people who want to harden their heart and all that, they’re going to pay, they’re going to pay a price. Okay, did he slay 185,000 Syrians to deliver Jerusalem? Yes. Herod, did he smite Herod with worms? Yeah. Yeah. Did he smite the sorcerer on the island of Cyprus with blindness? Yes. Did he kill the Roman soldiers who had, was given the responsibility to watch Peter, and Peter was delivered by an angel? Were those soldiers killed? Church, we don’t have a skosh of an idea how much God loves us and what his [unclear] intention is for his [unclear]. But one day the world is going to have this. Hallelujah.
What does it mean to be God’s witnesses?

He reads Acts 1:8 and says “You shall be what? Witnesses. Proof that I’m real.” He says of speaking in tongues, “that’s not the proof,” and from 1 John 3:7 that “he who practices righteousness is” righteous. He explains “All born of God do not sin” to mean “you cannot flagrantly, habitually sin.”
What does it mean to be God’s witnesses?

Don’t mess with the church. The church that is pursuing righteousness, I don’t care if they’re Catholics, I don’t care if they’re Protestant, I don’t care if they’re a Jew, if they’re pursuing Jesus and righteousness, don’t mess with them. They may not believe everything you believe, but those two things are the priority things. Could that be an amen? No. Then he says, “You are my witnesses.” A witness is an evidence, a witness is a person that experienced the event, they’re the proof that someone’s guilty or someone’s innocent. And in Acts chapter 1, verse 8, “You shall receive power after the Holy Ghost has come upon you, and you shall be,” tongue-talkers. You shall be Baptists. You shall be Pentecostals. You shall be Catholics. It’s not there. Why do we put that word in there? You shall be what? Witnesses. Proof that I’m real, proof that I can do what I set out to do, you are my proof. Hallelujah. And I speak in tongues, but that’s not the proof. 1 John 3:7, “Don’t be deceived, he who practices righteousness is,” what? Righteous. Well, I’m righteous by the blood of Christ. Well, wonderful, but that doesn’t help your wife you’re beating up. That doesn’t help your kid that you break their arms when you spank them. That doesn’t help your family when you’re squandering the money gambling on sports and, and drugs and other things. Hey, so you’re righteous by the cross, what good does that do you or anybody? Can I hear an amen? “He who practices righteousness is,” what? Righteous. “All born of God do not sin, for his seed,” what is the seed? Okay, Jesus and the word, yes. Say, Jesus is in us, the word is in us, so he cannot sin because he’s been born of God. Now what that really means: you cannot flagrantly, habitually sin because you’ve got Christ and the word gnawing at you, convicting you, and you repent and you get up, you do not continue in sin. Why? Because you were really born of the Spirit, that Spirit of Jesus and that Spirit of the word, and yeah, you may not be perfect today, but you keep changing. Why? Because that birthing is real.
What does it mean to be God’s witnesses?

Isaiah 43:10: “You are My witnesses,” says the LORD, “And My servant whom I have chosen, That you may know and believe Me, And understand that I am He. Before Me there was no God formed, Nor shall there be after Me. Acts 1:8: But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you; and you shall be witnesses to Me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” 1 John 3:7: Little children, let no one deceive you. He who practices righteousness is righteous, just as He is righteous. 1 John 3:9: Whoever has been born of God does not sin, for His seed remains in him; and he cannot sin, because he has been born of God.
What does grace teach, according to Titus 2:11?

He quotes Titus 2:11, that grace “offers salvation to” all, and says “it’s not just divine favor, it’s divine enablement by keeping the word of God.” He says “Grace says no” to ungodliness and worldly passions and yes to self-control, so that we live “upright and godly lives in this present world.”
What does grace teach, according to Titus 2:11?

Amen. And you’re just joined the church, there’s no power, but when you join the Jesus and his word, there’s power. Be convicted and live for him. Is that a good amen, church? Titus 2:11, “The grace of God offers salvation to,” how many? All. I’m not saved by grace, I’m not saved by faith, I’m saved by grace through faith, not of works, that’s in [unclear] both, okay. These people say, “By grace” and “Saved by grace,” I get sick of them justifying their life using the word grace. Let’s look at grace, how the apostles used it. Grace offers salvation to all men, but it also teaches us. So does grace have a doctrine? Yeah, it’s not just divine favor, it’s divine enablement by keeping the word of God. Wow, that was good. Did you guys get that? See, grace has a [unclear]. That we say no to ungodliness and worldly passions, worldly desires. We say what? No. I’m not going to get drunk, I’m not going to take drugs, I’m not going to join a gang, I’m not going to beat up my spouse, I’m not going to, uh, not work and be lazy and not provide for my [unclear]. No, I’m not going to do those things. Grace says no. So when you say, “I’m saved by grace,” you have the power to say no. Hallelujah. Now, and to live self-control. Every man and every woman wants to marry someone with self-control. Instead of shooting off their mouth all the time and displaying their anger and all this stuff, you know, yelling and screaming in front of the kids, arguing, which is just stupid, it’s fools do that. I’m just pausing, let it sink into you. Self-control comes from grace, as well as the Holy Spirit, as well as the Bible. And self-control is just controlling yourself. Work, provide for your home, go to church, pay your tithes, worship God, seek God, raise your family, your kids, in the way they should go. You say, “Self-control.” “Upright and godly lives,” living right, living godly lives in this, what? Present age. Don’t give me this rapture stuff, don’t give me this any-minute-coming. Okay, you have a goal of God for him to bring you to a place where you live self-control, upright and godly lives in this present world, so that they see the light in you and come and inquire of your God and bring honor to Jesus Christ. And that’s much better than him coming a second time. Church, this present age he wants to bless your life, he wants you to make a difference now.
What does grace teach, according to Titus 2:11?

Titus 2:11-12: For the grace of God that brings salvation has appeared to all men, teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly in the present age,
What does he say Romans 1:25 means for the world today?

He reads Romans 1:25, “Who changed the truth of God into a lie,” and asks whether governments are “changing the truth of God into a lie right now through this homosexual acceptance.” He says in the New Testament “idolatry is greed,” applies that to welfare for illegal aliens, and quotes “If a man doesn’t work, neither let him eat.”
What does he say Romans 1:25 means for the world today?

Romans 1:25, “Who changed the truth of God into a lie, worshiping the creature,” the human being, “instead of the Creator.” Or the living animals, human beings, and as you know, they were talking about idols, making idols of birds of the air and animals and planets and all this, and they were talking about homosexuality, women with women, men with men. You see, they change what? The truth of God into a what? Lie. Is our Congress, are our governors, are our state legislatures changing the truth of God into a lie right now through this homosexual acceptance? Amen. Are they? Now, in the New Testament, idolatry is greed. I don’t know if you’re aware of that, but that’s what the New Testament says. Are by money turning the truth of God into a lie by giving the, the illegal aliens freedom to come in, giving them welfare, giving them food stamps, giving people two years or more of, of, of unemployment pay so they don’t have to work. That is idolatry. “If a man doesn’t work, neither let him eat.” See, you got to know, you’re about us Christians have got to know our Bible. It sounds so sympathetic, these little kids are coming across our border, “Oh my gosh, it’s the,” and I heard on Fox News that it’s the Christian duty to help people. I said, that’s also the Bible duty to punish criminals, as homosexuals. Isn’t that right? You can’t use the Bible in one area and then distort it in another area. That was good. Hallelujah. Now, who was full of grace and truth? Jesus, right? And you see, when we mess around with grace, we’re messing around with who Jesus is. When we mess around with truth, we’re messing with who Jesus is. And the same glory that Jesus has is the same glory the church has, and what is that? Grace that says no to ungodliness and worldly lust, and grace that says yes to self-control and living right.
What does he say Romans 1:25 means for the world today?

Romans 1:25: who exchanged the truth of God for the lie, and worshiped and served the creature rather than the Creator, who is blessed forever. Amen. 2 Thessalonians 3:10: For even when we were with you, we commanded you this: If anyone will not work, neither shall he eat.
What does “You have not called upon me” mean as a hindrance to victory?

He lists this as the first hindrance, from Isaiah 43:22. He says “people go to church to be entertained in America,” while in poorer countries “they really pray,” and that “corporate prayer is important in the Bible.” He says lifting hands is “recognizing that there’s a higher power than us.”
What does “You have not called upon me” mean as a hindrance to victory?

Folks, that’s good, that should make it plain to you. Hallelujah. Then he repeats, “I will do a new thing, remember not the former things, I’ll make rivers in the desert to give to my people drink.” He repeats it, you can go to those lessons and learn that. “These people have I formed, fashioned for myself, they shall show forth my,” what? Praise. My honor, my boasting, and what is, how do we do that? By living right. Amen. And if we mess up, we, we repent, we get up, we keep going. Now, [unclear] he’s going to hit the hindrances to victory over afflictions. Number one, “You have not called upon me,” Isaiah 43:22 through 28. “You have not called upon me.” You know, people go to church to be entertained in America. People go to church in third world countries to exist, to survive. They don’t fake prayers, they really pray just for food, clothing, and shelter. See, they don’t have the abundance. They really worship Jesus, they’re genuine, they don’t stand there like a knot on a log, they worship Jesus because they need him and they love him. America is really, in a large portion of a Christian America, a big difference. A very big difference. They won’t call upon Jesus. They don’t have time for prayer in a service, they gotta be out so that the next crowd can come in, so there’s no time for prayer. Corporate prayer is important in the Bible. Amen. We won’t call on the Lord, we’re too proud to bend our knee, raise our hands, as the Bible says, “I would that men everywhere lift up holy hands without anger, without doubting.” Get the hands up. Amen. That’s giving recognition to a sovereign one. When we near, when we do these humiliating things, it’s recognizing that there’s a higher power than us, and that is Jesus Christ. Higher authority, we’re the peasants, he’s the power. Number two, “You’ve grown weary of me,” you’ve been weary of me, impatient with me. Isn’t that what Israel did in Egypt? They got impatient with God. Moses came down and they got impatient. Yeah, I know none of you this morning ever get impatient.
What does “You have not called upon me” mean as a hindrance to victory?

Isaiah 43:22-28: “But you have not called upon Me, O Jacob; And you have been weary of Me, O Israel. You have not brought Me the sheep for your burnt offerings, Nor have you honored Me with your sacrifices. I have not caused you to serve with grain offerings, Nor wearied you with incense. You have bought Me no sweet cane with money, Nor have you satisfied Me with the fat of your sacrifices; But you have burdened Me with your sins, You have wearied Me with your iniquities. “I, even I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake; And I will not remember your sins. Put Me in remembrance; Let us contend together; State your case, that you may be acquitted. Your first father sinned, And your mediators have transgressed against Me. Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary; I will give Jacob to the curse, And Israel to reproaches. 1 Timothy 2:8: I desire therefore that the men pray everywhere, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and doubting;
How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?

He says the second hindrance is impatience: “you get impatient with God,” and “we take matters in our own hands.” The third is “No burnt offering”: he says Jesus is our burnt offering, “the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving,” and “If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint.”
How do impatience with God and forgotten offerings hinder victory?

I know you’re just perfect Christians. You don’t want to get impatient with your spouse, you get impatient with God. “God hasn’t changed him yet. God, how come you don’t straighten that spouse of mine out? I’ll do it for you, you [unclear], son of a [unclear].” When the Bible plainly says that bad words and good words don’t come out of the same fountain. That was good too. Hallelujah. There’s something wrong with the source when you do that, you understand? Hallelujah. So we get impatient, we get tired, and so we take matters in our own hands. If God wants to straighten my kids out, I’ll straighten them out. Burn them, I’ll stab them. I’ve dealt with burnt kids, stabbed kids, whatever. Beaten with a razor strap or whatever. Number three, “No burnt offering.” Now I mean, you know that in Leviticus, as I just read Leviticus this week, there’s five offerings. The burnt offering is the covering for sin, the meal offering is the remembrance, it’s the remembrance offering. There, you remember that the burnt offering covers your sin. Who’s our burnt offering? Jesus Christ. We don’t do animal sacrifices because he already did it. The meal offering reminds me that Jesus Christ still forgives, still cleanses and delivers from sin even though I’m saved. And then you had the thank offering, the peace offering. That’s where you just thank God, “Thank you, Lord.” “I will enter his gates with thanksgiving in my heart.” You see, the way into the presence of God is thanksgiving. Hebrews, the last chapter, says, “By him therefore let us offer the sacrifice of praise,” that thank offering, that peace offering, and then explains what it is: “the fruit of our lips giving thanks unto God.” If you are a silent saint, you’re not a growing saint. You got to learn to lift up your lips. It’s a sacrifice, because you don’t want to do it. Man, it was humiliating when they said, you know, “Lift your hands and, and, you know, praise God.” Oh gosh, this guy died a thousand deaths. But I had to get to the place where I wanted God or I wanted myself. Then you have the sin offering and the trespass offering, the guilt offering. How many know your sins are forgiven?
